Propulsion Manufacturing Manager
Astro Mechanica
San Francisco, CA
$200,000.00/yr - $275,000.00/yr
ABOUT US:
Astro Mechanica is a vertically integrated aerospace company developing a scalable technology platform to power critical infrastructure, mission operations, and the future of flight. We apply aerospace engineering and quality standards across our products, delivering high performance, reliability, and efficiency for the most demanding operating environments. Astro Mechanica is backed by leading venture and strategic investors, including Andreessen Horowitz (a16z), Giant Step Capital, United Airlines Ventures, and Voyager Ventures.
WHO WE ARE:
We’re a team of passionate engineers dedicated to advancing aerospace. We’re generalists with specialist depth, united by a flat structure and a shared obsession with building things that work well. We move fast, stay pragmatic, and let engineering excellence speak louder than hierarchy.
WHO YOU ARE:
Astro Mechanica is seeking a Propulsion Manufacturing Manager
to establish and scale the manufacturing operations of our ground power systems. This is a hands-on role for someone who thrives at the intersection of engineering, manufacturing, and operations. You will build our production capability from the ground up, transforming development hardware into repeatable, reliable, production-ready products that can be delivered to customers.
You will own the manufacturing processes, production workflows, and team development needed to scale output while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and reliability. Working closely with engineering, supply chain, and facilities teams, you will resolve technical and operational challenges, drive continuous improvement, and help turn our hardware into a scalable business. You excel at streamlining development hardware into a high-quality marketable product.
WHAT YOU’LL DO:
Establish the manufacturing floor plan, assembly stations, material flow, tooling, and inventory control systems needed to support efficient production
Create and maintain standard operating procedures, work instructions, process documentation, and assembly workflows that enable consistent, high-quality builds
Coordinate build schedules, labor, materials, and equipment to meet production targets and customer delivery commitments
Collaborate with responsible engineers to resolve non-conformances, manage quarantine inventory, and implement corrective actions
Hire, train, and develop a team of manufacturing engineers and technicians responsible for assembly, inspection, and hardware acceptance testing
Coordinate with supply chain to manage work orders, component traceability, hardware kitting, work-in-progress tracking, and material flow throughout the facility
Identify and implement improvements to improve yield, unit cost, rework, and production throughput
WHAT WE’RE LOOKING FOR:
10+ years of hands-on experience establishing, launching, or scaling production lines for complex engineered hardware
Demonstrated ability to translate development builds into repeatable manufacturing processes and production workflows
Experience coordinating cross-functional teams, including engineering, technicians, supply chain, facilities, and operations, to resolve production challenges
Experience building and leading manufacturing engineering and technician teams
Familiarity interpreting engineering drawings, GD&T, work instructions, inspection requirements, and nonconformance documentation
Experience implementing manufacturing procedures, material tracking, inventory controls, and hardware traceability systems
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes, implement corrective actions, and drive continuous improvement
Ability to manage competing priorities while maintaining safety, quality, and production schedule requirements
Comfortable safely handling heavy equipment and hardware using lifting fixtures, hoists, and other material-handling equipment
Strong attention to detail and a commitment to workmanship, documentation, and product quality
PERKS & BENEFITS:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance, including Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
401(k) program and transparent stock option plan
Self-managed and flexible time-off policy, including PTO, paid holidays, and sick time
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION:
At Astro Mechanica, we highly value in-office work to foster collaboration and strengthen our company culture. We consider working in the office five days a week an essential part of the employee's role.
Astro Mechanica is an equal opportunity employer. We proudly recruit and hire a diverse workforce and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
Compensation Range: $200K - $275K

Job Summary
Manage the complete operation of the Atlanta Lubricant Manufacturing Facility to ensure maximum efficiency of blending, packaging and customer fulfillment processes. Direct the manufacturing of products and control the inventory of finished products, raw materials including base oils, additives and containers as the MRP controller. Control and direct facility staffing and organization plan. Responsible for achieving and maintaining safety, environmental, health and training goals. Responsible for implementing accounting and inventory control programs. Manage the corporate relationship with the local community and various government agencies. Establish and execute facility long range plan, expenses, capital and staffing budgets. Develop major plant improvements. Make recommendations on new business opportunities for the facility as well as the lubricants business in general.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Engineering or related field plus 8 years manufacturing experience OR 12 years of lubricant manufacturing experience if no Bachelor's Degree.
Job Duties
Safety and Compliance: Ensuring a safe working environment is a top priority. Plant managers implement safety training programs, enforce OSHA and environmental regulations, conduct audits, and investigate incidents to prevent future hazards. Ensure proper use of personal protective equipment and adherence to hazard communication standards.2. Operational Oversight: Plant managers coordinate daily operations, including production scheduling, workflow monitoring, and inventory control, to ensure that manufacturing objectives are met efficiently and cost-effectively. Manage the flow of materials, labor utilization, and equipment to maintain production levels and quality standards.
Leadership and Team Development: Hiring, training, mentoring, and evaluating staff are key responsibilities. Plant managers set performance expectations, conduct reviews, resolve conflicts, and foster teamwork and accountability across departments.
Budget and Cost Management: Plant managers prepare and monitor budgets, control operating expenditures, and implement cost-effective systems for labor, wages, and maintenance. Make strategic decisions regarding staffing, equipment, and resource allocation to optimize financial performance.
Job Duties II
Strategic Planning: Beyond daily operations, plant managers collaborate with corporate leadership to align plant capabilities with business goals, evaluate new technologies, scale capacity, and plan long-term improvements They analyze KPIs and production data to identify trends and implement continuous improvement initiatives.
Maintenance and Equipment Management: Plant managers oversee maintenance schedules, ensure machinery reliability, and coordinate preventive maintenance to minimize downtime.
Project management: Direct Plant projects to keep them on schedule in Budget and safely completed. May also manage capital assets and approve production schedules to maintain operational efficiency.
Communication and Coordination: facilitate cross-department collaboration, lead production meetings, report performance metrics to stakeholders, and ensure smooth coordination between production, maintenance, supply chain, and quality control teams.

evidence.text:
Plant Manager
MOBIS Corporate Center of America
Blythewood, SC
The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, management, and operational performance of the Mobis South Carolina Electrified Powertrain (MSCe) manufacturing facility. This role directs and coordinates plant operations, including Production, Quality, Production Control & Material Management (PCMM), Logistics, and Maintenance, to achieve company objectives related to Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Morale (SQDCM).
The Plant Manager serves as the senior operational leader of the facility and is accountable for plant readiness, launch execution, production ramp-up, operational excellence, customer satisfaction, and long term business growth. This position provides both strategic and day-to-day operational leadership to ensure the successful achievement of startup, equipment installation and commissioning, pilot production, Start of Production (SOP), capacity expansion, and customer delivery objectives.
The Plant Manager acts as the primary plant representative for customer visits, operational reviews,
business discussions, audits, and performance escalation matters while maintaining close collaboration with Headquarters, MCCA, customers, suppliers, and regulatory agencies. As a key member of the site leadership team, the incumbent drives cross-functional alignment, organizational development, and continuous improvement across manufacturing operations.
Responsibilities
(To perform successfully in this position, the incumbent must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. Other duties may be assigned.)
Plant Operations Leadership
Lead and oversee all manufacturing operations to achieve company goals, production targets, and customer requirements.
Develop and implement operational strategies supporting plant startup, production ramp-up, capacity expansion, and long-term growth.
Lead plant readiness, launch management, equipment installation, commissioning, pilot production, SOP, and production ramp-up activities.
Establish and monitor key operational metrics, including Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Morale, and Productivity.
Drive cross-functional problem solving and continuous improvement initiatives to enhance plant performance.
Ensure compliance with MOBIS policies, customer requirements, and applicable laws and
regulations.
Act as the primary plant representative for customer visits, operational reviews, performance escalations, and strategic discussions.
Production Management
Direct all production activities to achieve production schedules, capacity targets, product quality requirements, and customer delivery commitments.
Optimize manufacturing resources, manpower planning, line balancing, equipment utilization, throughput, and overall operational effectiveness.
Lead production readiness for new programs and support process validation, trial builds, pilot production, and manufacturing process improvements.
Coordinate cross-functional activities to resolve operational issues, remove launch constraints, and ensure stable production performance.
Quality Leadership
Ensure compliance with the quality management system, customer-specific requirements, and applicable automotive industry standards.
Lead quality improvement initiatives and foster a culture of defect prevention, accountability, and continuous quality excellence.
Oversee customer quality performance, corrective actions, root cause investigations, containment activities, and audit readiness.
Support the implementation and maintenance of quality systems and processes aligned with IATF 16949, VDA requirements, and applicable OEM customer-specific requirements.
Production Control, Material Management & Logistics
Oversee production planning, material planning, inventory control, warehousing, and logistics operations.
Ensure uninterrupted and timely material availability to support launch and production requirements.
Monitor inventory accuracy, material flow efficiency, warehouse performance, and on-time delivery results.
Coordinate supply chain activities with customers, suppliers, and internal teams to achieve delivery, inventory, and production objectives.
Maintenance & Facility Readiness
Oversee maintenance programs to ensure equipment reliability, uptime, preventive maintenance effectiveness, and operational readiness.
Lead maintenance readiness for equipment installation, commissioning, trial production, SOP, and production ramp-up.
Promote safe operating practices and coordinate with the responsible EHS function to support compliance, incident prevention, and corrective actions.
Support facility readiness, utility availability, infrastructure improvements, and technical issue resolution required for plant operations.
Customer Management
Serve as the senior plant contact for OEM customers regarding plant performance, launch status, delivery, quality, capacity, and operational concerns.
Lead preparation for customer visits, audits, operational reviews, business meetings, and escalation discussions.
Ensure timely cross-functional response to customer concerns and oversee implementation of sustainable corrective actions.
Maintain effective customer relationships and align plant priorities with customer expectations and business commitments.
Organizational Leadership & Profitability Management
Manage plant operating budgets, capital expenditures (CAPEX), cost improvement initiatives, and overall plant financial performance.
Drive productivity, cost reduction, waste elimination, and profitability improvement while protecting safety, quality, and delivery performance.
Develop department leaders and support workforce planning, succession planning, organizational capability, and employee engagement.
Collaborate with Business Administration and executive leadership to achieve operational, financial, and strategic business objectives.
AUTHORITY & SCOPE
This position is responsible for the overall management and operational performance of MSCe
manufacturing operations, including Production, Quality, Production Control & Material Management (PCMM), Logistics, and Maintenance. The incumbent exercises independent judgment in plant operations, launch execution, production planning, resource allocation, cost and profitability management, quality performance, customer response, and operational improvement initiatives within approved company guidelines. The position partners closely with executive leadership, Headquarters, MCCA, customers, suppliers, and regulatory agencies to achieve business objectives and operational excellence.
Matters involving significant financial impact, strategic business decisions, legal risks, major
organizational changes, or significant customer escalations are reviewed with executive leadership as appropriate.
Supervisory Responsibilities:
Yes, Directly oversees department leaders responsible for Production, Maintenance, Quality, Production Control & Material Management (PCMM), and Logistics. Provides strategic leadership and operational direction across all manufacturing functions, ensuring alignment with business objectives while driving operational excellence, employee development, accountability, customer satisfaction, and continuous improvement throughout the organization.
QUALIFICATIONS
(The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skills, and/or abilities required and preferred for this position.)
Required Education & Experience:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Business Management, or a related field.
Minimum 15 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including at least 7 years of leadership experience in automotive manufacturing operations.
Demonstrated experience leading plant startup, greenfield launch, equipment installation and commissioning, pilot production, SOP, or production ramp-up activities.
Required Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Strong knowledge of automotive manufacturing operations, production systems, launch management, and operational excellence methodologies.
Thorough understanding of automotive quality standards and core tools, including IATF 16949, APQP, PPAP, FMEA, SPC, and MSA.
Working knowledge of VDA requirements and OEM customer-specific requirements applicable to the assigned business.
Strong knowledge of production planning, material management, inventory control, logistics, and supply chain operations.
Knowledge of maintenance management, equipment reliability, preventive maintenance, and manufacturing facility readiness.
Understanding of OSHA requirements and the ability to partner effectively with the responsible EHS function to support a safe and compliant workplace.
Proven ability to lead large, cross-functional manufacturing organizations and drive measurable operational performance.
Strong leadership, coaching, employee development, succession planning, and organizational management skills.
Excellent communication, interpersonal, presentation, negotiation, customer management, and stakeholder management abilities.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, escalation management, and decision-making capabilities.
Experience managing operating budgets, cost reduction initiatives, capital investments, profitability, and business planning activities.
Ability to balance strategic planning with hands-on operational execution in a fast-paced startup and manufacturing environment.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel, PowerPoint, and Word, and experience with manufacturing reporting systems.
Preferred Education & Experience
Experience in automotive, electric vehicle (EV), battery, electrified powertrain, or advanced manufacturing environments.
Experience leading a greenfield project, startup plant, major plant launch, or capacity expansion.
Experience overseeing Production, Quality, Production Control & Material Management, Logistics, and Maintenance functions.
Experience working within a global manufacturing organization and matrix reporting structure.
Experience supporting OEM customer requirements, customer audits, launch reviews, and performance escalations.
Experience coordinating with Headquarters, regional leadership teams, suppliers, customers, and regulatory agencies.
Lean Manufacturing and Continuous Improvement leadership experience preferred.
Certificates, Licenses & Registrations
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt, Black Belt, or equivalent Continuous Improvement certification preferred.
Working Conditions:
Manufacturing plant environment with routine presence on the production floor and frequent interaction with Production, Quality, Maintenance, Logistics, and administrative personnel.
The incumbent is expected to regularly support plant readiness activities, equipment installation and commissioning, pilot production, SOP preparation, production operations, customer visits, audits, operational reviews, continuous improvement initiatives, and capacity expansion activities at the MSCe manufacturing facility.
Occasional domestic and international travel may be required for training, customer meetings,
benchmarking activities, business reviews, supplier visits, and coordination with Headquarters, MCCA, customers, and other MOBIS operations. The position may require extended working hours during plant startup, production ramp-up, major operational events, customer support activities, audits, or other business-critical situations.

Robotics Head of Production
Cleo Robotics
Boston, MA
Full-time, exempt
Boston, Massachusetts
On-site, five days per week

About Us
Cleo Robotics builds unconventional autonomous robotic systems designed to operate in the world’s most challenging and inaccessible environments. Our mission is to deploy intelligent machines into critical environments to improve operational efficiency, reduce unplanned downtime, and keep people out of harm’s way. Our technology is used across industries including energy, oil and gas, manufacturing, public safety, and defense. We’re a growing team of experts in robotics and autonomous systems with diverse backgrounds and skills. We value making an impact, thinking big, leading with empathy, and having fun along the way.
If you get excited about solving big problems and building robots straight from science fiction, and you thrive in a fast-paced environment, this role might be for you!
About The Role
Cleo Robotics is seeking a Head of Production to build our production function from the ground up. This is a foundational, first-of-its-kind role responsible for transforming our current small batch builds into scalable production.
You will begin as a hands-on builder, working directly on assembly while owning production strategy, supplier development, and team building.You will own production end-to-end — from first build to scaled manufacturing — including output, quality, cost, and delivery.
In the early stages, you will spend a significant portion of your time personally executing core production work (assembly, testing, inventory, fulfillment), while simultaneously designing the systems, infrastructure, and processes that will enable scale.

Director of Operations
Valmont Industries, Inc.
Plymouth, IN
15000 Valmont Plaza Omaha Nebraska 68154
Why Valmont
We’re Here to Move the World Forward.
Valmont impacts millions of people around the world every day, yet they might not realize the many ways. Our technology is helping feed the growing population, supplying the world with more reliable energy and access to renewables, enhancing connectivity in remote and urban locations to create a sustainable future and so much more. Simply put, Valmont is advancing agricultural productivity and reimagining vital infrastructure to make life better.
Join a Fortune 1000 company that respects hard work, honors diversity and invests in our employees as we focus on creating the world of tomorrow, today. We are the modern workforce. Are you ready to move the world forward? Apply now.
A Brief Summary Of This Position
The Director of Operations is responsible for the overall performance of assigned manufacturing locations, including safety, quality, delivery, cost, and asset utilization. This role provides leadership, direction, and accountability to ensure operations deliver predictable, high-quality output while supporting division and corporate objectives. The Director of Operations is accountable for building and sustaining disciplined, system-driven operations that scale throughput, improve reliability, and deliver consistent customer performance without reliance on reactive execution.
Essential Functions
This position reports to the VP GM North America Telecom.
The ability to travel domestically up to 50% of the time.
Drive performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and Cash (SQDCC)
Ensure operations run to a predictable, system-based plan, not reactive prioritization
Monitor and improve throughput, schedule adherence, and capacity utilization
Ensure customer commitments are met with consistency and discipline
Establish and enforce a structured Asset Care & Reliability (ACR) approach across all sites
Drive improvements in Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) through reduction of downtime and improved maintenance practices
Ensure visibility and management of key reliability metrics (OEE, MTBF, MTTR, downtime)
Partner with Maintenance, Advanced Manufacturing Engineering and Technology (AMET), and Global Engineering Manufacturing Solutions (GEMS) to improve equipment performance and uptime
Eliminate reliance on reactive maintenance and drive progression toward planned and predictive maintenance systems
Ensure quality is built into the process, not inspected at the end
Hold site leadership accountable for in-process quality execution and outcomes
Drive root cause problem solving for quality issues and eliminate repeat defects
Lead continuous improvement efforts focused on operational outcomes, not isolated projects
Integrate Continuous Improvement into daily operations across safety, quality, material flow, and production flow
Ensure disciplined execution of standard work, operating systems, and planning tools
Develop and coach site Plant Managers and leadership teams
Build leadership depth and succession capability across all sites
Drive accountability across cross-functional teams including Product Line, Sales, Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, and Maintenance
Other Important Details About The Role
Acts as the central leader for operational performance across assigned facilities
Balances strategic leadership with operational execution
Requires frequent presence on the production floor
Drives a culture of discipline, accountability, and system-based execution
Focuses on stability and predictability of operations rather than reactive performance
Partners closely with site leadership to remove systemic barriers
Success is measured by consistent, repeatable operational performance without reliance on heroics
Required Qualifications Of Every Candidate
Preferred Bachelors with 10+ years of relevant experience or associate’s degree with 12+ years relevant experience or 15+ years of relevant experience
10+ years of progressive operations leadership experience in a manufacturing environment
Multi-site leadership experience preferred
Strong understanding of manufacturing operations, maintenance systems, and continuous improvement
Proven ability to drive operational performance and reliability improvements
Strong problem-solving and analytical skills
Ability to lead cross-functional teams and drive accountability
Effective communication and leadership presence across all levels
Working Environment And Physical Efforts
Work is typically performed in a manufacturing plant environment and the incumbent needs to be able to move about the office and production environments. There is often exposure to conditions such as dust, dirt, heat, fumes, and cold as well as noise levels above 80 decibels. Many aspects of this role are physical and the incumbent has to be able to lift up to 50 lbs. The employee is regularly required to reach with hands and arms. The incumbent is frequently required to stand, walk, sit, use hands to finger, handle, feel, as well as balance, stoop, kneel, crouch, talk, and hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, and depth perception.

Healthcare (medical, prescription drugs, dental and vision)
401k retirement plan with company match
Paid time off
Employer paid life insurance
Employer paid short-term and long-term disability including maternity leave
Work Life Support
Tuition Reimbursement up to $5,250 per year
Voluntary programs like tobacco cessation, Type 2 diabetes reversal, one-on-one health coaching, mortgage services and more

evidence.quote: Bachelor’s degree in a relevant scientific, engineering, quality, or related field and at least 16 years of progressively responsible quality experience in biologics development and manufacturing; an advanced degree is preferred. Experience with vaccines, viral vectors, or similarly complex biologics is strongly preferred.
evidence.text:
Vice President, Quality
Sabin Vaccine Institute
United States
Description
Department:
Research & Development (R&D)
Reports to:
President, R&D
Location:
Remote Work, US only
Why Sabin
Our mission is to make vaccines more accessible, enable innovation, and expand immunization across the globe. We seek a future free from vaccine-preventable diseases. We are an innovative, collaborative, and engaged team that values accountability, teamwork, partnership, and driving impact. We are vaccine champions improving lives through immunization. Sabin staff, management, and the Board of Trustees are committed to ensuring that fairness, integrity, and opportunity remain at the core of how we operate.
Position Summary
At Sabin, R&D is focused on advancing vaccines through development and addressing unmet needs. The Vice President, Quality provides strategic and operational leadership for GxP quality across Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP), Good Clinical Practice (GCP), Good Pharmacovigilance Practices (GVP), and Good Laboratory Practice (GLP).
This role builds and sustains a phase-appropriate Quality Management System (QMS) for a virtual nonprofit organization, ensuring that development activities remain integrated, risk-based, data-driven, compliant, and inspection-ready as programs advance through late-stage development, outbreak-response and emergency-use readiness, Process Performance Qualification (PPQ), Phase 3 clinical trials, regulatory submissions, inspections, licensure, and commercial readiness.
The Vice President establishes and oversees a scalable sponsor oversight model that defines decision rights, delegated responsibilities, quality agreements, governance forums, performance expectations, escalation pathways, and records-access requirements across internal teams and a global network of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, consultants, and other critical partners. The role balances regulatory obligations, program timelines, organizational capacity, and mission-driven priorities.
As a member of the R&D Leadership Team, the Vice President establishes quality strategy and governance, strengthens quality culture, advises executive leadership, and builds a high-performing Quality organization. This position serves as Sabin’s primary authority on GxP compliance, quality risk management, and inspection readiness.
Responsibilities
Develop and execute a roadmap for evolving the current mid-stage clinical phase-appropriate QMS into a mature QMS spanning GMP, GCP, GVP, and GLP to support advanced development activities, licensure-enabling regulatory submissions and inspections, and commercial readiness.
Serve as a strategic advisor to executive leadership on quality, compliance, inspection readiness, and risk management.
Embed quality culture across functions, partners, and development programs and strengthen organizational capabilities for increasing regulatory complexity.
Own quality governance, metrics, escalation pathways, management review, and quality risk management frameworks.
Provide senior leadership, guidance, and direction for:
GMP quality activities supporting vaccine development, technology transfer, process validation, PPQ, commercial readiness, and lifecycle management.
GCP quality systems supporting clinical development, including audit programs, inspection readiness, vendor oversight, and quality risk management.
GVP quality activities supporting pharmacovigilance throughout clinical development and post-authorization, including adverse-event reporting, signal management, aggregate safety reporting, and regulatory compliance.
GLP-related quality activities supporting nonclinical studies, including pivotal nonhuman primate studies.
Establish and approve quality agreements and oversee risk-based qualification, auditing, monitoring, and periodic requalification of CDMOs, CROs, laboratories, depots, and other GxP partners. Ensure clear responsibilities, escalation and reporting requirements, audit and data-access rights, change and deviation notification, CAPA management, inspection support, and remediation.
Provide quality oversight for validated GxP systems, document and data governance, records retention, data integrity, and remote-inspection capabilities. Partner with IT to support cybersecurity and business-continuity requirements for GxP systems.
Lead inspection readiness and serve as the sponsor quality lead for FDA Bioresearch Monitoring (BIMO), Pre-Approval Inspections (PAIs), surveillance inspections, and other health authority inspections, including inspection logistics, subject-matter expert preparation, document production, response strategy, and closure of regulatory commitments.
Direct critical investigations involving serious breaches, significant safety or data-integrity concerns, material manufacturing deviations, or systemic quality failures, ensuring timely containment, root-cause analysis, regulatory assessment, and sustainable corrective and preventive action (CAPA).
Ensure quality systems and GxP documentation are complete, controlled, inspection-ready, and aligned with applicable FDA, EMA, ICH, WHO, and other regulatory expectations.
Identify and escalate quality risks, drive timely mitigation, and support alignment with internal stakeholders and funding partners.
Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing Quality professionals.
Provide strategic oversight and contribute to required quality content for Investigational New Drug applications (INDs), Biologics License Applications (BLAs), Marketing Authorization Applications (MAAs), responses to health authority information requests, and other associated regulatory submissions.
Provide Quality leadership for funding proposals and due-diligence activities.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in a relevant scientific, engineering, quality, or related field and at least 16 years of progressively responsible quality experience in biologics development and manufacturing; an advanced degree is preferred. Experience with vaccines, viral vectors, or similarly complex biologics is strongly preferred.
Proven people-leadership experience and success driving organizational change, preferably in a small biotechnology and/or virtual organization. Experience serving on an R&D or executive leadership team is preferred.
Demonstrated success developing or substantially transforming a QMS in preparation for late-stage development and licensure.
Direct experience supporting late-stage clinical development, process validation, PPQ, PAI readiness, and BLA/MAA submissions.
Experience leading health authority inspections and interacting with FDA and other global regulatory agencies.
Expert knowledge of GMP, GCP, GLP, and GVP requirements; relevant ICH guidelines, including ICH E6(R3), E8, E9, Q9, and Q10; and applicable FDA, EMA, MHRA, WHO, and other global regulatory expectations.
Demonstrated experience establishing sponsor oversight and quality governance across outsourced development and manufacturing networks, including CDMOs, CROs, and contract laboratories.
Broad understanding of the interdependencies among nonclinical development, translational science, Phase 3 clinical operations, pharmacovigilance, biostatistics and data management, CMC, regulatory strategy, and quality, with the ability to identify and mitigate cross-functional risks to licensure.
Demonstrated ability to lead collaboratively across technical functions, external partners, geographic regions, and matrixed teams, with strong judgment, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills.
Experience supporting U.S. government-funded projects is preferred.
Other
Must demonstrate interest in furthering Sabin’s mission.
Subject to a criminal background investigation.
Request for three professional references.
Verification of education/degrees.
Work Authorization
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States without employer sponsorship.
Compensation And Benefits
Sabin’s philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased, equitable, competitive compensation and benefits. Using benchmarking and salary survey data, the annual salary for this position is up to $315,000. The exact compensation may vary based on skills, experience, training, and certifications/degree. As a grant-funded organization, Sabin actively seeks funding for existing and new programs.
Sabin provides a comprehensive benefits package for eligible employees, featuring medical, dental, and vision coverage as well as flexible spending accounts. Eligible employees enjoy flexible vacation leave, sick leave, and both short-term and long-term disability options. The organization observes 10 federal holidays plus an end-of-year winter break. Additionally, Sabin offers an employer matching 401(k) plan.
Notice to Recruiters/Staffing Agencies
Recruitment vendors may not contact Sabin hiring managers, executives, or employees and must have an executed agreement on file. Unsolicited resumes do not create an agreement, and Sabin is not responsible for related fees.
Sabin is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to their race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, age, disability or genetic information, sex (including gender identity, pregnancy or sexual orientation), marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state or local laws.
Salary Description
$250,000 - $315,000

evidence.quote: 5+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, production, or operations.
evidence.text:
Director of Operations
Modern Herb Co
Canton, NC
Modern Herb Co is a cannabis brand focused on creating shippable, high-quality products through a blend of plant alchemy and scientific innovation. The company serves quality-conscious connoisseurs seeking reliable, targeted effects and elevated experiences. Modern Herb Co is known for award-winning live resin offerings that highlight the full spectrum of the plant. Team members join a culture that values craftsmanship, consistency, and responsible cannabis enjoyment. The company is committed to advancing modern cannabis formulations while maintaining strict quality standards.
Director of Operations
The Hemp Collect is growing fast, and our Canton manufacturing operation is at the center of that growth.
We are looking for a Director of Operations who can run the operation end to end today while building the systems, leaders, and accountability needed for tomorrow.
What You'll Do:
Own Production & Throughput
Own daily production output across production, packaging, and filling.
Establish and manage units-per-hour targets and the incentive structure connected to them.
Build production schedules around demand, inventory, labor, and laboratory capacity.
Identify and remove the constraints keeping teams from hitting production goals.
Drive continuous improvement in changeover time, scrap and waste, line balance, and labor productivity.
Build the staffing model, shift structure, training pipeline, and leadership structure needed to scale the packaging organization.
Own Inventory & Supply
Own inventory accuracy, PAR levels, cycle-count discipline, and transaction integrity.
Oversee purchasing and supply planning through the Inventory Control Manager and Inventory Data Analyst.
Ensure raw materials, components, packaging, and finished goods are available when needed.
Balance availability with working capital by preventing both production-stopping stockouts and unnecessary overbuying.
Use data to identify supply risks before they become production problems.
Protect Quality, Compliance & Laboratory Operations
Oversee the Formulation Supervisor and laboratory team across formulation, R&D support, and quality coordination. Partner with Product Dev team to coordinate on new launches and SKU pages outs*
Maintain the independence and integrity of quality operations.
Ensure GMP practices, batch records, labeling, retains, and audit readiness remain at a high standard.
Partner with Product Development and laboratory leadership to keep testing and product release moving.
Maintain a culture where quality and compliance are never compromised for speed.
Lead Fulfillment & Facility Operations
Oversee B2B and DTC fulfillment through the Facilities & Logistics Manager.
Own pick, pack, shipping accuracy, on-time delivery, and carrier compliance.
Maintain equipment uptime, facility safety, maintenance, and overall operational readiness.
Partner with leadership on capital planning and investments that improve capacity, efficiency, and reliability.
Build the Leadership Team
Establish clear goals, KPIs, expectations, and accountability rhythms.
Coach managers through performance, communication, delegation, and decision-making.
Address performance issues directly and consistently.
Build internal career paths from production and packaging roles into lead and supervisor positions.
Create cross-training and succession plans that strengthen the operation.
Partner with HR on hiring and organizational planning.
Build a culture where people understand what success looks like and have the support to achieve it.
What You Bring
5+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, production, or operations.
Experience leading multiple functions and multiple layers of management.
Demonstrated experience managing and developing managers.
Experience in a regulated or quality-controlled manufacturing environment such as GMP, food and beverage, pharmaceutical, supplements, cannabis, hemp, or a comparable industry.
Experience improving throughput, productivity, quality, and cost in an hourly workforce environment.
Hands-on experience with an MRP, ERP, WMS, or comparable operational system. Experience with Katana is a plus.
Strong understanding of inventory management and production planning.
Comfort using operational data and KPIs to make decisions and hold teams accountable.
A hands-on leadership style and willingness to spend the majority of your time on the production floor.
Must be 21+ and comfortable working in the hemp-derived cannabinoid industry.
Why Work With Us?
The Hemp Collect is building a company around high standards, quality products, ownership, and people who care about doing exceptional work.
We are a growing business in an evolving industry, which means there is meaningful work to do and real opportunity to make an impact. We give strong performers autonomy, trust, and room to grow, while investing in people who want to build something rather than simply maintain it.
This role offers:
A meaningful leadership role with direct influence over a growing manufacturing operation.
The opportunity to build systems and teams that can scale significantly.
A clear path toward General Manager for the person who earns it through results.
Competitive compensation and performance-based upside.
Cigna health insurance through Gusto.
Human Interest 401(k).
PTO and sick leave accrual.
Paid Holidays.
Employee product discount.
The autonomy to improve processes, develop leaders, and make a measurable difference.
Location: Canton, NC
Work Arrangement: On-site
Employment Type: Full-time, exempt
Age Requirement: 21+
This role operates in a manufacturing, laboratory, and warehouse environment. The position requires regular standing and walking, use of hands to operate equipment and handle materials, and occasional lifting of up to 50 pounds. PPE is required in designated production, laboratory, and shipping areas.
Pay: From $115,000.00 per year

items.title: Sr. Staff Manufacturing Engineer, Power Electronics

evidence.quote: Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering or a related engineering discipline; Master’s degree preferred
evidence.text:
Sr. Staff Manufacturing Engineer, Power Electronics
Rivian
Carson, CA
About Rivian
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
Role Summary
As a Sr. Staff Manufacturing Engineer for Power Electronics, you will serve as the principal technical authority bridging internal Design Release Engineers (DREs), Manufacturing Engineering (ME), and external supplier/Contract Manufacturer (CM) partners. You will ensure that future suppliers are rigorously vetted and that their manufacturing capabilities, processes, and equipment setups are sufficiently robust, reliable, and scalable before sourcing decisions and design locks are finalized.
In this role, you will evaluate and vet suppliers manufacturing critical power electronics components, including high pressure die-cast housings, high-voltage busbars, LV/HV headers, seals, DC link capacitors, metal brackets, EMI filter cores, and power modules used across traction inverters, DC charging power electronics modules, and energy management control units (EMCUs). Additionally, you will drive DFM/DFx reviews, partner with automation/equipment
integrators on process development, validate equipment capability (Cp/Cpk, GR&R), and support pilot line stand-up through full NPI and production ramp.
This position is based at our Carson, CA facility and reports directly to the Power Electronics Mechanical Engineering Director.
Responsibilities
Lead end-to-end technical vetting, auditing, and approval of potential suppliers, CMs, and equipment integrators. Conduct process capability evaluations, run-at-rate audits, and facility reviews (on candidate line setups or equivalent production lines) to prove supplier capability matches ramp plans prior to sourcing
Work side by side with mechanical design engineers to optimize power electronics assemblies for producibility, establish vendor-aligned design rules, reduce BOM cost and complexity, and resolve process risks prior to design freeze
Evaluate and validate manufacturing processes, tooling, and fixtures across core supplier components, including high-pressure die castings, HV/LV headers and busbars, seals, DC link capacitors, metal brackets, EMI filter cores, and power modules
Lead technical reviews of machine requirements and equipment designs with third-party automation suppliers. Drive formal equipment qualification processes, including system correlation, process capability analysis, and Gage Repeatability & Reproducibility (GR&R)
Partner with internal manufacturing teams and sourced integrators on pilot line setups, shop layout optimization, Factory Acceptance Testing (FAT), Site Acceptance Testing (SAT), and line handover for next-generation power electronics production lines (e.g.,900V EMCU and SPIM)
Lead architecture reviews and design phase gate decisions, ensuring solutions are scalable, manufacturable and aligned with program objectives
Design and engineer complex subsystems including high-pressure die castings, injection-molded plastics, busbars, sheet metal, HV/LV harnesses, sealing interfaces and PCBA mechanical integration
Own the full mechanical release cycle in ENOVIA, governing data integrity, design maturity and BOM accuracy across multiple concurrent programs
Drive weekly technical reviews with suppliers to resolve open design items, enforce DFM alignment, and maintain delivery commitments
Act as the senior technical escalation point for Supplier Quality on critical path issues
Support the generation of high-impact engineering documents including Component Technical Specifications (CTS), Statements of Work (SOW), system-level DFMEAs, and assembly manuals
Implement data-driven methodologies for workmanship, maintenance, process controls, and end-to-end data retention/traceability. Drive yield improvement initiatives and eliminate manufacturing bottlenecks to ensure supplier capacity meets demand
Lead structured root-cause and corrective action investigations (8D, 5-Whys) for process and prototype failures, leveraging advanced analytical failure techniques (e.g., Optical Inspection, X-Ray, Cross-Sectioning, SEM)
Function as a technical program bridge across ME, testing, DREs, Supply Chain, and executive leadership to align program schedules, manage risks, and ensure transparent status reporting
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering or a related engineering discipline; Master’s degree preferred
8+ years of progressive engineering experience in manufacturing engineering, supplier industrialization, or DFM roles, with a focus on high-volume automation, precision assembly, and tooling development
Proven track record vetting, auditing, and managing external suppliers, contract manufacturers (CMs), and equipment integrators
Hands-on process engineering experience with precision joining (laser welding, dispensing, heat staking, mechanical fasteners), thermal interface material (TIM) application, high-pressure die casting, and injection molding
Deep experience in manufacturing process verification, including equipment capability testing, GR&R, run-at-rate audits, and statistical process control (SPC)
Expert command of GD&T (ASME Y14.5) and a track record developing tolerance stack-up analysis for complex power electronics assemblies
Familiarity with failure analysis techniques (e.g., X-Ray, CSAM, SEM, EDS, Cross-Sectioning)
Demonstrated ability to lead structured root-cause analysis (8D, Fishbone, 5-whys) on complex field and manufacturing failures
Experience working with high-voltage automotive power electronics assemblies (e.g.,traction inverters, electrified powertrains, EMCUs, DC fast charging modules, or battery systems)
Excellent cross-functional leadership, negotiation, and communication skills to influence external partners and internal engineering teams
Willingness and ability to travel domestically and internationally to support supplier audits, CM activities, and equipment commissioning
Familiarity with 3D CAD software (CATIA V5/V6 preferred)
Pay Disclosure
The salary range for this role is USD 176,200-220,300 for Southern California based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors, including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic partner, and children up to age 26, including but not limited to paid vacation, paid sick leave, and a competitive portfolio of insurance benefits including life, medical, dental, vision, short-term disability insurance, and long-term disability insurance to eligible employees. You may also have the opportunity to participate in Rivian’s 401(k) Plan and Employee Stock Purchase Program if you meet certain eligibility requirements. Full-time employee coverage is effective on their first day of employment. Part-time employee coverage is effective the first of the month following 90 days of employment. More information about benefits is available at rivianbenefits.com.
You can apply for this role through careers.rivian.com (or through internal-careers-rivian.icims.com if you are a current employee). This job is not expected to be closed any sooner than October 15th, 2026.
Equal Opportunity
Rivian is an equal opportunity employer and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local fair employment practices laws. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender expression, gender identity, genetic information or characteristics, physical or mental disability, marital/domestic partner status, age, military/veteran status, medical condition, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Rivian is committed to ensuring that our hiring process is accessible for persons with disabilities. If you have a disability or limitation, such as those covered by the Americans with Disabilities Act, that requires accommodations to assist you in the search and application process, please email us at candidateaccommodations@rivian.com.
Candidate Data Privacy and Technology
Rivian may collect, use and disclose your personal information or personal data (within the meaning of the applicable data protection laws) when you apply for employment and/or participate in our recruitment processes (“Candidate Personal Data”). This data includes contact, demographic, communications, educational, professional, employment, social media/website, network/device, recruiting system usage/interaction, security and preference information. Rivian may use your Candidate Personal Data for the purposes of (i) tracking interactions with our recruiting system; (ii) carrying out, analyzing and improving our application and recruitment process, including assessing you and your application and conducting employment, background and reference checks; (iii) establishing an employment relationship or entering into an employment contract with you; (iv) complying with our legal, regulatory and corporate governance obligations; (v) recordkeeping; (vi) ensuring network and information security and preventing fraud; and (vii) as otherwise required or permitted by applicable law.
Rivian may share your Candidate Personal Data with (i) internal personnel who have a need to know such information in order to perform their duties, including individuals on our People Team, Finance, Legal, and the team(s) with the position(s) for which you are applying; (ii) Rivian affiliates; and (iii) Rivian’s service providers, including providers of background checks, staffing services, and cloud services.
Rivian may transfer or store internationally your Candidate Personal Data, including to or in the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, and the European Union and in the cloud, and this data may be subject to the laws and accessible to the courts, law enforcement and national security authorities of such jurisdictions.
How We Use AI in Our Hiring Process: To ensure transparency, we want candidates to know that Rivian uses iCIMS Talent Cloud Artificial Intelligence (TCAI) and AI-enabled tools to assist with screening, reviewing, organizing and highlighting profiles and applications that match the key requirements for each role.
AI does not make hiring decisions: Qualified candidate applications are reviewed by a member of our team, and all decisions throughout the process are made by humans. We use AI to support efficiency and consistency, not to replace human judgment. We are committed to a fair, thoughtful, and equitable experience for every candidate.
Participation in AI profile matching is entirely voluntary. If you prefer that your profile not be used in this process, you can opt out at any time. Opting out means your profile will be excluded from automated matching and will not be surfaced for additional roles through this system. Your current application remains active and will not be affected in any way.
Please note that we are currently not accepting applications from third party application services.

Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering
BD
San Diego, CA
We Are The People Who Give Possibilities Purpose
BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.
Job Description
We are the makers of possible
BD is one of the largest global medical technology companies in the world. Advancing the world of health™ is our Purpose, and it’s no small feat. It takes the imagination and passion of all of us—from design and engineering to the manufacturing and marketing of our billions of MedTech products per year—to look at the impossible and find transformative solutions that turn dreams into possibilities.
We believe that the human element, across our global teams, is what allows us to continually evolve. Join us and discover an environment in which you’ll be supported to learn, grow and become your best self. Become a maker
of possible
with us.
I. General Function
Reporting to the Integrated Supply Chain Sr Director of Global Sustaining Engineering, the Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering will lead and scale our manufacturing operations through innovation and automation within our Connected Care landscape. The Director of Advanced Manufacturing Engineering will play a pivotal role in designing, specifying and implementing cutting-edge manufacturing equipment, technologies and processes, driving innovation, and ensuring the delivery of high-quality products and components at scale.
This role involves strategic planning, cross-functional collaboration, and aligning product changes to processes within the product lifecycle. Additionally, is responsible for driving innovation, operational excellence, and must be able to identify new opportunities for that will meet the evolving technologies.
II. Responsibilities
Define and drive the Design Transfer and Commercialization roadmap in alignment with business goals and market trends.
Identify and evaluate opportunities through business and customer insights streamlining the transfer and commercialization swim lane
Lead the development, design, and implementation of advanced manufacturing equipment, systems, technologies and processes to support current and future production goals including the expansion and optimization of our state-of-the-art production facilities.
Leverage Industry technologies, world class vendors and know-how
Spearhead the integration of cutting-edge automation, robotics, and digital manufacturing tools, ensuring simultaneous product/process engineering, seamless operation and optimized throughput.

Collaborate with design engineering, product development, supply chain and quality teams to ensure design for manufacturability, cost efficiency, and product quality.

Enhanced Staffing is recruiting for a Plant Manager to lead the startup, operational buildout, and long-term production leadership of a new state-of-the-art precast manufacturing facility currently being developed in the Forth Worth area.

Director of Manufacturing
No longer accepting applications
Freestyle Snacks
Atlanta Metropolitan Area
Director of Manufacturing & Commercialization
Location: Remote, with regular travel to production facilities
About Freestyle Snacks
At Freestyle Snacks, we're building the future of savory snacking. We take bold, flavorful olives and pickles from the best growing regions in the world and reinvent them in convenient, mess-free packaging that fits seamlessly into modern life, creating an entirely new way to snack on foods people already know and love.
Since launching in 2022, Freestyle has expanded to more than 7,000 retail locations nationwide, including Whole Foods, Target, Walmart, Costco, and Delta Air Lines. We're growing quickly and looking for ambitious, curious people who are energized by hard problems, happy getting their hands dirty, and hungry for real ownership.
About the Role
Freestyle Snacks is seeking a Director of Manufacturing & Commercialization to own how we make our products and how new ones get to market. This is not a compliance or paperwork role.
We produce through partner facilities in the U.S. and abroad, and our biggest constraints are capacity, cost of goods, consistency, and speed to market on new items. This role owns all four. The day-to-day is managing our co-manufacturers, quality, and food safety. The longer-term work is commercialization: you’ll make the team’s new product ideas come to life by challenging co-manufacturer recommendations, exploring alternatives, and landing on the best, most cost-effective solution. You'll have project management support on launches, so your focus is on execution.
You should be comfortable walking a plant floor, reading a costing model, and pushing back on a supplier in the same week. A background in food science or R&D is a plus. You will work directly with the Founder & CEO and partner closely with operations, finance, sales, and marketing.
What You'll Do
Own and Scale the Manufacturing Network
Own the co-manufacturing network as primary point of contact, from day-to-day communication through weekly calls, QBRs, and on-site production oversight.
Build the capacity plan for our growth, and source and qualify new partners so no single facility is a point of failure.
Run partner scorecards on RFT, OTIF, cost per pound, yield, and complaint rate, and hold facilities to agreed standards and corrective action timelines.
Build relationships strong enough that partners flag problems early and prioritize us when capacity is tight, and represent their capabilities and constraints inside Freestyle.
Partner with operations on production planning, lead times, MOQs, and inventory strategy.
Communicate early and honestly when an issue will affect supply, cost, or a customer commitment.
Evaluate equipment, automation, and capital investment opportunities to improve manufacturing capacity, efficiency, and cost.
Lead Commercialization
Execute the commercialization of new products, line extensions, and formats, from concept through trials, scale-up, and first commercial run.
Translate concepts into specs and feasibility assessments with our manufacturing partners.
Challenge co-manufacturer recommendations and explore alternative processes, formats, packaging, ingredients, and partners to find the best, most cost-effective path.
Own benchtop work, plant trials, costing, packaging development, and shelf-life and food safety validation for new items, and make the go/no-go call on technical readiness.
Work alongside the project lead on each launch, providing technical input on timelines, flagging risks early, and delivering your workstreams on schedule.
Negotiate Cost Savings
Negotiate co-manufacturing rates, tolling agreements, and contract terms, plus ingredient and packaging supply through competitive bids where it makes sense.
Find savings through run size, formulation, packaging design, case pack, and freight.
Lead SKU rationalization based on complexity, margin, and velocity.
Deliver measurable, year-over-year margin improvement without compromising quality.
Drive Performance and Quality
Own specs and finished goods standards for every SKU, and lead projects that improve throughput and quality while reducing cost.
Lead root cause analysis and corrective action for service and quality failures, and catch risks before they reach a customer.
Track consumer complaint trends by lot, facility, and production date and close the loop on root cause.
Ensure partners maintain the food safety programs, certifications, and documentation our customers require, including during retailer onboarding.
Who You Are
5+ years in food manufacturing, R&D, commercialization, or operations, ideally in CPG.
Hands-on experience managing co-manufacturers (not just internal plants), including sourcing partners, structuring agreements, and negotiating real, quantified cost savings.
Direct experience commercializing food products with co-manufacturers from concept through first production run, with the technical depth to challenge their recommendations and propose credible alternatives.
Fluent in COGS, unit economics, and metrics like OTIF, yield, and cost per pound, and you use them to run relationships, not just report them.
Enough food safety and quality knowledge to write a spec, read an audit, and hold a plant accountable. No QA certification required.
Calm under pressure and rigorous about root cause. You follow through until the fix holds.
Thrives in a startup: comfortable building the system while operating it, moving with urgency, and making sound decisions with imperfect information.
Clear communicator who can turn technical and cost issues into recommendations for a non-technical team.
Willing to be on the plant floor and travel ~30–40%, including internationally.
Why Join Freestyle?
Join one of the fastest growing brands in the category and make an outsized impact on its trajectory.
Healthcare benefits, 401(k), flexible PTO, and professional development opportunities.
Unlimited olives and pickles.
If you would like to be considered for this role please send your resume to ally@freestylesnacking.com

evidence.quote: Translate quality strategy into measurable business results, ensuring quality priorities are directly connected to customer experience, operational performance, growth, profitability, and risk reduction.
evidence.text:
Vice President, Quality
nVent
St Louis Park, MN
We’re looking for people who put their innovation to work to advance our success – and their own. Join an organization that ensures a more secure world through connecting and protecting our customers with inventive electrical solutions.
The Vice President of Quality is an enterprise leadership role accountable for enterprise quality performance, not just quality systems. This leader will define and execute nVent’s quality strategy across the full value chain, with direct accountability for improving customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality performance, warranty performance, product reliability, on-time-to-customer impact, and launch quality. The role will shift quality from a primarily compliance- and governance-centered function to a performance-driving enterprise capability that improves customer outcomes, operational execution, and business growth.
Reporting to the Chief Supply Chain Officer, the Vice President Quality will serve as the senior-most quality leader for nVent, setting the vision, operating model, performance expectations, capabilities, and accountability mechanisms required to scale quality as nVent grows. This leader will partner closely with segment presidents, operations, engineering, product management, sourcing and procurement, digital, commercial, legal, and finance leaders to embed quality into business decision-making and deliver measurable improvements in customer experience, reliability, warranty, launch readiness, supplier performance, operational quality, and quality-related business risk.
What You Will Experience In This Position
Enterprise Quality Performance and Accountability
Own enterprise quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, launch quality, and the impact of quality issues on on-time-to-customer performance.
Translate quality strategy into measurable business results, ensuring quality priorities are directly connected to customer experience, operational performance, growth, profitability, and risk reduction.
Establish clear enterprise, segment, region, business unit, and site-level accountability for the quality metrics that matter most to customers and the business.
Lead operating reviews that move beyond reporting activity to identifying performance gaps, driving root cause ownership, and sustaining measurable improvement.
New Product Quality and Launch Excellence
Elevate new product quality as a core enterprise capability, ensuring quality is designed into high-growth platforms, strategic programs, and critical infrastructure solutions from concept through launch and field performance.
Partner with engineering, product management, operations, and commercial leaders to strengthen quality planning, design validation, process validation, risk assessment, reliability requirements, and launch readiness across major programs such as Saturn, Avatar, Data Solutions growth initiatives, and other strategic launches.
Ensure robust NPI quality gates, readiness reviews, and escalation criteria are in place to prevent launch defects, customer escapes, warranty exposure, and reliability issues.
Build feedback loops from field performance, warranty, customer quality, and manufacturing quality data into product development and launch processes.
Digital Quality, Analytics, and Enterprise Quality Intelligence
Lead the evolution of digital quality as an enterprise capability, including predictive quality, AI-enabled risk detection, manufacturing quality analytics, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
Partner with Digital and Integrated Supply Chain leaders to modernize eQMS capabilities, automate quality workflows, strengthen data integrity, and establish a single source of truth for enterprise quality performance.
Use advanced analytics to identify leading indicators of quality risk across product design, suppliers, manufacturing processes, field performance, warranty, and customer experience.
Move the organization from lagging quality reporting to predictive and preventive insights that enable faster decisions, better prioritization, and measurable performance improvement.
Quality Management Systems, Compliance, and Standards
Lead the modernization, standardization, and continuous improvement of nVent’s Quality Management System, ensuring systems and standards enable performance improvement rather than becoming ends in themselves.
Ensure readiness and sustained compliance with applicable quality and regulatory standards, including ISO 9001 and other business-relevant standards such as ISO 14001, AS9100, customer-specific requirements, and regional regulatory expectations.
Strengthen management review, internal audit, external audit, and corrective and preventive action processes to ensure systemic issues are identified, resolved, and prevented from recurring.
Partner with legal, compliance, engineering, operations, and commercial teams to manage quality-related risk and ensure quality commitments are understood, objective, and executable.
Customer, Supplier, and Operational Quality
Build customer quality capability that improves responsiveness, transparency, containment, corrective action effectiveness, customer confidence, and reduction of repeat escapes.
Advance supplier quality strategy, qualification, audit discipline, scorecards, supplier development, and escalation processes to improve supplier performance and protect customer commitments.
Embed quality into manufacturing and operational processes with a focus on defect prevention, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, error proofing, and flow to customer.
Use customer feedback, warranty data, supplier performance, manufacturing quality, field performance, and operational metrics to prioritize systemic improvement opportunities.
Leadership, Talent, and Quality Culture
Champion a quality-first culture where leaders model prevention-based decision-making and teams are empowered to stop, escalate, and resolve issues before they reach the customer.
Build, develop, and inspire a high-performing quality leadership team with clear accountability, succession depth, and strong capability across enterprise, segment, regional, and site quality roles.
Lead through influence in a matrixed environment, balancing enterprise standards with business-specific execution needs and measurable performance outcomes.
Model executive leadership behaviors, including strategic thinking, courageous decision-making, stakeholder engagement, talent development, collaboration, adaptability, and self-accountability.
You Have
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
15+ years of progressive quality, operations, engineering, or supply chain leadership experience in a global manufacturing environment, including significant leadership of multi-site or enterprise quality functions.
Demonstrated experience improving quality performance outcomes, including customer escapes, cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, supplier quality, warranty, reliability, and launch quality.
Strong experience in new product quality, design validation, process validation, launch readiness, reliability engineering, and quality risk management for complex product portfolios.
Experience advancing digital quality capabilities, including eQMS, quality analytics, digital traceability, predictive insights, and AI-enabled risk detection.
Proven ability to lead enterprise-level change across a complex, matrixed, global organization.
Exceptional communication, influencing, and executive presence, with the ability to translate quality priorities into business value.
Willingness to travel domestically and internationally as required.
Suggested Success Measures
Reduced customer escapes and repeat quality issues, with improved containment, responsiveness, and corrective action effectiveness.
Improved cost of poor quality, first-pass yield, process capability, reliability, warranty performance, and on-time-to-customer impact from quality issues.
Improved supplier quality performance through stronger qualification, development, governance, scorecards, and corrective action discipline.
Stronger new product quality outcomes, including improved launch readiness, fewer launch defects, reduced warranty exposure, and better reliability performance.
Expanded digital quality maturity, including predictive quality insights, AI-enabled risk detection, digital traceability, and enterprise quality intelligence.
Increased quality maturity from reactive issue management to proactive prevention, measurable performance improvement, and stronger enterprise accountability.
We Have
A dynamic global reach with diverse operations around the world that will stretch your abilities, provide plentiful career opportunities, and allow you to make an impact every day
nVent is a leading global provider of electrical connection and protection solutions. We believe our inventive electrical solutions enable safer systems and ensure a more secure world. We design, manufacture, market, install and service high performance products and solutions that connect and protect some of the world's most sensitive equipment, buildings and critical processes. We offer a comprehensive range of systems protection and electrical connections solutions across industry-leading brands that are recognized globally for quality, reliability and innovation.
Our principal office is in London and our management office in the United States is in Minneapolis. Our robust portfolio of leading electrical product brands dates back more than 100 years and includes nVent CADDY, ERICO, HOFFMAN, ILSCO, SCHROFF and TRACHTE. Learn more at www.nvent.com.
Commitment to strengthen communities where our employees live and work
We encourage and support the philanthropic activities of our employees worldwide
