evidence.quote: A minimum of 10 years of quality / regulatory experience including at least 5 years of prior experience leading a quality / regulatory role.
evidence.text:
Director Quality
Thermo Fisher Scientific
Middletown, VA
Work Schedule
Standard (Mon-Fri)
Environmental Conditions
Office
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you’ll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world’s toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
As Director of Quality and Compliance,
you will be responsible for taking a transformative approach to leading a dynamic and high-functioning Quality Assurance team at the Thermo Fisher Scientific, Clinical Diagnostics Division site in Middletown VA
The successful candidate will be responsible for raising the bar in process and culture across all aspects of quality system and compliance at the location, which performs development and manufacture of IVD products in adherence to applicable global regulations and standards such as US FDA QMSR, IVDD / IVDR, ISO13485:2016 (under MDSAP) and other GMP standards.
You will have responsibility for advising and collaborating with Manufacturing, Technical Operation and Commercial functions on quality and quality system requirements to ensure activities remain in compliance, and for driving continued evolution of the Quality function and site quality system to ensure it remains adequate to business needs and is successfully implemented.
This is a highly visible role at the site and Division level and, as a key member of the leadership team, you will report to the CDD Vice President, Global Quality Assurance & Regulatory Affairs.
A critical aspect of this role is serving as the primary quality representative for customers and regulatory authorities. As the site's Management Representative, the Director is responsible for ensuring the effectiveness of the Quality Management System and leading interactions during FDA inspections, MDSAP and ISO 13485 audits, and customer audits. This role requires strong leadership and communication skills to build customer confidence, maintain regulatory compliance, and represent Thermo Fisher Scientific with credibility and professionalism.
Key Responsibilities:
Acts as Management Representative of the Quality System and official correspondent of the site to all regulators (including US FDA). Primary contact at the site for all audits (regulator, Notified Body and customer).
Serve as a member of the site leadership team, providing strategic direction and influencing business decisions to ensure quality, compliance, and operational excellence are integrated into site objectives.
Establish strategies and drives actions to ensure the Quality Management System is adequate and successfully implemented to remain in sustained compliance with applicable regulations and standards.
Responsible for site product quality, compliance, conformance to quality requirements and specifications, and customer quality requirements. Supports regulatory recalls and interaction with government agencies.
Directly interacts with customers and OEM partners in relation to quality agreements, and quality matters associated with provided products and services.
Champion risk-based decision making by overseeing quality risk management processes and ensuring risks are identified, assessed, mitigated, and monitored throughout the product lifecycle.
Attracts, develops, and retains top talent to build an outstanding quality / regulatory function. Implements the required interpersonal structures and operating mechanisms to maintain appropriate oversight of the compliance status of the business and achieve results.
Grows and develops a customer-focused culture of personal quality in all site functions through leading, educating, and motivating site personnel using industry-leading practices.
Establishes and leads annual personnel resource and financial plans for the quality / regulatory organization.
Establishes annual site quality goals and objectives as part of annual Quality Improvement Plan and develops strategies and tactics to deliver associated results.
Leads and participates in cross functional teams for new product development, technology transfer, process improvement, and general operations.
Partners with regulatory affairs in all aspects of site regulatory processes that ensure the appropriate licensing, marketing and legal compliance of all appropriate diagnostics and medical device products globally.
Collaborate with global Quality and Regulatory leadership to standardize best practices, share lessons learned, and support enterprise quality initiatives.
Minimum Requirements/Qualifications:
A minimum of 10 years of quality / regulatory experience including at least 5 years of prior experience leading a quality / regulatory role.
Undergraduate degree in life science or biomedical engineering-related subject area preferred.
Strong demonstration of leadership capabilities required, with experience in driving organization and process change. Experience in leading transformations is preferred.
Strong solid understanding of QMS standards and medical device requirements/regulations (ISO 13485:2016 (preferably under MDSAP), US FDA QMSR, Health Canada, IVDD / IVDR)
Experienced in direct, professional interactions with customers and OEM business partners and regulatory authorities.
Ability to achieve results in a matrixed organization, using representatives from diverse cultures and embracing diversity.
Travel requirement:
<10% regional and international travel is expected.
Compensation And Benefits
The salary range estimated for this position based in Virginia is $145,500.00–$225,000.00.
This position may also be eligible to receive a variable annual bonus based on company, team, and/or individual performance results in accordance with company policy. We offer a comprehensive Total Rewards package that our U.S. colleagues and their families can count on, which includes:
A choice of national medical and dental plans, and a national vision plan, including health incentive programs
Employee assistance and family support programs, including commuter benefits and tuition reimbursement
At least 120 hours paid time off (PTO), 10 paid holidays annually, paid parental leave (3 weeks for bonding and 8 weeks for caregiver leave), accident and life insurance, and short- and long-term disability in accordance with company policy
Retirement and savings programs, such as our competitive 401(k) U.S. retirement savings plan
Employees’ Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offers eligible colleagues the opportunity to purchase company stock at a discount
For more information on our benefits, please visit: https://jobs.thermofisher.com/global/en/total-rewards

BioSpace

At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. Ensure site-wide compliance with cGMPs, procedures, standards, and regulatory commitments.
Lead the API Quality Team and manage its agenda.
Support quality forums (e.g., Deviation and Change Control Boards).
Develop and monitor a site Quality Plan and metrics.
Coordinate and manage regulatory inspections.
Review and approve manufacturing and quality system documents.

Use HR tools for performance management, staffing, and succession planning.
Contribute to QA business planning and site-wide strategic planning.

Bachelor's degree (STEM degree preferred)

Experience in Manufacturing, Development, QC, Technical Services, Engineering, or Regulatory Affairs
Proficient in statistical analysis and computer applications

Demonstrated problem-solving and analytical thinking

evidence.text:
Senior Director, Test & Product Engineering
No longer accepting applications
Renesas Electronics
Austin, TX
The Senior Director of Test & Product Engineering leads the strategy and execution of test and product engineering for power semiconductor modules, power ICs, and controllers supporting data center and high-performance applications. This role owns end-to-end product execution across characterization, qualification, yield ramp, test development, and high-volume manufacturing. The leader ensures delivery of scalable, cost-competitive, and high-quality products through strong cross-functional alignment with Design, Product Line, Quality, Reliability, and Operations.
Job Description
The role defines and executes a unified strategy across test and product engineering while leading global teams and establishing scalable processes for new product introduction, yield ramp, and sustaining operations. It requires a balance of strategic leadership and hands-on execution to drive predictable delivery and continuous improvement.
From a product engineering perspective, this leader owns the full product lifecycle, including silicon bring-up, qualification, ramp, and sustaining. Responsibilities include driving yield ramp and improvement, managing excursions, and optimizing product cost through yield, test efficiency, and manufacturing performance. The role ensures manufacturing readiness, production stability, and resolution of yield issues across fab, assembly, and test. It also owns product KPIs, manages change control processes (ECO/PCN), and partners with design teams on design-for-yield, parametric margining, and specification alignment.
From a test engineering standpoint, the role leads development and deployment of wafer sort, final test, and characterization solutions, ensuring strong test coverage while optimizing cost and efficiency. Responsibilities include driving test time reduction, multisite efficiency, and ATE platform standardization to enable scalable high-volume manufacturing.
The leader is accountable for resolving yield excursions, test escapes, and customer returns while partnering with Quality and Reliability teams to ensure robust qualification and mission-profile alignment. This includes establishing monitoring systems and controls to proactively manage risk and maintain alignment between product performance, test limits, and reliability targets.
The role works closely with Operations and manufacturing partners to ensure production readiness, capacity alignment, and continuous improvement across internal and OSAT sites. Strong cross-functional collaboration is required to align with Design, Product Line, and Applications teams on methodologies, cost targets, and customer requirements.
From a business standpoint, the Senior Director owns budget, headcount, and capital planning, while driving performance against key metrics such as yield, cost, quality, and cycle time. The role is also responsible for building a strong organization through hiring, development, and succession planning.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or related field (advanced degree preferred) with 15+ years of semiconductor experience across test and/or product engineering, including leadership of global teams. Strong technical background in power semiconductors (Si, SiC, GaN, modules, or power ICs) and a proven track record in yield ramp, cost optimization, and high-volume manufacturing execution are required. Deep understanding of ATE, characterization, and yield analysis, along with experience driving cross-functional execution across the full product lifecycle, is essential.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with data center power architectures (AC-DC, DC-DC) and familiarity with power module packaging, thermal behavior, and high-current test methods are preferred. Additional strengths include statistical yield analysis, reliability and qualification methodologies, and experience with test automation and data analytics in manufacturing environments.
Key Performance Indicators
Success in this role is measured by yield performance and improvement, cost of test reduction, product cost competitiveness, execution of NPI and ramp schedules, product quality and reliability, and improvements in cycle time and manufacturing efficiency.
What Success Looks Like
Success is defined by consistent product ramps with strong yield, quality, and cost performance, supported by predictable execution from development through production. The organization demonstrates rapid resolution of yield and quality issues and is recognized as a key driver of product competitiveness and customer satisfaction.
Additional Information
Renesas is an embedded semiconductor solution provider driven by its Purpose, To Make Our Lives Easier
. With a global team of over 21,000 engineers and problem solvers in more than 30 countries, we offer the opportunity to work on world‑leading technology for Automotive, Industrial, Infrastructure, and IoT, shaping a safer, healthier, greener, and smarter future.
At Renesas, TAGIE is our culture, grounded in being Transparent, Agile, Global, Innovative, and Entrepreneurial. It shapes how we work, grow and deliver on our purpose together. This collaborative spirit and mindset drive our semiconductor technology to transform industries and impact millions of lives.
We believe in rewarding our employees with a competitive benefits package alongside their salary. More information will be provided during the hiring process.
Are you ready to join our team and shape the future
with us?
Renesas Electronics is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer, committed to supporting diversity and fostering a work environment free of discrimination on the basis of sex, race, religion, national origin, gender, gender identity, gender expression, age, sexual orientation, military status, veteran status, or any other basis protected by law. For more information, please read our Diversity & Inclusion Statement.
Renesas Electronics deals with dual-use technology that is subject to U.S. export controls regulations. Under these regulations it may be necessary for Renesas to obtain U.S. government export license prior to release of technology to certain persons. The decision whether or not to file or pursue an export license application is at the sole discretion of Renesas.

evidence.text:
Head of Hardware
No longer accepting applications
Workshop Venture Partners
Austin, TX
About Drover
Drover is building a virtual fencing ear tag for cattle, and the platform around it to run the modern ranch.
Fencing is one of the oldest unsolved problems in agriculture. Ranchers spend billions of dollars a year building and maintaining physical fences, and every fence line locks land into a grazing pattern it wasn't made for. Virtual fencing is changing that, a generational shift in how ranches are run, bringing precision and productivity gains to an industry that has to feed a growing population with fewer resources.
But every system on the market today requires a collar: bulky, infrastructure-dependent, and built around electric shock. We're taking a path the industry thought impossible. We've shrunk virtual fencing into the ear tag, the form factor every cattle producer on earth already uses. Our tag combines low-power GPS, cellular and satellite connectivity, embedded sensing, solar power, and patent-pending muscle stimulation that guides cattle directionally rather than shocking them. Ranchers tag their cattle once and immediately start running their operation from their phone.
We were founded by Callum Taylor (Harvard, EE & fifth-generation ranching family) and Samuel Aubin (USYD, CS), who both grew up in Australian ranching towns. We built a working ear tag and a patent-pending stimulation method in twelve months (five times faster than competitors), and are now scaling manufacturing to put the technology on every head of cattle in the USA, Australia, and New Zealand.
We closed an oversubscribed seed round, signed a top-tier contract manufacturer, and are on track to launch commercially in Texas in Q1 2027.
We're headquartered in Austin, Texas.
About The Role
As Head of Hardware, you will lead all hardware development at Drover: taking our first-generation ear tag from design validation through production, standing up our supply chain and quality systems with our contract manufacturer, and shaping the roadmap for what comes next.
We're an early-stage startup. You'll have high ownership in what you build and the direction of future generations of our product. You'll own the device end-to-end, electronics, power, RF, mechanical integration, and the path to volume manufacturing, and work directly with the founders on scaling the hardware to cattle globally. As Drover scales, you'll build and lead the hardware engineering team.
What You'll Do
Own Drover hardware across the company. Set the technical direction for current and future generations of the product, and hire the team to build them
Drive manufacturing through EVT, DVT, and PVT, ensuring design maturity, test coverage, and release readiness at each gate
Lead electrical design and review across the full system: cellular and satellite connectivity, GNSS, power management and solar harvesting, embedded sensing, and our patent-pending low-voltage muscle stimulation circuit
Travel overseas to work hands-on with our contract manufacturer on DFM, test fixtures, yield, and production ramp for commercial launch
Work with our liaisons to build and manage the supply chain
Establish quality assurance and reliability testing for a device that has to survive years on a cow's ear in the sun, rain, and mud
Drive regulatory and certification work (FCC, CE, RCM, carrier certification, battery transport and safety)
Opportunity to work from our field offices located within an hour of Austin to prototype and review product iterations on working ranches
Requirements
5+ years as an electrical engineer, with at least one product taken from prototype to volume production
2+ years of leadership experience, and willing to hire and manage a team of engineers
Strong PCB design skills, including schematic capture, layout review, and lab debugging
Experience working with contract manufacturers and managing a hardware supply chain
Solid understanding of low-power embedded systems: battery-powered devices, power budgeting, energy harvesting
Comfortable guiding product development and product iteration cycles in a fast-paced environment
Willing to work in-person in Austin, TX
Nice to have
IoT, wearable, or asset-tracking products, especially rugged or outdoor devices
RF design and test experience: cellular modems, GNSS, antenna design
Mechanical and enclosure experience: mechanical design, injection moulding, ingress protection, environmental testing
Firmware fluency (Zephyr, nRF Connect, or similar) and comfort reading and debugging embedded code
Agricultural or livestock background, or a willingness to get to know our customers
Note: Even if you don't have all of the above and still think you're an excellent candidate, please reach out. We're always open to great people with core skillsets who are willing to push and learn.
Benefits
Meaningful equity package with a high trajectory start-up
Health, dental, vision insurance
Paid family and medical leave
Unlimited PTO
Collaborative environment with emphasis on strong team culture
Ownership and responsibility

Lead, coach, and develop a high-performance team of manufacturing engineers, process engineers, and technicians.
Establish departmental objectives, KPIs, and technical training and development plans.
Direct engineering activities supporting automated and manual assembly lines, injection molding, heat staking, ultrasonic/vibration welding, and vision inspection systems.

Conduct root-cause analysis and execute corrective actions for complex quality, production, and equipment issues.
Ensure manufacturing processes comply with IATF 16949, ISO 14001, customer-specific requirements, and internal quality standards.
Lead risk assessments and enforce strict Environmental, Health, and Safety (EHS) requirements for new processes, equipment, and tooling.
Partner cross-functionally with Operations, Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, and Design Engineering to ensure sustained manufacturing performance throughout the product life cycle.
Production Engineering Manager Requirements:
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial, Plastics Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Minimum of 8 years of progressive production or manufacturing engineering experience in an automotive environment (or 6+ years with an Advanced Degree).
Minimum of 3 to 5 years of direct leadership experience managing engineering personnel and large-scale capital projects.
Deep technical expertise in high-volume automated assembly, injection molding process development, and functional validation systems (leak testing, end-of-line testing)
Strong working knowledge of automotive quality systems and core tools (IATF 16949, APQP, PPAP, PFMEA, Control Plans, SPC).
Hands-on experience with continuous improvement methodologies (Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, TPM).
Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification and/or PMP certification preferred.
Tier 1 automotive supplier experience and experience leading launches for major OEM customers preferred.
Familiarity with industry systems including ERP/MRP, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and advanced Excel.
Strong business acumen, data analysis abilities, and excellent cross-functional communication skills.

Director of Supplier Quality
BAE Systems, Inc.
Fort Wayne, IN
Job Description
You don’t see it, but it’s there. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics – from saving emissions in the City of Lights to powering the Mars Rover to protecting the F-35 fighter jet. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The World®.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of?
Come build your career with BAE Systems at Fort Wayne, IN. Our flexible work environment provides you with a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. Fort Wayne is centrally located between Indianapolis, Detroit, and Chicago for nearby cultural offerings and professional sports. It is the perfect size city; having enough selections of a big city yet small enough for convenience.
The Successful Candidate
BAE Systems is seeking a Director of Supplier Quality, who will report to the Controls and Avionics Solutions (CAS) Senior Director of Quality and dotted line to the sector Senior Director of Supplier Quality. This role will be accountable for developing, maintaining, and optimizing Supplier Quality assurance strategy, reducing supplier quality risks and ensuring conforming products from the supply base. You will need to build strong relationships with the supply chain, operations, programs, and other quality functions to understand and translate requirements into a robust supplier quality executable plan that prevents disruptions and customer defects. In support of your supplier quality strategy, you will closely partner with the core teams of the sector supplier quality function to ensure the supply base is assessed, qualified, and consistently delivering a quality product. This will be a highly visible and key role to delivering value for the business. This individual must be a self-starting leader who can effectively partner with multiple functional organizations, internally, and suppliers, externally for success.
Key Responsibilities
Develop, communicate and drive a proactive Supplier Quality program for the business
Measure, maintain, analyze and communicate all Supplier Quality metrics, risks, and planned actions, and drive continuous improvements efforts at suppliers for improvement (CAR meetings, SRB, Mitigation meetings, etc.)
Partner with the Supplier Chain function to enforce contract/purchase order requirements, assess and develop suppliers, and drive robust RCCA with suppliers
Investigate, evaluate, and resolve supplier quality problems by analyzing defect trends, issuing SCARs, implementing improvement plans, conducting audits, and leading continuous improvement projects to drive a zero defects mindset
Responsible for developing a collaborative environment with suppliers, engineering, program quality, supplier chain, and operation leaders to resolve supplier issues
Engage/lead in all supply chain discussions to ensure proper selection of sourcing (throughout entire product life cycle) to mitigate risk and reduce overall cost of ownership of the parts
Partner with the sector Supplier Quality team to engage key supplier’s management in a business review process to monitor metrics, identify trends and implement programs to assure demonstrated performance improvements
Manages and develops a high performing team of Supplier Quality Engineers who can build relationships, interpret contractual and product requirements, and assist with flow down to suppliers
Owns and manages the Supplier Quality budget
Required travel of approximately 25%
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
Bachelor’s degree in technical field and 10+ years of experience or 14+ years of experience in lieu of degree
Experience in quality assurance/management within a regulated industry (aerospace, defense, medical), or the overall equivalent
Strong technical knowledge of quality science tools and methodologies, including statistical process control, APQP (PFMEA, Control Plans), and robust root cause analysis
Demonstrated success managing supplier improvements through audits and strong CAPA processes
Strong and demonstrated communication skills (written, verbal, visual) and interpersonal skills (listening and communicating within group working environment).
Organizational skills – can marshal resources to get things done, orchestrate multiple activities at once to accomplish a goal, use matrixed resources effectively and efficiently, and arrange information in a useful manner.
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
Engineering or Technical Bachelor's Degree
Master’s degree
Strong knowledge of AS9100/AS9102/AS9145
Supply Chain management experience
Lean Six Sigma Greenbelt or Black Belt Certified
ASQ Certification
Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
About BAE Systems, Inc.
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

As a global leader in animal health, we are dedicated to innovation and delivering products and services to prevent and treat disease in farm animals and pets. At Elanco, we are driven by our vision of Food and Companionship Enriching Life and our purpose – all to Go Beyond for Animals, Customers, Society and Our People.
At Elanco, we pride ourselves on fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. We believe that diversity is the driving force behind innovation, creativity, and overall business success. Making animals’ lives better makes life better – join our team today!

Provide both administrative and technical leadership to Quality Control teams overseeing Chemistry, Virology, Immunochemistry, and other key laboratory functions.

evidence.text:
Director, Quality & Regulatory
ALKU
Greater Boston
$170,000.00/yr - $200,000.00/yr
Director, Quality & Regulatory
Summary
The Director, Quality and Regulatory will lead the quality team in developing and executing Quality and regulatory operations in line with the Company's mission and vision. The Director will implement and monitor all company quality systems to demonstrate compliance with FDA requirements and applicable global regulations. This position is responsible for providing quality and regulatory guidance for design, development, manufacturing, commercialization, and post-market activities for electromechanical capital systems and consumables. The Director will oversee Quality Assurance, Quality Systems, Regulatory Compliance, inspection readiness, and interactions with regulatory authorities to ensure the organization maintains a state of continuous compliance. This is a hybrid role, expectations are to be in our Woburn, MA office 4 days per week, with flexibility 1 day remote.
Add to Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Provide strategic leadership and oversight of the company's Quality Management System (QMS) and Regulatory Compliance programs.
Serve as the primary quality representative during regulatory inspections, audits, and interactions with regulatory agencies, including the FDA, notified bodies, auditors, and other applicable authorities.
Develop and execute regulatory strategies supporting product development, product approvals, labeling changes, and post-market requirements.
Ensure compliance with FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR Part 820), ISO 13485, Medical Device Reporting (MDR), complaint handling, CAPA, risk management, and applicable international regulations.
Oversee internal and external audit programs, supplier quality management, and inspection readiness initiatives.
Provide guidance regarding regulatory risks, compliance gaps, remediation activities, and quality system improvements.
Lead quality and regulatory review activities related to design controls, verification and validation, software validation, change management, and product lifecycle management.
Ensure effective management of complaints, adverse events, corrective actions, and field actions in accordance with applicable regulatory requirements.
Establish quality and compliance metrics, monitor organizational performance, and communicate results to executive leadership.
Develop and maintain relationships with regulatory agencies, external auditors, consultants, and industry organizations to stay current on evolving regulatory requirements and industry best practices.
Maintain, prepare, 510K submissions.
Education and Experience
Demonstrated experience leading Quality and Regulatory Compliance programs within the medical device industry.
Strong working knowledge of FDA medical device regulations, including 21 CFR Part 820, Design Controls, CAPA, Complaint Handling, MDR, and Post-Market Surveillance requirements.
Experience supporting FDA inspections, ISO 13485 certification audits, and regulatory submissions.
Proven ability to manage regulatory compliance activities across product development, manufacturing, commercialization, and post-market surveillance.
Experience with risk management methodologies, including ISO 14971, preferred.
RAC (Regulatory Affairs Certification), ASQ Certified Quality Auditor (CQA), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), or similar certification preferred.
Additional Accountability Section
Regulatory and Compliance Oversight
Own the company's quality and compliance framework, ensuring ongoing adherence to FDA, ISO, state, federal, and international regulatory requirements.
Identify, assess, and mitigate regulatory risks that may impact business operations, product approvals, or market access.
Report quality and regulatory compliance status, risks, trends, and remediation plans to executive leadership.
Drive a culture of quality, compliance, continuous improvement, and inspection readiness throughout the organization.

evidence.text:
Continuous Improvement Director
iTradeNetwork, Inc.
Charlotte, NC
About ITradeNetwork
At iTradeNetwork, we provide advanced supply chain software and insights tailored to the food & beverage industry. Our mission is clear and ambitious: To feed the world.
From the start, we’ve been dedicated to tackling the most pressing challenges within food and beverage supply chains, delivering innovative solutions and expert support that make a measurable impact.
Our cutting-edge technology helps businesses streamline complex procurement and fulfillment processes, minimize food waste, optimize inventory, manage compliance risk, and scale profitably. We’re proud to serve an elite customer base, including 13 of the top 25 North American grocers, 8 of the top 10 foodservice distributors, and 8 of the top 10 global food and beverage manufacturers.
Today, we're building an AI-first company — meaning AI isn't a feature we bolt on, it's the foundation for how we design products, make decisions, and ship software. Cerena is proof of that in action: powered by the most connected supply chain network in food and beverage, iTradeNetwork's Solution Suite replaces error-prone manual workflows with faster, smarter tools — driving real results for our customers, and ultimately, for the consumers who depend on them.
iTradeNetwork's Leadership Principles
iTradeNetwork’s purpose is to feed the world — and everything we do is guided by the principles below. Every team member is expected to embody and champion these principles across the organization.
Bias for Action
We value speed and avoid analysis paralysis. We develop conviction, make informed decisions quickly, and take calculated risks to maintain momentum — knowing that swift progress is essential for innovation and growth.
Customer Obsession
We work relentlessly to delight our customers. We work backward from their needs to solve pain points and create solutions that surprise and earn their loyalty. We obsess over customers, not competitors.
Data & Metrics Driven
We operate with facts, not opinions. We dive deep into data and use metrics to measure progress, ground every decision in rigorous analysis, and push for clarity and measurable outcomes.
Raise the Bar
We continuously push for improvement — in ourselves, our teams, and the company. We hire and develop exceptional talent, setting ever-higher standards that elevate performance and drive excellence.
Operational Excellence Through Process
We build lasting processes that optimize for efficiency. By developing, testing, and documenting each process, we create consistency and scale through automation, enabling continuous improvement across the business.
Ownership Mindset
We take responsibility for our work and aim for long-term success. We use resources wisely, stay accountable, and roll up our sleeves to get things done — no task is beneath us.
Earn Trust
We build trust through integrity, transparency, and mutual respect. We communicate openly, own our mistakes, listen actively, and remain open to feedback as an opportunity for growth.
Job Summary
We are seeking a Continuous Improvement Director to work directly alongside cross-functional teams—Product, Engineering, Customer Support, Operations, and Corporate functions—embedding structured, repeatable continuous improvement practices at the team level. Rather than defining strategy from the top down, you will roll up your sleeves with teams to run Kaizen events, structured problem-solving, and process mapping, coaching them until that thinking becomes second nature and the work outlasts your involvement. You will bring practical AI tools into the process-improvement work you lead where they genuinely help, and you will translate leadership's priorities into clear, actionable project plans that teams can execute with confidence.
Key Responsibilities
Cross-Functional Project & Portfolio Leadership
Partner directly with cross-functional teams (Product, Engineering, Customer Support, Operations, and Corporate) to plan, run, and deliver a portfolio of continuous improvement projects.
Take priorities set by leadership and translate them into actionable, structured project plans with clear owners, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Manage project intake, prioritization, and resourcing across the CI portfolio, keeping initiatives moving and unblocked.
Act as an embedded thought partner to team leads and managers, coaching them through structured problem-solving rather than directing from above.
Continuous Improvement / Operational Excellence
Facilitate Kaizen events, workshops, and root-cause analysis sessions, guiding teams toward running these independently over time.
Champion structured problem-solving as the core, repeatable approach teams use to diagnose issues and drive improvement, working directly alongside them.
Coach team members and managers on structured problem-solving so the habit becomes self-sustaining, rather than dependent on this role.
Map and redesign end-to-end value streams and processes together with the teams that own them, eliminating waste and reducing cycle time.
Establish standard work and lightweight process controls so improvements stick after your engagement with a team ends.
Work within each function's Business Operating System (BOS) at the team level, helping them track metrics, problem-solve when metrics are missed, and build charters and action plans for initiatives.
AI-Enabled Process Improvement
Bring practical AI and GenAI tools into active CI projects where they can remove friction or accelerate root-cause analysis, prototyping alongside the team.
Identify opportunities within in-flight improvement projects to pilot lightweight automation or AI-assisted workflows, in partnership with Technology, Data, and Product.
Run hands-on workshops that build AI fluency within the specific teams currently engaged in CI work, grounding adoption in real project use cases.
Apply the organization's responsible-AI guidelines (data privacy, model oversight) when introducing AI tools into a team's workflow.
Track the adoption and impact of AI-assisted process changes as part of standard project outcome reporting.
Change Leadership & Culture-Building
Lead change management within individual CI projects: stakeholder analysis, readiness assessment, communication, and training to drive team-level adoption.
Build buy-in with team leads and frontline staff without formal authority, meeting teams where they are.
Convert successful project outcomes into simple, reusable playbooks and toolkits that other teams can pick up.
Model and reinforce structured problem-solving in day-to-day team interactions so it becomes the team's default way of working.
Metrics, Reporting & Culture
Support enterprise KPI frameworks (baseline → target → control plan) by ensuring the projects and teams you work with feed accurate, timely data into them.
Contribute project and initiative updates into the monthly MBR process, ensuring the work you lead is represented with rigor and accuracy.
Translate project-level outcomes into clear, simple before/after impact stories for the teams and their leadership.
Support the CI culture-building efforts led by executive leadership by demonstrating and reinforcing the mindset at the team level.
Help train and mentor CI champions embedded within the teams you work with.
What You’ll Need
Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, Operations, Computer Science, or a related field (advanced degree strongly preferred).
8-10+ years of progressive experience leading continuous improvement and operational excellence initiatives in technology/SaaS, manufacturing, supply chain, or high-volume operations environments.
Demonstrated facilitation expertise in Kaizen events and structured problem-solving methodologies (e.g., A3, PDCA, root-cause analysis), with a relevant certification or equivalent hands-on track record.
Deep expertise applying Kaizen, structured problem-solving, and process mapping to both knowledge-work and cross-functional processes, not just traditional operations optimization.
Proven track record of hands-on change management, with the ability to influence without formal authority, motivate cross-functional teams, and build trust at every level of the organization.
Strong analytics and business acumen: ability to define metrics, quantify impact, and translate data into clear, practical recommendations for the teams you work with.
Exceptional written and verbal communication, coaching, and facilitation skills (clear status updates, crisp storytelling, and leading cross-functional workshops).
Ability to thrive on solving complex problems, translating priorities into action with precision and follow-through.
Nice-to-Have Qualifications
Experience standing up new Continuous Improvement or Operational Excellence functions from the ground up.
Experience improving SaaS delivery and reliability using Agile/DevOps and service management practices (e.g., incident/problem/change management, continuous delivery).
Familiarity with digital collaboration tools (e.g., Miro, Lucidchart), work and service management tooling (e.g., Jira, ServiceNow), and BI/analytics platforms (e.g., Power BI, Tableau).
Experience scaling execution through workflow automation (low-code/RPA) and/or AI-assisted operational decisioning.
Experience applying AI/GenAI tools within process-improvement or operational workflows.

Experience contributing to or supporting an internal AI community of practice or champions network.

Lean Six Sigma or other structured-methodology credential, change management training/certification (e.g., Prosci/ADKAR), and/or a program management credential (e.g., PMP).

The position carries full site P&L accountability and responsibility for business performance, manufacturing, quality and regulatory compliance, facilities, capital projects, supply chain, EHS and people leadership.
The successful candidate will oversee facility completion, equipment qualification, trial production and transition into commercial operations, establishing a safe, compliant and profitable peptide CDMO business.
Key Responsibilities
Site Strategy and Business Leadership
Translate corporate strategy into a site operating plan, revenue targets and performance objectives.
Own the site P&L, annual operating budget and capital investment programme.
Lead business reviews covering delivery, quality, safety, cost, capacity and supply chain performance.
Report site performance, investment requirements and material risks to executive leadership.
Build relationships with pharmaceutical customers and oversee significant delivery, scheduling and quality matters.
Manufacturing and Technical Operations
Oversee clinical and commercial peptide manufacturing, including synthesis, purification, fill-finish and packaging.
Lead production scheduling and capacity planning across multiple customers and programmes.
Ensure adherence to approved processes and batch documentation, working with Quality on deviations, change controls, CAPAs and batch release.
Direct technology transfer, process validation and cleaning validation.
Improve manufacturing yields, productivity, material utilisation and delivery performance.
Quality and Regulatory Compliance
Hold executive accountability for site GMP compliance while maintaining appropriate Quality oversight and decision-making.
Oversee manufacturing, laboratory and quality management systems.
Maintain inspection readiness and lead site participation in regulatory inspections and customer audits.
Ensure compliance with applicable FDA, EU GMP, ICH, USP, workplace safety and environmental requirements.
Embed data integrity, risk management and continuous improvement throughout the organisation.
Facilities, Capital Projects and EHS
Lead facility completion, commissioning, qualification and expansion activities.
Oversee cleanrooms, laboratories, manufacturing equipment and critical utilities.
Establish preventative maintenance and equipment reliability programmes.
Hold overall accountability for workplace safety, hazardous materials, waste management and emergency preparedness.
Coordinate Engineering, Validation and Quality activities through operational readiness and commercial launch.
Supply Chain and Business Support
Oversee procurement, supplier qualification, inventory, warehousing and logistics.
Manage supply risks and support equipment and material procurement for new programmes.
Partner with Finance, HR, IT and other support functions to establish effective site operations.
People Leadership
Recruit, develop and retain the site leadership team and wider workforce.
Establish departmental objectives, performance reviews and succession plans.
Build a culture of safety, compliance, customer service and operational accountability.
Apply Lean, Six Sigma and other improvement methods to strengthen performance.
Protect confidential customer information, intellectual property and proprietary processes.
Qualifications and Experience
Master’s degree in Organic Chemistry, Peptide Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Engineering or a related biopharmaceutical discipline; PhD preferred.
At least 12 years of comprehensive management experience within GMP peptide/API contract manufacturing, including extensive recent peptide CDMO experience.
At least five years of full-site General Manager or equivalent executive leadership experience.
Demonstrated GMP facility start-up experience spanning construction completion, qualification, validation, trial batches and commercial production.
Proven leadership of FDA inspections and strong knowledge of US pharmaceutical, environmental and workplace safety requirements.
Extensive experience in commercial peptide synthesis, purification, process scale-up and multi-client capacity planning.
Direct P&L ownership, capital and operating budget management, and cost optimisation experience.
Experience building a US workforce of 100 or more employees and leading multidisciplinary management teams.
Familiarity with ERP, LIMS, project management and financial planning systems.
Relevant GMP auditing, pharmaceutical compliance and safety training certifications are advantageous.

Staff Manufacturing Engineer, Barracuda
Anduril Industries
Ashville, OH
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Site
Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyper-scale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed at which autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America's defense industrial base, strengthening America's warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.
About The Product
The future of defense is being built right now, and Anduril's Barracuda product is at its leading edge. Barracuda is a family of air-breathing autonomous air vehicles (AAVs) purpose-built for hyper-scale production and mass employment. The Barracuda family consists of Barracuda-100, Barracuda-250, and Barracuda-500. Each increment offers increasing size, range, and payload capacity, but all Barracudas are compatible with a host of payloads and employment mechanisms, support a variety of different missions, and provide warfighters with an adaptable and upgradeable capability to counter evolving threats.
About The Team
The Barracuda Launch Team (BLT) will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1, our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. As Barracuda transitions from low-rate initial production at Anduril HQ to high-rate manufacturing at Arsenal-1, this team will own the technology transfer, stand up production lines, and sustain the floor operations that make that ramp possible. You will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for up to 2 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.
About The Job
As a Staff Manufacturing Engineer, you will drive the enterprise-wide manufacturing strategy for Barracuda at Arsenal-1 and architect how Anduril builds autonomous air vehicles at hyper-scale. You'll lead the end-to-end technology transfer from HQ, design the production systems and line architecture for high-rate output, and establish the manufacturing process frameworks — RCCA systems, MES strategy, yield management programs, takt time structures, and scaling playbooks — that become organizational standards. This role sits at the intersection of deep hands-on electromechanical manufacturing expertise and strategic program leadership. You'll balance short-term production demands with long-term capability development, pioneering manufacturing approaches that create lasting competitive advantage.
This role requires relocation to Costa Mesa, CA for an initial training program of up to 2 months. Housing, transportation, etc. will be provided during your stay.
What You'll Do
Drive the enterprise-wide manufacturing strategy for Barracuda, aligning production systems, processes, and capacity plans with Anduril's long-term business objectives and Arsenal-1's ramp targets.
Architect and lead the technology transfer of Barracuda production from Anduril HQ to Arsenal-1 — designing the production line layout, process flow, MES architecture, and quality systems for high-rate output.
Establish the manufacturing process frameworks that become organizational standards: RCCA systems, yield management programs, takt time structures, line balancing methodologies, and scaling playbooks.
Lead transformational line optimization initiatives that fundamentally redefine production capability — targeting step-change improvements in throughput, cost, and quality across the Barracuda program.
Define and own the MES strategy for Barracuda production at Arsenal-1: system selection, workflow architecture, data models, and integration with quality and supply chain systems.
Pioneer novel manufacturing approaches for complex electromechanical integration at scale; develop proprietary methods with potential for patent protection.
Direct large-scale capital improvement programs with enterprise-wide impact; manage multi-million dollar portfolios of interdependent projects from justification through validation.
Develop comprehensive manufacturing technology roadmaps, evaluate emerging technologies and create adoption strategies with quantified business impact.
Establish manufacturing excellence models that balance efficiency, quality, and flexibility; lead breakthrough cost reduction programs delivering 7-figure annual savings.
Serve as the company's foremost authority in electromechanical manufacturing processes for Barracuda; resolve the most complex technical challenges that impact critical business outcomes.
Develop comprehensive technical career paths and competency models for the manufacturing engineering organization; design mentorship programs that accelerate development of high-potential engineers.
Represent Anduril's manufacturing capabilities to key customers, partners, and industry bodies; establish strategic relationships with equipment suppliers and technology providers.
Translate executive-level business strategies into manufacturing capability requirements; develop cost models that inform product strategy and pricing decisions.
What We're Looking For
12+ years in manufacturing of electromechanical hardware, with progressive leadership of complex production programs and scaling operations.
Degree in an engineering or technical field preferred, or equivalent depth of hands-on manufacturing experience.
Deep, demonstrated expertise in complex electromechanical integration at production scale — you've built it, optimized it, and scaled it.
Track record of standing up or transforming production lines: technology transfer, line design, process architecture, and ramp to rate.
Mastery of the manufacturing process ecosystem: work instructions, MBOMs, RCCA, line optimization, takt time management, yield programs, MES strategy, and scaling operations.
Experience leading transformational manufacturing initiatives with enterprise-wide impact and multi-million dollar scope.
Proven ability to resolve the most complex technical challenges where no established solution paths exist.
A world-class quality and mission-assurance mindset with the judgment to balance competing priorities across quality, cost, schedule, and manufacturability.
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
Preferred Qualifications
High-rate manufacturing background in aerospace, defense, automotive/EV, or similar high-volume precision environment.
Experience architecting production systems for a new facility or major production line standup from the ground up.
Exposure to aircraft, aerospace, and defense programs at a strategic or program leadership level.
Harness and PCBA fabrication experience, including SMT process expertise at scale.
Hands-on experience with autonomous systems, flight vehicles, or related control systems.
Lean Six Sigma (Black Belt or higher); deep familiarity with J-STD-001, IPC-A-610, and IPC/WHMA-A-620.
Experience selecting, deploying, or architecting MES platforms for high-rate production environments.
Published work, patents, or recognized contributions to manufacturing technology advancement.
Software scripting ability in any language.
Current active U.S. Secret security clearance.
US Salary Range
$143,000—$191,000 USD
Benefits
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.
Data Privacy
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

evidence.text:
Senior Director, Quality Control
Crescent Biopharma
Waltham, MA
Crescent Biopharma’s vision is to build a world leading oncology company bringing the next wave of therapies for cancer patients. The Company’s clinical-stage pipeline includes its lead program, a PD-1 x VEGF bispecific antibody, as well as novel antibody-drug conjugates. By leveraging multiple modalities and established targets, Crescent aims to rapidly advance potentially transformative therapies as single agents and as part of combination regimens to treat a range of solid tumors. For more information, visit www.crescentbiopharma.com and follow the Company on LinkedIn and X.
We are seeking an experienced Senior Director, Quality Control to join as a key leader within Crescent's Quality organization, responsible for providing strategic and hands-on Quality Control leadership across company’s biologics and ADC programs, and future pipeline growth. Partnering closely with Analytical Sciences, GMP Quality Assurance, CMC/Technical Operations, Supply Chain, and Regulatory Affairs, you will provide phase-appropriate QC oversight from early development through late-stage development and commercialization within a global outsourced testing and manufacturing network. You will ensure reliable release and stability testing while building the QC infrastructure, laboratory network, and operating controls needed to advance programs into Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA submission, and commercial readiness.
Crescent's operating model requires clear, collaborative accountability between Analytical Sciences and QC. Analytical Sciences leads analytical development and performs the primary technical work through method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and PPQ readiness. QC provides oversight and operational input during early development, assumes increasing responsibility for method transfer, validation execution oversight, laboratory readiness, and GMP testing as programs mature, and takes primary ownership of routine QC operations and analytical method lifecycle management following transition to late-stage and commercial operations.
Success in this role requires a collaborative, hands-on leader who understands both analytical development and commercial QC operations, can establish effective governance across internal and external partners, and thrives in a fast-paced biotechnology environment while balancing scientific rigor, compliance, speed, and pragmatism.
\n
Responsibilities
Define and implement Crescent's phase-appropriate QC strategy and operating model across early development, Phase 3, PPQ, regulatory submission, and commercialization, with clear decision rights and handoffs among Analytical Sciences, QC, and GMP QA.
Oversee QC activities for drug substance, drug product, intermediates, finished goods, in-process, release, characterization, and stability testing across the portfolio.
Provide QC oversight and operational requirements during early development while Analytical Sciences leads method development, characterization, qualification, validation strategy, and method maturation through PPQ readiness.
Partner with Analytical Sciences on integrated Phase 3 and PPQ readiness, including method validation and transfer, laboratory qualification, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, stability, sample management, and testing timelines.
Lead QC execution oversight for method transfer, validation, and laboratory readiness; following transition to GMP QC operations, own routine method lifecycle management, performance monitoring, changes, revalidation, transfers, and remediation.
Lead outsourced GMP QC operations, including sample management and testing coordination, and ensure timely, compliant release and stability testing for clinical supply, PPQ, batch disposition, regulatory commitments, and future commercial supply.
Partner with Analytical Sciences, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, and QA on specifications and stability strategy; lead operational implementation, stability execution, data review, trending, and escalation within the QC network.
Establish and oversee reference standard and critical reagent programs, including qualification, bridging, inventory, monitoring, replacement, and lifecycle planning.
Provide technical leadership for OOS, OOT, OOE, atypical results, invalid assays, laboratory deviations, CAPAs, and change controls, ensuring scientifically sound, timely investigations and risk-based escalation.
Lead selection, onboarding, qualification, governance, and performance management of CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including agreements, capacity, metrics, issue management, data integrity, and inspection readiness.
Provide QC input to CMC and regulatory strategies and support IND/IMPD, BLA/MAA, health authority, and inspection activities; ensure commitments are implemented within the laboratory network.
Lead alliance management with business partners on QC matters, including governance, roles and responsibilities, shared testing and release requirements, issue escalation, decision-making, and alignment on development, regulatory, and future commercial priorities.
Establish scalable QC procedures, systems, metrics, budgeting, forecasting, and resource plans; support compliant use of LIMS, stability, analytical data, and trending tools, and build internal QC capability as Crescent advances toward commercialization.
Mentor staff and consultants and foster a culture of scientific rigor, collaboration, accountability, inclusion, and continuous improvement while staying current with evolving GMP, ICH, compendial, and industry expectations.
Education & Experience
Bachelor's degree in life sciences, analytical sciences, biochemistry, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related discipline; advanced degree preferred.
A minimum 10-12 years of progressive experience in biologics QC, analytical development, or related CMC functions, including leadership of GMP QC operations in an outsourced environment.
Experience with biologics analytical methods, including cell-based bioassays/potency assays; ADC and other complex biologic modality experience is preferred.
Experience supporting biologics from clinical development through Phase 3, PPQ, BLA/MAA, and commercial readiness; bispecific antibody, ADC, or other complex modality experience is a plus.
Proven experience transitioning methods from development into routine GMP QC use, including qualification, validation, transfer, implementation, performance monitoring, and lifecycle management.
Strong experience with release and stability testing, specifications, reference standards and critical reagents, OOS/OOT/OOE investigations, analytical trending, deviations, CAPAs, and change control.
Demonstrated success overseeing CDMO QC functions and contract laboratories, including qualification, governance, investigations, capacity, performance, and issue resolution.
Strong knowledge of global GMP regulations, FDA/EMA/ICH guidance, compendial expectations, data integrity, Part 11 / Annex 11, and phase-appropriate application across development and commercial operations.
Experience supporting regulatory submissions, health authority questions, pre-approval inspections, and commercial inspection readiness.
Ability to establish clear roles and effective collaboration among Analytical Sciences, QC, GMP QA, CMC/Technical Operations, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and external partners.
Strategic thinker with a hands-on approach, solutions-oriented leader who communicates clearly, applies pragmatic science- and risk-based judgment, works effectively in a fast-paced small-company environment, and can travel to external sites as needed.
Commitment to living Crescent’s core values and operating norms.

evidence.quote: Leads the department’s quality audit and corrective action process by providing training, facilitation, recommendations, and leadership, as required to achieve best results.
evidence.text:
Director of Quality - MIA
FEAM Aero
Miami, FL
FEAM Aero is currently seeking an experienced Director of Quality to join our Miami, FL team. We pride ourselves on consistently exceeding our customers’ expectations and creating lifelong relationships with our clientele. The Director of Quality reports to the Vice President of Safety & Quality and is responsible for the overall management of the Quality Assurance and Quality Control functions. The Director of Quality has the authority to establish and revise repair station policies, procedures, and instructions; serves as the AS9110 Quality Management Representative; and holds final authority for return to service. This role ensures continuous compliance with applicable CFRs, manufacturer requirements, customer programs, and company policies through oversight of inspection standards, methods, and procedures across all repair station activities.
Duties & Responsibilities:
Responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable rules, regulations, organizational standards, and quality expectations in all Company operations.
Directly oversees the Chief Inspector and Quality Assurance Managers.
Ensure that quality department objectives are established, managed, remain current, and are updated or revised as necessary.
Act as designated liaison for regulatory bodies and accrediting organizations and Interface with customers on quality issues.
Represents the repair station in matters of airworthiness and safety with the FAA and with customers.
Maintains currency on regulatory requirements and quality standards.
Develop and maintain regulatory manuals, documentation, records and SOPs.
Responsible for conducting risk assessments of the impact of proposed organizational and operational changes on existing and new processes and procedures within the quality department and assist in the development and implementation of mitigation strategies to eliminate or reduce identified risks.
Leads the department’s quality audit and corrective action process by providing training, facilitation, recommendations, and leadership, as required to achieve best results.
Performs and directs the investigation of quality escapes. Reviews investigation findings, root cause analysis, and works with operations to determine corrective actions are implemented to prevent recurrence.
Ensure that all inspections are properly performed on all completed work and that proper inspection records, reports and forms, used by the repair station are properly executed prior to returning any component to service.
Assures that all technical data used to inspect, or repair aircraft, engines or component parts are current.
Assures that no defective, unserviceable, or non-airworthy parts are installed on any aircraft or component part thereof that is returned to service by the repair station.
Submits reports of defects and unairworthy conditions to the local FAA Flight Standard District Office in accordance with 14 CFR Part 145.221.
Assures that the FAA Form 337 and/or the FEAM Maintenance Release are properly executed.
Maintains files of records of all maintenance and inspections in such a manner that the file corresponding to a specific item inspected and repaired can be readily located for review.
Responsible for the Repair Station Roster of Management Supervisory and Inspection Personnel
Ensures that the outside repair agency and subcontractor approval program including the inspections, as required, of their facilities is accomplished.
Reviews and approves work to be performed for 14 CFR Part 121,125, 135 and foreign 129 operators to ensure that 14 CFR Part 145.205 is strictly adhered to.
Ensures that the Approved Vendor List is maintained in a current status.
Responsible for the Quality Assurance Program in accordance with the Repair Station Manual.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) to track and report on quality metrics, driving data-based decision-making.
Ensure the quality management system conforms to the requirements of the AS9110 Standard.
Ensure that the processes are delivering their intended outputs.
Report on the performance of the quality management system and on opportunities for improvement to top management.
Ensure that the integrity of the quality management system is maintained when changes to the quality management system are planned and implemented.
Ensure all direct reports maintain currency and competency appropriate for their duties, through continuing education and training as appropriate.
Other duties as assigned by the Vice President of Safety & Quality.
Minimum Qualifications:
Minimum of five (5) years of CFR Part 145 repair station or 121 air carrier quality assurance experience
Must hold an FAA Airframe & Powerplant license with experience in Line Maintenance and/or Heavy Check operations.
Thorough knowledge of 14 CFR Part 145 & 121 regulations, FAA & EASA airworthiness certification requirements and other regulatory bodies
Proficiency in the use of Microsoft Outlook and Office Suite
Excellent Communication skills, both written and verbal. Successful candidate must be able to write effective reports, business correspondence, and manuals.
Several years of supervisory experience
Must have a valid driver's license
Skills/Abilities:
Able to interface in a pleasant and professional manner with all departments, levels of management, customers and vendors.
Be able to analyze information and utilize problem solving and critical thinking skills
Must have strong organizational skills to set and meet deadlines.
Detail-oriented and can work in a fast-paced environment with constantly shifting priorities.
Ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.
Be able to work under adverse conditions in a production/aircraft maintenance environment.
Must be willing to work an irregular schedule and be able to travel when required.

Full-Time, Exempt
Position Summary
Nextpower is evolving from a solar tracker company into an integrated utility-scale energy technology platform spanning trackers, eBOS, foundations, power conversion, energy storage, robotics, and other adjacent solutions. As the company grows through organic expansion and acquisitions, it needs greater alignment, standardization, scalability, and execution across the enterprise.
Reporting to the Vice President, Operational Excellence & Transformation, the Director leads a portfolio of priority initiatives and manages the day-to-day delivery of the Operational Excellence Office. The role concentrates on Operations—manufacturing, supply chain, planning, procurement, quality, logistics, and field operations—and leads cross-functional work involving Finance, Engineering, Sales, IT, HR, and other functions when processes span organizational boundaries. The Director turns strategic priorities into executable programs, builds Lean and Kaizen capability, partners on systems and automation, and delivers measurable improvements in customer experience, productivity, operating margin, working capital, and cash flow.
Key Responsibilities
Program Portfolio and Governance
Translate VP priorities into initiative charters, integrated plans, milestones, resource needs, risks, and decisions.
Manage portfolio reviews, stage gates, executive reporting, and escalation processes; recommend sequencing based on value, capacity, and execution risk.
Lead program managers as we build up the team, and workstream owners to resolve dependencies and deliver commitments across functions.
Operational Excellence and Transformation
Lead redesign and simplification of priority processes, including cross-functional handoffs, controls, and ownership.
Deploy Lean, Kaizen, standard work, visual management, structured problem solving, and value stream improvements across selected Operations areas.
Partner with site and functional leaders to standardize practices while accommodating justified local needs and acquired businesses.
Systems and Automation
Set up and manage Operations Excellence portal for methodologies, documents, and training videos.
Partner with IT and process owners to define business requirements and integrate process redesign with enterprise systems, analytics, workflow automation, and appropriate AI-enabled solutions.
Drive adoption and effective use of Oracle and other enterprise platforms; reduce manual and spreadsheet-driven work where practical.
Establish consistent measures and reporting for the initiatives in the assigned portfolio.
Performance and Value Realization
Build baselines, benefit cases, milestones, and measurement plans with Finance and business owners.
Track Finance-validated impact on productivity, cost, margin, working capital, cash flow, and service; intervene when delivery or adoption falls short.
Develop a pipeline of improvement opportunities and ensure business owners sustain results after implementation.
Team and Change Leadership
Work individually while building a team. Manage and coach assigned program managers, improvement leads, and analysts; strengthen project management and problem-solving capability.
Build stakeholder alignment, communicate changes, and coordinate training and adoption plans.
Promote accountability, collaboration, respect for people, and data-driven decisions.
Qualifications
A minimum of 12 years of experience leading complex, cross-functional transformation or operational improvement programs in manufacturing, industrial technology, energy, or engineered products.
Demonstrated people leadership and ability to influence functional and site leaders without direct authority.
Practical knowledge of Lean, Kaizen, Six Sigma, A3, PDCA, or comparable methods.
Experience with enterprise systems implementation, process automation, performance metrics, and change management.
Strong financial acumen and experience quantifying and tracking operational benefits with Finance.
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Business, Finance, or a related discipline; Master’s degree preferred.

A governed portfolio of priority initiatives has clear owners, plans, milestones, risks, and a regular review cadence.
Initial initiatives deliver Finance-validated improvements in service, productivity, margin, or working capital.
Priority processes have documented standards and measurable adoption of Lean, Kaizen, systems, or automation improvements.
Functional leaders use consistent performance reporting to address delivery issues and sustain gains.
Working Relationships
Works closely with the Vice President and leaders across Operations, Engineering, Finance, IT, Sales, HR, business units, and sites to deliver the assigned transformation portfolio.
