evidence.text:
Senior Manager, Supply Chain (Robot Production)
Genesis
San Carlos , California 
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
Every part that goes into our robot: who makes it, at what price, on what lead time, to what quality. This is the hands-on role. You build the supplier base for production, develop domestic sources for the sub-systems that need them, and make sure the line never waits on a part. You start with a bill of materials, a design team and a few suppliers; you end with a qualified, dual-sourced supply chain that supports production with our manufacturing partner. You are at our facility, at the partner and at suppliers more than you are at a desk.
What you'll do
Be on the floor: at our facility, at our manufacturing partner and at suppliers; first articles, line-down calls and recoveries are yours.
Build the supplier base: source, qualify and manage suppliers for machined and cast structures, gears and actuators, motors, PCBAs, harnesses, shells, batteries and sensors; two sources for every critical sub-system.
Develop domestic suppliers for the sub-systems that need them, and keep the content records that come with selling into regulated markets.
Run the commercial work day to day: RFQs, should-cost, piece price and tooling negotiation, payment and warranty terms; work with Legal on supplier agreements.
Sit in design reviews from the start: flag long-lead, single-source and high-risk parts before design freeze; bring supplier capability into the design.
Own clear-to-build and the plan: every unit on the schedule has a complete kit before it starts; a rolling plan the line, the partner and the suppliers all see; capacity planning with suppliers ahead of demand; inventory accuracy and safety stock by part class.
Own the BOM in production: cost roll-ups by phase, engineering change control with the design team and Manufacturing Engineering, cost-down from pilot to volume.
Build the supplier quality loop with Manufacturing Engineering and Quality: first article and PPAP where it applies, incoming inspection, supplier scorecards and quarterly reviews, corrective action and recovery.
Run logistics: inbound, between our facility and our partner's, import and export paperwork with Legal, spares and service parts.
Run the systems we have and help stand up the next ones: part numbering, BOM control, MRP; own the weekly numbers (clear-to-build, on-time delivery, PPV, inventory).
What we are looking for
You have built a supplier base for a hardware product going into production, not managed or handed to you, and you produce results in weeks, not quarters.
Deep experience with machined and cast metal parts, gears or actuators, motors, PCBAs and harnesses, and the suppliers who make them; you read drawings and GD&T.
You have developed new suppliers in new regions and qualified them to a standard.
Strong commercial record: you have negotiated price, tooling and terms with suppliers and contract manufacturers.
You are fluent in BOMs, change control, should-cost and cost roll-ups, and comfortable with the people who design the product.
8 or more years in supply chain, sourcing or supplier development for complex hardware, with time in a mature organization so you know what the systems look like at scale; you have led a small team or are ready to; engineering degree preferred.
Bonus: robotics or automotive; contract manufacturer selection and transition; import and export compliance; APICS or CPSM.
Working Conditions
Office and production environments; travel to suppliers and partner sites, including international, up to 30%.
How we work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition.
We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency.
Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun.
Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency.
Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism
. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego.
Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey.
We take pride in the craft, enjoy the ride, and make space to laugh. Happiness is part of how we get there.

items.title: Electrical Engineering Section Manager - Production Support

evidence.quote: 10+ years experience in HW Engineering with a proven track record of leading multidisciplinary engineering teams through the full product lifecycle (from proposal and design through production and sustainment).
evidence.text:
Electrical Engineering Section Manager - Production Support
BAE Systems, Inc.
Austin, TX
Job Description
See what you’re missing. Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics from Electronic Threat Detection being used by F-35 pilots to Software Defined Airborne Tactical Radios (ATRs) enabling Warfighter communication, to Identification Friend or Foe (IFF) radars ensuring the safety of airborne platforms around the world. Spanning air, land, sea, and space, we are developing the technology of tomorrow, delivered today. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. Our flexible work environment provides you a chance to change the world without giving up your personal life. We put our customers first – exemplified by our mission: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of? Come build your career with BAE Systems. Our engineers are the lifeblood of our company. With our robust offering of educational and career development opportunities, your chances to grow are limitless.
Given our continued growth, we have an immediate role available for an experienced and highly motivated Production Support Electrical Engineering Manager to join our team. As a member of the Continued Engineering Services (CES) team, you will have the chance to provide engineering support to the production of complex electronic assemblies and manage a team of electrical engineers, supporting multiple product lines and business areas. You will have the opportunity to work closely with cutting-edge hardware fielded on the most advanced Military Platforms.
Activities Day To Day Will Vary And May Include
Working with multiple Program Management Offices (PMOs) to understand and plan for the Electrical Engineering staffing needs to support production in our Austin Business Center.
Assignment of Electrical Engineering resources to support various businesses and product lines
Training and development of the electrical engineering team
Leading and peer reviewing issue resolution for electrical product defects
Utilize a metric-based approach to drive product yield and affordability improvements across product lines
Leading/Supporting transition to production of new products
Collaborate with colleagues and stakeholders across multiple sites and states to ensure on time deliveries of quality products to support the War Fighter.
If you are looking to be immersed in a myriad of new technical challenges, this role is for you! At BAE Systems, we thrive in a diverse, and dynamic team-oriented environment with principles of respect and trust. Our engineers interact with colleagues and peers of various disciplines and backgrounds to arrive at innovative solutions to problems. We encourage collaboration and foster an environment of knowledge sharing and continuous learning. Take the first step towards achieving your career goals with us and apply today!
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
BSEE from a 4 year accredited school.
10+ years experience in HW Engineering with a proven track record of leading multidisciplinary engineering teams through the full product lifecycle (from proposal and design through production and sustainment).
Demonstrated experience as a direct line people manager with a proven ability to provide daily direction, mentorship, and professional development for junior electrical engineers.
Strong track record of driving discrete tasks to closure and "owning the design" while managing deadlines and deliverables.
Experience interfacing with Operations, Quality, and Program Management across multiple sites and states to drive root-cause defect resolution.
Ability to present complex technical information clearly to internal program teams and external customers.
Advanced ability to apply electrical engineering principles to solve complex problems involving high-speed digital and RF products.
Experience in a manufacturing environment, specifically in developing test methodologies to reduce cost, increase yield, and improve throughput.
Proficient in analyzing test data to identify trends and execute yield improvement plans.
Expertise in generating and reviewing engineering specifications, drawings, reports, and Engineering Change Orders (ECOs).
Hands-on experience troubleshooting complex electronic systems, modules, and sub-assemblies in a production environment.
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
MSEE preferred
Active Secret Clearance HIGHLY PREFERRED
Exposure to microwave electronics a plus
Six Sigma Green Belt Certified
Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $149603 - $254317
Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.
Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
About BAE Systems, Inc.
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.
Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.
This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

items.title: Senior Manager, Facilities Remote Operations Center

evidence.quote: Pay range for this role is $168,000.00 - $264,000.00
evidence.text:
Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader
DuPont
Edina, MN
At DuPont, our purpose is to empower the world with essential innovations to thrive. We work on things that matter. Whether it’s providing clean water to more than a billion people on the planet, producing materials that are essential in everyday technology devices from smartphones to electric vehicles, or protecting workers around the world. Discover the many reasons the world’s most talented people are choosing to work at DuPont. Why Join Us | DuPont Careers
Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader
DuPont Water Solutions is seeking a passionate and high-performing individual to lead our reverse osmosis (RO) and ultrafiltration (UF) manufacturing network. The Multi-Site Manufacturing Leader is responsible for leading a global portfolio of (7) manufacturing sites and driving safe, reliable, customer-focused, and cost-effective operations aligned to DuPont’s business strategy. This role provides enterprise manufacturing leadership across a diverse network of sites, partnering closely with business, commercial, supply chain, engineering, quality, EHS, technology, and operational excellence leaders to align manufacturing priorities with customer needs, deliver performance, build capability, maximize value, and enable growth.
This individual will be accountable for establishing and sustaining a lean manufacturing culture that improves every day, reduces waste and variation, strengthens daily management, and develops problem-solving capability at all levels of the organization. Success requires a visible, hands-on leader who can set strategy, drive disciplined execution, inspire global teams, and role model DuPont’s core values of Safety & Respect, Integrity & Accountability, Grow and Improve, and Solve Problems with Customers.
Key Responsibilities
Lead global manufacturing performance: Own performance across the portfolio of RO and UF manufacturing sites, delivering results in safety, quality, delivery, inventory, productivity (cost), compliance, asset reliability, and customer service.
Drive lean manufacturing and operational excellence: Establish and deploy lean manufacturing practices, daily management systems, standard work, visual management, value stream mapping, kaizen, structured problem solving, root cause analysis, and waste elimination across the manufacturing network.
Align manufacturing strategy to business priorities: Develop and execute integrated manufacturing plans that support growth, margin improvement, customer commitments, supply reliability, and long-term competitiveness.
Sponsor and ensure progress of priority projects and investments: Develop priorities for capital investments based on economic models and ensure proper resource allocation to support realization of business strategy. Partner with capital organization and manufacturing technology on developing optionality and strong basic data with cross functional review in support of capital allocation process.
Improve customer experience through end-to-end excellence: Partners closely with commercial, customer service, procurement, logistics and supply chain to ensure end-to-end processes supporting customer expectations around lead time and excellent delivery performance. Sponsor efforts to streamline processes and drive improvements across the order-to-cash process.
Partner with Commercial to align on customer needs and value creation: Work closely with commercial and business leaders to understand customer requirements, market expectations, service priorities, and growth opportunities; translate those needs into manufacturing initiatives that improve reliability, responsiveness, quality, cost competitiveness, and overall customer value.
Build a culture of continuous improvement: Create an environment where leaders and teams challenge the status quo, solve problems at the source in real-time, learn from failures, and continuously improve processes, performance, and ways of working.
Lead through metrics and operating cadence: Use KPIs, bowler metrics, tiered accountability, operating reviews, and data-driven insights to identify performance gaps, prioritize improvement opportunities, develop action plans, execute Kaizens and sustain results.
Develop manufacturing talent and capability: Attract, develop, coach, and retain strong manufacturing leaders and technical talent; build lean capability, succession depth, and engaged shop-floor teams across regions.
Strengthen manufacturing systems and standards: Partner with Operational Excellence, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Supply Chain, and IT/OT teams to standardize best practices, codify tools and processes, and accelerate adoption of scalable manufacturing systems.
Lead change across a global network: Influence and align stakeholders across businesses, regions, functions, and sites. Partner with sites and manufacturing technology to develop the Kaizen funnel and top opportunities across the portfolio and ensure improvements are implemented, sustained, and leveraged to sister sites.
Improve cost, productivity, and asset effectiveness: Drive productivity, yield improvement (reduce cost of poor quality), cycle-time reduction, scrap and waste elimination, energy efficiency, and asset utilization while maintaining strong safety, quality, and compliance standards.
Role model DuPont culture and values: Set the tone through consistent behaviors, decision-making, and communications that reinforce safety, respect, integrity, accountability, continuous improvement, and customer-focused problem solving.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, or a related discipline required.
10+ years of progressive manufacturing, operations, engineering, or supply chain leadership experience. Experience leading manufacturing operations in a multi-site or global environment preferred.
Proven track record delivering sustained improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, productivity, asset reliability, and customer performance.
Deep practical experience applying lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, operational excellence, and structured problem-solving methods; Lean Six Sigma certification preferred.
Experience leading significant transformation at manufacturing sites, including culture change, operating system deployment, capability building, and performance management.
Strong financial acumen with the ability to connect manufacturing performance, productivity, and cost actions to business strategy, margin improvement, and enterprise value.
Demonstrated ability to lead in matrixed global organizations and influence across senior leaders, plant teams, commercial partners, functional partners, and business stakeholders.
Strong knowledge of EHS, quality, compliance, process safety, management of change, and operational risk management expectations in manufacturing environments.
Ability and willingness to travel globally to manufacturing sites as business needs require.
Expected Leadership Capabilities
Strategic and enterprise-minded: Understands business strategy, customer needs, commercial priorities, and market dynamics; makes decisions that optimize enterprise value rather than local or functional outcomes alone.
Execution-focused: Translates strategy into clear priorities, operating rhythms, accountability, and measurable results; drives issues to closure with urgency and discipline.
Lean practitioner and teacher: Coaches leaders and teams in lean thinking, daily management, problem solving, standard work, kaizen, and continuous improvement behaviors.
Visible and people-centered: Builds trust on the shop floor, engages teams directly, listens actively, and creates an environment where people are empowered to identify and solve problems.
Change leader: Leads transformation with clarity, resilience, and practical execution; anticipates resistance and ensures new ways of working are embedded and sustained.
Talent builder: Develops strong leaders, builds succession depth, creates growth opportunities, and holds teams accountable for both performance and behaviors.
Collaborative influencer: Partners effectively across Operations, Commercial, Supply Chain, Engineering, Quality, EHS, Technology, HR, and Finance to deliver integrated business outcomes.
Data-driven problem solver: Uses facts, metrics, benchmarking, and structured analysis to identify root causes, prioritize action, and improve performance.
Preferred Experience
Experience leading or operating within a business system or production system-driven organization.
Demonstrated success deploying lean manufacturing practices across multiple sites, regions, or business units.
Experience leading global manufacturing networks that include varied technologies, operating models, customer requirements, and regulatory or compliance expectations.
Experience partnering with commercial and supply chain leaders to connect manufacturing performance to customer value, service reliability, and growth.
Experience using digital tools, automation, analytics, or IT/OT systems to improve manufacturing visibility, productivity, and decision-making.
Location and Travel
Preferred locations are Edina, Minnesota, Midland, MI or Wilmington, Delaware.
30% Global travel to manufacturing sites is expected.
Join our Talent Community to stay connected with us!
DuPont is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will be considered without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, national origin, age, veteran status, disability or any other protected class. If you need a reasonable accommodation to search or apply for a position, please visit our Accessibility Page for Contact Information.
DuPont offers a comprehensive pay and benefits package. To learn more visit the Compensation and Benefits page.
The Pay range for this role is $168,000.00 - $264,000.00 Annual
How Base Pay is Determined:
DuPont has job leveling frameworks that help organize roles based on progressive levels of responsibility, proficiency and qualifications. Each role has an associated pay range (or an established pay rate for some roles) based on the competitive market in each country where we operate. Each individual’s pay is based on a variety of factors, including their role and the associated pay range for that role, their geographic location (i.e., country, state, metropolitan area), as well as their skills, experience, education and certifications, and performance.

evidence.quote: 10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
evidence.text:
Plant Manager
Forte Opening Solutions
Marshfield, WI
At Forte Opening Solutions, we don't just manufacture doors; we create pathways to possibilities. We empower our employees to shape the future of our industry. Join a team where craftsmanship meets cutting-edge technology, and where your ideas can open new doors. Together, we build not just products, but a culture of excellence, innovation, and collaboration.
We are seeking an experienced Plant Manager with a strong background in particle board or engineered wood panel manufacturing to lead our production facility. This individual will be responsible for the overall safety, operational performance, quality, financial results, and continuous improvement of a high-volume manufacturing operation. The ideal candidate has extensive experience leading continuous manufacturing processes, developing high-performing teams, and optimizing production while maintaining the highest standards of safety, quality, and environmental compliance.
Responsibilities
Lead all aspects of plant operations, including Safety, Quality, Production, Maintenance, Engineering, Shipping, Environmental, and Continuous Improvement.
Champion a world-class safety culture and ensure full compliance with OSHA, EPA, environmental permitting, and all company safety policies and procedures.
Drive operational excellence using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, TPM, and other continuous improvement methodologies to improve safety, productivity, yield, uptime, and cost performance.
Lead production of high-quality particle board products by optimizing fiber preparation, drying, blending, forming, pressing, finishing, and packaging operations.
Ensure efficient utilization of raw materials including wood fiber, resin systems, wax, and additives while minimizing waste and maximizing recovery.
Monitor and improve key manufacturing metrics including Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), throughput, yield, press efficiency, uptime, scrap, energy consumption, customer complaints, and on-time delivery.
Develop production schedules that meet customer demand while maximizing plant capacity and operational efficiency.
Partner with Maintenance and Engineering to improve equipment reliability through preventative and predictive maintenance programs.
Build, coach, and develop a high-performing leadership team focused on accountability, engagement, and continuous improvement.
Foster a culture of employee engagement through coaching, communication, training, and leadership development.
Maintain compliance with quality systems and ensure products consistently meet customer specifications.
Drive capital improvement projects that improve plant capability, automation, safety, efficiency, and cost competitiveness.
Own the plant's operating budget and full P&L responsibility while partnering with Finance, Sales, Supply Chain, Procurement, and Corporate Leadership to achieve business objectives.
Analyze operational data to identify trends, eliminate losses, and drive sustainable improvements.
Serve as the plant's primary leader during customer visits, audits, and regulatory inspections.
Perform other duties as assigned.
Qualifications
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business, Forestry, Wood Products, or a related field preferred.
10+ years of progressive manufacturing leadership experience.
Minimum of 5 years of leadership experience within particle board, MDF, OSB, engineered wood products, wood composites, or other continuous panel manufacturing environments.
Previous Plant Manager or Operations Manager experience in a continuous manufacturing operation strongly preferred.
Demonstrated experience leading large manufacturing teams in a 24/7 operation.
Proven success managing plant financial performance and P&L responsibility.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Extensive knowledge of particle board manufacturing processes including:
Wood handling and fiber preparation
Drying systems
Resin blending and application
Mat forming
Hot press operations
Sanding, trimming, and finishing
Panel quality testing and process control
Strong understanding of resin chemistry, moisture control, density profiles, panel properties, and process optimization.
Experience managing continuous production systems with a focus on maximizing uptime and throughput.

evidence.quote: Significant manufacturing leadership experience, including running a plant and leading operational excellence or operations across multiple sites.
evidence.text:
Vice President of Operations
Genesis Products
Goshen, IN
Genesis Products is looking for a VP of Operations to take a strong manufacturing foundation and turn it into a competitive weapon. This is a new, company-wide role created for one reason: our customers move fast, our business is getting more complex, and we want manufacturing systems smart enough to make complexity an advantage.
You won't inherit a mess to clean up. You'll inherit working systems, monthly audits, committed plant teams, and leaders who want to get better. Your job is to protect what works, raise the bar, and build what comes next, in the plants, in the warehouse, on the road, and in the software that ties it together.
About Genesis Products
Genesis is a multi-plant manufacturer rooted in Elkhart, Indiana. Our capabilities include lamination, mouldings, panel processing, and composite forming operations, serving customers whose needs change quickly and often. Genesis serves the RV, Kitchen & Bath, Fleet & Heavy Vehicle, and Commercial Markets with 14 plants and 900 employees. We have a passion for growth and are always improving.
We're customer- and product-driven at our core. Our business group leaders live close to customers and products, and they make the daily calls that keep us responsive. Behind them, we've built real operating discipline: a proprietary MRP platform developed and refined in-house over two decades, monthly audits across safety, 5S, manufacturing excellence, people, and warehouse, and a growing logistics operation with our own managed fleet.
We're growing, including through acquisition, and we intend to keep doing both. We're stable and able to make decisions quickly, without layers of bureaucracy between a good idea and the plant floor.
The role
The VP of Operations owns how Genesis manufactures: the systems, standards, and accountability that let every plant perform and adapt. Reporting to the President & CEO, you'll be the company's senior manufacturing leader and its go-to problem solver.
This is a role of influence and ownership, not a traditional chain of command. Plants report through operations managers to our business group VPs, who stay close to customers and make day-to-day calls. You'll design the systems those teams run on, coach and challenge them to use them well, and keep the whole company honest about maintaining them. When a customer need changes overnight, our group VPs decide what to do; your systems make sure we can do it well, safely, and profitably. The role will have direct reports and responsibility for safety, logistics, warehouse excellence, and continuous improvement, with the opportunity to take on manufacturing HR as the role grows.
If you want to shape how an entire company runs, with direct access to leadership and the freedom to act, read on.
What you'll lead
Safety.
Own safety policy and accountability across every site. Make Genesis a place where people go home safe, and where safety performance is measured, visible, and owned.
Manufacturing excellence.
Own our quality and operational excellence systems, and the monthly audit process behind them. Keep what works, raise the bar as plants mature, and make sure findings turn into lasting improvement, not just scores.
Systems for agility.
Design physical and digital systems that let us absorb fast-changing customer demand: changeovers, flexible staffing, scheduling, and smarter use of our in-house MRP platform. Turn floor problems into clear requirements and see them through to adoption.
Turnarounds.
Partner with business group teams to diagnose and fix underperforming plants, bringing structure, urgency, and hands-on problem solving.
Launches and overhauls.
Lead the start-up of major new operations and the redesign of existing ones, from layout and flow to people and process.
Acquisition integration.
Alongside our executive leadership and CFO, integrate and onboard acquired operations, bringing them onto Genesis systems and standards while keeping customers served. Build the playbook we'll use again and again.
Warehouse and material excellence.
Raise the standard for organization, barcoding, tracking, and inventory accuracy, so material is always where it should be.
Logistics.
Lead our logistics function and managed fleet, and expand it beyond Elkhart into a true competitive advantage.
What success looks like in your first two years
Safety and audit results are improving across every plant, and leadership reviews system health as seriously as revenue and margin.
Our existing systems are stronger than when you arrived, and no plant has slipped backward.
Underperforming operations have been turned around with results that last.
Plants respond to customer changes faster, with less disruption and lower cost.
Warehouse accuracy and material flow are visibly better, supported by tools people actually use.
Plant and operations leaders see you as the person who makes them better, and come to you first when something is hard.
Who you are
You've run plants, and you've made multiple plants better. You're at home on the floor and in the boardroom, and people on both trust you.
What you bring:
Significant manufacturing leadership experience, including running a plant and leading operational excellence or operations across multiple sites.
A track record of turnarounds, launches, or integrations, with results you can measure and that lasted after you moved on.
Deep experience in high-mix, customer-driven manufacturing, where demand and specs change often. You see that variability as a design problem to solve, not noise to eliminate.
Hands-on fluency with continuous improvement, quality systems, and safety leadership, applied practically rather than by the book.
Real digital fluency: you've connected physical process changes to software changes, written clear requirements, and gotten floor teams to adopt new tools. Experience with custom or homegrown systems is a plus.
Experience in warehouse, material flow, or logistics is a strong plus.
How you work:
You build on what's there.
You learn why existing systems work before changing them, and you improve them instead of replacing them to leave your mark.
You lead through influence.
You can get plant teams who don't report to you to adopt new standards, because they see you making them better.
You know when to yield and when to push.
The customer comes first, and you're comfortable when daily decisions go to the business. But you'll speak up, to anyone, when a shortcut is turning into a habit.
You'd rather fix it than talk about it.
You roll up your sleeves, show up in the plants, and stay until it works.
You develop people.
You leave plant leaders more capable than you found them.
Why this opportunity
Real impact, fast.
Your work will show up across every plant, not buried in one corner of a large organization.
A foundation worth building on.
Strong systems, committed teams, and leadership that values operational discipline.
Software that moves at your speed.
Our in-house MRP platform can evolve with your ideas, instead of you working around someone else's limitations.
Room to grow.
Acquisitions, new operations, and a growing logistics network mean the role grows as the company does.
A seat at the table.
Work directly with company leadership on where Genesis goes next.

Plant Manager
Ferrellgas
Tavares, FL
Overview
Join a team that keeps America grilling! Blue Rhino, a Ferrellgas company, was recently named one of America's Most Trustworthy Companies by Newsweek for 2025 — and that trust starts with our people.
Blue Rhino is seeking an experienced, safety-driven Plant Manager
to lead operations at our propane tank exchange production facility in Tavares, FL.
This position is ideal for an experienced operations leader with a background in propane, oil and gas, chemical processing, hazardous materials, or other highly regulated industrial environments.
A strong understanding of OSHA regulations, safety compliance, and operational risk management is essential.
The Plant Manager oversees all aspects of a single production facility, including first- and second-shift operations, production planning, staffing, equipment maintenance, regulatory compliance, and continuous improvement. This position directly oversees the facility's shift supervisors and is responsible for developing a strong safety culture while meeting production and operational goals.
Why You’ll Love Working Here

items.title: Vice President of Engineering, Missile R&D

evidence.quote: Experience with DoD customers, export-controlled technology, or military operational requirements.
evidence.text:
Vice President of Engineering, Missile R&D
SerenX
Melbourne, FL
About SerenX
SerenX is building the next generation of portable, autonomous defensive missile systems to protect America and our allies. Our mission is to deliver advanced, affordable air defense capabilities at a fraction of the cost and complexity of traditional systems.
We're an institutionally funded defense technology company performing work on U.S. Department of Defense contracts, with a founding team that includes Y Combinator alumni, former Special Operations leaders, and experienced aerospace engineers.
We design, build, fly, test, break, and improve our own hardware. We're looking for the engineering leader who will build the organization around those people.
The Role
We're hiring a Vice President of Engineering, R&D to build SerenX's engineering headquarters in Melbourne, Florida.
Melbourne is not a satellite office. It is where the technology begins, where the systems are engineered and tested, and where we support American and allied operators around the world. The pace we are building for is chalkboard to first operational employment in months, not years, when the hardware, the law, and the end user allow it.
You may have spent years on flight hardware at a place like SpaceX, Blue Origin, L3Harris, or Northrop Grumman. You learned how ambitious hardware gets built, and you learned how a large organization can make that work harder than it needs to be. You want to build something of your own.
The Founder and CTO sets the technology. You lead the people, the execution, and the engineering organization that turn that direction into working, fielded systems. In 2027, working with him, you will grow this team to about 30 people and carry three missile programs at once. You are not inheriting that organization. You get to build it.
Location: Melbourne, FL (On-site)
Employment: Full-time Compensation: $210,000–$255,000 annually + equity
Reports to: Founder & CTO
What You'll Do
Grow a multidisciplinary engineering headquarters across mechanical, electrical, aerospace, flight software, autonomy, integration, prototyping, and flight test.
Hire for ability, integrity, curiosity, and how someone treats the people beside them.
Give every engineer clear ownership, and a path to get better that does not require them to become a manager.
Teach. Know what each person is trying to become, and invest in it.
Make disagreement normal, including from the junior engineer and the technician. Credit goes to the people who did the work.
Carry three missile programs at once, and build leads who can run a piece of that work without you in the room.
Keep the interfaces, the tests, and the field feedback connected.
Keep the pace high without burying the shop in meetings. Enough record to know what flew, what changed, and why.
Bring what the range, the operators, and the defense-services teams learn back into the next design.
Protect the team's time and its standards. Extraordinary effort when the work needs it. Not exhaustion as the normal week.
Stay close enough to the hardware and the range to be useful, and support the people who want to train, travel, and see the work with operators, including overseas.
What We're Looking For
12+ years in aerospace, defense, missiles, autonomous aircraft, or other flight hardware, with real time on integration and test, not only reviews.
5+ years leading engineers across more than one discipline, including hiring, coaching, and developing people into larger roles.
Evidence you have led, or are ready to lead, on the order of 15 to 50 people, and that you can name the leads who made that possible.
You have taken complex hardware from design through integration, test, and use, and you can talk about what broke and what the team learned.
Enough depth in one discipline to be useful beside a senior mechanical or flight-software lead, and the habit of leaving the pencil in their hand.
A record of recruiting and growing engineers who would work for you again.
You can move fast and still stop a test, a design, or a date when the evidence says to.
Willingness to work on-site in Melbourne, Florida and be on the range with the team.
A bachelor's degree in engineering, physics, or a related field, or equivalent depth of engineering and leadership experience.
Particularly Valuable Experience
A director or senior director ready to leave SpaceX, Blue Origin, L3Harris, Northrop Grumman, Collins, Lockheed Martin, Rocket Lab, Anduril, or a smaller shop that actually flies hardware, and build the organization you wish you had worked in.
You have already been the person between a founder, or a chief engineer, and a team.
You have grown a team from a small founding group toward a larger multidisciplinary shop, and developed the leads as you went.
Missiles, interceptors, UAVs, spacecraft, propulsion, or flight test.
Configuration, test readiness, and production discipline put in place without freezing a young program.
Experience with DoD customers, export-controlled technology, or military operational requirements.
An active U.S. Government security clearance. Secret, Top Secret (TS), or TS/SCI is useful. We can sponsor the right person.
Who Thrives Here
You have reached the point where building great engineers matters as much to you as building great machines. You remember what it was like to be young, with an ambitious idea, and to have someone senior who believed in you. You want to be that person for someone else.
You can stand at the bench, listen, and clear the obstacle. You are not trying to prove you are the smartest person in the room. You know the quiet technician who sees a failure nobody else sees can matter as much as the person who drew the system.
You know when to push, when to turn, and when to stop. You can make a hard call without becoming hard on people. You measure your leadership by what your people become able to do, not by how much they still need you.
We move quickly. We take calculated technical risk. We will break expensive hardware when that is how we learn something that matters. We are not building a traditional aerospace bureaucracy, and we are not replacing one with a shop that runs on emergencies and burnout.
How to Stand Out
We care more about the people you have developed, and the hardware you helped deliver, than the number of people who reported to you.
Send three stories. An engineer or a team you taught, and what they can do now that they could not do before. A program you carried through a failed test, a bad date, or a hard stretch, and how the team came through it. A leadership decision you made to protect the team's work or its culture.
Tell us what you would build differently if you got to shape an engineering organization from its early days. We are hiring the person whose old team would follow them to Melbourne.
Export Control & Equal Opportunity
This position involves access to ITAR-controlled defense articles and technical data. Candidates must qualify as a U.S. person under 22 CFR 120.62.
SerenX is an equal opportunity employer. Employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs, without unlawful discrimination based on any legally protected characteristic.
Learn more: https://serenx.com/careers/vice-president-engineering-rd

Establish the plant’s strategic goals and objectives and ensure alignment with the business team.
Focus and drive the management team to innovative solutions to productivity gains, waste reduction (yield optimization) and minimization of overhead costs.
Actively pursue benchmarking to set new standards for safety, quality, productivity, service and costs using competitive knowledge and industry information.
Sets and maintains high safety standards ensuring proper accountabilities and implementing processes to eliminate unsafe work practices. Ensure compliance with the Occupational Health and Safety Act, Regulations, and the Company health and safety roles and responsibilities.
Develop and implement new business strategies for creating or improving processes and procedures to improve plant performance.
Meet regularly with department heads/business unit leaders; facilitate resolution of issues/problems between business units and/or departments.
Responsible for appropriate staff levels to meet requirements of the facility.
Maintain positive employee relations at the facility.
Enable teamwork and collaboration through information sharing meetings with all departments.
Support and develop operations policies, procedures and systems to meet the goals of the Company such as the Intertape Performance System, lean manufacturing philosophies and the ISO Quality System.
Review and approve plans for the control of planned output, budget spending, material efficiency, waste, engineering effectiveness and human resources.
Budget preparation and monitoring of P&L.
Monitor financial performance to ensure the plant is meeting or exceeding budgetary commitment.
Analyze and report on the plant’s daily, monthly and annual key performance indicators and industry trends.
Develop and implement strategies around improving the financial performance of the departments.
Handle customer enquiries and complaints which are escalated from the departments.
Analyze the customer’s concern and present options to solve the issue.
Review and use the monthly profit and loss statements to ensure expense control and proactively plan production goals.
Examine reports (e.g., inventory, production and daily reports) to determine the operational activities of the Company and ensure optimum performance.
Ensure that all reporting employees adhere to Company policies and procedures.
Perform other duties as required.

Bachelor’s degree in Business Management, Industrial Technology or Engineering or equivalent experience.
Master’s degree in Operations Management preferred
5+ years’ previous management experience in a manufacturing environment with proven leadership abilities.
Experience with self-directed work teams or high level of employee involvement.
Experience with lean manufacturing principles and implementing a lean culture.

We are seeking a hands-on, results-driven Director of Operations and Manufacturing
to lead production operations across both plants — a transformation role, not a maintenance role. The company is on a trajectory to double sales, double throughput, and cut manufacturing lead-time in half
. This leader will own the operational side of that mission, driving step-change improvements in safety, housekeeping, quality (QC & QA), process discipline, throughput, and utilization, and will plan and launch second shifts at both locations
to unlock capacity.

Safety & Housekeeping

Lead incident investigations, root-cause analysis, and corrective action closure
Quality (QC & QA)

Create and lead an ISO style monthly Management Review meeting
Position the company for relevant certifications as appropriate (e.g., AISC, IAS AC472)

Cut manufacturing lead-time by 50% through flow improvement, scheduling discipline, and constraint management
Partner with engineering, detailing, and purchasing to remove upstream delays that constrain the shop floor
Procurement & Vendor Quality

Partner with Finance on inventory strategy, min/max levels, and cash-conscious buying that still protects production continuity

Double plant throughput through a combination of process improvement, capacity planning, staffing, and equipment utilization
Establish OEE (Overall Equipment Effectiveness) or equivalent measurement on key equipment — roll formers, purlin line, pull-through welder, brakes, saws — and drive systematic improvement
Develop and execute the plan to launch second shifts in both Adel and Tampa
, including hiring plans, shift leadership structure, training, and cross-shift communication routines
Build production scheduling and capacity models that align shop loading with the sales pipeline
Leadership & Talent

Recruit, train, and retain skilled trades talent (welders, sheet metal workers, machine operators) in competitive labor markets
Establish daily management routines: tiered meetings, KPI boards, Gemba walks, and escalation processes
Foster alignment and consistent standards between the Adel and Tampa operations
Business Partnership
Own the manufacturing operating budgets for Adel and Tampa, including annual planning, monthly forecasts, labor costs, operating expenses, and capital expenditure recommendations
Own manufacturing P&L performance and plant-level financial results in partnership with Finance; review actual results against budget, explain variances, and lead corrective actions to improve margin and control costs
Support ERP-driven operations (NetSuite), including production data discipline, inventory accuracy, and work order integrity
Partner with Sales and the CRO to ensure promised lead-times are competitive and consistently achieved
Financial Accountability, Budgeting & Overtime Control
Own overtime authorization, scheduling, monitoring, and reduction across both plants; hold plant managers accountable for overtime approvals, staffing plans, and labor efficiency without compromising safety, quality, or delivery
Develop and manage annual plant operating budgets, labor budgets, and rolling forecasts; track actual spending against plan and address unfavorable variances

The ideal candidate combines strong manufacturing and financial acumen with experience leading both internal operations and international third-party manufacturing partners.
The COO will partner closely with commercial, product development, engineering, and finance leaders to improve profitability, introduce new products, and scale operations while preserving quality, craftsmanship, and an entrepreneurial culture.

Enterprise Strategy & Operational Execution

Establish consistent operating reviews, performance dashboards, and accountability across locations.

Lead applicable ISO certification efforts, audit readiness, corrective actions, and continuous improvement.
Strengthen supplier quality controls, process consistency, and product reliability.
Promote a culture of safety and accountability across all locations.
Engage directly with key customers and distributors to address quality concerns and build confidence in operational performance.

Develop the operations technology roadmap, including ERP/MRP capabilities, planning tools, dashboards, and process controls.
Improve data accuracy, visibility, and decision-making across facilities.
Partner with finance to improve product costing, gross margins, productivity, inventory, and working capital.
Evaluate capital investments using clear business cases and return-on-investment analysis.
Leadership & Organizational Development
Build, develop, and retain a high-performing team of facility leaders and functional managers.
Clarify organizational responsibilities, decision authority, goals, and performance expectations.
Strengthen succession planning and leadership development.
Foster collaboration across operations, sales, engineering, product development, and finance.
Serve as a trusted operational advisor to the CEO and contribute to board and investor discussions as appropriate.
Qualifications
15+ years of progressive operations leadership experience, including significant responsibility for multi-site manufacturing and supply chain.
Prior experience as a COO, Senior Vice President, Vice President of Operations, or equivalent executive leader.
Experience overseeing both in-house manufacturing or assembly and outsourced production.
Demonstrated experience managing international supply chains and manufacturing partners, including Asia.
Proven success improving productivity, quality, delivery, margins, and working capital in a growing business.
Strong ownership of SIOP or integrated business planning.
Experience leading new product introductions, strategic sourcing, supplier development, and manufacturing process improvements.
Working knowledge of quality management systems, ISO standards, and continuous improvement.
Strong financial acumen, including product cost, gross margin, budgeting, capital allocation, and investment analysis.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems and operational analytics to drive performance.
Demonstrated ability to develop leaders and build accountability across geographically dispersed teams.
Preferred Background
Experience in a private equity-backed, founder-led, or entrepreneurial manufacturing business.
Background in automotive, performance aftermarket, metal fabrication, engineered products, industrial equipment, public safety, defense, or other quality-critical manufacturing environments.
Experience with high-mix production, international operations, acquisitions, or operational integration.
Experience presenting to boards, investors, and executive leadership teams.
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, operations, supply chain, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent experience considered.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or higher, or comparable practical experience, strongly preferred.

The successful candidate will be an action-oriented executive who moves comfortably between strategic planning and hands-on problem-solving. This leader will earn credibility with executives, facility teams, and skilled trades through sound judgment, clear communication, and consistent follow-through.
A strong sense of urgency, attention to detail, and commitment to people development are essential, along with the ability to introduce structure while preserving the culture and expertise that make the business successful.

Director, Quality Assurance & Regulatory Affairs (QA/RA)
Mazza Healthcare
Lincolnshire, IL
Location / Work Arrangement
This is primarily an in-office position based at Mazza Healthcare's corporate headquarters in Lincolnshire, Illinois. Regular in-person presence is expected given the leadership and cross-functional responsibilities of the role.
Company Description
Mazza Healthcare is a healthcare solutions company with strong expertise in global sourcing and private label portfolio development. We advance the cost-effectiveness and quality of healthcare products while remaining committed to patient safety. Mazza Healthcare has experienced rapid growth over the past several years and is currently seeking a Director of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs.
Job Description
The Director of Quality Assurance and Regulatory Affairs (QA/RA) will play a key leadership role in the management, maintenance, and continued effectiveness of Mazza Healthcare's Quality Management System (QMS). This position is strategically important to the success of our commercialization efforts, regulatory compliance, customer relationships, and commitment to product quality and patient safety.
The Director of QA/RA will serve as a subject matter expert in quality and regulatory affairs, providing guidance to the business regarding ISO 13485, FDA requirements, regulatory compliance, and documentation supporting domestic and international product commercialization. This individual will have significant responsibility for maintaining the QMS, supporting organizational compliance, and coordinating ISO certification and surveillance audits, customer audits, and other applicable quality and regulatory activities.
Working closely with Management and departmental leaders, the Director of QA/RA will help drive continuous improvement, strengthen internal quality processes, and promote a culture of quality and accountability throughout the organization. The position requires an individual who combines strong technical QA/RA expertise with sound business judgment and the ability to develop practical, compliant solutions that support broader business objectives.
The Director of QA/RA will interact directly with customers, manufacturers, suppliers, and auditors and must be capable of clearly communicating complex quality and regulatory concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences. The successful candidate must be comfortable leading customer discussions, presenting information, and representing Mazza Healthcare professionally in external meetings.
This role is ideally suited to a highly motivated, detail-oriented self-starter who takes ownership of responsibilities, manages competing priorities, and drives initiatives through completion with limited day-to-day oversight.
Duties / Responsibilities
Support the development, implementation, maintenance, and continual improvement of Mazza Healthcare's Quality Management System (QMS), ensuring compliance with ISO 13485, applicable FDA regulations, and other regulatory requirements.
Serve as a key subject matter expert for quality and regulatory matters, providing practical guidance to Executive Management and other departments.
Support and coordinate ISO certification and surveillance audits, including preparation, execution, and corrective actions.
Coordinate Quality Department activities, including managing priorities, supporting team members, and ensuring timely completion of assigned deliverables.
Partner with Executive Management, Sales, Sourcing, and Operations to support new and existing products, customer opportunities, and domestic and international commercialization.
Represent Mazza Healthcare in customer, manufacturer, supplier, and auditor discussions, clearly communicating complex quality and regulatory concepts.
Oversee customer complaints, investigations, risk assessments, corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), and other quality-related matters through timely resolution.
Support the qualification, evaluation, and ongoing management of manufacturers and suppliers, including Quality Agreements and supplier audits as appropriate.
Evaluate regulatory and QMS requirements associated with new products, suppliers, processes, and business opportunities and ensure appropriate actions are implemented.
Ensure compliance with applicable customer, federal, state, and international quality and regulatory requirements.
Drive continuous improvement of quality processes, product specifications, documentation, and overall organizational effectiveness.
Proactively identify quality and regulatory risks, establish priorities, and independently drive initiatives and outstanding matters through completion.
Desired Qualifications
7+ years of Quality Assurance, Regulatory Affairs, and/or Quality Management System experience, including demonstrated leadership experience.
Minimum of 5 years of experience within the medical device industry.
Strong demonstrated knowledge and practical experience with ISO 13485, FDA medical device regulations, cGMP, and other applicable regulatory requirements.
Demonstrated experience managing or co-leading a medical device QMS and leading ISO certification, surveillance, customer, and/or regulatory audits.
Strong business acumen with the ability to balance quality and regulatory requirements with practical business objectives.
Proven leadership and management skills with the ability to establish priorities, develop employees, delegate effectively, and promote accountability and ownership.
Highly self-motivated, detail-oriented, and capable of independently managing multiple priorities and driving matters through completion with limited oversight.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills with the ability to clearly communicate complex concepts and confidently represent Mazza Healthcare with customers, manufacturers, suppliers, and auditors.
Ability to operate effectively in a dynamic, entrepreneurial environment and contribute beyond specifically defined responsibilities when necessary.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Word, Excel, Access, and PowerPoint.
Ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed.
Compensation & Benefits
This is a salaried position with the opportunity to earn an annual performance-based bonus. Mazza Healthcare also offers employees a comprehensive benefits package, including health insurance and a 401(k) retirement plan with a Safe Harbor employer contribution.

evidence.text:
Sr. Manager, Quality Engineering ADD
PCI Pharma Services
Rockford, IL
Life changing therapies. Global impact. Bridge to thousands of biopharma companies and their patients.
We are PCI.
Our investment is in People who make an impact, drive progress and create a better tomorrow. Our strategy includes building teams across our global network to pioneer and shape the future of PCI.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The essential duties and responsibilities include the following but other duties may be assigned.
Provides strategy and leadership over the Quality Engineering (QE) teams at both Rockford Linden sites that are involved in supporting design transfer/control/assurance, risk management, statistical analysis of data, deviations, complaints, change management, and quality improvement projects.
Direct oversight and development of Quality Engineers responsible for Advanced Drug Delivery business segment assigning them to projects based on technical expertise and project priority
Leads QE team to support New Product Introduction and tech transfer for product launches as well as supporting the sustaining commercialized products
Accountable for overall management, reviewing, planning and administering of resource allocation and workload planning for the Quality Engineering staff.
Serve as subject matter expert (SME) and process owner for the Design Control and Risk Management procedures within the Quality Management System, including a risk management program aligned to ISO 14971
Oversee and approve PCI investigations including calibration OOS and laboratory or environmental monitoring product impact investigations.
Oversee and approve site supplier nonconformances and supplier related quality metrics
Process owner for Measurement System Analysis (MSA), Control Plans, Process Flow Maps, Inspection plans and techniques, GR&R, test requirements and Test Method Transfer/Validation.
Technical evaluation of change controls including risk assessment / implementation of risk mitigation strategies.
Provide high level guidance on complex design validation and verification (V&V) strategies, sampling plans and root cause investigations for design failure.
Oversee the feedback loop between Post-Market Surveillance (Complaints) and internal or external design assurance teams to trigger necessary design changes or CAPAs based on field reports.
Serve as the final Quality approver for major "Stage Gate" transitions, ensuring all design inputs, outputs, and transfer activities are complete and compliant.
Ensure design assurance strategies align with evolving global standards, including ISO 13485 and FDA 21 CFR 820
Apply scientific statistical analysis techniques to proactively identify trends, identify root causes and implement actions to mitigate recurrence.
Oversees and provides input for statistical assessment of data to drive improvements.
Supports and maintains quality assurance programs and systems, policies, processes, procedures and controls ensuring that performance and quality of products conform to established standards and agency requirements to ensure customer and regulatory satisfaction.
Participates as a member in various steering committees to guide and influence the company’s focus on new products, new customers, and strategic initiatives.
Prepares reports to company management detailing the status of open projects that support the capacity, regulatory and quality improvement requirements of the plant.
Presentation of quality standards, process flows, inspection plans, and/or issues both internally to stakeholders and externally to clients with confidence and accuracy.
Establishes and ensures the Quality Engineering team achieves the appropriate levels of compliance and develops actions to ensure ongoing performance is achieved and maintained through metrics and other forms of KPI’s.
Support the recruitment, coaching, and development of Quality Engineers to achieve excellence and efficiency when programs are scaled.
Creates a “learning” culture that enables individuals to reach their maximum potential and builds the capability of the organization and generates energy, enthusiasm and commitment from others.
Ensures budget development and the preparation of periodic projections of spending against budgets; and manages and controls departmental spending.
Partners with internal teams (Business Unit, Quality, Operations, Engineering, Validation) to achieve company goals
Participates in regulatory inspections, customer audits, visits and conference calls.
Supervisory Responsibilities
Leads a group up to 10 direct reports across multiple sites.
Qualifications:
The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required for the stated position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Required
College or Trade Degree required (engineering degree or related scientific degree). Must have a minimum of 5+ years of experience in an FDA regulated industry with strong preference to medical device or combination products.
Demonstrated proficiency with personal computers, business software (e.g., MS Office) and technical software (ERP and eQMS systems). Ability to create, use and interpret scientific tables, charts, and graphs.
Advanced Computer Skills: Ability to perform the most complex computer tasks and operate various computer programs.
Full Professional Proficiency: Ability to speak, read, and write fluently and accurately on all levels pertinent to professional needs.
Analytical ability to drive effective Root Cause Analysis (RCA) and critical thinking for complex problem solving.
Preferred
Possesses excellent organizational, time management and multi-tasking skills to meet commitments and deadlines.
Prior experience in technical writing and utilizing root cause analysis tools is required.
Critical thinking skills along with a strong collaborative approach is required.
Lean Six Sigma or other formal process improvement skillsets are highly desirable.
Technical knowledge and experience around Test Method validation, MSA, and Medical Devices processes is preferred.
The hiring rate for this position is $122,000-$152,500 plus eligibility for an annual 15% performance bonus. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including but not limited to specific and relevant experience, education, credentials, geography, and subject matter expertise. PCI offers full-time employees a competitive benefits package that includes paid time off, health insurance coverage (including dental and vision), a flexible spending account, and a 401(k) plan.
Join us and be part of building the bridge between life changing therapies and patients. Let’s talk future
Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) Statement
PCI Pharma Services is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer. We do not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, age, sex, creed, national origin, ancestry, citizenship status, marital or domestic or civil union status, familial status, affectional or sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, genetics, disability, military eligibility or veteran status, or any other protected status.
At PCI, Equity and Inclusion are at the core of our company’s purpose: Together, delivering life-changing therapies. We are committed to cultivating an inclusive workplace by holding ourselves accountable to the highest standards of understanding, fairness, respect, and equal opportunity – at every level. We envision a PCI community where everyone can belong and grow, and we strive to bring this vision to reality by continuously and intentionally assessing our people practices, policies and programs, marketing approach, and workplace culture.

evidence.text:
Plant Manager
SkyWater Search Partners
Thomson, GA
We are partnering with a growing metal fabrication manufacturer on a retained search for a Plant Manager to lead its Thomson, Georgia facility.
This is a hands-on leadership opportunity within a site entering a significant growth phase. The operation is ramping production quickly behind several major customer programs and is expected to roughly double in headcount as the facility expands across multiple shifts.
The Plant Manager will have broad ownership of day-to-day operations while helping build the team, processes, accountability, and operating structure needed to support that growth. This is an opportunity for someone who enjoys being close to the floor, developing people, solving problems, and building an operation rather than simply maintaining one.
Responsibilities
Lead all day-to-day manufacturing operations for the Thomson facility
Build, develop, and lead the production organization as the site scales
Support the expansion into multiple shifts, including weekend production
Drive performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost
Establish clear expectations, accountability, and operating discipline across the shop floor
Develop supervisors and front-line leaders as the organization grows
Partner with leadership on staffing, capacity planning, equipment needs, and facility improvements
Identify and implement opportunities to improve throughput, workflow, labor efficiency, and quality
Maintain a visible, hands-on leadership presence throughout the operation
Qualifications
Manufacturing leadership experience as a Plant Manager, Operations Manager, Manufacturing Manager, Production Manager, Supervisor, or similar role
Experience leading hourly manufacturing teams in a hands-on production environment
Background in metal fabrication, welding, machining, heavy equipment, industrial products, or a similar manufacturing setting strongly preferred
Strong technical aptitude and understanding of manufacturing processes
Demonstrated ability to build teams, develop people, and improve operational performance
Comfortable operating in a growing environment where processes and structure are still being developed
Strong problem-solving, communication, and leadership skills
Bachelor’s degree not required; technical education, associate degree, apprenticeship experience, or equivalent manufacturing experience will be considered

evidence.text:
Director, Manufacturing Engineering, Body
Blue Bird Corporation
Fort Valley, GA
About Blue Bird Corporation
Blue Bird (NASDAQ: BLBD) is recognized as a technology leader and innovator of school buses since its founding in 1927. Our dedicated team members design, engineer and manufacture school buses with a singular focus on safety, reliability, and durability. School buses carry the most precious cargo in the world – 25 million children twice a day – making them the most trusted mode of student transportation. The company is the proven leader in low- and zero-emission school buses with more than 25,000 propane, natural gas, and electric powered buses sold. Blue Bird is transforming the student transportation industry through cleaner energy solutions. For more information on Blue Bird’s complete product and service portfolio, visit www.blue-bird.com.
Job Summary
Reporting to the Plant Manager, the Director of Manufacturing Engineering will champion the technical vision of the production floor. This senior leader will direct a high-performing team of engineers and technicians to resolve manufacturing bottlenecks, manage capital expenditures (CapEx), and enforce rigorous safety standards. By partnering with cross-functional stakeholders, you will drive continuous improvement, optimize process capabilities, and implement scalable manufacturing solutions to ensure on-time delivery and top-tier customer satisfaction.
ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Team Leadership & Strategy
Direct and develop a team of Manufacturing Engineers and Technicians, setting clear performance expectations, individual goals, and conducting annual appraisals.
Allocate engineering resources to ensure the timely delivery of tooling, labor standards, routers, and process instructions for all engineering changes.
Oversee the entire capital spending plan, actively participating in budgeting, recommending improvements, and drafting justification data for capital equipment procurement.
Process Optimization & Continuous Improvement
Architect the manufacturing strategy for new product launches, ensuring seamless transitions from prototype to pilot to full-scale production.
Eliminate operator decision points and mitigate risks by analyzing line complexity drivers and deploying effective poka-yoke (error-proofing) solutions.
Spearhead lean manufacturing initiatives, production support, and line material presentation to drive cost reductions and process improvements.
Quality, Design & Compliance
Partner with Design Engineering to resolve chronic Design for Manufacturing (DFM) issues and implement corrective actions.
Perform rigorous evaluations of projects to ensure top-tier performance, safety, and reliability.
Review engineering analyses including PFMEA, DVP&R, and 8D root cause analysis to continuously improve product designs.
Maintain strict compliance with ISO 9000 standards, producing comprehensive and customer-ready documentation.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES:
Process Optimization: Expert in line balancing, process development, and eliminating bottlenecks to increase throughput.
CapEx Management: Proficient in capital expenditure oversight, financial planning, and construction management.
Tooling Integration: Skilled in the transition, calibration, and maintenance of error-proofing torque tooling.
Financial Planning: Adept at developing project budgets, cost analyses, and estimating production labor and equipment costs.
Project Management: Highly proficient in managing multiple, complex projects simultaneously from inception to completion.
Technical Software: Advanced user of MS Office Suite, with experience in MS Project.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Proven ability to bridge the gap between departments, fostering teamwork and achieving shared objectives at all levels of the organization.
Strategic Problem Solving: Methodical, balanced, and dynamic approach to resolving operational challenges.
People Management & Conflict Resolution: Empathetic leadership style focused on motivation, assertiveness, and maintaining high team morale.
Communication & Organization: Strong written and oral communicator, capable of translating complex ideas into clear, actionable presentations.
Professional Ethics: Committed to a strong work ethic, professional conduct, and the highest standards of integrity.
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE
:
Bachelor's in Engineering required
10+ years of manufacturing engineering experience required
5+ years of relevant professional leadership experience
All candidates must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility at the time of hire.
Preferred Education And Experience
7+ years of relevant professional leadership experience, preferred
Experience in Production Supervision required
Knowledge of World Class Manufacturing (WCM) principles preferred
PMP Certification and recognized process improvement training (Lean, Six Sigma), preferred
WE VALUE
Ability to anticipate and understand customer needs and provide guidance
Excellent interpersonal and customer relationship skills to handle difficult and sensitive matters.
Strong project management skills. Exposure to difficult or complex projects a plus.
Ability to influence stakeholders
Effective communication and ability to communicate complex details in a clear manner.
Flexible workspaces and work hours that help you unleash the best you.
Working in a collaborative team and balancing the needs of individual stakeholders while delivering corporate objectives.
INCLUDES
Continued Professional Development
Benefits including medical, dental and vision insurance, 14 paid holidays, vacation time and 401k matching
WORK CONDITIONS
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Office environment and production environment
Must work in a manufacturing environment with exposure to heat, cold and noise
Fast-paced production area with moving objects and sheet metal
Occasional periods of standing or sitting for extended periods of time
You must wear appropriate PPE when and where required
Frequent weeks working 40+ hours
Frequent communication with people throughout the day
The specific statements shown in each section of this description are not intended to be all-inclusive. They represent typical elements and criteria necessary to successfully perform the job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions
Blue Bird® is an equal opportunity employer and makes employment decisions on the basis of merit. We strive to have the best available talent in every job based on the Knowledge, Skills and Abilities each person brings. Blue Bird is committed to compliance with all applicable laws providing equal employment opportunities. This commitment applies to all persons involved in Company operations and prohibits unlawful discrimination in all forms.
All candidates must be a U.S. citizen or permanent resident. Candidates must be authorized to work in the United States and will be required to provide proof of employment eligibility at the time of hire.
