evidence.text:
Head of Production
No longer accepting applications
Abstract Bio
San Francisco, CA
How to apply
Apply through the form below. It takes about 10 minutes. Along with your CV, it asks for:
a short message on why Abstract, why now and why you
one example of how you use AI at work
We read every application ourselves and reply within a week.
You will only be considered if you apply through the link below: https://abstractbio.notion.site/abstract-bio-careers
TLDR
We are building the biological inputs factory that will unlock AI for biology, starting from DNA, the first building block of every biomolecule. Demand for our first DNA product outran our capacity within months of launch, and we are now scaling 10x. As our Head of Production, you will own the factory: every order from the moment it lands to the moment it ships, and the people, processes and numbers that make that happen. You will relaunch production on a 10x larger platform, keep our quality and turnaround promises on every order, and drive our cost per base-pair down every quarter. The best candidate has run a production operation that ships biology to customers, still steps onto the floor when a run is in trouble, is AI-native, and treats every missed ship date as a root cause to find. Your role will evolve with time; you should be excited by that and step up when needed. THIS IS NOT A 9 TO 5.
Story and mission
The Bessemer process made steel cheap and set off the Second Industrial Revolution. AI is now doing the same to biological design, and cloud labs and robots are doing it to testing. That pushes the bottleneck to the build step: the physical inputs. Every protein and every RNA starts as DNA, and DNA is still expensive. With current suppliers, the DNA to test one therapeutic antibody design costs around $100 per data point; a good antibody needs thousands of them, and a good antibody model needs millions. Abstract Bio is building the factory for those inputs, starting from DNA, the first building block.
We brought a DNA product, 4-10x cheaper than incumbents, to market within 6 months of founding the company. With a team of three and word of mouth alone, demand quickly outran our capacity, so we are now building for true scale. This means a 10x larger production platform, adding long and plasmid DNA, and starting the first R&D on RNA and proteins.
Building a 10x factory is half the problem. The other half is running it every day: thousands of orders, each on time and each correct, without quality slipping as volume climbs. That is the job of the Head of Production. Our North Star is to be the biological inputs factory that gives scientists any biomolecule, on demand: the missing part of the stack that will unlock AI for biology.
Role description
We are turning DNA into a commodity, and a commodity wins on cost and reliability. For a customer, reliability means one thing: the right sequence, at the promised quality, on the promised date, every time. The Head of Production owns that promise.
You sit at the centre of the factory. Our Head of R&D decides what the factory will make next year; our Head of Automation decides how it gets made at scale; our Lab Manager keeps the lab stocked, calibrated and safe; you run the factory today. You receive methods from R&D and lines from Automation, and you are accountable for what they deliver in production: throughput, yield, first-pass success, turnaround and cost per order. When something goes wrong, you find out why and make sure it does not happen twice. When a shift is short or a batch is at risk, you are on the floor.
You are AI-native. Our factory is built so that software can read it and AI agents can act in it. Every order, plate, run and QC result lands in a structured record, and you run production on those records, not on whiteboards and memory. You use AI every day to plan capacity, triage failed orders, flag difficult sequences before they reach the line and write the reports nobody wants to write, and you build or commission the tools that do it. You report to the founders, and as we scale you will hire and lead the production team.
This is a company-defining role. We will give you the autonomy to run the factory the way you believe it should run, a budget for the people and systems to do it, and the room to grow into the operations leader of a multi-site biological inputs factory.
What you will do
Relaunch production at 10x.
Own the ramp plan, capacity model, staffing and go-live criteria.
Own the order-to-ship loop.
Every order has a status, an owner and a promised date, and you know which are at risk before the customer does.
Own the numbers.
Publish throughput, yield, first-pass success, turnaround and cost per base-pair weekly, and improve them every month.
Control the process.
Run on SOPs, QC gates and SPC; every failure gets a root cause, and the fix stays fixed.
Gatekeep new methods.
Nothing from R&D or Automation enters production without your sign-off.
Build the AI-native factory.
Run on structured data, with tools for capacity planning, failed-order triage and flagging hard sequences at intake.
Hire and lead the production team.
Build a team of shift leads, operators and QC specialists who are productive in their first week.
Be the customer's voice in the factory.
Handle escalations with data and turn every complaint into a process change.
What you will need to succeed
You have run production that ships.
You have 5+ years making biological products, 2+ of them leading the operation.
You understand the biology.
When a batch fails, you can tell a chemistry problem from a process or operator problem.
You think in throughput and cost per unit.
Capacity models, bottleneck analysis and process control are home turf.
You are AI-native.
You use AI daily and are comfortable with a LIMS, a dashboard and a query.
You lead from the floor.
You have run multi-shift teams and can step into a shift without slowing it down.
You are obsessively reliable.
A late order is an incident.
You move fast and stay calm.
You run the simple version this week, stay clear when a batch fails the night before it ships, and write things down.
Nice-to-haves
You have scaled a factory.
You have taken a production line from pilot to 10x volume, or brought up a new facility or second site, and you know what breaks on the way.
You have lived in a high-throughput service lab.
Gene synthesis, oligo, sequencing or CRO operations where every batch is a customer order with a due date, and you know what a good weekly on-time rate looks like.
You have run automated lines.
You have managed production built on liquid handlers, workcells and schedulers, and you know how to run humans and robots side by side without either waiting on the other.
You have shipped product under a quality system.
Experience in an ISO 9001, ISO 13485 or similar certified production environment, including batch records, CAPA, customer audits and supplier qualification.
You speak operations.
Lean, Six Sigma, SPC, an MES or ERP: you have used the toolkit and you know which parts of it a fast-moving startup actually needs.
You can multiply yourself.
You know shift leads, operators and QC specialists who would follow you to the right opportunity, especially if you are the one sounding the horn.
If you've read this far, start your motivation message with the word "Incident".

From our Bothell, WA headquarters, we design vehicles with the maneuverability, resilience, and adaptability needed for the next era of orbital operations. Joining Portal means stepping into a team that believes in bold engineering, fast iteration, and the power of small groups to change what’s possible. If you want your work to directly shape the future of in-space mobility, join us.
We are seeking a hands-on Senior Manager, Manufacturing Operations to build, lead, and scale production operations at our satellite manufacturing facility. This is a foundational leadership role responsible for establishing production processes, developing the production team, and ensuring safe, consistent, and efficient execution as the business transitions from early builds to sustained rate production.
Reporting to the VP of Manufacturing, you will own day-to-day production execution, workforce readiness, production planning, and operational performance within the production organization. You will lead production supervisors, team leads, technicians, and other personnel assigned to your organization, establishing the processes, systems, and accountability needed to meet production commitments.
You will work closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Facilities, Maintenance, and Environmental, Health & Safety (EHS) specialists to ensure manufacturing readiness and resolve operational challenges. Engineering will retain responsibility for product design and engineering authority, while Quality and EHS will provide functional expertise and governance within their respective areas.
This is a build-and-scale role, not a steady-state operations position. You will balance immediate production needs with the discipline required to establish repeatable processes, develop frontline leaders, and build a production organization capable of supporting increasing manufacturing rates.
Key Responsibilities
Production Leadership & Execution
Lead the production organization, including assigned supervisors, team leads, technicians, and production coordinators.

Ensure production personnel have approved work instructions, required training, and appropriate tools and equipment before performing assigned tasks.

Workforce Development & Team Performance

Recruit, onboard, coach, and develop production personnel and frontline leaders as the organization scales.

Establish processes to verify employee competency and readiness for assigned manufacturing tasks.
Develop supervisors and team leads through coaching, performance management, and leadership development.
Foster a culture of safety, quality, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement on the factory floor.
Safety, Quality & Standardized Work

Ensure production personnel follow applicable safety procedures, including requirements for lockout/tagout, personal protective equipment, chemical handling, and emergency response.

Identify bottlenecks, reduce unnecessary work-in-process, improve cycle time, and increase production capacity.

Drive corrective and preventive actions based on performance trends, production issues, audit findings, and employee feedback.

evidence.text:
Director of Quality
No longer accepting applications
Confidential
Washington DC-Baltimore Area
$180,000.00/yr - $220,000.00/yr
The Director of Quality is accountable for establishing, maintaining, and continually improving the company’s Quality Management System (QMS) and for ensuring products, processes, and suppliers consistently meet customer, contractual, regulatory, and internal requirements.
This operational leader will build a proactive quality culture that prevents defects, reduces cost of poor quality, improves on-time delivery, and protects customer confidence.
This role leads AS9100/ISO 9001 compliance and, where applicable, FAA, DoD, ITAR/EAR, customer flow-down, special-process, configuration-management, and source-inspection requirements. AS9100 leadership expectations include integrating the QMS into core business processes, applying risk-based thinking, and reporting QMS performance to leadership.
Travel requirement: Up to 15-25%, including supplier and customer visits as needed.
U.S. Citizenship is required, as only U.S. Citizens are authorized to access information under this program/ contract.
Core Responsibilities
Quality Strategy and Leadership
Develop and execute a quality strategy aligned with the company’s growth plan, operational objectives, customer commitments, and risk profile.
Establish annual quality objectives, operating plans, staffing models, capital needs, and improvement roadmaps.
Serve as the senior authority for product quality, QMS effectiveness, release readiness, audit response, and regulatory/customer quality matters.
Build a culture in which quality is owned by every function—not merely inspected at the end of production.
Partner with the COO, Engineering, Operations, Supply Chain, and Program Management to integrate quality into SIOP, program reviews, production readiness, make/buy decisions, supplier selection, and new-product introduction.
Lead management-review processes and provide clear executive reporting on quality performance, key risks, corrective actions, and resource needs.
Quality Management System and Compliance
Own the design, maintenance, certification, and continual improvement of the QMS, including policies, procedures, work instructions, records, document control, training, and internal-audit processes.
Maintain AS9100D and/or ISO 9001 certification, as applicable; prepare the organization for registrar, customer, government, and regulatory audits.
Ensure controlled processes for nonconformance, corrective action, preventive action, root-cause analysis, change control, risk management, calibration, inspection, traceability, and record retention.
Ensure quality requirements are incorporated into operating procedures, engineering processes, work instructions, purchasing documents, and supplier flow-downs.
Oversee compliance with customer, contractual, statutory, and regulatory requirements, including export-controlled information where applicable.
Product and Process Quality
Lead quality planning from proposal through design, prototype, qualification, production launch, sustainment, and field support.
Establish robust quality gates for contract review, design transfer, first article inspection, production readiness, in-process inspection, final acceptance, and shipment release.
Ensure effective use of APQP-like planning, PFMEA, control plans, first article inspection (FAI), process validation, capability studies, and risk-based inspection plans as appropriate.
Drive containment, root-cause analysis, and permanent corrective actions for internal defects, escapes, returns, customer complaints, and field failures.
Ensure material, product, and configuration traceability requirements are met throughout the value stream.
Approve or oversee disposition of nonconforming material, including material review board (MRB) processes, use-as-is/rework decisions, and escalation of significant quality risk.
Supplier Quality
Lead the supplier-quality program, including supplier qualification, risk segmentation, audits, scorecards, source inspection, receiving inspection strategy, and supplier development.
Establish quality flow-down requirements in purchase orders and supplier agreements.
Partner with Supply Chain to improve supplier delivery, incoming quality, responsiveness, and capacity reliability.
Lead supplier corrective action requests (SCARs), verification of corrective-action effectiveness, and escalation for chronically underperforming suppliers. A SCAR formally requires a supplier to investigate nonconformance, identify root cause, implement corrective action, and demonstrate resolution.
Support supplier selection and make/buy decisions with a clear assessment of technical, quality, compliance, and supply-continuity risk.
Audits and Customer Interface
Serve as the primary quality representative for customers, government representatives, registrars, and third-party auditors.
Lead preparation for and response to customer audits, surveillance audits, source inspections, quality reviews, and corrective-action requests.
Communicate material quality issues promptly, factually, and constructively with customers and internal executives.
Ensure audit findings, customer complaints, and corrective actions are closed on time and validated for effectiveness.
Support major proposals, customer reviews, production readiness reviews, and new program launches by demonstrating QMS maturity and execution readiness.
Continuous Improvement and Analytics
Establish a practical quality operating system using KPIs, daily/weekly management routines, layered process audits, quality alerts, escalation paths, and recurring problem-solving reviews.
Deploy Lean, Six Sigma, 8D, A3, 5 Whys, Ishikawa, DOE, statistical process control, and mistake-proofing methods at the appropriate level of rigor.
Reduce cost of poor quality through prevention, early detection, process capability improvement, and supplier-performance improvement.
Use data to identify systemic issues across product lines, sites, programs, processes, and suppliers.
Develop team capability through coaching, certification, cross-functional problem solving, and succession planning.
Qualifications
Required
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, quality, operations, manufacturing, or a related technical discipline; equivalent experience may be considered.
10+ years of progressive quality leadership experience in aerospace, defense, electronics, industrial manufacturing, or another highly regulated environment.
5+ years leading a quality organization with responsibility for QMS, quality engineering, inspection, supplier quality, and audit performance.
Demonstrated experience leading and maintaining AS9100, ISO 9001, or an equivalent regulated-industry QMS.
Working knowledge of design assurance, configuration management, document control, product traceability, first article inspection, MRB, calibration, inspection/test, and supplier-quality management.
Strong command of structured problem solving and corrective action, including 8D, 5 Whys, fishbone analysis, FMEA, CAPA, and verification of effectiveness.
Experience leading customers, registrar, government, or regulatory audits and closing audit findings.
Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional leaders and make sound risk-based decisions under schedule and delivery pressure.
Preferred
ASQ certifications such as Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Six Sigma Black Belt (CSSBB), or Certified Quality Auditor (CQA).
Experience with FAA Part 21 production approval, DCMA/customer source inspection, Nadcap, special processes, or mission-critical electronics.
Experience in a private-equity-backed, high-growth, turnaround, or acquisition-integration environment.
Master’s degree in engineering, operations, quality, or business administration.
Lean/Six Sigma Black Belt certification and demonstrated deployment of measurable improvement programs.
Experience with ERP, MES, QMS, PLM, statistical-analysis, and dashboard tools.
Leadership Profile
The successful candidate is:
A hands-on, visible leader who can move comfortably between the executive staff meeting, manufacturing floor, supplier audit, and customer quality review.
Commercially pragmatic while uncompromising on safety, product conformity, ethics, and regulatory compliance.
Skilled at shifting the organization from detection-based quality to prevention-based quality.
A disciplined operator who uses metrics, standard work, escalation paths, and accountability—not bureaucracy—to improve performance.
A clear communicator who can explain risk, technical detail, and corrective-action status to operators, engineers, customers, and executives.
Confident in exercising stop-work or stop-ship authority when necessary, while working collaboratively to restore compliant flow quickly.

Drive continuous improvement, standardization, and root-cause problem solving utilizing Lean / Six Sigma frameworks.

Partner with Business Development and Program Management to assess customer fit, risk profiles, and project feasibility.
Provide engineering assessments for quotation packages, including DFM/DFT analysis, tooling requirements, process routing, cycle times, and technical risk factors.
Guide Design-for-Manufacturability (DFM) and Design-for-Test (DFT) reviews to optimize yield, reliability, and assembly costs.
New Product Introduction (NPI) & Document Control:
Steer engineering participation across the complete NPI lifecycle from quoting through full-scale production ramp, ensuring seamless transition into manufacturing.
Oversee manufacturing process documentation, stencils, fixture design, machine programming, and work instructions for complex and quick-turn assemblies.
Oversee engineering component engineering, including regulatory declarations, obsolescence management, and product lifecycle health.
Ensure Document Control delivers rigorous, audit-ready, and revision-controlled documentation meeting internal, customer, and regulatory standards.
Operational & Floor Engineering Support:
Provide escalation leadership and troubleshooting support to Manufacturing, Quality, and Process Engineering teams on complex production disruptions.
Direct defect analysis reviews, 8D root-cause investigations, and corrective action implementations for recurring or critical line issues.
Lead validation planning, IQ/OQ/PQ execution, and engineering change order (ECO) management.
Ensure technical processes maintain strict alignment with ISO, aerospace, defense, and medical regulatory standards.
Qualifications & Experience Requirements
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related engineering discipline (or an equivalent combination of education and direct industry experience).
Industry Experience:
Minimum 10+ years of progressive engineering experience within the Electronics Manufacturing Services (EMS) / contract manufacturing industry.
At least 5+ years dedicated to leading New Product Introduction (NPI) and manufacturing process development.
Demonstrated track record leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams in a high-reliability SMT / PCBA environment.
Background in highly regulated sectors (e.g., Aerospace & Defense, Medical Devices, High-Reliability Industrial).
Technical & Process Expertise:
Deep technical command of SMT equipment and line processes: solder paste printing, SPI, high-speed pick-and-place, reflow profiling, AOI, automated X-ray (AXI), wave/selective solder, and rework.
Proven experience with DFM/DFT methodologies, tooling/stencil design, component defect analysis, and testing strategies (ICT, Flying Probe, Functional).
Working knowledge of IPC and J-STD quality standards (IPC-A-610 Class 1–3, J-STD-001); formal IPC certifications preferred.
Hands-on familiarity with PCB design and CAD/CAM software (Valor, Cadence, CAM350, AutoCAD, SolidWorks, or equivalent).
Continuous Improvement & Business Acumen:
Demonstrated success championing Lean / Six Sigma implementations and organizational change; Six Sigma Black Belt certification preferred.
Solid grasp of business finance, capital budgeting, margin preservation, and the financial impact of engineering decisions.
Communication & Leadership:
Exceptional executive presentation and interpersonal skills, capable of influencing senior client stakeholders, suppliers, and internal executive teams.
Outstanding analytical reasoning, complex problem solving, and decisiveness in fast-paced manufacturing settings.
Work Environment & Physical Guidelines
Modern, well-lit, climate-controlled manufacturing and engineering office environment.
Compliance with facility Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) standards, including ESD-safe apparel and safety footwear in designated production zones in accordance with OSHA and facility guidelines.

evidence.text:
Deputy Head of Production, Connected Warfare
Anduril Industries
Ashville, OH
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Site
Anduril, a leader in autonomous systems and weapons manufacturing, is building Arsenal-1, its first hyperscale manufacturing facility, just south of Columbus, Ohio in Pickaway County. Arsenal-1 is redefining the scale and speed that autonomous systems and weapons can be produced for the United States and its allies and partners. This is a monumental and essential step toward rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, strengthening America’s warfighting capabilities, and enhancing deterrence amid rising international threats.
About The Team
The Connected Warfare will set the standard for building the future at Arsenal-1
,
our state-of-the-art manufacturing facility in Ashville, OH. This team will have the opportunity to train under our world-class manufacturing team at Anduril HQ in Costa Mesa, CA for 3 months before bringing that standard of excellence back to Ohio.
About The Role
As the Connected Warfare Deputy Head of Production, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of defense manufacturing by directly influencing the production of Anduril’s Connected Warfare product line. You will own the short-to-mid-term strategic development and execution of manufacturing operations, driving products to full-rate production. This role requires a dynamic leader who can serve as both a strategic architect and a hands-on executor, leading cross-functional teams to meet aggressive timelines and deliver products of the highest quality for our customers. You will contribute significantly to Anduril's vision of becoming a next-generation aerospace and defense manufacturer.
What You'll Do
Production Ownership & Strategy: Own all production outcomes for the Connected Warfare product line, including ramp plans, headcount, and the standing up of new manufacturing lines. Develop and execute a long-term strategy to rapidly scale production volumes to full-rate production.
Leadership & Team Management: Serve as a strategic leader and tactical do-er, driving all people and resources across production to achieve outcomes. Lead cross-functional teams (including Production, Supply Chain, Quality, and Manufacturing Engineering) through strong leadership, advocacy, and a consistent on-site presence, holding them accountable to meeting demands, deadlines, and goals.
Operational Excellence: Drive processes and systems needed throughout the product development lifecycle to mature products to full-rate production. Establish and manage the team to key performance indicators (KPIs) for financial, quality, and on-time delivery to optimize manufacturing operations' impact on the business.
Quality & Compliance: Be accountable to AS9100D guidelines and drive a "quality-first" culture across all manufacturing operations.
Process & Technology Advancement: Advise on development and oversee the implementation of digital technologies, from PLM and ERP to our custom MES and QMS systems, that enable our production operations to efficiently scale while meeting customer requirements. Shape corporate tools and processes to support the unique needs of aerospace production.
Required Qualifications
8+ years of proven experience overseeing the production and test of complex electromechanical products.
Strong leadership experience managing large (100+ person) manufacturing teams and directing large cross-functional teams across planning, supply chain, manufacturing engineering, quality, and production to deliver products of the highest quality.
A strong background in quality assurance, with a track record of driving a "quality-first" culture in a production environment and accountability to standards like AS9100D.
Past success operating in both low-rate prototype and high-rate manufacturing environments, with a proven ability to scale production.
High ownership and the ability to effectively manage multiple large projects and priorities in parallel, at a rapid pace, and report out on progress regularly.
Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.
Ability to work onsite five days a week at our Asheville, OH campus (Arsenal 1).
Preferred Qualifications
Success scaling production operations in a high-complexity manufacturing environment.
Deep experience with the niche supply chains for aerospace and robotics.
Demonstrated experience implementing and leveraging digital manufacturing technologies (PLM, ERP, MES, QMS) to drive efficiency and scale.
US Salary Range
$190,000—$252,000 USD
Benefits
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.
Data Privacy
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

evidence.text:
Director of Manufacturing Engineering, EW
Anduril Industries
Irvine, CA
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
Anduril's Electromagnetic Warfare (EW) Manufacturing team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare. This responsibility spans the full manufacturing value chain — from Design for Manufacturability through full-rate production — including tool design and selection, process creation and optimization, vendor sourcing, quality planning, system integration, and work documentation for the hardware our engineers own.
About The Job
As the Director of Manufacturing Engineering for EW, you will provide strategic oversight and tactical management of manufacturing engineering to support both the development of new products and the scaling of high-volume production. You are charged with ensuring rigorous manufacturing processes are in place, resulting in the consistent delivery of superior quality defense hardware to our customers. Your leadership will guarantee the fulfillment of manufacturing capacity commitments while driving advancements in tools, automation, and methodologies to improve design, analysis, and execution. This role demands an innovative and adaptable leader who thrives in a fast-paced, resource-constrained environment solving complex manufacturing challenges for electromechanical defense systems.
What You'll Do
Build & Lead the Manufacturing Engineering Team: Recruit, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of manufacturing engineers with deep product knowledge in mechanical, electrical, system integration, and environmental testing. Foster a culture of innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement across the organization.
Drive Manufacturing Strategy & Technology: Develop and implement a long-term manufacturing engineering strategy aligned with Anduril EW's growth objectives. Drive adoption of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance efficiency and scalability across development and high-volume production.
Lead New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with Design Engineering teams in early to late phases of the development process to ensure seamless transition of new products from design to production. Champion Design for Manufacturability (DfM), Design for Assembly (DfA), and broader DFx principles to de-risk production scaling.
Scale Production Capability: Evaluate, plan, and prioritize supply chain, production, and test optimizations to ensure the value stream can reliably meet production output goals. Develop process flows that break down large, complex electromechanical assemblies into logical subassemblies and sub-processes. Build business cases for vertical integration or supplier diversification where strategic partnerships will accelerate scalability.
Drive Continuous Improvement & Quality: Lead initiatives to improve yield, reduce cycle time, and lower cost across the manufacturing value chain. Drive operational excellence through Kaizen events, RCCA burndowns, component and supplier rationalization, and process standardization. Be a strong partner with Product Quality Engineering to tackle key issues both internally and externally to EW Production.
Own the Manufacturing Value Chain: Take holistic ownership of the manufacturing value chain for EW products, including tool design and selection, vendor sourcing and interaction, quality planning, and work documentation. Contribute to end-customer hardware mechanical or electrical design, including interconnects, board fabrication, and inspection.
Resource & Budget Management: Manage budgets, staffing, and capital equipment planning for the manufacturing engineering organization. Forecast headcount and operational needs to support rapid scaling, including classified production environments.
Define Cross-Functional Workflows: Establish effective collaboration frameworks across Design Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and Production teams. Set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and drive rapid project execution.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field; Master's degree or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing engineering and operations, with at least 5 years in a leadership role managing manufacturing engineering teams.
Demonstrated experience owning manufacturing value chains for complex electromechanical hardware — defense, aerospace, or adjacent industries strongly preferred.
Strong background in make-vs-buy analysis, contract manufacturer management, and supplier development for precision hardware.
Experience managing NPI and scaling production in high-growth environments with condensed timelines.
Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver electromechanical hardware in a resource-constrained environment.
Demonstrated ability to bring up assembly operations for electromechanical assemblies, including PCBA, harness, and RF hardware.
Knowledge of automation, advanced manufacturing technologies, and digital manufacturing tools.
Proficient with ERP, CAD, PLM, and FRACAS software. Familiarity with quality systems (ISO 9001/AS9100) and MES systems.
Hands-on experience physically manufacturing hardware (assembly, soldering, machining, fabrication, etc.).
Excellent leadership, communication, and cross-functional collaboration skills.
Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
US Salary Range
$220,000—$292,000 USD
Benefits
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To Ensure Your Safety And Help You Navigate Your Job Search With Confidence, Please Keep The Following Critical Points In Mind
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

Director, Operational Excellence
Sunbelt Rentals, Inc.
Fort Mill, SC
Join Our Team!
Sunbelt Rentals strives to be the customer's first choice in the equipment rental industry. From pumps to scaffolding to general construction tools, we aim to be the only call needed to outfit a job site with the proper equipment. Not only do we offer a vast fleet that ranks among the best in the industry, we pair it all with a friendly and knowledgeable staff. Our employees are our greatest asset, and although we present a comprehensive equipment offering, our expertise and service are what truly distinguish us from the competition.
We pride ourselves on investing in our workforce and offer competitive benefits, as well as extensive on-the-job training for all eligible employees.
As a highly successful national company, we are constantly looking for talented individuals to support our growth. If you are interested in pursuing a rewarding career, we invite you to review our opportunities!
Job Description Summary
Position Objective:
Sunbelt Rentals is hiring a Director, Operational Excellence to lead our Operational Excellence function, driving operational performance, growth, and customer experience through the identification, piloting, and scaling of high-impact operational initiatives across our multi-site North American network. This is a builder's role: you and a small, senior team (Analysts and field-facing Managers) will scan the landscape across 1,400+ locations, get into branches and markets, design and run pilots hands-on, and package validated playbooks for enterprise-wide rollout. Success in this role requires equal parts strategic thinking, operational execution, and field credibility. You'll also be a key translator of new technology and new ways of working into operational reality the field can actually use — reporting directly to the VP, Operational Excellence and working daily with senior operating leadership.
You'll have a unique opportunity to influence how Sunbelt operates at scale — helping shape the future of field operations, service delivery, logistics, and technology adoption across more than 1,400 locations, while partnering directly with senior leadership on some of the company's most important strategic priorities.
Position Responsibilities:
Partner with operations leadership across the organization to surface and prioritize the biggest operational opportunities — logistics performance, service and maintenance performance, process gaps and other high impact opportunities.
Drive measurable improvements in productivity, asset utilization, customer experience, and profitability through operational initiatives and operating model enhancements.
Personally lead the scoping, design, and in-market piloting of top initiatives, iterating rapidly on field feedback before scaling — this is hands-on work, not just oversight.
Partner closely with local and regional operations leadership to ensure solutions are practical, scalable, and grounded in real-world, on-the-ground realities.
Quantify operational and financial impact, developing clear, fact-based recommendations that support executive decision-making.
Act as an early, hands-on evaluator of new technology and platforms, shaping rollout and change management plans so new tools and processes get adoption from operations team.
Own the initiative pipeline end-to-end, from prioritization through handoff to enterprise execution teams, staying engaged as initiatives scale.
Lead, coach, and grow a small, high-caliber team, including managers who bring direct, hands-on operating experience into the group.
Requirements:
Education & Experience:
Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience, plus 10–15 years of progressive experience in operations, operational excellence, strategy, or project/portfolio management within a multi-site or geographically distributed business.
A demonstrated track record of turning financial/operational data into business cases that moved the needle on real performance metrics across multiple locations or markets.
Experience designing, piloting, and scaling operating model changes across a multi-site network — cost reduction, logistics/service redesign, shared services, or process re-engineering.
Comfort operating at both altitudes: building the analytical case for change and getting into the field to build the solution yourself.
Preferred:
Background in equipment rental, industrial distribution, implementation / turn-around consulting, logistics, field service, construction services, or another multi-site, asset-intensive operating environment.
Experience leading large-scale operational transformations or business performance improvement programs across a distributed network of locations.
Leadership experience overseeing multiple locations, a district, or a region, with direct accountability for multi-site performance.
A career path that combines early strategic or advisory experience with a subsequent move into direct operating or field leadership roles.
Experience driving adoption of new technology, digital tools, and operational platforms across multiple sites.
Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement methodology experience is a plus.
Physical Demands:
Must be able to bend, squat, crouch and/or reach and lift up to 25 pounds or more, as required by the job. Some Sunbelt jobs may require driving for long periods of time, loading and unloading heavy equipment, performing work in extreme weather conditions including rain, wind, or excessive temperatures and/or night and weekend work. All duties must be performed according to Sunbelt’s safety policies and guidelines. Reasonable accommodations may be made to comply with ADA/ADAAA.

Sunbelt Rentals is an Equal Opportunity Employer — Minority/Female/Disabled/Veteran and any other protected ground

Starting rate of pay may vary based on factors including, but not limited to, position offered, location, education, training, and/or experience. Please visit https://www.sunbeltrentals.com/careers/ for more information on our benefits and to join our Talent Network.

At Sunbelt Rentals our leaders including District Managers and above enjoy the freedom of Flex Time. Job Summary
General Atomics Aeronautical Systems, Inc. (GA-ASI), an affiliate of General Atomics, is a world leader in proven, reliable remotely piloted aircraft and tactical reconnaissance radars, as well as advanced high-resolution surveillance systems.
We have an exciting opportunity for a Program Director!
This position is responsible for the planning, managing and technical performance of significant program to support new production. The Program Director is responsible for leading major production programs from start to finish, overseeing multiple developing products or components that are important to the company’s future growth and strategic objectives. They coordinate the use of new technologies and methods to meet program requirements and typically manage through subordinate managers rather than directly supervising individual staff. The role involves making high-impact decisions, where errors could result in substantial time and resource expenditures.

Leads all phases of major production programs from contract award and conceptualization through completion and aircraft delivery, ensuring cost, schedule, quality, business, and financial objectives are achieved.
Develops and maintains overall program strategy, roadmap, and execution plans aligned with customer requirements and company objectives, including new program plans and delivery methods that may span multiple products and customers.
Manages the establishment of design concepts, criteria, and engineering efforts for research, development, testing, integration, and production.
Works with cross‑functional teams and Supply Chain to ensure material availability, supplier quality, and on‑time delivery, while monitoring and mitigating supply chain risks.
Serves as the primary customer and senior management contact for all program matters, leading formal program reviews and ensuring timely, accurate program reporting.
Directs and influences the preparation of proposals, business plans, work statements, operating budgets, and contract terms and conditions, including acquisitions, negotiations, and modifications.

Ensures technical leadership and excellence by attracting, developing, and retaining key management, professional, and technical talent.
Contributes to long‑term Group and Company objectives by leading the development and expansion of new business opportunities, partnerships, and programs.

Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance, if required by program.

Typically requires a bachelor’s, master’s, or PhD in engineering, science, or a related technical field, as well as fifteen or more years of progressively complex program administration experience, with at least nine of those years managing programs; may substitute equivalent experience in lieu of education.

Justified by the need for single‑point leadership and accountability over all production execution activities, ensuring alignment between Program Management, Operations, Supply Chain, Quality, and Engineering.

Master’s degree in engineering.
Formal program management certification (e.g., PMP or equivalent) or completion of an internal PM development program.
Direct experience in unmanned systems, ISR payloads, or similar GA product lines.
Experience transitioning programs from development/qualification into full‑rate production.
Experience managing multi‑year, multi‑site, or international production programs.

The incumbent provides leadership, direction, planning, and control across manufacturing, materials/purchasing, production scheduling, and shipping to ensure products are produced safely, meet customer and regulatory requirements, and are delivered complete and on time. This role drives continuous improvement and operational excellence, develops and coaches leaders, and manages budgets and cost controls to optimize productivity, quality performance, and overall plant profitability.
Essential Functions
Ensure that all administrative, supervisory and hourly positions are staffed with the best qualified personnel available.
Drive team engagement through regular coaching, feedback and involvement in day-to-day operations.
Foster an environment of open communication.
Maintain required professional competencies; assess staffing levels and capability; and develop direct reports through training and development opportunities.

Safety: OSHA recordable incident rate (TRIR) and VSI leading indicators
Quality: CoPQ: Internal (scrap and rework) and External (customer defects/complaints)

The Director of Manufacturing is responsible for production, delivery and quality of highly engineered aerospace fasteners, utilizing machining, forging, thermal treatment and coating operations. In addition to these responsibilities, the Director of Manufacturing will also be responsible for safety, environmental results, efficiencies and effectiveness of the assigned production unit and/or groups. The individual will act as a senior management representative in the assigned production units and ensure that company policies and guidelines are accurately interpreted and implemented. Develops and implements optimal, cost-effective manufacturing processes and methods in accordance with product specifications and quality standards. Minimize process variation and maximize efficiency of both existing and new product manufacturing process.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
Other duties may be assigned. Reasonable accommodation for disabilities may be made for one or more of the following:

Analytical – Ability to analyze and understand complex information, product specification, and critical technical information. Able to resolve complex problems to resolution. Able to scrutinize information providing direction and guidance on risks, strategy, planning, and actions
Technical Skills – Technical knowledge including but not limited, to specification interpretation, product application, product quality, quality systems, International Standards, safety and environmental management, customer relationship management, project management, Lean concepts, Six-Sigma, and people development and leadership.
Oral Communication - Speaks clearly and persuasively in positive or negative situations; listens intently to others and seeks clarification; Provides clear and pleasant responses to inquiries regardless of the situation; Presents complex concepts in a simple manner to achieve understanding at all levels of the organization. Demonstrates group presentation skills working in a global environment; actively participates in meetings providing clear information.
Written Communication – Writes documents clearly and accurately. Transfers production data into meaningful written documents that can be understood by all levels of the organization. Writes comprehensive well-developed policies and work instructions. Writes clear actions and audit reports.
Teamwork - As management Team Member must lead by example, adhere and apply all company and legal regulations. Balances team and individual responsibilities; Exhibits objectivity and openness to others' views; Gives and welcomes feedback; Contributes to building a positive team spirit; Places success of team above own interests; Able to build morale and group commitments to goals and objectives; Supports everyone's efforts to succeed; Follows the company guiding principles and values; Recognizes accomplishments of team members.
Business Acumen - Understands business implications of decisions; Displays orientation to profitability; Demonstrates knowledge of market and competition; Aligns actions and department activities and action plans to mission, vision and strategic goals.
Cost Consciousness - Works within approved budget; Develops and implements cost saving measures; Contributes to profits and revenue; Conserves organizational resources.
Adaptability - Adapts to changes in the work environment; Manages competing demands; Changes approach or method to best fit the situation; Able to deal with frequent change, delays, or unexpected events.
Planning/Organizing - Prioritizes and plans work activities of self and others; Uses time efficiently; Plans for resources in a creative way only adding cost as absolutely necessary; Sets goals and objectives; Organizes or schedules other people and their tasks; Develops realistic action plans.
Professionalism - Approaches others in a tactful manner; Reacts well under pressure; Treats others with respect and consideration regardless of their status or position; Accepts responsibility for own actions; Follows through on commitments.

Directly and/or indirectly supervises Supervisors/Managers, and other team members assigned to the production units and production groups; Responsible for the overall direction, coordination, and evaluation of the assigned production units. Carries out supervisory responsibilities in accordance with the HSE responsibility, organization's policies and applicable laws; Responsibilities include but are not limited to interviewing, hiring, and training employees; planning, assigning, and directing work; appraising performance; rewarding and disciplining employees; addressing complaints and resolving problems.
ESSENTIAL JOB REQUIREMENTS, SKILLS AND ABILITIES
Education and/or Experience

Minimum of 5 years of management experience in the Aerospace Industry or Manufacturing environment preferred.

Ability to define problems, collect data, establish facts and draw valid conclusions. Ability to interpret an extensive variety of technical instructions in mathematical or diagram form and deal with several abstract concrete variables.
Computer Skills

Certificates, licenses, registrations

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit for extended periods of time, and to speak or listen. Safety and Environmental
The responsibilities of the position include compliance with company and governmental safety, environmental and hazardous materials regulations and procedures. Employees will be required to wear personal safety equipment such as safety glasses, hearing protection, or proper footwear PPE in specified areas.
Fully responsible for implementing safety and environmental rules within area of responsibility. Must uphold all safety standards and have in-depth knowledge of safety. Must be a coach and model safety excellence by wearing prescribed PPE and ensuring employees under his span of control are adhering to all safety rules. Has ultimate responsibility and authority to stop production if any hazard is present that may affect the safety of the employees in the shift.

evidence.text:
Associate Manager, Production Control, Semi (Night Shift)
Tesla
Sparks, NV
What To Expect
As an Associate Materials Manager for Production Control, you will be playing a critical role in ensuring the materials team is able to support the production goals of the Semi Factory. You will be asked to work cross-functionally, interfacing with engineering, production, and planning to ensure production goals are being met.
What You'll Do
Tesla people leaders are responsible for a variety of Environmental Health and Safety (EHS) assurance functions, including ensuring their teams’ safety training is current, documenting EHS incidents, proactively correcting workplace hazards in the areas, and empowering others to continuously improve operations
Lead and manage people, projects and resources to optimize production for on-time delivery. Coordinate material input to ensure on time delivery and output schedules, lead in the attainment of increased production efficiency and cycle time reduction and manage the flow of material through the supply base to support on-time delivery performance
Ensure timely and accurate material movements through all inventory areas (receiving, stockroom, floor, and shipping) at the lowest total possible cost while maintaining high inventory accuracy
Provide business analysis and process/system development to optimize transactions and provide required information to the operation in a timely manner to optimize materials management performance, and drive the development and implementation of internal systems and software
Support all planning and production scheduling; inventory control; warehouse operations; logistics integration; production planners and material planners (buyers) for Tesla’s manufacturing plant to ensure minimization of excess/obsolete inventory and increase annual turns and establish and maintain appropriate inventory levels for all products
Support interaction with internal customers and suppliers to obtain feedback, and ensure collaboration between Tesla, other operations, suppliers, and customers result in the development and deployment of supply chain solutions that improve quality, performance and service levels. Provide feedback on suppliers’ performance on overall cost, delivery, and quality
Monitor and drive down overall cost of materials including freight expenses, administration expenses, and cost of materials management
What You'll Bring
Ideal candidate will have 5-7 years of experience working in a manufacturing environment
Expertise in material distribution through the manufacturing process by orchestrating the efficiency of moving material from the warehouse through manufacturing operations in an organized fashion
Proven examples of continuous improvement in efficiency, accuracy, and effectiveness of the materials function within high growth, fast paced, manufacturing environment
Proven success in managing department(s) responsible for some or all aspects of materials control functions
Demonstrated financial understanding of materials and supply chain performance
Strong communication and management skills combined with business analytics, process and system development and change management
, Tesla

Plant Manager
Best Block Company
Baton Rouge, LA
We are seeking a Plant Manager
to join our team!
This is an on-site role, and will not be remote or hybrid, at any time.*
What We Offer
Opportunity for Growth and Development
Health, Dental, and Vision plans
Retirement Benefits - 401k
Competitive Salary
Vacation
Paid Holidays
About The Role
As a Plant Manager with Best Block,
you are responsible for:
Ensure company safety programs are being followed and utilized to ensure the safety of our employees. Provide safety training and task specific guidelines for all employees. Complete monthly and yearly compliance audits and activities that drive continuous improvement throughout the business. Weekly & Monthly safety meetings.
Develop and maintain high plant standards of safety and work conditions, administer safety programs, and ensure compliance with all safety regulations.
Utilize our facilities, equipment, and personnel to achieve the highest level of product production while ensuring safety and quality standards are met at the lowest possible cost.
Continuous improvement in product quality that includes product testing to ensure our manufactured products meet all specifications and requirements.
Maintain equipment readiness, plant cleanliness and storage, and production line efficiency.
Maintaining an adequate inventory of raw materials, packaging materials, spare parts, and molds.
Utilize downtime tracking and productivity data to drive all maintenance activities, which include predictive, preventative, and corrective actions.
Effectively communicate organizational policies and procedures and provide daily direction to various staff functions, including production scheduling, administration, inventory management, order process, and transportation.
Provide leadership and direction to the Team, which includes selection, development, and evaluation of personnel in all positions. Ensure all machine operators receive training that improves their level of knowledge and proficiency of safe plant operations.
Possess a deep understanding of all manufacturing processes and production equipment.
Ensure all quality procedures are adhered to and documented in compliance with company policies.
Schedule production shifts and personnel so that production schedules and timelines are met, while being adaptable to any changes in business levels.
Requirements
Experience with Concrete Products Manufacturing is a plus!
Understanding of Programmable Logic Controlled (PLC) equipment.
Proficient in a variety of PC-based software applications.
Demonstrated history of working in a team-oriented environment with excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Positive “can do” attitude and ability to motivate team.
Self-starter. Able to work independently, plan, prioritize, coordinate, delegate, manage and complete work.
Able to analyze problem circumstances, solve problems, and give direction regarding problem resolution in an expeditious fashion.
Possesses effective time management skills. Able to “switch gears” between tasks without losing focus.
Submit resume and cover letter with salary requirements through this posting!

Lead and develop the Continuous Improvement organization while partnering with global, regional, and Cell & Gene Therapy leadership to align transformation efforts, share best practices, and maximize business results.

Demonstrated ability to operate as a senior leader and trusted partner to a General Manager or site head, including executive governance, operating reviews, decision support, and cross functional accountability.
Proven experience building or maturing a management system, daily management system, production system, or business operating system across multiple functions.

Track record delivering measurable business results through transformation, including quality, delivery, productivity, cost, inventory, compliance, cycle time, or client performance improvements.
Strong business acumen with the ability to connect operational performance to financial outcomes, client commitments, capacity, working capital, labor productivity, and site competitiveness.
Demonstrable leadership experience at Catalent (including but not limited to participation in Catalent-sponsored leadership programs such as NGGL, GOLD, LEAD Now, GM Excellence, and GROW) may be considered in place of external experience;

evidence.text:
Operations Readiness Director
the LEGO Group
Richmond, VA
Job Description
Are you ready to lead a groundbreaking factory start-up, driving innovation by integrating automated systems and sophisticated digital technologies at LEGO's newest site?
Lead the charge in revolutionizing manufacturing within LEGO's Greenfield LVA factory, where you'll drive groundbreaking automation, champion global standards, and ensure flawless operations from Day 1.
Core Responsibilities
Lead the end-to-end Start-Up journey for the LVA Greenfield factory, ensuring robust and empowered operations.
Translate global program achievements into local readiness actions, creating a unified delivery roadmap.
Lead the Global Start-Up Management Framework, ensuring operational ownership beyond technical sign-off.
Drive risk mitigation continuously, activating assessments and ensuring visibility throughout execution.
Build organizational capability and readiness, including training plans and operational management systems.
Establish performance acceleration routines to ensure fast, stable ramp-up of operations.
Integrate automation and digital tools into operations, ensuring maturity and full lifecycle readiness.
Ensure detailed DQP compliance, facilitating decision-making across R&D, suppliers, and partners.
Play Your Part in Our Team Succeeding
The Greenfield Automation Program is redefining the LEGO Group’s future for automated Packing, Molding, and Logistics, setting standards for next-generation factories. As the first site for these innovations, LVA represents a significant achievement. Your leadership will ensure the site's readiness for a stable ramp-up, setting benchmarks for future deployments.
Do You Have What It Takes?
Proven experience leading large-scale industrial or automation start-ups, ideally greenfield or new factory environments.
Significant expertise in start-up of production lines, technology ramp-up, and operational readiness.
Strong end-to-end operations and value chain understanding across manufacturing, quality, engineering, and supply chain.
Experience embedding readiness frameworks such as CQV, DQP, FMEA, PDCA, and associated risk/quality tools.
Demonstrated ability to lead through complexity, ambiguity, and fast-paced change.
Exceptional leadership presence with experience working and influencing global and local partners
Strong capability-building leadership competency models, training plans, uplifting capability, and readiness validation.
Advanced education in engineering, manufacturing, operations, or similar, or equivalent experience, is highly desired
Nice To Have
Experience supporting multi-site or multi-technology ramp-ups.
Familiarity with Lean, DfM, continuous improvement, or structured problem-solving frameworks.
Understanding of digital manufacturing (MES, SCADA, data analytics, traceability, automation platforms).
A global mentality with a passion for building diverse, high-performing teams.
Energy, resilience, and growth-mindset orientation — adopting challenge as opportunity.
A team-oriented, fun, and humble approach that reflects LEGO values shared success, curiosity, creativity, and positivity.
Additional
Long-term, the selected candidate must be willing to relocate to other sites, globally, to support future LEGO growth
Relocation will be provided
Some international travel will be required

The salary for this position has a range of $158,376.00 - $237,564.00 based on anticipated responsibilities, market benchmarks, and organizational constraints. Here are some of what to expect
Family
Care
Leave –
We offer enhanced paid leave options for those important times.

All colleagues are covered by our life and disability insurance which provides protection and peace of mind.

– We do our best work to succeed together. When goals are reached and if eligible, you'll be rewarded through our bonus scheme

We support our employees in being there for the moments that matter in life and celebrate families of all kinds, the loved ones that make us who we are. Being part of the LEGO Group also means taking part in our annual Play Day, playing a part in building a sustainable future and continuing our mission to “inspire and develop the builders of tomorrow.”
The LEGO Group is fully committed to Children’s Rights and Child Wellbeing across the globe. Candidates offered positions with high engagement with children are required to take part in Child Safeguarding Background Screening, as a condition of the offer.
Thank you for sharing our global commitment to Children’s Rights.
We conduct drug screening as a part of our drug free workplace policy and in support of our commitment to the health and safety of our employees.

Then make it real.

evidence.text:
Director, Supply Chain and Manufacturing Operations (AI2556)
SiMa.ai
San Jose, CA
Description
Job Title: Director, Supply Chain and Manufacturing Operations
Job Location: San Jose, CA (This position requires a full-time, on-site presence in our San Jose, CA office)
Job ID:
AI2556
Job Description
SiMa.ai is seeking a Director, Supply Chain & Manufacturing Operations
to own end-to-end hardware supply, from demand and supply planning and sourcing through all EMS/ODM manufacturing engagement, fulfillment, and sustaining operations, and to build and lead the team. This role will sit in Operations, partner closely with Engineering, HW, Product, and Finance, and will be accountable for delivering product on time, at target cost, and at the right quality while managing risk (LTs, NCNR, export, multi-year buys). Ideal for someone who has scaled an early-stage semiconductor / system company and isn’t afraid to work at both strategy and spreadsheet level.
Key Responsibilities
Areas of focus and key responsibilities (include, but not limited to):
What You’ll Do
Team Leadership
Build and lead the supply chain and manufacturing operations team (planning, sourcing, materials and inventory control); set KPIs (on-time delivery, inventory accuracy, turns, cost) and operating cadence.
Own Sales & Operations Planning / Demand-Supply Alignment
Consolidate customer, program, and internal build plans into a single view of demand.
Run monthly/quarterly supply reviews; drive scenario planning for upside, push-outs, and constrained parts.
Translate design/NPI ramps into material and capacity plans.
Sourcing, Material & Supplier Management
Manage end-to-end material lifecycle for MLSoC, SoM/board-level products, and accessories (heatsinks, cables, enclosures, eval kits).
Lead strategic sourcing and manage foundry/OSAT/packaging/PCB/PCBA/ODM/CM partners (RFQs, should-cost, dual-sourcing, supplier selection with Quality); negotiate pricing, terms, supply agreements, and NCNR protections.
Drive supplier scorecards, QBRs, and continuous improvement.
Contract Manufacturing / EMS & ODM Execution
Lead all engagement with EMS/ODM partners for product manufacturing: selection, manufacturing agreements, NPI transfer, capacity, and business reviews.
Own day-to-day interfaces with CMs/EMS/ODMs: MPS, WIP visibility, upside asks, expedites, DOAs/RMAs.
Own manufacturing work orders and all inventory transactions in the ERP system: receipts, transfers, component consumption, production completions, returns, and shipments; control all materials and inventory across CM and SiMa.ai locations.
Ensure accurate BOMs, AVL, and rev control flow from Engineering to manufacturing.
Drive yields, rework strategies, and RMA/FA loops back into design and test.
Risk, Readiness & Compliance
Build and maintain a rolling 6–18 month supply strategy to support customer evaluations, pilots, and production.
Proactively mitigate supply constraints with fabs, OSATs, and other suppliers (LTA parts, PMICs, memories, etc.).
Ensure export control, trade compliance, and country-of-origin/customer-specific requirements.
Cost & Operations Analytics
Track and report COGS, PPV, MOQ/MLQ exposure, inventory turns, and material liability.
Recommend multi-quarter buys, buffer strategies, and SERV/insurance-aligned NCNR structures to de-risk demand variability.
Partner with Finance and Sales on PO cadence, accruals, and revenue-enable dates; support month-end inventory reconciliation, with Accounting owning costing, valuation, and review of inventory adjustments.
ERP, Process & Tools
Own and scale SiMa.ai’s ERP/MRP platform (requirements, system selection, and implementation as the business grows), covering MRP, purchasing, inventory, work orders, and RMA, with integration to PLM and Finance; own process design, data migration, and user adoption.
Define and document scalable processes for NPI → volume → sustaining.
Drive ISO/QMS-oriented discipline in Operations, in partnership with Quality.
Travel up to 20%, including EMS/ODM sites in Asia
Required Background
Bachelor’s in Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, or related field with 10–15+ years in hardware supply chain / operations roles, ideally in semiconductor, edge/embedded, or high-mix electronics; 5+ years building and managing teams.
Proven experience running CM/EMS/ODM production and closing the loop between Engineering, Ops, and the factory.
Strong fluency in BOMs, AVL, ECOs, lead times, NCNR, LTAs, multi-quarter material strategies, and inventory control (work orders, cycle counts, consigned inventory at CMs).
Demonstrated success in demand/supply planning in a low-volume, high-mix, rapidly changing environment.
Comfortable negotiating with suppliers on price, terms, liability, and upside flexibility; experience leading RFQs, cost modeling, and supplier selection.
Hands-on experience implementing and scaling ERP/MRP systems at a hardware company (e.g., NetSuite, Fishbowl)
Data-first mindset; advanced Excel/Sheets; bonus for SQL/analytics.
Excellent cross-functional communication; able to translate operations constraints to Execs, Sales, and Engineering.
Excellent verbal and written communication and presentation skills
Fluent in English
Personal Attributes
Can-do attitude with a strong sense of ownership and accountability.
Strong team player who collaborates effectively across functions.
Curious, creative, and resourceful problem solver.
Execution- and results-oriented.
Self-driven and proactive.
Thinks strategically and takes a broader business perspective.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills.
Highly accountable with a strong commitment to delivering results.
The annual salary for this position ranges from $196,435 - $304,470. The actual annual salary offered will depend on several factors, including - among others - job-related skills, experience, technical expertise, qualifications, work location, and business needs. The annual salary range for this position is subject to change and may be adjusted in the future.
In addition to base salary, this role is also eligible for private company equity, and a comprehensive package of employee benefits. Please note that the salary ranges listed for U.S. roles reflect base salary only and do not include equity or other forms of compensation.
EEO Employer:
SiMa is an equal opportunity employer; all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, Veteran status, or any other protected classification.
