evidence.text:
Director, Operations
Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases
Santa Ana, CA
Company Overview
Nikkiso Clean Energy & Industrial Gases
is a leading provider of cryogenic pumps, heat exchangers, process systems, services, and solutions for the LNG and industrial gases industry. We are a subsidiary of Nikkiso Company Ltd, a leading industrial manufacturer headquartered in Tokyo, Japan, with over $1.5 B in annual revenue, 8000 + employees worldwide, and publicly traded on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
Nikkiso ACD
is an engineering and manufacturing company specializing in machinery designed to operate at cryogenic temperatures as low as – 420 degrees Fahrenheit, the boiling point of Liquid hydrogen. For over 50 years, Nikkiso ACD has specialized in centrifugal and reciprocating pumps as well as turbines for air separation. Nikkiso ACD has the most diversified product line in the industry covering nearly every application requiring pumps or turboexpanders.
Job Overview
The Director, Operations is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the manufacturing process. This role will develop and implement strategies that optimize the efficiency and effectiveness of the manufacturing operations to ensure the delivery of high-quality products on time and within budget.
Responsibilities
Develop and implement operational strategies that improve the efficiency, productivity, and profitability of the manufacturing operations for cryogenic pumps
Ensure that manufacturing operations comply with all relevant safety and environmental regulations
Develop and manage the annual manufacturing budget and monitor and control expenses to ensure that they remain within budgetary constraints
Identify and implement process improvements that increase efficiency, reduce costs, and enhance product quality while reducing product cost and increase margins
Manage and develop a large team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential
Collaborate with cross-functional teams, including engineering, design, and sales, to ensure that products meet customer requirements
Maintain positive relationships with key stakeholders, including suppliers, customers, and outsourced manufacturing partners
Develop and implement consistent processes and best practice strategies, policies, procedures, and goals
Work cross-functionally with product manager, product development, engineering and project management teams to ensure company goals are met and the necessary support to deliver on time is provided
Lead the effort in identification, recruiting, interviewing, onboarding, training, and ongoing engagement of high-performance team members
Monitor and analyze key performance indicators for manufacturing such as safety, quality, delivery, cost, cash and, people
Address escalated customer issues with speed and urgency, orchestrating resources across the company as appropriate
Identify and remove obstacles to delivering products consistently on time with the right quality
Qualifications
Bachelor's or Master’s degree in Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations Management, or related field or equivalent work experience
Minimum of 10 years of experience in a manufacturing leadership role, preferably in the rotating equipment industry
Extensive knowledge in manufacturing that are consistent with pump products, and how they are manufactured for the cryogenic industry preferred
Proven track record of developing and implementing operational strategies that improve efficiency, productivity, and profitability
Experience managing budgets and controlling expenses for operations
Strong understanding of regulatory requirements and environmental and safety regulations
Extensive knowledge in lean manufacturing
Strong knowledge of quality control systems and procedures
Hands-on experience working with global manufacturing operations
Broad knowledge of multi-functional and multi-site teams working in a global environment
Broad knowledge working with cryogenic industries
Hands-on experience with Problem Solving / Six Sigma
Project Planning / Project Management experience is preferred
Ability to communicate effectively with senior management
Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook
Progressive experience in roles leading manufacturing operations
High adaptability and flexibility, including the ability to manage deadline pressure, ambiguity, and change
Strong interpersonal skills and the ability to connect with and positively influence leadership at all levels of the organization
Self-motivated with extremely strong sense of urgency-act as a change agent in the organization
Demonstrates excellence in interpersonal skills - verbal and written communication, self-starter, positive make-it-happen attitude, team player
Able to travel domestically and internationally as needed
Supervisory Responsibility
Reports to Director, Operations and manages and develops a team of manufacturing professionals, providing coaching and mentoring to enable them to reach their full potential.
Work Environment
This job operates in both a professional office environment and a manufacturing/production environment. Commitment to safety is essential. This role routinely uses standard office equipment such as laptop computers, photocopiers, and smartphones.
Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to talk or hear. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision and ability to adjust focus. This would require the ability to lift files, open filing cabinets and bend or stand on a stool as necessary.
Other Duties
Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.
Salary Range:
$140,000 - $210,000 per year.
EEOC Statement
Nikkiso CE&IG is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against on the basis of disability. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

evidence.quote: 7 - 10+ years of experience in production, manufacturing, and/or supply chain (food/CPG or regulated environment strongly preferred)
evidence.text:
Vegan CPG Manufacturing Director
LeafSide
Mesa, AZ
Vegan CPG Manufacturing Director
Help Build a Healthier World
What if you could make a real difference, every day, for people’s health, animals, and the planet — working with a passionate vegan team?
You certainly can, at LeafSide! We are a growing company, offering innovative 100% whole-food plant-based (WFPB) vegan meals that deliver the highest standards in lifestyle medicine. Our mission is to make optimally healthy, whole vegan eating so easy and enjoyable that it becomes a societal norm.
Role Summary
LeafSide is seeking a CPG Manufacturing Director to scale our operations through clear leadership, project management, supply chain optimization, and production automation.
As our team’s hands-on Manufacturing Director, you’ll be responsible for overseeing and improving the team making LeafSide's life-changing magic meals. From supply-chain to production to fulfillment, you'll lead daily execution excellence, and key strategic improvements — while staying aligned with LeafSide’s vision and values. Being a great manager and coach is central to this role too. Other expectations include overseeing clear & effective (not excessive) documentation, and data-backed reasoning & problem-solving in general
It’ll all be happening in the fast-paced environment of a growing, mission-driven company — so we’re looking for someone who will see this role as not just another job, but key to their career and aligned with their life’s calling.
This role is on-site in Mesa, AZ.
What This Role Is
This role is:
Hands-on leadership and coaching of staff across supply chain, production & fulfillment, and special projects therein; some cross-functional projects may also arise.
Data-centric, with concise written analysis and reporting — including plans, briefs, tables/spreadsheets, predicting tradeoffs, doing due diligence, and sharing crisp updates to staff.
Where progress and results are delivered by disciplined follow-through, risk tracking & mitigation, root cause analysis, and steady systems improvements.
Expectations
Production & Operations Execution, Reliability, and Scalability
Keep production going to meet demand, with daily operational excellence across all Ops functions, and strategic improvements in productivity, training, and quality assurance.
Oversee SOPs, checklists, playbooks, and documentation.
Own & maintain effective dashboards and trackers that show progress and constraints.
Drive steady, measurable progress that lowers manual effort and costs while maintaining or raising quality.
Strengthen supply chain forecasting, ordering cadence, and risk visibility.
Coach and develop emerging leaders to proactively problem-solve and run their work with clarity and determination.
How We Work
LeafSide operates with high rigor. Success in this role requires readiness for:
Writing-first thinking: Plans, status, decisions, and risks are concisely documented.
Data-backed reasoning: e.g. tables, comparisons, assumptions, and proof.
Execution within constraints of time and budget.
Qualifications
7 - 10+ years of experience in production, manufacturing, and/or supply chain (food/CPG or regulated environment strongly preferred)
3 - 5+ years in production leadership (manager level or above)
Fluent with business & operations software, e.g. spreadsheets and software/operations tools
AI-empowered and constantly learning
Track record of coaching teams to higher standards and responsibilities
Salary & Benefits
We offer market-competitive compensation & total rewards, plus bonus, dependent on experience and qualifications.
Total time off per year starts at 5 weeks per year. (8 paid holidays, 5 sick days, and 12 PTO days) with sick and PTO time accrued per fully employed pay period.
Health, dental, and vision plans are offered, with full or partial coverage by the company depending on the plan chosen.
Complimentary LeafSide meals every workday and employee discount on LeafSide products. Unlike most food companies, we eat our own products every day, and high-quality food drives us to perform our best!
Knowing directly from customers that your work uplifts the health & lives of people all across the country.
Our Application Process
Email your application to:
me-for-ops@goleafside.com
Subject line:
CPG Manufacturing Director – [Your Full Name]
Include:
Your full name & phone number
LinkedIn profile link
Resume (PDF)
Include this exact sentence in your email:
“I’m ready to lead, track, and improve production & operations at LeafSide with mission-driven gusto and clear communication.”
In the body of the email, please answer these prompts (concise is fine; clarity matters):
Are you vegan?
If yes: How long and what was the most decisive reason that made you commit?
If no: What is your personal core-connection to our mission?
Describe one of the most important business changes you drove, that required getting buy-in from several stakeholders.
What was your process?
What were the options?
What data or comparisons did you include?
What did you recommend and why?
Supply chain leadership:
Please briefly share your biggest supply chain win: a crisis you led the team through, or a struggling operation you turned around? Where and when, and what was your role?
What was the result in the result, in before and after numbers?
Job Type: Full-time
Benefits:
Dental insurance
Employee discount
Health insurance
Paid time off
Relocation assistance
Vision insurance

Bachelor’s degree in Quality, Mechanical, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical field or equivalent relevant experience.

Senior Director of Operations (Multi-Unit Fitness)
No longer accepting applications
Blue Rock Search, LLC
Miami-Fort Lauderdale Area
Position Overview
Blue Rock Search has partnered with an established and rapidly growing fitness franchise that is seeking a dynamic, people-focused Senior Director of Operations
to lead and enhance the performance of its growing portfolio of company-owned studios. This newly created leadership role will initially oversee approximately 20 corporate locations, with plans for continued expansion via extensive club engagement & field presence. The Senior Director will establish the operational standards, organizational structure, and scalable processes needed to support continued corporate growth, while developing a strong operational foundation that can ultimately be extended across the brand's franchise network.
Revenue Generation & Topline Growth: This leader will drive studio-level sales performance, member engagement, retention, and overall business results through effective leadership, coaching, and execution. The Senior Director will assess the current organizational structure, establish clear expectations and measurable goals, and develop high-performing teams that consistently deliver an exceptional member experience.
The ideal candidate will bring a strong background in multi-unit operations, team development, and sales, with the ability to cultivate a positive culture while introducing greater structure, accountability, and consistency across the organization.
Roles and Responsibilities:
Lead and Strengthen Company-Owned Studio Operations
Oversee the day-to-day operations and performance of the company-owned studios, ensuring consistency, accountability, and operational excellence across markets.
Evaluate existing operations, organizational structure, and team capabilities to identify opportunities to improve effectiveness, clarify responsibilities, and prepare the business for continued growth.
Establish clear operating standards, performance expectations, and measurable goals for studio leaders and field operations teams.
Maintain a strong focus on the member experience, ensuring each studio reflects the company's commitment to delivering an exceptional, welcoming, and community-driven fitness experience.
Regularly visit company-owned clubs in key home markets to assess performance, engage with studio teams, identify improvement opportunities, and ensure consistent execution of operational standards. Extensive Travel will be required.
Build High-Performing Teams and a Strong Company Culture
Assess the current team structure, talent, and leadership capabilities; identify opportunities to strengthen roles, improve alignment, and develop future leaders.
Recruit, develop, coach, and retain talented operations leaders and frontline team members who embody the company's mission, values, and service standards.
Foster a positive, collaborative, and accountable culture that motivates employees, supports professional development, and encourages consistent performance.
Guide the organization’s evolution from a generalist operating model toward a more specialized structure as the business scales, ensuring clear ownership, defined responsibilities, and effective collaboration across teams.
Establish a consistent approach to leadership development, performance management, and accountability across the studio portfolio.
Develop Operational Standards, Metrics, and Playbooks
Create and implement standardized operating procedures, training resources, and operational playbooks that promote consistency, efficiency, and accountability across company-owned studios.
Document proven processes and best practices in practical, repeatable playbooks that support future corporate expansion and, where appropriate, can be adapted for use by franchisees.
Establish and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) related to studio operations, sales, staffing, member experience, retention, and overall business performance.
Use performance data and field-level insights to identify opportunities for improvement, strengthen execution, and support informed business decisions.
Support Growth and Scalable Operations
Drive revenue growth through brand activations, community events, local marketing initiatives, strategic partnerships, and cooperative marketing opportunities that increase membership, strengthen community engagement, and improve club-level sales performance.
Drive studio-level sales and business performance by strengthening execution, coaching leaders, and reinforcing consistent operating practices.
Build an operational foundation that can accommodate the continued expansion of the company's corporate studio portfolio and evolving business needs.
Identify opportunities to improve operational efficiency, resource allocation, staffing models, and consistency without compromising the brand’s distinctive member experience.
Partner with senior leadership to evaluate operational priorities, implement new initiatives, and align studio-level execution with broader business objectives.
Leverage company-owned studios as a platform for testing, refining, and documenting best practices that can support future growth across the franchise system.
Qualifications and Experience
5–7+ years of progressive leadership experience in multi-unit operations, preferably within fitness, health and wellness, hospitality, retail, or another customer-focused, multi-location business.
Demonstrated success leading, developing, and motivating teams across multiple locations or markets.
Prior sales experience and a strong understanding of the relationship between people leadership, customer experience, sales performance, member retention, and overall business results.
A proven track record of building strong team cultures, developing leaders, and establishing clear expectations and accountability.
Experience evaluating organizational structures, clarifying responsibilities, and implementing operational processes to support business growth.
Ability to establish performance metrics, evaluate results, identify performance gaps, and translate business objectives into practical operating standards and repeatable processes.
Strong communication, coaching, and change-management skills, with the ability to build trust and influence at both the frontline and leadership levels.
A hands-on, results-oriented leadership style, with the ability to balance strategic thinking with consistent field-level execution.
Franchise experience is beneficial but not required; demonstrated multi-unit operating experience is the priority.
Follow us on LinkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/blue-rock-search/

evidence.quote: Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
evidence.text:
Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
Genesis
San Carlos , California 
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.
This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.
What you'll do
Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.
What we're looking for
You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.
Working conditions
Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.
Why this role
You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.
How we work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition.
We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency.
Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun.
Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency.
Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism.
We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego.
Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey.
We take pride in the craft.

Sr. Manager, Game Production (Production Lead) - Unpublished R&D Product
Riot Games
Los Angeles, CA
Producers at Riot lead passionate cross-functional teams to craft creative content and incredible experiences for our players. We encourage teams to collaborate and drive development, smashing through obstacles to deliver products into players’ hands. We support concepting, building and delivering content at all stages of production
As a Sr. Manager, Game Production
on an unannounced R&D product, you will own the production approach that turns creative ambition, product strategy, and team capabilities into clear plans, healthy operating rhythms, and shipped player value. You will help move games from early ideas through production, launch, and live operations. You will build production systems that create clarity without over-prescribing the work, helping the team adapt as the product, audience, and opportunity become clearer. You’ll work through ambiguity, energized by hard tradeoffs, and work across design, art, engineering, product, QA, analytics, publishing, and external development. You will partner closely with game leadership and discipline leads to build and own the production operating model for the game. This includes how teams plan, make commitments, manage dependencies, use vendors and co-development partners, and prepare for future stages of development. You will help the team scale from a small, adaptive group into a larger production organization without losing momentum, accountability, or care for players and team health. You will report to the Director, Game Production.
Responsibilities
Own the game’s production approach through each phase of development, helping the team make strong decisions today while preparing for future launch and live-service needs.
Translate product strategy and creative direction into actionable plans, milestones, rituals, and decision-making systems.
Partner with game leadership and discipline leads to align scope, quality, staffing, timelines, and delivery expectations.
Lead cross-functional production across design, art, engineering, product, QA, analytics, publishing, and external development.
Build scalable planning, dependency, risk, and accountability systems as the team grows.
Identify delivery risks, organizational gaps, and execution constraints early; drive resolution with the appropriate leaders and teams.
Manage production relationships with vendors, outsourcing teams, and co-development partners.
Maintain clear visibility for stakeholders on progress, tradeoffs, risks, and decisions.
Foster healthy team dynamics, strong feedback loops, psychological safety, and productive conflict.
Required Qualifications
10+ years of professional experience working in game production.
6+ years of in production leadership roles on cross-disciplinary game teams.
Experience shipping at least one game or major game initiative with production responsibility from pre-production through launch.
Background in cross-platform and live-service game development or live operations.
Strong command of milestone planning, roadmap execution, dependency management, risk management, and launch readiness.
Proven ability to lead through ambiguity, scale, changing priorities, and complex production tradeoffs.
Strong cross-discipline fluency across game design, art, engineering, product, QA, analytics, publishing, and external development.
Vendor, outsourcing, or co-development management background.
Deep understanding of games, player audiences, team health, modern development tools, production technology, and emerging AI-enabled tools and workflows.
Desired Qualifications
Experience as a Lead Producer, Principal Producer, Production Director, or equivalent senior production owner on a shipped game.
Shipped and operated multiple cross-platform, multiplayer, or live-service games.
Experience building production practices for a new game, new team, or ambiguous development environment as it scaled.
Familiarity with studio operations, business planning, workforce planning, budgeting, player insights, economy, content operations, release management, or liveops planning.
For this role, you'll find success through craft expertise and a collaborative spirit that prioritizes the delight of players. We will look at your past studies and experience, but for this role, we also look for dedicated people with a personal relationship with games. If you embody player empathy and care about players' experiences, this is the role for you!
Our Perks
Riot focuses on work/life balance, shown by our open paid time off policy and other perks such as flexible work schedules. We offer medical, dental, and life insurance, parental leave for you, your spouse/domestic partner, and children, and a 401k with company match. Check out our benefits pages
for more information.
At Riot Games, we put players first. That mission drives every decision in our quest to create games and experiences that make it better to be a player. Whether you’re working directly on a new player-facing experience or you’re supporting the company as a whole, everyone at Riot is part of our mission. And just like in our games, we’re better when we work together. Our goal is to create collaborative teams where you are empowered to bring your unique perspective everyday. If that sounds like the kind of place you want to work, we’re looking forward to your application.
It’s our policy to provide equal employment opportunity for all applicants and members of Riot Games, Inc. Riot Games makes reasonable accommodations for handicapped and disabled Rioters and does not unlawfully discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, handicap, veteran status, marital status, criminal history, or any other category protected by applicable federal and state law. We consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state and local law, including the California Fair Chance Act, the City of Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, and the Washington Fair Chance Act.
Duties
Per the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance, the following core duties may create a basis for disqualifying candidates with relevant criminal histories:
Safeguarding confidential and sensitive Company data
Communication with others, including Rioters and third parties such as vendors, and/or players, including minors
Accessing Company assets, secure digital systems, and networks
Ensuring a safe interactive environment for players and other Rioters
These duties are directly related to essential operations, safety, trust, and compliance obligations within our organization. Please note that job duties may evolve based on business needs and additional responsibilities may be assigned as necessary to maintain operational efficiency and security.
(Los Angeles Only) Base salary range between $206,700.00 - $289,000.00 USD + incentive compensation + equity + 401K with company match + medical, dental, vision, and life insurance + short and long-term disability + open PTO.
(Mercer Island only) Base salary range between $206,700.00 - $289,000.00 USD + incentive compensation + equity + 401K with company match + medical, dental, vision, and life insurance + short and long-term disability + open PTO.
(Redwood City only) Base salary range between $222,200.00 - $310,600.00 USD + incentive compensation + equity + 401K with company match + medical, dental, vision, and life insurance + short and long-term disability + open PTO.

evidence.text:
Director of Operations
Amphenol
Cary, NC
Join Temposonics – A Global Leader in Sensing Technology
Temposonics is a leading innovator in advanced sensing technologies, delivering high-precision position and speed measurement solutions for automation and safety-critical systems. Our cutting-edge sensors and transmitters help drive performance and minimize downtime in a wide range of industrial, mobile hydraulics, and process technology applications.
With a continually expanding product portfolio and a strong commitment to regional customer support, we work closely with clients to deliver customized solutions that boost productivity and operational success.
Our success is rooted in outstanding product quality, hands-on expertise, and a passion for innovation. We invest heavily in research, development, and production to create next-generation sensor systems that meet evolving industry needs.
Since April 2021, Temposonics has been part of Amphenol Corporation (NYSE: APH), one of the world’s largest manufacturers of interconnect products. As part of the Amphenol family, we offer customers and employees access to a broader range of technologies, resources, and opportunities. See our story here: 50 Years Temposonics - Watch Our Story Learn more: introduction | Temposonics https://www.linkedin.com/company/temposonics
More Reasons to Join the Team At Temposonics, you’ll find a highly collaborative, team-focused environment where every employee matters. We believe that only by working together can we achieve our ultimate goal: total customer satisfaction and long-term success for everyone.
Your satisfaction and growth are important to us. That’s why we offer a wide range of benefits, including:
Competitive medical, dental, and vision plans for you and your family
A progressive 401(k) with a 75% company match on employee contributions up to 6%
Generous paid time off and company-paid holidays
Ongoing employee development opportunities to help you advance your skills and career
Come join a team where your contributions make a difference and your future is a priority.
As the Director of Operations at Temposonics, LLC you will be responsible for planning, directing and managing all areas of Manufacturing in the Cary, NC facility through subordinate management to ensure approved products are manufactured on-schedule and within quality standards and cost objectives. This role is responsible for the creation and sustainability of Manufacturing Excellence throughout Operations.
Major Areas of Accountability:
1. Translates the implications of the strategy on manufacturing, sets direction and develops short- and long-range plans to meet business strategies and goals.
Formulate and recommend manufacturing policies and programs that guide the organization in maintaining and improving its competitive position, the profitability of the operation and supports Class A processes.
Develop strategic and annual manufacturing plans and establish procedures for maintaining high standards of manufacturing operations to ensure that products conform to customer and company quality standards.
Provides leadership to Operations Managers/Supervisors and their subordinate staff for manufacturing planning, staffing and execution.
Develops and oversees Manufacturing systems and processes to ensure cost, quality and delivery requirements are met.
2. Direct and monitor production managers to accomplish goals of the manufacturing plan, consistent with established manufacturing and safety procedures. Act as liaison between department management/subordinate levels, as well as, executive/department manager levels to inform personnel of communications, decisions, policies and all matters that affect their performance and results.
3. Direct and monitor EHS and Facilities Manager to accomplish goals of the manufacturing plan, consistent with established manufacturing, overall building operation and safety procedures. Directs quality standards, process improvement and operational efficiency within Operations by identifying and implementing process improvement opportunities, working with cross-functional leaders.
Determines measurements to quantify results and to identify corrective actions needed.
Establishes and tracks key operational and quality metrics to ensure control of operations is maintained and ISO standards are consistently applied within the Operations area.
Develops processes and methods to identify technical problems before they become crises and works cross functionally to determine appropriate action to solve technical problems
Drives Lean Principles across the Manufacturing Value Stream to improve our Operation Excellence (safety, quality, delivery, cycle time, productivity & cost).
5. Ensure resources, floor space and capital requirements are available to effectively and efficiently manufacture and deliver products and projects. Takes action to manage demand peaks and valleys to both meet customer expectations and drive level load scheduling.
6. Establishes annual operating budget and manages against that budget. Monitors performance, directs corrective action and continuous cost improvements for all areas, including labor, expenses, assessments, and capital.
7. Responsible for the on-going management and development of assigned employees. Determines staffing and skill requirements to meet departmental needs, and implements plans to satisfy those requirements. Forecasts staffing levels to ensure proper capacity and mix of personnel skills needed to meet the shipment/revenue plan.
8. Knows and applies the division's quality policy and procedures of ISO 9001 as it relates to area of responsibility and the organization. Follows all standard operating procedures as prescribed and notifies appropriate personnel of any non-conformance.
9. Other duties as assigned.
Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Business or Engineering, or equivalent; MBA preferred.
Minimum 10 years of manufacturing operations experience; plus, minimum 5 years’ experience in supervision.
Must have demonstrated ability to drive change and continuous improvement across a broad level/scope.
Ability to apply process improvement tools to achieve significant quality, cost, productivity, and cycle time improvement.
Ability to build relationships, lead cross-functional teams, and build consensus among a large group.
Proven ability to successfully solve complex business and technical problems.
Experience in developing BOMs with MRP systems.
Working knowledge of manufacturing standards, practices, and regulations.
Additional Benefits:
Medical/Dental and Vision Insurance for you and your family
HSA and PPO Copay plan options for medical
Paid Time Off
Employer paid basic life insurance, short- and long-term disability insurance
401k Company Match
Tuition Reimbursement
Company paid holidays, employee discounts, and other employee recognition
Physical Demands (U.S. only)
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit; use hands to finger, handle, or feel; reach with hands and arms; and talk or hear. The employee is occasionally required to stand; walk; and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.
Temposonics, LLC is an equal opportunity employer

General Manager - Boat Manufacturing & Sales
Boutique Recruiting
Perry, FL
Position Title:
General Manager - Boat Manufacturing & Sales
﻿
We are seeking an experienced General Manager to lead the manufacturing operations and commercial growth of a premium custom boatbuilding business in Perry, Florida. This hands-on leadership role oversees fiberglass and composite boat production, quality control, financial performance, and business development. The General Manager will drive sales growth, expand dealer and broker relationships, strengthen operational efficiency, and ensure the delivery of exceptional custom fishing boats.
The ideal candidate brings extensive firsthand experience in premium boatbuilding, proven success selling high-end boats, and the entrepreneurial mindset to lead an experienced production team while building a profitable, growing marine business.
Salary Range:
$120,000 base with OTE $240K+
Responsibilities
Oversee daily manufacturing operations, including fiberglass and composite construction, laminating, finishing, rigging, quality control, and final delivery
Lead, mentor, and manage an experienced boatbuilding team while maintaining exceptional craftsmanship and production standards
Drive sales growth by developing relationships with high-net-worth buyers, marine brokers, dealers, and industry partners
Expand dealer and broker distribution networks across domestic and potential international markets
Represent the business at boat shows, industry events, customer meetings, and dealer presentations
Manage production schedules, labor, purchasing, inventory, and material costs to improve operational efficiency and profitability
Establish measurable performance standards for production output, quality, revenue, and financial performance
Oversee customer contracts, build specifications, order fulfillment, and delivery coordination
Monitor financial performance, control operating expenses, and identify opportunities to improve margins
Strengthen existing customer relationships while generating new business opportunities and expanding market presence
Collaborate with ownership on strategic growth initiatives, potential product expansion, and long-term business development
Balance increasing customer demand with manufacturing capacity to maintain premium quality and timely delivery
Requirements
Extensive hands-on experience manufacturing premium fiberglass or composite center-console, fishing, or custom recreational boats
Strong technical knowledge of fiberglass laminating, carbon fiber, composite materials, boat construction, and marine production processes
Proven success selling high-end boats to affluent buyers and developing relationships within the marine industry
Demonstrated experience leading boat manufacturing operations, production teams, and quality control processes
Strong business development capabilities with experience expanding customer relationships, dealer networks, or broker partnerships
Ability to manage manufacturing budgets, material costs, inventory, purchasing, and operational profitability
Proven ability to lead experienced craftspeople while establishing accountability and improving production processes
Strong negotiation, relationship-building, communication, and leadership skills
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to independently manage operations and drive measurable business results
Willingness to spend at least 50% of working time at the Perry, Florida manufacturing facility and travel for business development
Flexibility to work additional hours as needed to support production deadlines, customer commitments, and business growth
Experience developing premium marine brands or established relationships with custom boat buyers and dealers preferred
Experience scaling marine manufacturing operations or expanding product lines preferred
Benefits
Competitive base compensation with potential performance-based bonus opportunities
Negotiable paid time off
Flexible geographic arrangement with potential lodging accommodations in Perry, Florida
Opportunity to lead both manufacturing operations and commercial growth
Direct collaboration with ownership on business strategy and expansion
Potential for additional performance-based compensation, subject to finalized terms
Significant leadership autonomy and opportunities for long-term professional growth
If you are a proven boatbuilding leader who knows how to deliver exceptional craftsmanship, develop high-value customer relationships, and grow a premium marine business, we encourage you to apply and take ownership of this exciting opportunity.

evidence.text:
Director, Site Operations - Memphis
SpaceXSI
Memphis, TN
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today, SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of making life multiplanetary and expanding consciousness to the stars.
SpaceXSI is building Super Intelligence to help humanity understand the universe. Our teams are building the full Super Intelligence stack: from our Colossus supercomputers, to Grok models, to our suite of applications, including Grok Bot, Grok Build, Grok Imagine, Grok Voice, and X. We're creating a powerful flywheel where more compute trains better models, better models power more useful products, and what we learn from people using those products shapes what we build next.
DIRECTOR, SITE OPERATIONS
As the Director of Site Operations, you’ll own node and rack uptime for SpaceXSI's AI supercompute cluster—the most advanced of its kind. This role is the extreme owner of cluster health and customer Service Level Agreements across 5+ sites operating 24/7. You’ll lead a 250+ person organization of site managers, shift supervisors, and technicians, plus the site reliability engineering team that monitors cluster health and drives fault mitigation at scale. We’re looking for a hands-on operations leader who can build a culture of excellence and accountability, partner tightly across the company, and keep uptime exceptional as we grow.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Own cluster uptime by serving as extreme owner of node, rack, and cluster health across 5+ sites running 24/7, accountable for customer Service Level Agreements and consistently exceptional uptime on SpaceXSI's supercompute cluster
Lead a large operations organization, directing a 250+ person team spanning site managers, shift supervisors, and technicians across four 24/7 shifts, building a culture of excellence and accountability at every layer of the org
Drive node and rack remediation by ensuring systematic recovery of failed nodes and racks through command-line and physical intervention, driving mean time to repair to the feasible minimum
Partner across functions by coordinating with facilities operations to limit downtime from power and cooling faults and proactive maintenance; with network engineering on cluster upgrades; and with tenant representatives on node remediation and planned and unplanned downtime
Own vendor execution, directing vendors through hardware rework and field operations so repairs, replacements, and capacity work happen at the speed the cluster requires
Lead site reliability engineering, owning the SRE organization responsible for proactive cluster health monitoring, reactive fault mitigation at scale, root cause analyses for node, rack, and cluster issues, and site-wide reliability procedures and fault documentation
Run data-driven improvement by leading continual improvement and efficiency initiatives, using operational data to balance team resources and raise uptime, repair time, and SLA performance across sites
Command incidents at scale and set the standard for incident response during cluster-impacting events, providing clear direction, fast recovery, and tight communication with internal and external partners

Vice President Operations
No longer accepting applications
Doorvest
Austin, TX
VP of Operations
Location:
Cleveland, OH or Austin, TX (with regular travel to our markets) · Type:
Full-time, exempt · Reports to:
Chief Operating Officer
About Doorvest
Doorvest is a venture-backed, long-term-rental property management company. We acquire small property management businesses and integrate them onto one platform, one operating model and one team. Today we manage roughly 2,300 homes across Ohio (Cleveland and Dayton), Texas, Georgia, Oklahoma, Tennessee, Oregon and Florida, built through five acquisitions in under two years, with more under letter of intent. We expect to pass 3,000 doors by year-end and to roughly triple from there in 2027.
We run the business as a multi-site company, not a San Francisco startup with field offices. Our central back office (resident services, collections, evictions, housing programs and compliance, owner success, ops finance) is specialized and partly offshore; our markets are run by General Managers with in-house technicians, local vendors and leasing agents on the ground. We run on Rentvine, Nutiliti, Second Nature and RentEngine, and we build a lot of our own tooling with AI rather than waiting on an engineering sprint.
The role
We are hiring a VP of Operations to own field operations: every market's P&L, maintenance and turns, and the General Managers and maintenance leadership who run them. You will inherit a working structure, not a blank page. Our Senior Maintenance Manager runs company-wide maintenance process, personnel and revenue today and will report to you on day one. Our General Managers (Cleveland, Florida, Oregon) and our Dayton Market Lead report to him today and move to you after a 60-day ramp. In-house technician crews already exist in Cleveland and Oregon, with offshore maintenance coordinators dispatching in every market.
Your job is to make that structure perform and then make it repeatable: turn maintenance into a profit center run in-house wherever the numbers support it, get every market to the same turn times and work-order SLAs, and build the playbook that lets us add the next acquisition's doors without adding chaos. Central Operations owns the phone, the tenant and the owner relationship; you own the truck, the key and the market. The work order is the hand-off between the two, and you will be measured on how fast and how cleanly your side of it closes.
This is a leadership seat with an operator's workload. You will manage managers, but you will also be in the dispatch queue, on a job site and in a vendor negotiation when the week requires it. If you have spent the last several years exclusively managing managers, this will be uncomfortable.
What you will own
Market P&L across every market.
Revenue, margin and cost for field operations and maintenance, market by market, with the General Managers accountable to you for their numbers and you accountable to the COO for the total.
Maintenance as a business.
Pricing, scope capture, billable-hour capture on every work order, the margin between in-house or vendor cost and billed work, estimate review, and the work-order-to-accounts-payable hand-off (billable backfill, invoice coding, owner/tenant/company cost split). The company measures leakage weekly; you own closing it.
Turns and work-order SLAs.
Dispatch, in-house technicians, vendor scheduling, turns, rent-ready and move-in readiness in every market. Resident Services creates the move-out inspection and turn work orders and decides security-deposit charges; your teams complete the inspection with photos, findings and estimates back on the work order within three business days of move-out, then complete the turn.
The field leadership team.
Manage the Senior Maintenance Manager from day one and the General Managers and Market Lead after the ramp. Set each market's scorecard (turn days, work-order SLA, occupancy, escalation SLA, statement exceptions cleared before owner-statement close) and run the weekly business review against it. Hire the next General Managers as we open markets.
Local vendor networks and local hiring.
Source, price, onboard and performance-manage vendors and contractors in every market; decide where in-house crews beat vendors and build them; approve maintenance spend per the authority matrix you will help write.
Inspections, violations and physical loss.
City, Section 8 and lead-safe inspections that Central Operations schedules and your market teams attend; violation cure; property insurance claims coordination for fire, water, mold and displacement, with Owner Success handling the owner.
Business continuity and after-hours.
Incident response for storms, fires and outages; the maintenance on-call layer behind the central after-hours line.
Acquisition integration, field side.
Product owns the integration plan; you own the maintenance and field migration inside it: vendor account transfers, technician onboarding, work-order and SLA standards live in the new market from day 0 to day 90.
Tooling and data.
Build the dispatch views, vendor scorecards, leakage and margin dashboards you need with AI tools, then partner with Product and Engineering to productionize what proves out. Our current dashboards are slow and incomplete; you will help rebuild them.
Playbooks and training.
Document the field SOPs (dispatch, turns, inspections, vendor onboarding, in-house crew standards) into the company knowledge base and run the training that makes a new General Manager productive in 60 days.
How we will measure you
Turn days and work-order SLA attainment by market
Maintenance revenue and margin; billable hours captured on every work order
Move-out inspection work orders closed within three business days: 100%
Leakage dollars (unbilled work, miscoded invoices) trending to zero
Occupancy and in-market escalation SLA per General Manager scorecard
Time from acquisition close to field operations on standard
Who you are
8+ years running multi-site or multi-market operations with a physical component, such as field services, residential or commercial maintenance, home services, construction or renovation, logistics or last-mile, or property management at scale. Multi-market experience is required.
5+ years managing people, including managing managers, and managing a mixed workforce of in-house crews and external vendors to hard SLAs.
You have carried a P&L or a margin target and can say concretely how you moved it. You have built or grown a maintenance, service or field operation as a revenue line, not only a cost center.
A player-coach who has led a team while still doing work of their own, and who is energized by that rather than insulted by it.
Data-driven and AI-native: you already reach for LLMs and spreadsheets to analyze problems and build the tools you need, and you would rather fix the system than firefight one ticket at a time.
You communicate well with technicians, vendors, homeowners and executives, and you write things down: SOPs, scorecards, hand-offs.
Comfortable with a flexible schedule (occasional evenings, weekends and holidays as the business requires) and regular travel to our markets, including the ones you don't live in.
Helpful but not required: single-family rental or multifamily property management, acquisition integration experience, and exposure to property-management software such as Rentvine.
What this role is not
It is not a traditional property manager job and it is not a single-market job. It is not a purely strategic seat where someone else runs the work. It is not an office job: Cleveland and Austin are where you will be based, and our markets are where the work is. We are looking for an operator who has run a distributed, physical operation, wants to own it as a business, and wants to build the next version of it with real technology and data behind them.
Compensation and benefits
Competitive base salary, based on skills and experience
Meaningful equity
Full benefits package
Ownership of a core operating vertical, with a team already in place, during a period of rapid growth
Doorvest is an equal opportunity employer.

A player-coach who has led a team while still doing work of their own, and who is energized by that rather than insulted by it.
Data-driven and AI-native: you already reach for LLMs and spreadsheets to analyze problems and build the tools you need, and you would rather fix the system than firefight one ticket at a time.
You communicate well with technicians, vendors, homeowners and executives, and you write things down: SOPs, scorecards, hand-offs.
Comfortable with a flexible schedule (occasional evenings, weekends and holidays as the business requires) and regular travel to our markets, including the ones you don't live in.
Helpful but not required: single-family rental or multifamily property management, acquisition integration experience, and exposure to property-management software such as Rentvine.
What this role is not
It is not a traditional property manager job and it is not a single-market job. It is not a purely strategic seat where someone else runs the work. It is not an office job: Cleveland and Austin are where you will be based, and our markets are where the work is. We are looking for an operator who has run a distributed, physical operation, wants to own it as a business, and wants to build the next version of it with real technology and data behind them.
Compensation and benefits
Competitive base salary, based on skills and experience
Meaningful equity
Full benefits package
Ownership of a core operating vertical, with a team already in place, during a period of rapid growth

evidence.text:
Vice President, Operations
Nextpower
Fremont, CA
Job Description
VP, Operations Engineering
Nextpower
Role Mission
Lead Nextpower's transformation from a portfolio of rapidly expanding technologies and acquired businesses into a scalable, integrated, and globally competitive product platform.
Distinctly focused on 1) New Product Introduction (NPI) and the product industrialization and engineering readiness of those new products for high volume manufacturing and 2) Operations Engineering to drive process capacity (CpK) that enable quality, cost, and cycle time goals. This role will continuously innovate and evolve the processes, systems, supplier strategies, and cross-functional operating model required to move products rapidly from concept through and into high volume commercial production with a high process capability and low defect rate.
Key Responsibilities
New Product Introduction & Industrialization
Own the NPI process from R&D (Product Engineering) handoff to the Supply Chain volume capable handoff, while partnering with Products Engineering, Supply Chain, Sales, and other functional groups for continuous improvement throughout the entire product development and go-to-market process.
Continuously improve the stage-gate NPI process, design reviews, configuration management, change control, and launch-readiness product introductions.
Own and Drive Design for Manufacturing, Assembly, Cost, Quality, Service, and Supply Chain (DFx) into product development.
Partner with Products, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain to ensure products are commercially scalable with an effective blend of quality, cost, and functionality —not simply technically complete.
Establish launch metrics and accountability for schedule, cost, quality, yield, reliability, and supply readiness.
Operations Engineering
Drive ongoing quality, process capability (CpK), and cost goals within the internal and supplier factories with direct engagement on supplier quality, means and methods, process and value engineering, should-cost analysis, and design-to-cost initiatives.
Establish critical node control points and data acquisition (EDI/API) and establish and maintain a Statistical Process Control (SPC) monitoring and control program.
Integrate supplier strategy into product development and NPI from the earliest design stages.
Innovate and streamline NPI transitions to Supply Chain for the following aspects: Strategic sourcing, supplier qualification, dual-sourcing, localization, capacity planning, and supply-risk mitigation strategies for critical components.
Partner with Supply Chain and Operations to establish financially effective cost, availability, lead time, quality, and geopolitical requirements as product-design inputs.
Establish and ensure supplier tooling, capacity, quality, and production readiness are aligned with product launch requirements.
Organization & Leadership
Build a high-performing, cross-functional Ops Engineering organization capable of rapidly ramping and commercializing new products (NPI) and driving operational engineering improvements that improve process CpK, quality, cost, and cycle time
Develop engineering talent, processes, and organizational capabilities required to support Nextpower's growth.
Develop a seamless connectivity between Products Innovation and Supply Chain high volume processes.
Foster a highly accountable, high ownership, biased-for-action organization that thrives on delighting our Customers by partnering with them to deliver high quality, on-time new products.
Measures of Success
Reduced concept-to-commercial and volume-launch cycle time
Improved on-time NPI and production launches
Improved first-pass qualification, production yield, reliability, and field performance
Reduced cost and engineering changes following production release
Increased process Capability (CpK) within factories
Increased supplier readiness and qualified/dual-source coverage
Improved product cost, lead time, and supply availability
Increased component commonality and platform reuse
Successful integration of acquired technologies and organizations
Increased domestic/localized supply capability where strategically advantageous
Establishment of a scalable engineering operating model capable of supporting Nextpower's growth
Leadership Profile
Proven executive leadership in NPI, product industrialization, engineering, manufacturing, and/or supply chain within complex hardware businesses.
Experience taking products from development through qualification, production ramp, and commercial scale.
Strong understanding of mechanical, electrical, power electronics, controls, software, manufacturing, and supplier ecosystems.
Demonstrated success integrating acquisitions, technologies, suppliers, and organizations.
Strong commercial orientation with experience managing cost, quality, schedule, capacity, and supply risk.
Ability to operate strategically while driving detailed execution across multiple product lines and business units.
Experience building organizations and operating processes in a high-growth environment.
At Nextpower, we are driving the global energy transition with an integrated clean energy technology platform that combines intelligent structural, electrical, and digital solutions for utility-scale power plants. Our comprehensive portfolio enables faster project delivery, higher performance, and greater reliability, helping our customers capture the full value of solar power. Our talented worldwide teams are redefining how solar power plants are designed, built, and operated every day with smart technology, data-driven insights, and advanced automation. Together, we’re building the foundation for the world’s next generation of clean energy infrastructure.
Nextpower is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
We are Nextpower

Director of Manufacturing
Mesodyne
Somerville, MA
// Careers
Director of Manufacturing
We are seeking a Director of Manufacturing to own the complete manufacturing and supply chain operations of our LightCell product line. You will be responsible for ramping assembly throughput, managing internal production, building and scaling our vendor network, and ensuring delivery of high-quality products on schedule. This is a hands-on leadership role that demands both strategic thinking and operational excellence — you'll spend time in the lab and on the factory floor while also setting the vision for how we manufacture at scale.
You will report directly to the CEO and work closely with our CTO, CGO, Chief Engineer, and the broader operations team. This role is critical to our growth and will carry significant equity participation and a clear path to VP of Operations or Chief Operating Officer.
THE OPPORTUNITY
We're scaling from small-scale assembly to low rate production, with larger production to follow. Our current team assembles units in-house with a mix of internal work and strategic vendor partnerships. Over the next 18 months, we need to:
Scale from tens to hundreds of units per year without sacrificing quality
Transition from hand assembly to repeatable, documented, scalable processes
Build and manage a network of precision vendors (brazing, metal fabrication, electronics, coatings)
Achieve consistent delivery timelines and cost targets as design matures
Lay the groundwork for potential manufacturing partnerships or contract manufacturing as we grow beyond 50+ employees
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Assembly Operations & Manufacturing Engineering
Oversee all aspects of in-house assembly, quality control, and production scheduling
Identify and eliminate bottlenecks in the assembly workflow; drive efficiency improvements through process redesign and automation opportunities
Develop and continuously improve standard operating procedures (SOPs) for all production activities
Manage assembly staffing, training, and quality culture; build a team that takes pride in their work
Implement production control systems (visual management, inventory tracking, scheduling) appropriate for our scale
Work closely with R&D to ensure designs are manufacturable and can scale efficiently
Supply Chain & Vendor Management
Source, qualify, and manage relationships with critical vendors (metal fabrication, brazing, coatings, electronics, precision components)
Negotiate contracts, manage costs, and ensure on-time delivery from all suppliers
Establish quality standards and inspection protocols with vendors; drive continuous improvement
Develop contingency plans and diversify the vendor base for critical components to reduce supply chain risk
Coordinate vendor performance reviews and escalate issues proactively
Build long-term partnerships with vendors who can grow with us
Quality & Compliance
Establish and enforce quality checkpoints throughout assembly and testing
Implement traceability and documentation systems to support customer delivery and warranty management
Prepare for and drive certifications (ISO 9001, as appropriate) or customer-specific quality requirements
Investigate and resolve quality issues; implement corrective actions
Manage product testing and field feedback loops to inform manufacturing improvements
Scaling Strategy & Planning
Develop a manufacturing roadmap that anticipates volume growth and infrastructure needs
Make build-vs.-buy decisions on key manufacturing capabilities (which processes to keep in-house vs. outsource)
Plan for facility needs, equipment, and staffing as production scales from current levels to 500+/year
Explore manufacturing partnerships or contract manufacturers if and when internal scaling becomes uneconomical
Drive cost reduction initiatives without compromising quality as production scales
Team Leadership & Culture
Build and lead a growing operations team (assembly technicians, quality inspector, supply chain coordinator)
Create a manufacturing culture focused on quality, continuous improvement, and safety
Mentor junior team members and develop future supervisors
Collaborate effectively with R&D, finance, and sales teams to balance innovation, profitability, and delivery
QUALIFICATIONS
Required
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field (or equivalent experience)
10+ years of manufacturing or operations experience, with at least 5 years in a leadership/management role
Hands-on experience with precision assembly operations (electromechanical, aerospace, automotive, energy, or similar specialty manufacturing)
Proven track record managing supply chains and vendor networks, including sourcing, qualification, and relationship management
Experience scaling manufacturing operations from small volume (10s-100s/year) to larger volumes (1000s/year)
Strong knowledge of manufacturing best practices, quality systems (SPC, inspection protocols), and lean/continuous improvement
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills — able to influence R&D, finance, and executive leadership
Demonstrated ability to make decisions with incomplete information and adapt to changing priorities
Preferred
Experience in a startup, scale-up, or small manufacturing company (50–200 people)
Background in specialized or precision manufacturing (aerospace, photonics, semiconductor packaging, thermal management)
Experience with energy technology, power electronics, or related hardware
Knowledge of brazing, welding, or high-temperature assembly processes
Track record with ISO 9001 or similar quality certifications
Experience with ERP/MRP systems or production planning software
Hands-on experience with supplier quality management and performance metrics
Familiarity with 3D printing, tooling design, or manufacturing process optimization
WHO WILL THRIVE IN THIS ROLE
You've spent years on the factory floor and understand how to drive real improvements in throughput and quality
You are genuinely excited about building operational excellence from the ground up — not just maintaining existing processes
You can manage specialists and PhDs in R&D while also rolling up your sleeves on the shop floor
You see vendor relationships as partnerships and believe in building trust and collaboration, not just extracting price concessions
You are comfortable in environments with some ambiguity and are confident making calls without perfect information
You believe that operations is strategic, not just tactical — that how you manufacture affects what you can build next
You are energized by growth and the challenge of scaling a precision manufacturing operation
COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
Competitive base salary commensurate with experience and role level
Equity reflecting the criticality of this role to company success
Health, dental, and vision coverage
Paid time off and flexible scheduling
Opportunity to build and scale manufacturing operations from the ground up
Direct influence over product roadmap through manufacturing-driven design improvements
This position is based at our facility in Somerville, MA.
Join Mesodyne and be part of a pioneering company at the forefront of power generation technology. If you are a motivated self-starter ready to embrace challenges in a dynamic startup environment, we encourage you to apply here.

Interested in learning more about the LightCell or scheduling a demonstration?
