evidence.text:
Deputy Director, Product Platforms
GLOBALFOUNDRIES
Richardson
About GlobalFoundries:
GlobalFoundries is a leading full-service semiconductor foundry providing a unique combination of design, development, and fabrication services to some of the world’s most inspired technology companies. With a global manufacturing footprint spanning three continents, GlobalFoundries makes possible the technologies and systems that transform industries and give customers the power to shape their markets. For more information, visit www.gf.com.
Summary of Role:
The Deputy Director, Product Platforms will be the entrepreneurial product leader for a differentiated compute-platform portfolio. The role combines product vision, market insight, technical depth, customer leadership, ecosystem development, and commercial accountability. The successful candidate will turn reusable processor, memory, interconnect, security, safety, AI acceleration, I/O, software, and development-tool assets into compelling customizable platform families and derivative products that customers can adopt and scale.
This is not a product-planning-only role. The leader will engage deeply across hardware and software, work directly with customers and partners, drive disciplined product execution, and remain accountable for successful launches, design wins, adoption, and sustained revenue growth.
Essential responsibilities:
Define and own the multi-year platform vision, product strategy, roadmap, business plan, and investment priorities for the 12nm compute portfolio.
Maintain an architecture and IP-reuse strategy that is anchored in 12nm but can extend to an adjacent process node when supported by market demand, customer requirements, performance / power / cost needs, supply strategy, or portfolio economics.
Translate market trends and customer use cases into platform requirements spanning CPU architecture, memory hierarchy, coherent interconnect / NoC, accelerators, high-speed I/O, security, functional safety, package, power, software, tools, and reference systems.
Create a coherent platform family and derivative strategy rather than isolated one-off products; define where configuration, customer IP integration, chiplets, companion devices, or custom derivatives create differentiated value.
Own product requirements, target specifications, competitive positioning, pricing strategy, business cases, lifecycle plans, and clear go / no-go recommendations.
Lead cross-functional platform execution with architecture, silicon design, verification, physical design, DFT, package, test, validation, software, applications, operations, quality, finance, sales, and marketing.
Drive the full launch process from concept and business approval through platform definition, development, pre-silicon enablement, sampling, production release, market launch, customer ramp, and post-launch optimization.
Build the whole-product plan, including virtual platforms, FPGA prototypes, evaluation systems, SDKs, Linux / RTOS enablement, drivers, toolchains, reference designs, documentation, training, and field collateral.
Develop and manage an ecosystem of processor / IP providers, EDA partners, OS and middleware vendors, toolchain and debug partners, design services firms, board partners, distributors, and application-domain partners.
Establish executive-level relationships with strategic customers and partners; lead discovery, roadmap alignment, product definition, commercial framing, design-win strategy, and escalation resolution.
Partner with sales and field teams to build the opportunity pipeline, segment target accounts, improve customer identification and win rate, and convert early engagements into design wins and production revenue.
Own platform KPIs, including roadmap execution, launch readiness, design wins, qualified pipeline, ecosystem readiness, customer adoption, gross margin, forecast accuracy, revenue growth, and return on investment.
Continuously assess competitive offerings, technology shifts, market inflections, and build / buy / partner choices; adjust the roadmap with speed and discipline.
Communicate a clear, credible platform narrative to executives, customers, partners, field teams, and engineering organizations, balancing vision with evidence and execution realism.
Commercial judgment: ability to balance NRE and customer specific developments with a platform reuse approach, derivative economics, margin, schedule, customer specificity, and long-term portfolio leverage.
Other Responsibilities:
Perform all activities in a safe and responsible manner and support all Environmental, Health, Safety & Security requirements and programs.
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a closely related technical field; advanced technical or business degree is a plus.
8+ years of semiconductor, embedded-computing, processor, SoC, platform, or closely related product experience, including 5+ years in product management, platform leadership, product marketing, applications, systems, or a comparable customer-facing technical leadership role.
Strong background in 32-bit or 64-bit compute products, with 64-bit MPU, application-processor, edge-compute, infrastructure, or Linux-class product experience strongly preferred.
Demonstrated understanding of SoC hardware and software, including prior hands-on or leadership involvement in both domains. Experience may include silicon architecture, systems, applications, firmware, BSP / SDK, operating systems, drivers, validation, or product engineering.
Proven record of successful semiconductor or embedded-platform launches, from market definition and requirements through customer adoption and production ramp.
Demonstrated product revenue growth, design-win creation, portfolio expansion, or turnaround results supported by concrete business metrics.
Experience creating or scaling a software, tools, IP, and partner ecosystem around a compute product or platform.
Strong customer and partner relationships, with the credibility to engage engineering leaders, product executives, architects, procurement, and business decision makers.
Ability to build rigorous market models, product P&Ls, pricing and margin frameworks, investment cases, forecast ranges, and measurable launch plans.
Excellent leadership and influence skills across matrixed organizations; able to align strong technical and commercial stakeholders without relying solely on direct authority.
Clear executive communication, strong judgment under uncertainty, high ownership, and willingness to move between strategy, detail, and customer execution.
Preferred Qualification:
Experience with RISC-V, Arm, MIPS, or comparable processor architectures; multicore SoCs; MMUs and virtualization; coherent fabrics; cache / DDR subsystems; PCIe, Ethernet, SerDes, or other high-speed interfaces.
Experience with Linux-class products and software enablement, including boot flow, firmware, drivers, SDKs, virtual platforms, FPGA prototyping, evaluation boards, and developer tooling.
Exposure to AI / ML acceleration, vector processing, edge inference, networking offload, functional safety, cybersecurity, HSM / root of trust, or long-lifecycle industrial and automotive products.
Experience managing process-node, foundry, package, test, yield, cost, supply, and lifecycle tradeoffs for semiconductor products.
Experience with configurable platforms, product derivatives, custom silicon, customer IP integration, or platform reuse across multiple end markets.
Established network across customers and ecosystem partners in edge compute, industrial, robotics, machine vision, infrastructure or automotive.
Experience leading geographically distributed teams and operating across engineering, field, partner, and executive communities.
Leadership Profile
Visionary and market-back
Connects technology inflections and customer pain points to a differentiated, investable platform roadmap.
Self-motivated owner
Creates momentum, closes gaps, and drives decisions without waiting for a fully defined playbook.
Technical product leader
Can challenge architects and software leaders while translating tradeoffs into customer and business outcomes.
Commercially accountable
Treats launch, adoption, margin, and revenue as core product responsibilities, not downstream sales tasks.
Ecosystem builder
Understands that processors win through software, tools, partners, reference systems, and developer confidence.
Customer credible
Builds trust through preparation, transparency, technical command, and reliable follow-through.
Platform thinker
Optimizes for reuse and scalable derivatives while recognizing when a strategic customer-specific investment is justified.
Decisive and adaptable
Makes evidence-based decisions with incomplete information, explicitly manages risk, and adjusts quickly as facts change.
Success Measures
Clear, approved platform strategy and roadmap with explicit market, customer, product, software, ecosystem, financial, and process-node choices.
Launch milestones achieved with measurable readiness across silicon, software, tools, boards, documentation, field enablement, supply, and quality.
Priority customer opportunities converted into architecture engagements, design wins, and credible production-revenue paths.
Platform and derivative portfolio demonstrates disciplined reuse of IP, software, validation, infrastructure, and commercial investments.
Ecosystem gaps identified early and closed through internal development, licensing, co-development, or strategic partnerships.
Revenue, margin, design-win pipeline, product adoption, and portfolio return improve against agreed business targets.
Field, customer, partner, and engineering teams operate from one product narrative, one prioritized roadmap, and transparent decision gates.
Preferred Target Talent Pools
Product or platform leaders from embedded processor, MPU, BMC, industrial compute, vision SoC, networking, data-center infrastructure, or edge-AI semiconductor companies.
Experience with products serving multiple markets rather than only a single customer or single vertical.
Experience with customer-funded or anchor-funded platform development models, derivative roadmaps, and ecosystem/software readiness.
Customer-facing credibility with engineering, architecture, platform, and advanced technology teams.
The strongest candidate will combine engineering credibility, whole-product hardware/software judgment, customer and ecosystem leadership, successful launch evidence, and quantified revenue ownership. 64-bit product experience is preferred, but an exceptional 32-bit platform leader with credible SW/Market Focos/ Linux / MPU adjacency should remain in scope.
Expected Salary Range
$171,000.00 - $296,000.00
The exact Salary will be determined based on qualifications, experience and location.

Requests for accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis. Please note that only inquiries concerning a request for reasonable accommodation will be responded to from this email address.

evidence.quote: 10+ years in manufacturing operations, with significant time managing contract manufacturers or outsourced production.
evidence.text:
Director, Contract Manufacturing Operations
Aether
United States
$140,000.00/yr - $200,000.00/yr
About Aether
Aether engineers enzymes and uses them to make materials that are difficult or impossible to produce any other way. The long-term goal is to manufacture more or less anything, quickly and cheaply, anywhere, by drawing on a few billion years of evolution rather than inventing the chemistry from scratch. Today that work pays for itself through advanced print materials. These are shipping into defense and unmanned systems, with revenue and strong customer feedback. Aether is a Series A company that has raised a little over $60M, with a small team based in the San Francisco Bay Area.
The role
Aether manufactures its materials through a network of contract manufacturing organizations (CMOs), covering everything from chemical synthesis through compounding and finished material production. This role owns that network day to day. The VP of Manufacturing selects and qualifies CMO partners. From there, you make sure each partner delivers what it committed to: on time, on spec, and at the agreed cost.
You’ll be Aether’s representative on site at each partner. You’ll know the production plan at every CMO, keep partners accountable to their contracts, and act quickly when things go off track. This role works at the level of plant and site leadership. It’s the counterpart to our process engineers, who work with CMO engineering teams on the technical details. You’ll also keep manufacturing execution in line with commercial demand, so that what Aether sells is what the network can actually produce.
This is one of the first hires in a new manufacturing organization. You’ll be setting how Aether manages its CMO partners for years to come.
What you’ll do
Own day-to-day performance of Aether’s CMO network across multiple sites and production stages.
Ensure each partner has credible production plans that meet Aether’s schedule, specifications, and cost targets.
Hold partners accountable to supply agreements, and escalate and resolve issues directly with site and plant leadership.
Be on site for production campaigns and new CMO onboarding, and support the VP of Manufacturing in standing up new partners.
Coordinate schedules and handoffs between partners where different stages of production happen at different sites.
Translate commercial demand into production plans the CMO network can execute, in partnership with the commercial and supply chain teams.
Track partner performance on delivery, cost, and output, and report it to manufacturing leadership.
Work with quality and process engineering so that CMO execution reflects Aether’s specifications and process requirements.
What you bring
10+ years in manufacturing operations, with significant time managing contract manufacturers or outsourced production.
Experience in chemicals, polymers, specialty materials, or similar process industries.
A track record of holding external partners to commitments. You’re comfortable escalating to plant leadership and can do it without damaging the relationship.
Working fluency in supply agreements, production scheduling, and manufacturing cost drivers.
Strong organizational and program management skills across multiple sites at once.
Willingness to travel 30 to 50% of the time.
Nice to have
Experience working at a CMO or tolling facility, so you know the other side of the table.
Experience at an early-stage or fast-growing company.
Familiarity with ISO 9001 quality systems.
Note
The pay range for this role is $140,000 to $200,000 per year plus equity, with final compensation based on skills and experience.
Aether is committed to building an inclusive and diverse workplace. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and do not discriminate on the basis of age, disability, gender identity or expression, marital or civil-partner status, pregnancy or maternity, race, religion or belief, sex, or sexual orientation. All employment decisions are based on qualifications, merit, and business needs.
We are committed to providing reasonable accommodations for candidates throughout the recruitment process. If you require any adjustments to participate fully in interviews or assessments, please let us know and we will work with you to support your needs.

Collaborate with Manufacturing, Test, and Quality teams to ensure equipment meets production, safety, and compliance requirements
Support equipment upgrades, obsolescence management, and capacity expansion as production scales

Mentor junior engineers and technicians and provide technical leadership across equipment-related efforts
Manage external vendors and integrators as needed for equipment design, build, or modification

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related field
8+ years of experience supporting production equipment, test racks, or test cells in a manufacturing or test environment
Strong hands-on experience with electromechanical systems, controls, instrumentation, and data acquisition
Proven ability to troubleshoot complex equipment issues across hardware, software, and controls domains
Experience developing and maintaining technical documentation for production equipment
Ability to work effectively on the factory floor and in cross-functional engineering teams

Experience supporting automated or semi-automated production and test equipment
Familiarity with PLCs, HMIs, industrial networks, or test software (e.g., LabVIEW, Python, or similar)
Experience with equipment safety standards, lockout/tagout, and risk assessments
Background in scaling equipment from prototype or low-rate production to higher-rate manufacturing
Experience mentoring engineers or leading technical projects without direct authority

VP, Production & Sourcing
Delta Galil Industries
Secaucus, NJ
Company Overview
Delta Galil USA, Inc. is a global manufacturer and marketer of branded and private label apparel products for men, women and children. Since its inception in 1975, the company has continually endeavored to create products that follow a body-before-fabric philosophy, placing equal emphasis on comfort, aesthetics and quality. Delta Galil develops innovative seamless apparel, including bras, shapewear and socks; intimate apparel for women; underwear for men, including under its owned brands Schiesser, Eminence, Organic Basics and Athena; babywear, activewear, sleepwear and loungewear, including under its owned P.J. Salvage and Delta brands. Delta Galil also designs, develops, markets and sells branded denim and apparel under the brand 7 For All Mankind®, and ladies’ and kids’ apparel under the brand Splendid®. In addition, it sells its products under brand names licensed to the company, including adidas, Wolford, Wilson, Columbia, Tommy Hilfiger and others.
Role Overview
The Vice President of Production is responsible for overseeing the end-to-end production process of our product line, ensuring the highest quality of products, timely deliveries, cost-effectiveness, and adherence to the company's standards and values. This role requires strong leadership, strategic planning, and a deep understanding of production processes and industry trends.
﻿Responsibilities
Strategic Oversight: Work cross-functionally with design and sales counterparts to ensure the timely development of fabric, trims, and samples
Leadership: Lead, mentor, and manage the production team, ensuring professional growth and departmental cohesiveness.
Capacity Planning: Work with Core Vendors to ensure Capacity Plans related to fabric, trim, and production are executed in a timely manner to help ensure factory utilization and efficiency
Mills: Ensure the cost of fabric is in line with corporate objectives
Costing: Thorough knowledge of Global CMs (or CPM’s), Estimated Yields, and open costing
Budget Management: Develop and manage production budgets, ensuring cost-efficiencies and profitability.
Vendor Management: Cultivate and maintain relationships with suppliers and vendors, negotiating contracts to achieve optimal terms.
Quality Assurance: Implement quality control measures to ensure the premium quality of the product.
Trend Analysis: Stay updated with industry trends and technological advancements to continuously innovate and improve production processes.
Operational Excellence: Streamline operations to maximize efficiency and minimize waste, maintaining the highest production standards.
Collaboration: Work closely with the design, sales, ESG, and marketing teams to align production with company goals and market demands.
Inventory Management: Collaborate with the logistics team to ensure optimal inventory levels and timely distribution.
Risk Management: Identify potential production risks and implement mitigation strategies.
Sustainability: Advocate and implement sustainable production practices, ensuring environmentally friendly operations.
Requirements:
Minimum 15 years of progressive leadership experience in sourcing, production, and/or global supply chain within the apparel industry, including senior executive (VP-level) responsibility
Proven ability to build, lead, and scale high-performing global sourcing and production organizations across multiple regions
Deep expertise in global costing strategy, including CPMs, CMs, yield optimization, and end-to-end margin architecture
Strong command of raw materials, fabric innovation, trims, and the full product development lifecycle, with the ability to influence product and cost decisions at the concept stage
Demonstrated track record of driving enterprise-level margin improvement through strategic vendor negotiations, cost engineering, and supply chain optimization
Must have experience with intimates.
Extensive experience developing and managing global vendor ecosystems, including offshore partners, with a focus on long-term partnerships, performance, and risk mitigation
Strategic business leader with the ability to translate sourcing and production decisions into financial impact, aligning closely with executive leadership and company-wide goals
Advanced analytical capabilities with a data-driven mindset; leverages tools and insights to inform strategy, forecasting, and decision-making (beyond hands-on execution)
Exceptional executive presence with strong cross-functional leadership and influencing skills across Design, Merchandising, Finance, and Operations
Proven ability to lead through complexity, drive transformation, and implement scalable processes in fast-paced, high-growth environments
Highly strategic, results-oriented, and solutions-driven, with strong operational rigor and a bias for action
Willingness and ability to travel internationally as needed to support global operations and partnerships
This is a hybrid role, with 4 days in our Secaucus, NJ office

Director, New Glenn Program Planning & Controls (PP&C)
Blue Origin
Greater Seattle Area
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
This role supports the development and operations of New Glenn, a single-configuration, heavy-lift orbital launch vehicle capable of routinely carrying people and payloads to low-Earth orbit, geostationary transfer orbit, cislunar, and beyond. Its first stage is fully reusable, and the vehicle was designed from the beginning to be human-capable.
About Blue Origin
Blue Origin is committed to building the infrastructure for humanity's future in space. Our mission is to make space accessible for the benefit of Earth, and New Glenn represents a transformational capability for commercial and government customers. As a leader in commercial spaceflight and aerospace innovation, we are advancing the technologies and processes that will enable humanity to thrive beyond Earth.
About the Role
Blue Origin is seeking an exceptional leader to own the Program Planning & Controls (PP&C) function for the New Glenn program — spanning both 7x2 and 9x4 rockets. As the senior PP&C authority for the program, you will set the multi-year strategy for schedule and risk integration; build and lead a multi-team organization through subordinate managers; integrate AI and automation into all of our scheduling and schedule reporting tools; and serve as the definitive voice on program health in company and customer-facing reviews with NASA, the US Space Force, Amazon, and other stakeholders. You will operate as a peer to Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, and Finance leadership, and will hold decision rights on program-level schedule tradeoffs, baseline change authority, and gate criteria.
What You'll Do
Schedule & Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) Leadership
Build and lead a multi-team PP&C organization through subordinate managers, spanning scheduling, planning, and schedule risk analysis across the 7x2 and 9x4 New Glenn programs
Build and manage relationships with internal and external customers and stakeholders reliant on the New Glenn schedules
Own organizational design, headcount planning, and talent strategy for the PP&C function, including hiring plans to support increasing flight and production cadence
Develop managers and senior individual contributors; build succession depth in schedule, cost, and risk disciplines
Establish the functional standards, guidelines, metrics, and change-management rules that govern PP&C practice across the program
Develop and integrate AI and automation into the scheduling and schedule reporting
Foster a culture of accountability, precision, and collaborative problem-solving aligned with Blue Origin's mission-driven values
Strategy & Decision Authority
Set the multi-year PP&C roadmap for New Glenn, including the maturity path from current state to a fully integrated schedule/risk environment supporting high-rate operations
Hold baseline change authority for the program IMS; approve or escalate baseline changes per program governance
Own "what must be true" decision frameworks and greenlight gate criteria; serve as the accountable authority for the schedule and risk inputs underpinning go/no-go recommendations
Represent the PP&C function in program-level priority and resource tradeoff decisions as a peer to Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, and Finance leadership
Serve as the program's senior functional interface to Blue Origin corporate PP&C, capital governance, and Finance leadership
Schedule & IMS Leadership
Own the program Integrated Master Schedule across the 7x2 and 9x4 New Glen programs and upgrades, including multi-level schedule products (e.g., executive/customer-facing and deeply detailed execution)
Direct critical path and negative float identification, mitigation planning, and executive schedule reviews through subordinate managers
Establish and govern schedule baselines, change control procedures, and variance/trend analysis
Set the methodology standard for schedule risk analysis, including probabilistic and Monte Carlo modeling informing rate runway, capacity planning, and contingency strategy
Own schedule interfaces across vehicle development, production, supply chain, facilities, and launch operations
Sponsor automation and material requirements planning (MRP) integration efforts to simplify status, reporting, and production-system alignment
Ensure risk and opportunity action plans are integrated into schedule products
Program Planning & Controls
Define and own end-to-end PP&C processes spanning schedule, cost, risk, and performance management (Earned Value Management [EVM] or equivalent) across both vehicle generations
Establish the single source of truth integrating supply chain, facilities, and production readiness milestones
Own rolling forecasts and earned value reporting supporting program health visibility to executive leadership
Ensure alignment with operations teams and production systems without duplication
Executive & Customer Engagement
Serve as the accountable schedule and program-controls authority in executive and customer briefings
Own schedule health packages, negative float summaries, cadence updates, and risk assessments presented to senior leadership and external stakeholders
Provide the defensible, data-driven basis for decision memos and go/no-go recommendations
Represent Blue Origin PP&C posture directly to government and commercial customer leadership
Partner with enterprise and business unit technology leadership to mature schedule tooling and capability
What You Bring
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Business, or related technical field (or equivalent professional experience)
14+ years of program planning, scheduling, or PP&C experience in aerospace, defense, or other complex hardware/manufacturing programs
8+ years of leadership experience, including 3+ years managing managers or leading multi-team functions
Demonstrated experience standing up or substantially maturing a PP&C function at program or enterprise scale
Deep expertise in IMS development, critical path method, and schedule risk analysis (Monte Carlo or similar)
Proven experience as the accountable functional authority in executive and external customer forums
Experience owning functional budget and headcount planning (new)
Strong proficiency with scheduling tools (Primavera P6, MS Project, or OPP) and PP&C/EVM systems
Demonstrated ability to operate in high-ambition, fast-paced environments balancing cost, schedule, and technical tradeoffs
Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and cross-functional collaboration skills
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting both a legacy/production vehicle program and a next-generation development program simultaneously
Familiarity with launch vehicle or spacecraft production environments, high-rate manufacturing ramp-up, or similar complex first-of-a-kind industrial scale-up
Experience with capital planning, value engineering, and facility/production capacity planning
Knowledge of NASA or government contracting processes, regulations and customer requirements
Active or eligible for a security clearance
PMP, IPMP, or similar program management certification
What Success Looks Like in This Role
A single, trusted, fully integrated and defensible IMS across cadence and development programs that leadership and customers rely on for decision-making and confidence
Reduced schedule surprises through proactive critical path and negative float management, enabling predictable program execution; using AI and automation tools to efficiently capture and communicate schedule
A mature, scalable PP&C organization led by a developed management bench scalable PP&C organization capable of supporting increasing flight/production cadence without loss of rigor or visibility
Strong cross-functional trust and alignment between Program, Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, Facilities, and Operations
Demonstrated ability to influence executive decision-making through clear, data-driven schedule and risk communication
A team of engaged, skilled planners and controls professionals who take ownership of program health and continuous improvement and work to a standard set of guidelines, metrics and change management rules
Base Pay Range for:
WA applicants is $203,165.00 - $284,430.30
Other site ranges may differ
Culture Statement
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
Export Control Regulations
Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
Background Check
Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
Benefits
Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
Paid Time Off: Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.
Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.
Equal Employment Opportunity
Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.
Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation
Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. Please note this is a publicly managed inbox. Please do not include any personal medical information in your request.

evidence.text:
Sr. Manager, SIOP & Operational Excellence
G&H (Gooch & Housego)
New Port Richey, FL
About Us
Join a Global Photonics Leader: Engineering Solutions from the Deep Ocean to Outer Space!
Gooch & Housego (G&H) is a global precision photonics manufacturer serving the industrial, aerospace & defense, life sciences, and semiconductor markets. With operations across North America, Europe, and Asia, G&H designs and manufactures advanced optical components, systems, and subsystems that enable some of the world’s most demanding applications.
THE OPPORTUNITY
We are seeking a Sr. Manager, SIOP & Operational Excellence
, to lead and strengthen the Sales, Inventory, and Operations Planning process and drive operational excellence across our Optical Systems US operations. This role will align demand, supply, capacity, and financial plans and establish a consistent operating model to improve operational performance, delivery reliability, and inventory management.
Site leadership retains ownership of execution and results at each site. This role owns the planning process, standards, governance, and performance visibility, and partners with site teams to align on common standards and drive operational excellence across US sites.
The successful candidate will work closely with Sales, Operations, Finance, Engineering, and Supply Chain to establish consistent planning processes, improve visibility, and support informed business decisions across a complex, high-mix manufacturing environment.
This role requires 25% to 50% of travel to our locations in Keene, NH, Tampa, FL, Rochester, NY and Moorpark, CA.
Key Responsibilities
SIOP Leadership & Process Management
Lead the end-to-end SIOP process, including demand and supply reviews, executive planning meetings, and alignment of operational and financial objectives.
Establish and continuously improve standardized planning processes, governance, and performance metrics across Optical Systems US operations.
Drive accountability and cross-functional alignment to ensure planning decisions support business priorities, capacity requirements, and customer commitments.
Demand, Supply & Capacity Planning
Partner with Sales and Product Management to establish the demand planning process, review forecasts and customer requirements, and identify potential changes in demand.
Partner with site Operations, Engineering, and Supply Chain leaders, who own production, procurement, and capacity plans, to ensure those plans are aligned with demand and achievable.
Work with site teams to identify supply constraints, capacity limitations, and operational risks, and ensure scenarios and mitigation plans are in place to support business continuity.
Inventory & Operational Performance
Partner with site leadership to define inventory strategies and policies that optimize material availability, working capital, and service levels while minimizing excess and obsolete inventory.
Define standards for inventory targets, safety stock requirements, and planning parameters, and monitor adherence across sites.
Monitor and report key performance indicators across US sites, including forecast accuracy, on-time delivery, backlog, inventory turns, and capacity utilization, and partner with site leaders on improvement actions.
Analytics, Systems & Continuous Improvement
Leverage ERP/MRP systems, reporting tools, and data analytics to improve planning accuracy, visibility, and decision-making.
Provide leadership with actionable insights, performance reporting, and recommendations to address risks, trade-offs, and improvement opportunities.
Strengthen planning and continuous improvement capabilities across sites through process standardization, cross-functional collaboration, coaching, tools, and methods so improvement is owned and sustained locally.
Operational Excellence
Work closely with site management to establish a common operating cadence, standards, and governance by which sites plan, execute, and improve, with site leadership retaining ownership of execution and results.
Develop and lead a multi-year operational excellence roadmap aligned with business strategy and company priorities.
Partner with site teams to define which processes are common across the business and which are site-specific, and keep both current as the business grows.
Support a consistent performance management framework across sites, including tiered accountability (Tier 1 through 3), KPI definitions, data standards, and reporting, so performance is visible, comparable, and acted on at every level.
Support site leaders through change management as new sites, systems, and processes are integrated into a consistent way of operating.
Identify and prioritize improvement opportunities across cost, quality, delivery, and working capital, and report results and measurable business impact to senior leadership.
Skills & Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field; advanced degree preferred.
8 to 12+ years of progressive experience in supply chain, operations, planning, or business transformation, including 3 to 5 years in SIOP, operations, or transformation leadership roles.
Experience in high-mix, low-to-medium volume manufacturing environments; precision optics, aerospace and defense, or similar industries preferred.
Demonstrated success implementing, leading, or improving SIOP or operational excellence processes across complex manufacturing operations.
Experience leading multi-site process standardization and organizational change.
Strong knowledge of demand forecasting, capacity planning, inventory management, and supply chain optimization.
Proficiency with ERP/MRP systems and planning tools, including SYSPRO, SAP, Oracle, or comparable platforms.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to translate complex data into actionable business recommendations.
Excellent communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.
Proven ability to manage competing priorities, navigate operational constraints, and drive accountability and continuous improvement.
APICS/ASCM certifications (CPIM or CSCP) or IBF certification preferred.
Additional Notes
This job description is not intended to be exhaustive in every respect, but rather to clearly define the fundamental purpose, responsibilities and dimensions for the role. Therefore, this job description does not describe any individual role holder. In addition to the contents of this job description, employees are expected to undertake all other reasonable and related tasks allocated by their line manager.
This position involves access to technology and data controlled under U.S. export regulations (ITAR/EAR); U.S. citizenship is required.
The Company is committed to providing equal employment opportunities for all employees and applicants for employment.

Director, Product Development Engineering (CNC Machining)
VulcanForms Inc.
Ayer, MA
About Us
Founded in 2015 to develop the world’s first industrially scalable laser metal additive manufacturing solution, VulcanForms is reshaping how the world manufactures critical products. We build and operate advanced digital infrastructure that enables innovation, accelerates growth, and supports sustainability across aerospace, defense, medical, and other essential industries. Through our vertically integrated capabilities, including scalable additive manufacturing and precision machining, we deliver true end-to-end production at scale by combining cutting-edge technology with a foundation of proven industrial craftsmanship. Our team brings deep expertise in manufacturing, materials science, software, automation, and operations, united by a shared commitment to quality, curiosity, and accountability. We foster an inclusive culture where people take ownership, solve meaningful problems, and continuously learn, because we believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes.
Job Purpose
As the Director, Product Development Engineering (CNC Machining) at VulcanForms, you will serve as the strategic technical executive responsible for leading, scaling, and unifying our medical device product development engineering organization for precision subtractive manufacturing. In this high-visibility role, you will architect the overarching engineering strategy for multi-axis CNC machining platforms (5-axis milling, Swiss turning, EDM), advanced CAM workflows, fixture design, and post-processing integration specifically tailored for high-consequence medical device applications. Products in this portfolio are manufactured through laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF), with CNC machining performed on 3D-printed, near-net-shape substrates to achieve final geometry, tolerances, and surface finish. You will own the phase-gated pathway from medical device design input through process validation and a formal handover to Operations for full-rate serial production—translating customer requirements into scalable engineering frameworks that set industry standards for dimensional accuracy, surface finish, system reliability, and yield across our commercial medical programs. You will manage and grow a multidisciplinary team of senior, principal, and product development engineers while acting as a key technical authority across hardware, software, tooling, quality, and operations. By establishing rigorous engineering governance, driving Design for Manufacturability (DFM) methodologies, building robust inspection strategies, optimizing manufacturing workflows, and expanding customer technical partnerships, you will ensure VulcanForms delivers production-ready, implantable, and surgical-grade components for our most strategic medical device customers.
Key Responsibilities
Executive Engineering Leadership & Strategy: Define and execute the long-term roadmap for medical device product development engineering for subtractive (CNC) manufacturing, from customer design input through production release; establish organizational KPIs, engineering governance, and resource loading models to support rapid company scaling.
Phase-Gated Development & Transfer to Operations: Govern the end-to-end framework for transitioning complex multi-axis CNC machining processes, fixture architectures, and digital CAM workflows through a phase-gated development process (feasibility, process development, verification and validation via IQ/OQ/PQ, and pilot production) into high-volume serial production; define gate entry/exit criteria and lead a formal handover to Operations covering released process documentation, control plans, trained operators, and demonstrated process capability (Cpk), with defined post-transfer sustaining support.
Team Building & Talent Development: Build, mentor, and retain a world-class team of product development engineers, CAM programmers, tooling specialists, and technical leads; cultivate a culture of technical excellence, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Strategic Customer & Executive Engagement: Serve as the primary technical authority for tier-one medical device OEM customers, executive leadership, and strategic partners; lead high-stakes technical reviews, program launches, and co-development initiatives.
Top-Down DFM & Cross-Functional Governance: Institutionalize advanced Design for Manufacturability and Inspectability (DFM/DFI) methodologies, applied early in the medical device design cycle and tailored to precision CNC machining (milling, turning, grinding, EDM) and ensure seamless cross-functional integration with upstream processes (e.g., LPBF blank feeds) and downstream operations (heat treatment, passivation, surface finishing, and automated CMM inspection).
Manufacturing Workflow Optimization & Yield: Optimize end-to-end manufacturing workflows (cycle time, setup reduction, toolpath and fixture strategy, work-cell flow, and in-process automation) using lean and value stream mapping; drive organization-wide corrective and preventive action (CAPA) frameworks for complex machining defects, tool wear anomalies, and geometric stack-up issues, leveraging advanced data analytics, statistical process control (SPC), and iterative testing to maximize yield.
Inspection Methods, Quality & Compliance: Define risk-based inspection strategies across CMM, optical/vision metrology, surface roughness measurement, in-process probing, and CT scanning; lead test method validation (TMV) and measurement system analysis (gauge R&R); establish and govern standardized operating procedures (SOPs), tooling/fixturing baselines, First Article Inspection (FAI) protocols, and engineering change management processes compliant with ISO 13485 and FDA QMSR (21 CFR 820) requirements.
Qualifications
10+ years of progressive engineering and technical leadership experience in advanced subtractive manufacturing, with a proven track record of building and managing high-performing engineering teams in multi-axis CNC machining (5-axis milling, Swiss turning, EDM) for implantable and surgical medical device product development.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Aerospace, or Systems Engineering; Master’s degree is preferred.
Demonstrated executive presence with a track record of driving cross-functional alignment across R&D, Operations, Quality, and Commercial teams while serving as a trusted technical partner to C-suite leadership and external customers.
Deep mastery of precision subtractive manufacturing fundamentals, including advanced multi-axis CNC machining, fixture design, tool path optimization, metallurgy, complex GD&T (ASME Y14.5), inspection methods (CMM, optical/vision metrology, surface profilometry, in-process probing, and CT), measurement system analysis (gauge R&R), and statistical process control (SPC).
Proven experience leading phase-gated medical device product development, through design transfer, process validation (IQ/OQ/PQ), and formal handover to Operations for full-rate serial production, under ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820.
Strong expertise in manufacturing workflow optimization (lean, value stream mapping, cycle-time and setup reduction) and integrated manufacturing workflows, including hybrid manufacturing (additive-to-subtractive workflows), passivation, electropolishing, cleanroom packaging, and non-destructive testing (NDT).
Practical, hands-on manufacturing skills, including medical device cleaning and cleaning validation, cleanroom packaging and sterile barrier systems, and QC inspection (receiving, in-process, and final inspection using CMM, optical comparators, and manual gauging), with the ability to work directly on the shop floor alongside technicians and operators.
Preferred Qualifications
Prior experience building or scaling product development or application engineering departments within high-growth medical device or advanced manufacturing technology companies.
Experience processing 3D-printed metal substrates (e.g., LPBF parts), including datum establishment on as-built geometry, support removal, stock allowance management, and machining of near-net-shape features.
Experience with enterprise-level CAD/CAM software, machining simulation tools, and digital manufacturing suites (e.g., Siemens NX CAM, Mastercam, Esprit, Vericut).
Hands-on familiarity with medical-grade materials (Titanium Ti-6Al-4V ELI, CoCr, Stainless Steel 316L/17-4PH, PEEK) and associated cutting tool physics/coolant delivery methodologies.
Certified Quality Engineer (CQE) or Six Sigma Black Belt credentials.
VulcanForms offers a competitive salary and equity package. Actual compensation is based on factors such as the candidate's skills, qualifications, and experience. In addition, VulcanForms provides comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, and life insurance; generous paid time off; and a 401(k) plan with company match.
The annual base salary range for this position is $176,000 to $242,000

About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
As the Principal Manufacturing Engineer (Payloads)
at Varda, you will own the manufacturing and integration processes for the mission-critical payload systems that define what Varda's reentry capsules actually do in space. Varda's payloads — including pharmaceutical processing hardware, microgravity experiment modules, and government and commercial customer systems — represent the core value proposition of every mission. This role demands both technical breadth and meticulous process discipline: you will interface with external payload customers, internal design teams, and the vehicle integration team to ensure every payload is ready to fly. Continuous Improvement Manager
Arcosa Inc.
Steele, AL
Meyer Utility Structures, an Arcosa subsidiary, is searching for a Continuous Improvement Manager for our Steele, Alabama plant. In this role, you will drive sustainable continuous improvements within the facility, delivering breakthrough results in safety, quality, delivery and cost while developing cultural change and engagement throughout the organization.  The CI Leader works closely with plant leadership and department employees to achieve results.  This position requires strong technical lean manufacturing and hands-on leadership skills, along with a passion for operations excellence to be successful.
What You'll Do
Implement operational excellence and continuous improvement strategies that directly tie-in with the site’s KPI’s (measurable results and sustainment will be tied in with performance reviews)
Lead and facilitate data-driven Kaizen events to identify constraints and drive sustainable improvements and work closely with plant personnel
Lead and facilitate events to identify and systematically reduce all forms of waste.
Develop and execute improvement action plans with specific owners and completion dates
Develop a Lean Culture within the facility engaging individuals from the shop floor up
Develop tracking tools and measures to support key KPI initiatives such as increasing efficiency, throughput/capacity, and reducing shop cost per unit rates
Develop business case justification for projects and initiatives
Create best practices to better leverage resources across all facilities
Provide and teach CI tools to team members
Build a CI culture across the organization
Assist in the development and implementation of capital projects, including equipment feasibility studies, working with key stakeholders
Provide guidance on staffing, training, employee relations and performance management to develop and enhance the Operations function, working closely with direct reports
What You'll Need
Minimum of five (5) years in a manufacturing environment
Minimum of three (3) years of Continuous Improvement experience required
Extensive technical skills and hands-on experience in continuous improvement manufacturing activities
Self-starter who can easily engage other individuals across all jobs and responsibilities within the plant and organization
Strong application knowledge of LEAN manufacturing techniques and related Continuous Improvement tools
Knowledge of Lean Daily Management, Kaizen, Value Stream Mapping, Standard Work, 5S, Kanban, 8 wastes, TPM and SMED changeover reduction
Bachelor’s degree from an accredited four-year college or university (Engineering, Math, Science, Business or Operations preferred) or equivalent combination of education and work experience

Plant Integrated Work Systems Manager
Golden State Foods
Burleson, TX
Description
ABOUT GOLDEN STATE FOODS
Golden State Foods is a distinguished leader in the food service industry, offering an extensive array of products and services to a diverse clientele. Rooted in the values of quality service and integrity, we are dedicated to creating a supportive and inclusive atmosphere where employees can advance, innovate, and contribute to our ongoing success.
Job Summary
Directs, manages and provides guidance in driving positive change in the facility, including development and up skilling of 200+ associates. The key areas of focus are safety, training and implementing the GSF defined improvement process. Ensures appropriate measurements are developed and implemented to create benchmarks and targets. Develops plans and actions to ensure goals are achieved or exceeded.
Primary Responsibilities
Serving as a member of the Plant Leadership Team to collaboratively set strategies, masterplan activities, employee engagement activities, loss elimination ideas, and results delivery.
Developing the cultural vision for the plant that provides the foundation for the IWS journey.
Continually expanding and enhancing knowledge levels of Integrated Work Systems, lean manufacturing, Total Productive Maintenance, and industry “best in class” manufacturing methodologies and operations practices to develop a culture of continuous improvement – will need to stay about 12 months ahead of the plant in personal knowledge.
Leading the plant leadership team in the integration of the appropriate actions to support the cultural vision and to support the delivery of the Compelling Business Need. Be the change agent within the plant leadership team that brings a focus to ‘how’ results are delivered and sustained (“IWS is the work”).
Building capability of the site leaders to implement IWS systems, tools, methodologies, capabilities, and standards.
Ensuring CI tools and methodologies are used to drive all site result opportunities and to ensure all results are being sustained or improved per the site masterplan – own “how” breakthrough performance is achieved at the plant level.
Responsible for the phased implementation of IWS at the plant & benchmarking with other plants in the division to drive best practices & standard work.
Leading the Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE) process including maintaining measurement standards, coaching on improvement plans and strategies, training, coaching, and monthly reporting.
Establishing and maintaining plant KPI’s and visual plant tools.

Education and experience equivalent to:
Education/Certification
Bachelor’s degree in engineering preferred from an accredited college or university.
Experience
5 or more years of relevant work experience.
Knowledge, Skills And Abilities
Knowledge of (B/basic; J/journey; E/expert):
Project management concepts and techniques (J)
Regulatory policies and procedures (J)
Budgetary concepts and procedures (J)
PC word processing/spreadsheet/presentation/database software (J)
Continuous Improvement concepts and processes (E)
Skill And Ability To
Strategically influence all levels of the organization.
Serve as a team member, facilitator and/or leader as the team role warrants
Manage and motivate employees in a team-based environment
Prepare a variety of comprehensive administrative and technical documents and reports
Prepare and deliver presentations to a variety of customers
Travel via airplane and drive an automobile
Work effectively in a general business environment, with a focus on high levels of quality and customer service
Act in accordance with GSF’s Values and Creed
Experience / working knowledge of continuous improvement methodologies – TPM, lean manufacturing, IWS, etc.
Ability to teach, coach, & develop others – both on the plant floor & on the plant leadership team
Long term planning (strategic) with intermediate actions along the way (tactical)
Process-driven, loss-focused, results-oriented approach
Problem solving skill-set (by degree – engineering or by experience)
Proven leadership skills
Collaboration – ability to partner with & influence others
LEADERSHIP/MANAGEMENT RESPONSIBILITY
Directs Safety/Training Manager and TPM Supervisor. May manage various external vendors.

Productivity/quality standards: accuracy, timeliness, thoroughness
Training budget and related expenses

Teamwork within the department and across departments
Project/assignment standards
Customer satisfaction
Employee development to meet GSF’s projected near- and mid-term objectives

People First: At Golden State Foods, we're not just a company; we're a dynamic community where your talents are celebrated, and your ambitions are nurtured.

evidence.text:
Engineering Quality Manager, CPU
Arm
Austin, TX
Job ID
2026-19684 Date posted
28/10/2026 Location
Austin, Texas Category
Quality
Interested in working with some of the world's most advanced processor technologies and helping make them even better?
We are looking for an Engineering Quality Manager
to join our Central Engineering Quality and Compliance team and work closely with Arm's CPU teams to improve product quality and how we develop, deliver and maintain our IP.
This role covers the CPU development lifecycle, from requirements and design to verification, release and long-term maintenance. It involves working directly with engineers, reviewing existing practices, using data to identify problems and helping teams find better ways of working.
We value curiosity, technical understanding and people who enjoy solving complex problems, asking questions and learning new things. There are opportunities to work across different teams, explore new methods and tools, and contribute your own ideas.
What You'll Do
Provide independent quality oversight for CPU product development and readiness, working with engineering teams to identify risks, review evidence and support decisions throughout the product lifecycle.
Lead quality circles and problem-solving activities, contributing to engineering review boards, defect investigations, root cause analysis and corrective actions. Support urgent customer issues and errata resolution, working with teams to assess impact and resolve issues.
Improve verification effectiveness and engineering quality, introducing practical tools and helping teams strengthen requirements, design and verification practices to prevent problems and detect defects earlier.
Use quality data to identify problems and trends, analyzing errata, quality metrics and customer feedback to understand recurring issues and areas requiring attention.
Find ways to simplify development activities, reduce unnecessary work and share effective methods and lessons learned across Arm.
What We're Looking For
Experience in semiconductor development, verification or engineering quality, with an understanding of RTL/VLSI design, defect management or complex IP development.
Good analytical and problem-solving skills, including root cause analysis, risk identification and the ability to use engineering data to support decisions.
Curiosity about how engineering processes work and an interest in finding ways to improve them.
Good communication skills, with the confidence to challenge experienced engineers constructively, collaborate across teams and respond quickly when priorities change.
Nice to Have
Experience in any of the following areas would be valuable, but is not essential:
CPU architecture, semiconductor productization or hardware/software integration.
Engineering standards, Quality Management Systems, Functional Safety, Automotive Quality or Cybersecurity.
Engineering quality metrics, data analytics, AI or automation tools.
We welcome candidates from different engineering backgrounds. Experience in every area listed above is not required.
Salary Range
$249,900-$338,100 per year
We value people as individuals and our dedication is to reward people competitively and equitably for the work they do and the skills and experience they bring to Arm. Salary is only one component of Arm's offering. The total reward package will be shared with candidates during the recruitment and selection process.
Our 10x Mindset
About
At Arm, we believe progress happens when people are empowered to think bigger and push beyond what seems possible. Our 10x mindset is about curiosity, ambition and creating impact that will be used by millions. We learn fast, prioritise collaboration and turn bold ideas into real technology. We look for people who are inspired by this way of working and want to grow in an environment where bold ideas are welcomed. Discover how the 10x mindset shapes life at Arm:
Use of AI in Your Application
At Arm, we embrace the benefits AI can bring, including in recruitment. You may use AI to support your preparation, such as improving the clarity of written responses, practicing interview questions, or learning more about our industry. However, your application and interview responses must reflect your own thinking, experience, and abilities. We want to understand your authentic perspective, creativity, and approach to problem solving. As such, you may not use AI to complete assigned tasks as part of any assessments. If you plan to use AI-supported or assistive technologies as part of a reasonable adjustment, please contact
Recruitment Adjustments and Accommodations
At Arm, we want to build extraordinary teams. If you need an adjustment or an accommodation during the recruitment process, please email
Hybrid Working
Arm’s approach to hybrid working is designed to create a working environment that supports both high performance and personal wellbeing. We believe in bringing people together face to face to enable us to work at pace, whilst recognizing the value of flexibility. Within that framework, we empower groups/teams to determine their own hybrid working patterns, depending on the work and the team’s needs. Details of what this means for each role will be shared upon application. In some cases, the flexibility we can offer is limited by local legal, regulatory, tax, or other considerations, and where this is the case, we will collaborate with you to find the best solution. Please talk to us to find out more about what this could look like for you.
Equal Opportunities
Arm is an equal opportunity employer, committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal opportunities are available to all applicants and colleagues. We are a diverse organization of dedicated and innovative individuals, and don’t discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

evidence.quote: You have 5-7+ years of varied experience in an operating role at a high-growth technology company, starting a venture, or in finance or consulting
evidence.text:
Head of Business Line Operations - Tactical Effects
Anduril Industries
Costa Mesa, California, United States
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
The Tactical Recon and Strike (TRS) team at Anduril develops aerial small drones (Group 1-3) and all equipment to test, deploy and operate. The team is responsible for taking products like Ghost, Bolt, Anvil, and Altius from paper sketches to operational systems. The Tactical Effects Team is a cornerstone business line of the TRS group that is going through tremendous growth. We work in close coordination with specialist teams to solve some of the hardest problems facing our customers. The TRS Operations team is a small but mighty team of business generalists who ‘solve for scale’ the specific business problems that hamper efficiency or productivity. One project may have you solving staffing inefficiencies across engineering teams, while another project may have you working across manufacturing, supply chain, and quality teams to help address capacity or production challenges. We are looking for the Head of Operations to support our Ghost and Precision Engagement Systems business lines, based in Costa Mesa, CA.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Own all aspects of business operations and infrastructure, ensuring business development, engineering, and production teams have what they need when they need it to execute
Serve as the General Manager’s chief strategist to balance resource and execution risk against our massive growth plans, regularly monitoring financials to help guide us toward our profitability targets
Translate growth signals into demand across all operational infrastructure including staffing, real estate, test ranges, classified infrastructure, and production and collaborate with cross-functional partners across Anduril to deliver
Own the business line’s governance structure from business reviews to annual planning and employee onboarding to all hands, developing and evolving information pathways as the organization scales
Collaborate closely with division leadership to evolve the organizational structure and define and implement strong hiring, onboarding, and execution standards for key functions so we maintain a culture of “doing things differently”
Execute on special projects, evolve internal processes, spearhead the stand up of new functions, and lead M&A efforts as needed
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
You have 5-7+ years of varied experience in an operating role at a high-growth technology company, starting a venture, or in finance or consulting
You love solving complex, ambiguous, cross-functional problems in a people-centric way
You’re both high ownership and low ego, approaching everything with strong outcome orientation and high humility
You’re highly detail oriented and data-driven
You’re discerning and an incredibly fast learner
You’re tactical and enjoy getting into the details.
US Salary Range
$183,000—$243,000 USD
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
Benefits
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.
Data Privacy
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

evidence.text:
Director, Manufacturing
ASTEC
Parsons, KS
BUILT TO CONNECT
Astec is a global, environmentally focused infrastructure and manufacturing company of asphalt road building and aggregate processing. Our mission is to design and build the most innovative products for the industries we serve. Leveraging innovative solutions and technologies, we serve customers all over the world.
About The Position
The Director of Manufacturing will lead manufacturing activities while executing strategic initiatives and coordinating resources to fabricate, paint, and assemble heaters, tanks, piping, and accessories. The Director of Manufacturing will provide oversight to management and operations staff with the primary goal being to ensure a work environment that promotes safety, quality, and productivity while driving continuous improvement activities.
Key Deliverables
Responsible for all manufacturing operations including the safety, production efficiencies, quality, and customer service.
Leads team members by managing and executing plant processes.
Supports continuous improvement processes to ensure safety, quality, goals are cost, and customer service are met.
Creates and maintains an engaged and team-oriented workforce to meet business demand.
Comply with all of Astec’s safety protocols.
Key Activities & Responsibilities
Manage the manufacturing facility by ensuring all safety, quality, delivery, and financial goals and standards are consistently met
Ensure a healthy and safe working environment while complying with federal and state regulations through active collaboration with environmental, health, and safety (EHS) staff
Lead the manufacturing organization to build a strong culture of employee engagement and involvement, productivity, and accountability
Assist general manager with long-range operational goals, expansion efforts, and implementation of new and advanced technology to drive improvement and reduce costs in our products
Organize departmental management structure and teams for optimal, efficient operations
Work with company controller to develop operating budgets and meet targets for efficiency, costs, hours, and absorption.
Participate in the S&OP (Sales and Operation Planning) process with other site managers to understand the business conditions and make manpower and continuous improvement decisions to support the operation
