Senior Manager, Product Operations
Anduril Industries
Costa Mesa, California, United States
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
ABOUT THE TEAM
Frontier Systems (AFS) is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized hardware and software products for defense, law enforcement, and intelligence customers. We work alongside our customers to understand their requirements and deliver exquisite capabilities across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers' most pressing national security requirements.
Product Operations is the team accountable for the health of the systems and technology that delivers the capabilities that our customers depend on. The function identifies, triages, and drives resolution of incidents across the deployed fleet, and converts what we've learned into the reliability and sustainment insights that product and engineering teams act upon. We work in close coordination with product engineering, reliability, quality, program management, and field operations teams to maximize capability availability for our end users and inform the next cycle of iterations.
ABOUT THE ROLE
As the Senior Manager of Product Operations for Frontier Systems, you will own product operations across the division's product portfolio and the programs that deliver those products. You will lead multiple Product Operations managers, each of whom runs a team of technical specialists and engineers focused on supporting and improving fielded products. The division's portfolio is scaling, and this role exists to scale support alongside it, both for the products the function covers today and for the ones that reach the field next.
This is a function maturation and growth role as much as an operating one, and the work rewards depth. The position requires a strong problem-solving mindset, enough technical depth to follow the work of the engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic systems, and the judgment to make decisions whose impact reaches beyond your own team and the current planning cycle. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Lead and Grow the Function: Lead Product Operations across the Frontier Systems portfolio, managing multiple teams and driving the growth of both sustainment capability and resourcing across the division. Own hiring, performance, development, and organizational design, while also maturing the function itself: the operating model, the standards, and the capability of the people in it.
Own Service Quality, Internal and External: Hold accountability for the quality of product support delivered to external customers and to internal Anduril teams. Understand the work at every level, both how it is expected to be done and how it is actually being done, and close the distance between the two.
Scale Support Operations Across the Portfolio: Think strategically about how support scales across the division's full portfolio, current and future. Extend Product Operations coverage to new products and programs as they reach fielded maturity, standing up scope, coverage, escalation paths, and support infrastructure where none exists. All while holding service quality steady as the fielded population grows.
Align Capacity to Demand: Align support headcount demand to measured support volume, fielded asset population, and product delivery schedules. Own annual headcount planning for the function and produce defensible demand calculations when planning cycles call for them.
Own the Failure Signal and the fielded product Reliability Loop: Own the workflow that converts field failures into structured, trustworthy signal for product and reliability engineering, spanning failure mode classification, root cause corrective action cycle performance, and recurrence measurement. Partner with engineering to abstract individual incidents into systemic improvements, holding engineering partners accountable to the signal provided and your own organization accountable to its fidelity.
Set the Support and Sustainment Standard: Establish and enforce the standards by which the organization triages, diagnoses, escalates, and resolves product incidents, including the severity discipline that determines what reaches engineering and when. Mature the sustainment approach for complex electromechanical products supporting the evolution of maintenance, spares and hardware action, configuration and calibration management, and the self-service and tooling investments that reduce support burden over time.
Sponsor Function Initiatives: Outline and sponsor the initiatives that mature the function, defining the end state, the measure of success, and the resourcing. Then hold program management partners accountable for leading and delivering the targeted outcomes.
Be the Interface for Support Requirements: Serve as the point of contact program teams come to when assessing product and customer service support requirements for new and expanding programs. Characterize the cost of the service and define the contract and pricing structures that fund it, in support of proposals and modifications.
Brief Executive Stakeholders: Represent product support to business line and division leadership through recurring reviews of fleet health, reliability trends, sustainment cost, and the maturation of the service. Surface systemic problems with evidence, drive cross-functional prioritization, and help deeply technical teams, program stakeholders, and operators in the field understand each other.
Travel and Availability: Ability to travel up to 20% to support customer needs and operations, and to work non-standard hours when fielded operations require it.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Proven Technical Leadership: 8+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (robotics, aerospace, defense, automotive, or other electromechanical domains).
Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, industrial, or field support).
Organizational Leadership: Experience leading managers and multi-team organizations, with accountability for outcomes across more than one product line or program.
Incident Workflow Ownership: Experience owning incident-driven workflows at a standard-setting level, including triage, diagnosis, severity assignment, escalation, and resolution across a fielded fleet.
Technical Depth: Enough technical depth to follow the work of engineers and specialists supporting fielded robotic and electromechanical systems, including the ability to reason across hardware, software, and networking boundaries.
Reliability Workflow Familiarity: Demonstrated familiarity with product improvement or reliability lifecycles and processes.
Sustainment Approach: Experience defining a sustainment model for fielded hardware across its service life, spanning maintenance, spares, and the tooling or self-service investments that reduce support burden.
Capacity and Cost Modeling: Experience building and defending quantitative models that size support demand, headcount, or cost, including owning annual planning for a function and stating the assumptions behind the model.
Program Management: Project and program management ability applied outside a project management role: decomposing requirements into deliverables, synthesizing information from several sources into a clear recommendation, and driving that recommendation to a result across multiple functions.
Executive Influence: Proven ability to align senior cross-functional leadership and influence outcomes without authority over the people who deliver them, including briefing executive stakeholders on operational performance.
Communication: Excellent written, visual, and verbal communication skills, and confidence navigating ambiguity and establishing new ways of working where none exist.
Clearance: Active or eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance. Holding clearances or background investigations in the past is a plus.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:
Experience establishing a product support or sustainment function from the ground up, including defining the operating model, growing the team, and running remote support operations for complex robotics systems.
Defense, law enforcement, or other government agency experience leading air defense, intelligence, and/or force protection teams.
Consulting or process maturation project experience, and formal training or certification in a continuous improvement or project management disciplines (such as Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, Agile, or PMP).
Fluency with structured root cause methods such as fault tree analysis, fishbone, or 8D problem solving.
Working knowledge of reliability engineering fundamentals, including failure distributions, mean time between failure and maintenance, and reliability growth.
Hands-on exposure to the failure behavior of fielded robotic and sensor systems, including actuation, power systems, sensing, embedded compute, radar, RF detection, and electro-optical and infrared sensing, and the ability to diagnose connectivity and networking faults across distributed field systems.
Comfort reading logs, telemetry, and test data, including hands-on use of Linux command-line interfaces and tooling such as Grafana, Datadog, Jira, Git, SQL, and Palantir Foundry.
Experience translating support scope into contract or pricing structures for operations and sustainment, and familiarity with proposal efforts.
Fluency with the data layer of sustainment, including incident management systems, asset and configuration data, service bill of materials, and cost association.
Experience in on-call support operations and limited risk tolerance environments.
An active U.S. Secret clearance or higher, prior military service, or a defense and STEM background.
US Salary Range
$147,000—$196,000 USD
The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:
Benefits
At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next. For more information, Explore Our Benefits.
Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams
Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.
To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:
No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.
Please always verify communications:
Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.
Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.
Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach: If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.
What to Do If You Suspect Fraud: Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to contact@anduril.com. Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.
Data Privacy
To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/.
By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency. Use of this provider helps to ensure compliance with applicable laws and protect technology, intellectual property, and organizational security.

evidence.text:
Director of Quality Assurance
Sound Community Services, Inc.
New London, CT
Position Title:
Director of Quality Assurance
Department/Area:
Quality Assurance
Reports to:
Senior Director of Quality Assurance
Employment Status:
Full-Time; Non-Union
EXCELLENT BENEFITS PACKAGE:
Earn an additional week of paid time off including floating holidays, and personal time! Plus,
13 paid holidays per year, and paid sick time!
Company paid Life Insurance,
Company paid Accidental Death & Dismemberment Insurance,
401K,
Opt-in benefits available: Pet Insurance, Employee/Spouse/Child Life Insurance, and Long Term Disability,
Plus, Medical, Dental, & Vision Insurance!
Organization Overview:
Sound Community Services, Inc. (SCSI) is a private, not-for-profit organization dedicated to educating, assisting, and supporting individuals with persistent mental illness and substance use disorders. We work tirelessly to create a culture and environment in which recovery and wellness are possible.
Position Overview:
The Director of Quality Assurance (QA) oversees all agency activities related to quality improvement, compliance, data integrity, and regulatory preparedness for the agency. This position provides leadership in the development, implementation, and monitoring of systems that support clinical excellence, consumer rights, performance measurement, and regulatory compliance. The Director plays a critical role in the maintenance, configuration, and optimization of the Electronic Health Record (EHR); oversees required state reporting; maintains the centralized repository of all Department of Mental Health and Addiction Services (DMHAS) reported data; and ensures accurate and timely data submission. This role also leads the agency’s preparation for external audits (ex., Commission on Accreditation of Rehabilitation Facilities (CARF), Department of Public Health (DPH), DMHAS), coordinates customer satisfaction activities, and serves as the agency’s Client Rights Officer.
This position is responsible for the monitoring and analyzing of processes to meet Fidelity and contractual requirements across the agency. Ongoing analysis of health care information obtained from a variety of sources, including patient care, financial, and demographic data is necessary. This role involves the development and preparation of information for state reporting and organizational best practices. This position will maintain repository of all state reported data for all DMHAS programs. A heavy importance is placed on collaborating with program leaders across the agency, ensuring accuracy of data reported and driving agency performance.
Essential Functions
Department Leadership, Training, and Support
Directly supervise two (2) employees in the Quality Assurance department and serve as backup to staff as needed.
Provide Daily Living Activities Functional Assessment (DLA-20), program specific documentation, and recovery planning training to the agency.
Train employees and monitor compliance across programs with state reporting requirements.
Function as an internal information expert to the entire management team when special and critical quality issues occur.
Consult with senior leadership to resolve quality, service, and efficiency problems.
State Reporting, Data, and Surveys
Facilitate and coordinate annual DMHAS Consumer Satisfaction Surveys and quarterly CARF Satisfaction surveys.
Provide DMHAS Data Performance System (DDaP) data and informational support to other departments, including DDaP 101 supervisor training, share DMHAS information with leadership, and present quarterly and annual DMHAS Report Cards to leadership.
Electronic Health Record (EHR) and Systems Support
Triage QA tickets. Issues include, but are not limited to, document management, on/off-boarding, medical staff onboarding, system outages, etc.
Facilitate within the EHR the build and support of procedures, forms, and form development; implement training to identified employees.
Foster ongoing support to assigned programs and serve as a liaison between staff and vendors for effective responses to users’ needs.
Audit Readiness, Compliance, and Quality Improvement
Provide support to programs in preparation for routine external audits, including CARF survey, fidelity reviews, and Department of Public Health licensing.
Facilitate completion of all corrective action plans and audit follow-up, including quarterly and annual program compliance reviews.
Monitor and assist with corrections and work with programs to identify and resolve root causes as needed.
Ensure compliance with SCSI’s policies, quality assurance programs, and safety; ensure EHR compliance with regulatory agencies like DMHAS, DPH, CARF, etc.
Participate in quality improvement initiatives.
Serve as the agency’s Client Rights Officer (CRO), observing and adhering to the role outlined by DMHAS.
Agency Participation and Policy Compliance
Participate in all agency activities pertaining to health and safety, training, drills, etc.
Adhere to SCSI policies and procedures.
Physical Requirements
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to sit, use hands to finger, handle or feel objects, tools, or controls, and climb stairs. The employee frequently is required to walk, talk and/or hear; speaking and hearing ability sufficient to communicate effectively by phone or in person at normal volumes; vision adequate to read correspondence, computer screen, forms, etc. The employee is occasionally required to stand and climb or balance. The employee must occasionally lift and/or move up to 25 lbs. Specific vision abilities required by this position include the ability to adjust focus. The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Strong understanding of Connecticut DMHAS standards, documentation requirements, and reporting systems (including DDaP).
Demonstrated ability to supervise, lead, and coach staff.
Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data, identify trends, and communicate findings clearly.
Demonstrated technology and software application skills; ability to learn new software packages; highly skilled in office productivity software (e.g., Word, PowerPoint, Excel, email).
Excellent written and oral communication skills.
Ability to be proactive, flexible, and customer service focused and to work effectively with others.
Qualifications
Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree required, or an equivalent combination of education and related experience.
Minimum experience:
Experience working with electronic health record system, i.e., CareLogic; experience providing training; and experience with accreditation standards such as CARF, DMHAS, DPH, or similar regulatory bodies.
Preferred qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Social Work, Psychology, Healthcare Administration, or a related field. Masters degree preferred.
Preferred license:
Licensed Clinical Social Worker (LCSW) or Licensed Professional Counselor (LPC)
Driver’s license requirement:
A current valid driver’s license is required.
Background check, credentialing, health screening, or other employment requirements:
Successful completion of required background checks and any other applicable agency employment requirements.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religious creed, age, sex, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, marital status, civil union status, national origin, ancestry, citizenship, present or past history of mental disability, intellectual disability, learning disability, physical disability, including but not limited to blindness, genetic information, veteran status, sexual orientation, status as a victim of domestic violence, status as a victim of sexual assault, status as a victim of trafficking in persons, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.
Other Duties
This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work performed by individuals assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all duties, responsibilities, or qualifications. Employees may be required to perform other job-related duties as assigned.

Director, Production and Test Engineering
No longer accepting applications
True Anomaly
Denver Metropolitan Area
Space is a warfighting domain. True Anomaly seeks those with the talent and ambition to build the technology that secures it.
OUR MISSION
True Anomaly delivers decisive capabilities for space superiority. We build autonomous spacecraft, advanced payloads, mission software, and space-based interceptors — enabling the U.S. and its Allies to secure the space environment and counter threats from the ultimate high ground.
OUR VALUES
Be the offset. We create asymmetric advantages with creativity and ingenuity.
What would it take? We challenge assumptions to deliver ambitious results.
It’s the people. Our team is our competitive advantage and we are better together.
BENEFITS & PERKS*
Best-in-class healthcare: 100% company-paid medical, dental, and vision coverage for you and your dependents, with HSA/HRA options
Generous time off: Flexible Time Off (FTO) for exempt employees, accrued PTO of up to 25 days for non-exempt employees, plus 12 paid holidays; Parental Leave; Sick Leave
Fuel for your day: Daily catered lunch and unlimited snacks for in-office employees
And more: 401(k) retirement plan, fitness reimbursement, and Dog Fridays
Equity participation: Equity is included as part of our total compensation package, giving you an opportunity to share in the company’s success.
Do not apply to fixed term and temporary roles
YOUR MISSION
As Director, Production and Test Engineering, you will lead the Denver-based team of technicians, production engineers, test engineers, and manufacturing engineers to deliver fully qualified spacecraft on aggressive timelines. You will own the build and test processes, schedules, and capacity planning required to execute production commitments. You will partner closely with Program Management and Engineering to provide inputs to the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), align capacity with demand, and drive disciplined execution against production milestones. Beyond delivery, you will be accountable for continuously improving efficiency, automation, and process maturity to reduce turn time and increase throughput. This role requires both strategic foresight and hands-on leadership: setting standards, driving automation, solving problems, and developing people to their full potential while ensuring every spacecraft meets mission assurance standards.
Responsibilities
Lead and mentor a high-performing team across production, test, and manufacturing engineering.
Own execution of production and test schedules to meet program delivery commitments.
Drive load capacity planning - forecast demand, balance resources, and ensure teams are properly staffed and focused.
Provide accurate inputs to the Integrated Master Schedule (IMS), aligning production and test activities with program needs.
Own and continuously improve build and test processes, ensuring efficiency, repeatability, and compliance with AS9100/ISO9001 standards.
Champion efficiency and automation initiatives to reduce cycle time, improve first-time yield, and scale production capability.
Oversee test execution, including requirements verification, procedure development, data analysis, and anomaly resolution.
Lead root cause investigations and ensure corrective actions are implemented effectively.
Invest in developing team members through coaching, mentorship, and growth opportunities, enabling them to reach their full potential.
Ensure facilities and workspaces are clean, organized, and optimized for safety and efficiency.
What Success Looks Like
Production and test schedules executed predictably, with milestones met or exceeded.
Efficiency and automation drive measurable reductions in turn time and increase throughput.
Capacity plans that accurately anticipate workload and prevent bottlenecks.
High first-time yield and reduced anomalies demonstrate process maturity.
Denver team engagement, technical excellence, and professional growth consistently visible.
Build and test processes that are scalable, disciplined, and trusted by stakeholders.
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in manufacturing, Mechanical, Aerospace Engineering, or a related discipline.
Over 10 years of experience in space component, spacecraft production, and testing.
In-depth knowledge of AS9100/ISO9001 production standards, requirements, and testing protocols.
Proven track record in managing high-rate, complex components and assemblies, as well as executing detailed test plans.
Extensive experience with MRP, PLM, and MES application systems, and the integration of automation components across these systems.
Strong expertise in lean manufacturing principles, rapid prototyping methodologies, and environmental testing such as vibration, thermal, or shock testing.
Solid understanding of spacecraft testing facilities and tooling, including vibration tables, TVAC, EMI/EMC chambers, optical alignment stations, and FlatSats.
Experience with ESD sensitive component and assembly manufacturing.
Demonstrated ability to effectively manage and maintain a cleanroom environment, ensuring organization and cleanliness to the highest standards.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in manufacturing, mechanical, aerospace engineering or equivalent discipline.
15+ years of experience in space component and/or spacecraft production and testing.
Experience with CNC, tube bending, and other production equipment.
Familiarity with LabVIEW, MATLAB, or Python for data processing or test automation.
Capable of building and maintaining IMS schedules with Program Management and schedulers with a deep understanding of critical paths and mitigation techniques.
Active DoD clearance or ability to obtain one is a plus.
Compensation
Base Salary: $190,000 - $265,000
Equity + Benefits including Health, Dental, Vision, HRA/HSA options, PTO and paid holidays, 401K, Parental Leave
Your actual level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, location, and experience.
Additional Requirements
Work Location—Successful candidates will be located near Denver, CO. While we observe a hybrid work environment, some work must be done on site.
Work environment—the work environment; temperature, noise level, inside or outside, or other factors that will affect the person's working conditions while performing the job.
Physical demands—the physical demands of the job, including bending, sitting, lifting and driving.
This position will be open until it is successfully filled. To submit your application, please follow the directions below.
To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR) you must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the U.S., protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), or eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State.
True Anomaly is committed to equal employment opportunity on any basis protected by applicable state and federal laws. If you have a disability or additional need that requires accommodation, please do not hesitate to let us know.
To protect candidates and our company from application fraud and impersonation, we use third-party tools to verify applicant identity and detect fraudulent applications. Learn more in our Privacy Notice.

evidence.text:
Senior Manager, Fulfillment and Logistics Operations, Ford Energy
Ford Motor Company
Dearborn, MI
We made history and now we work to transform the future – for our customers, our communities and our families. You'll see your work on the road every day, helping people move freely and pursue their dreams. At Ford, you can build more than vehicles. Come build what matters.
Ford Energy is a newly formed, wholly-owned subsidiary of Ford Motor Company dedicated to accelerating U.S. energy independence. Leveraging Ford’s century of manufacturing excellence and world-class battery energy storage systems (BESS) technology, Ford Energy designs, manufactures, and services grid-scale and commercial DC battery energy storage systems (BESS). Ford Energy is uniquely positioned to capture the growing demand for reliable, US-built energy storage systems. We are not just building batteries; we are building the infrastructure for the next generation of the American grid.
Why Ford Energy?
At Ford Energy, you have the backing of an industrial manufacturing powerhouse with the agility of a dedicated energy startup offering industry leading technology. We offer a competitive compensation package including performance-based bonuses, Ford vehicle discounts, and the opportunity to shape the energy strategy of one of the world's most iconic brands.
In this position...
The Senior Manager, Fulfillment & Logistics Operations is a senior leadership role accountable for the end-to-end fulfillment, logistics, and parts supply performance of the Project Operations & Performance value stream. This leader sets the direction for inventory and supply planning, parts replenishment, warehousing, distribution, and outbound product shipping, and owns the service, cost, and working capital outcomes of the network. The role also delivers the digital capabilities that give customers real-time visibility into parts inventory, order status, and shipment information, making fulfillment a differentiator in the customer experience. Partnering with Product Creation & Industrialization, Finance, Sales, and Procurement, this leader combines deep supply chain and logistics expertise with change leadership and the ability to build high-performing teams, delivering measurable business impact. [Scope: add annual logistics and inventory spend, number of facilities and 3PL partners, and team size.]
What you'll do...
1. Strategy & Transformation
Own the fulfillment and logistics strategy across the Project Operations & Performance value stream, aligned with growth and customer experience goals.
Lead transformation from concept to measurable results, including integration with Product Creation & Industrialization.
Champion the Voice of Customer, resolve issues quickly, and incorporate insights into product, service, and fulfillment improvements.
2. Parts Supply, Inventory & Warehousing
Lead end-to-end spare parts planning, inventory, and distribution, balancing availability, cost-to-serve, and working capital.
Optimize inventory through segment-specific safety stock and reorder strategies, procurement controls, and clearance of slow-moving stock.
Hold warehouse partners accountable for inventory accuracy, productivity, and safety.
Partner with Finance to improve inventory velocity and the cash conversion cycle.
3. Outbound Logistics & Delivery
Own delivery performance from factory release to customer or site, establishing service targets and driving perfect-order execution.
Manage carrier, freight forwarder, and 3PL relationships, including contracts, rates, capacity, mode selection, and performance reviews.
Ensure battery energy storage shipments meet hazardous materials and oversize/overweight transport requirements, including DOT, packaging, labeling, documentation, and permits.
Coordinate production, shipping, installation, and site readiness across Sales, Manufacturing, Customer Project Teams, and Finance; resolve delays, damage claims, and exceptions.
Reduce freight costs and lead times through route optimization, load consolidation, and standardized, system-integrated workflows.
4. Digital Capabilities & Customer Visibility
Deliver customer self-service access to parts availability, consumption, order status, shipment tracking, and estimated delivery.
Partner with IT, Product, and Sales to connect ERP, planning, warehouse, and carrier data through customer portals and API/EDI integrations.
Provide proactive alerts for delays, backorders, and delivery changes; measure adoption, satisfaction, and reductions in order-status inquiries.
Replace manual processes with automated workflows using SAP, advanced planning systems, and integrated data.
5. Supplier & Production Alignment
Partner with Procurement to monitor Tier 1 and Tier 2 supplier performance and mitigate material risks before they disrupt production.
Align factory priorities with high-value customer orders and strategic inventory needs.
6. Leadership, Performance & Continuous Improvement
Build and develop a high-performing fulfillment, logistics, and supply chain team.
Present performance, risks, and investment cases to senior leadership and align cross-functional stakeholders.
Own KPIs such as OTIF, forecast accuracy, inventory turns, backorders, fill rate, lead time, and cost-to-serve; quantify the financial and operational impact of improvements.
Improve service and field performance through shorter repair cycles, higher first-time-fix rates, and greater product reliability.
Lead change adoption and apply Lean and Six Sigma methods to eliminate waste and reduce fulfillment lead times.
You'll have...
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business Administration, or at least 10 years' of experience in a related field
8+ years of progressive experience in aftermarket operations, service supply chain, fulfillment, or logistics, including leading managers and multi-functional teams.
Proven record of leading large-scale operational or digital transformation initiatives across multi-functional teams.
Deep expertise in spare parts planning, inventory management, warehousing, distribution, and outbound logistics.
Financial acumen, including budget ownership and working capital management.
Executive-level communication and influencing skills, with the ability to partner with and present to stakeholders at all levels.
Must be able to travel 50% as needed
Even better, you'll have...
Master's Degree in Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, or APICS CPIM certification is a plus.
Experience in the automotive or heavy equipment aftermarket/service industry.
Experience delivering customer-facing digital capabilities, such as portals, order and shipment visibility tools, or API/EDI integrations.
Experience in transportation, outbound logistics, or freight management, including hazardous materials or oversize/overweight shipping.
Knowledge of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile).
Experience working with Salesforce and/or SAP S4 HANA.
Experience in high-mix, global manufacturing or consumer/industrial industries.
Additional Information:
Work Location: Dearborn or Kentucky (United States), but the company is willing to consider a hybrid modality
Required Travel: Up to 50% travel required
You may not check every box, or your experience may look a little different from what we've outlined, but if you think you can bring value to Ford Motor Company, we encourage you to apply!
As an established global company, we offer the benefit of choice. You can choose what your Ford future will look like: will your story span the globe, or keep you close to home? Will your career be a deep dive into what you love, or a series of new teams and new skills? Will you be a leader, a changemaker, a technical expert, a culture builder…or all of the above? No matter what you choose, we offer a work life that works for you, including:
Immediate medical, dental, vision and prescription drug coverage
Flexible family care days, paid parental leave, new parent ramp-up programs, subsidized back-up child care and more
Family building benefits including adoption and surrogacy expense reimbursement, fertility treatments, and more
Vehicle discount program for employees and family members and management leases
Tuition assistance
Established and active employee resource groups
Paid time off for individual and team community service
A generous schedule of paid holidays, including the week between Christmas and New Year’s Day
Paid time off and the option to purchase additional vacation time.
This position is leadership level 5 and ranges from $141,700-$268,300.
Final determination of salary grade will be based on candidate's skills and experience, and base salary will be set within the applicable range according to job scope, responsibility and competitive market value.
For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/LL5
For more information on salary and benefits, click here: https://fordcareers.co/GSR
Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
Candidates for positions with Ford Motor Company must be legally authorized to work in the United States. Verification of employment eligibility will be required at the time of hire.
We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, religion, color, age, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability status or protected veteran status. In the United States, if you need a reasonable accommodation for the online application process due to a disability, please call 1-888-336-0660.

Jensen Metal Products 
Racine, WI
Description
Lead Strategy. Drive Performance. Shape the Future.
KSP Group, Inc/Jensen Metal Products is seeking a hands-on manufacturing leader to drive operational excellence, strengthen accountability, improve execution, and build scalable operating systems across our manufacturing businesses. This is not a corporate executive role designed to lead from a conference room.
We are looking for a proven change agent who is equally comfortable reviewing financial results, leading daily operational reviews, solving production challenges on the shop floor, and developing frontline leaders.
This is a multi-site position, initially focused on Jensen Metal Products and Jensen Powder Finishers. The successful candidate will build the structure, discipline, and performance culture needed to support long-term growth across KSP Group.
The ideal candidate brings deep experience in fabrication and manufacturing environments, a strong operational and financial mindset, and a proven ability to lead teams through growth and transformation.
About KSP Group
KSP Group is a family-owned organization with a diverse portfolio of manufacturing and consumer product companies
Jensen Metal Products
– Custom metal fabrication, welding, machining, laser cutting, engineering and contract manufacturing solutions (Racine, WI)
Jensen Powder Finishers
– Advanced powder coating and finishing services (Sturtevant, WI)
Jensen Castings
– Manufacturer of premium GFRC concrete fire features (Richland Center, WI)
Real Flame

Report on operational performance and improvement initiatives to executive leadership

Demonstrated success leading directly from the manufacturing floor, including personal involvement in:

From engineering to packaging, our goal is to be a one-stop shop that exceeds our customers’ expectations for quality, delivery, great customer service and cost. evidence.quote: 10 or more years of progressively responsible manufacturing engineering experience, including at least 5 years leading engineering teams and major capital projects. Multi-site leadership experience preferred.
evidence.text:
Director of Manufacturing Engineering
LaMotte Company
Newark, DE
Position Summary:
The Director of Manufacturing Engineering reports to the Vice President of Operations and provides strategic direction and leadership for engineering across LaMotte's Newark, Delaware and Chestertown, Maryland facilities. This role owns LaMotte's Operational Excellence (OpEx) process and leads capital investment, automation, and continuous improvement to support business growth and improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost performance. The Manager translates business priorities into engineering and capacity plans, develops engineering talent, and establishes consistent practices across both sites. Working with Operations, Quality, Maintenance, R&D, EHS, and Finance, this leader ensures projects and improvements deliver measurable, sustainable results without compromising product quality or safety.
Job Responsibilities:
1. Strategic Direction
Develop and maintain a three- to five-year engineering, capacity, and technology roadmap aligned with LaMotte's business strategy, sales growth, and manufacturing requirements.
Translate the roadmap into annual priorities, resource plans, and capital requirements; identify capacity constraints, equipment risks, and opportunities to improve competitiveness.
Advise executive leadership on investment alternatives, expected benefits, risks, and timing; communicate progress and recommend adjustments as business needs change.
2. Engineering Leadership Across Both Facilities
Direct engineering activities across Newark and Chestertown, balancing resources and project priorities with plant leadership while maintaining a regular presence at both sites.
Lead, coach, and develop engineering personnel; establish clear responsibilities, performance expectations, technical training, and succession plans.
Establish standardized equipment and process specifications, including internal and supplier standards, engineering documentation, PLC and HMI programming, and equipment software requirements, to drive consistent operating procedures and best practices across both facilities.
Partner with R&D, Quality, Operations, Maintenance, and EHS on new-product scale-up, process changes, equipment reliability, and resolution of significant manufacturing issues.
3. Ownership of Operational Excellence
Serve as the process owner for LaMotte's Operational Excellence program across both facilities, defining its framework, standards, project selection process, performance measures, and management review cadence.
Partner with department and value-stream leaders to establish annual improvement goals, assign project ownership, prioritize resources, and review progress through Operations & Quality Leadership Team meetings.
Build employee participation and problem-solving capability through training and coaching; ensure improvements are documented, adopted, and sustained, with operating leaders accountable for execution and results.
4. Capital Investment and Automation
Own the annual and multi-year capital expenditure (CapEx) planning process and manage the approved portfolio and budget across both facilities, balancing growth, replacement, safety, quality, and productivity needs.
Develop business cases covering capacity, cost, staffing, return on investment, payback, and risk; recommend priorities and obtain approvals through LaMotte's authorization process.
Lead capital projects from requirements, justification, and supplier selection through design reviews, installation, commissioning, and handover; manage scope, schedule, spending, and supplier performance.
Define and execute the automation strategy, selecting practical technologies that improve process consistency, throughput, ergonomics, and labor productivity while addressing reliability, maintainability, and training needs.
Establish measurable equipment acceptance criteria and oversee factory and site acceptance testing (FAT/SAT), documentation, and training. Verify results against the approved business case after implementation.
5. Continuous Improvement and Manufacturing Performance
Lead a prioritized pipeline of improvements that reduce bottlenecks, downtime, scrap, rework, changeover time, and manufacturing cost while improving flow, yield, and delivery performance.
Sponsor and lead Kaizen events and structured problem solving using Lean, Six Sigma, statistical process control (SPC), design of experiments (DOE), and root-cause analysis. Partner with Maintenance to apply Total Productive Maintenance (TPM) principles.
Track throughput, labor productivity, overall equipment effectiveness (OEE), quality, and verified savings. Validate benefits with Finance and operating leaders, standardize successful changes, and report sustained results to leadership.
Qualifications / Requirements:
Bachelor's degree in engineering; chemical, mechanical, electrical, or industrial engineering preferred.
10 or more years of progressively responsible manufacturing engineering experience, including at least 5 years leading engineering teams and major capital projects. Multi-site leadership experience preferred.
Demonstrated success developing engineering strategies, managing capital budgets, implementing automation, and delivering measurable Operational Excellence and continuous improvement results.
Lean, Six Sigma, engineering, or project management certifications are a plus.
Strong technical, analytical, financial, and project management skills; ability to interpret engineering documentation and evaluate equipment and process performance.
Ability to lead cross-functional teams, develop people, manage competing priorities, and communicate technical recommendations and business results effectively to employees and executive leadership.
Miscellaneous
Lead by example, maintain company confidentiality, and comply with all company policies. Escalate significant production, equipment, safety, quality, and project risks and coordinate timely resolution. Identify training needs and support knowledge sharing across manufacturing areas. Perform other duties consistent with the role as assigned.
Environmental Factors & Mental / Physical Demands
Work is performed in office, manufacturing, and laboratory areas, with potential exposure to operating equipment, chemicals, powders, and testing solutions; training and required protective equipment are provided. The role requires regular travel between Newark and Chestertown and occasional supplier visits, standing and walking through production areas, and safely accessing equipment and work areas. Wear required personal protective equipment, including task-specific respiratory protection when required. Manage multiple priorities and make timely technical and business decisions.
Work-life and Culture:
LaMotte Company, a 100+ year-old global industry leader in developing and manufacturing premier water analysis solutions, operating in Newark, DE, Chestertown, MD and Warwick, UK. Our products are used around the world to accurately, quickly, and conveniently test water in a multitude of applications.
LaMotte relies on the success of our employees and are committed to supporting their growth. We offer competitive pay, along with performance-based increases. LaMotte offers a range of different shifts such as mornings, afternoons, evenings, and 12-hour shifts between both facilities to fit employee’s needs. LaMotte offers paid time off including vacation, sick leave, and paid holidays. We have several employee events including holiday events, employee appreciation events, community events, employee engagement, etc.
Full-time employees, who regularly work at least 30 hours per week, are eligible for employer-provided insurance including health, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, and supplemental insurance. Full-time employees are eligible to contribute to our 401(k) plan with an employer match available.
LaMotte is committed to a policy of Equal Employment Opportunity and will not discriminate against an applicant or employee on the basis of race, color, religion, creed, national origin or ancestry, sex, age, disability, military status, genetic information, sexual orientation, or any other legally recognized protected basis under federal, state, or local laws.

Application Close Date

At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
Work Location: On-site Huntsville, AL
We are a diverse team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable space flight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin’s vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
As part of a diverse and hardworking team of engineers, you will oversee the manufacturing engineering team that specializes in a rocket engine assembly produced at the Huntsville site. You will share in the team’s impact on all aspects of manufacturing and increasing production rate. From a technical aspect, you and your team will be responsible for the translation of engineering intent and drawings into operational steps and processes to produce hardware at a high rate. This is inclusive of shop-floor work order operational definition as well as process definition. You will also identify, develop, and deploy methods to improve quality, reduce cost, and optimize build sequence and schedules. As an integral member of the team, you will lead DFM and PFMEA studies to strengthen the feedback loop between design and build, which is integral to bringing the product up to rate. As the manager, you will be responsible for working closely with peer organizations to develop goals and career paths, training, functional processes, and manage roles, responsibilities, and accountability for each team member. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your dedicated commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable human spaceflight.
We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!

Job Description
DescriptionDirector of Operations - Wisconsin & Illinois
Department: Operations
Reports To: COO
Location: Wisconsin and Illinois; regular travel between assigned facilities
Direct Reports: Assigned General Managers, and Site Managers
Summary
The Director of Operations leads the operational and financial performance of the company's Wisconsin and Illinois facilities. This position oversees conventional caged and cage-free layer production, pullet operations where assigned, shell egg grading and packing, egg breaking and liquid egg processing, feed mills, and supporting operational functions.
The Director translates company strategy into clear site-level priorities, develops strong leaders, and holds teams accountable for safe operations, animal welfare, food safety, customer service, and profitability. This role requires a visible, hands-on leader who drives consistent execution, improves operating practices, and builds collaboration across locations and corporate functions.
Key Responsibilities
Regional Leadership and Accountability
Lead regional operations to achieve production, processing, quality, service, and financial goals.
Establish clear expectations, performance measures, and operating plans for each facility.
Hold General Managers and operational leaders accountable for results, timely corrective actions, and follow-through.
Maintain a regular presence at facilities to evaluate conditions, coach leaders, and address operational barriers.
Standardize effective practices across locations while accounting for differences in housing systems, equipment, and customer requirements.
Communicate performance, risks, resource needs, and recommendations to executive leadership.
Live Production and Animal Welfare
Oversee conventional caged and cage-free layer operations.
Oversee pullet rearing and replacement flock readiness where assigned.
Drive flock performance through effective management of production, mortality, livability, egg quality, feed conversion, body weight, and flock uniformity.
Ensure consistent execution of ventilation, lighting, water, feeding, litter, and manure management programs.
Partner with veterinary and nutrition teams on flock health, disease prevention, vaccination, pest control, and nutrition programs.
Ensure compliance with company animal welfare standards and applicable certification and customer requirements.
Enforce biosecurity expectations for employees, visitors, equipment, contractors, and transportation.
Shell Egg and Breaking Operations
Oversee shell egg receiving, grading, packing, storage, and shipping.
Oversee egg breaking and liquid egg processing, including pasteurization where applicable.
Improve egg recovery, saleable yield, throughput, labor efficiency, equipment utilization, and product quality.
Reduce checks, cracks, losses, rework, downtime, and customer complaints.
Coordinate production and processing schedules with sales, planning, and logistics to meet customer commitments and manage inventory.
Partner with Quality Assurance to maintain sanitation, traceability, food safety programs, audit readiness, and timely corrective actions.
Ensure reported production, gradeout, yield, and inventory results are accurate and supported by operational records.
Feed Mill Operations
Oversee assigned feed mills to ensure safe, reliable, and cost-effective feed manufacturing and delivery.
Align mill capacity, production schedules, and delivery plans with flock requirements.
Partner with nutrition and procurement teams on ingredient quality, availability, formulation implementation, and inventory management.
Ensure controls for batching accuracy, mixing consistency, ingredient receiving, storage, sanitation, and feed traceability.
Monitor feed manufacturing costs, shrink, downtime, maintenance needs, and delivery performance.
Address feed quality concerns promptly with appropriate technical and operational support.
Financial and Business Performance
Own regional operating performance against approved budgets and business plans.
Lead annual budgeting, forecasting, labor planning, and capital planning for assigned operations.
Review site financial results and operating metrics to identify variances, determine root causes, and implement corrective actions.
Improve cost per dozen, processing costs, feed manufacturing costs, asset utilization, and overall profitability.
Ensure purchasing discipline, accurate inventory controls, and compliance with spending authority.
Develop capital requests supported by operational need, expected benefits, financial justification, and implementation plans.
Maintenance and Supporting Operations
Oversee maintenance, preventive maintenance, equipment reliability, utilities, and facility condition.
Support transportation, egg movements, feed delivery, warehousing, and other assigned logistics activities.
Ensure effective manure handling, storage, and removal, along with environmental stewardship and housekeeping.
Coordinate contractors, construction, equipment installations, and facility improvement projects.
Maintain emergency response and business continuity plans for disease events, fires, utility failures, severe weather, and equipment breakdowns.
People, Safety, and Culture
Build and develop a capable regional leadership team through coaching, succession planning, and performance management.
Partner with Human Resources on staffing, retention, training, employee relations, and leadership development.
Set clear expectations for professional communication, teamwork, and respectful treatment of employees.
Promote a culture in which employees raise concerns, leaders address issues promptly, and commitments are completed.
Partner with EHS and site leadership to improve workplace safety, investigate incidents, and close corrective actions.
Ensure employees receive appropriate training and have the resources needed to perform their work safely and effectively.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in poultry science, agriculture, operations management, business, or a related field preferred; equivalent relevant experience considered.
Typically 10 or more years of progressive agricultural or food manufacturing experience, including significant leadership responsibility across multiple facilities.
Strong knowledge of commercial layer production, including conventional caged and cage-free systems.
Experience overseeing shell egg processing, egg breaking, and feed mill operations strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to manage budgets, interpret financial results, and improve operational performance.
Working knowledge of animal welfare, biosecurity, food safety, employee safety, and environmental requirements.
Proven ability to develop leaders, manage change, resolve problems, and hold teams accountable.
Strong communication, planning, analytical, and decision-making skills.
Measures of Success
Performance will be evaluated through a balanced set of regional and site-level measures, including:
Financial: Budget performance, controllable costs, and verified improvement results.
Live production: Egg production, mortality, livability, feed conversion, and egg quality.
Processing: Yield, recovery, throughput, labor efficiency, downtime, and order fulfillment.
Feed mills: Feed quality, manufacturing cost, inventory accuracy, and delivery reliability.
People and safety: Leadership development, retention, training completion, safety performance, and corrective action closure.
Compliance and execution: Animal welfare and food safety results, data accuracy, audit readiness, and completion of operating and capital priorities.
Working Conditions
This position requires frequent travel between Wisconsin and Illinois facilities and availability to support operations outside normal business hours when necessary. Work includes time in poultry houses, processing plants, feed mills, and outdoor environments, with required adherence to site biosecurity, food safety, and personal protective equipment procedures.

evidence.text:
Senior Manager, Manufacturing
Bausch + Lomb
Greenville, SC
Bausch + Lomb (NYSE/TSX: BLCO) is a leading global eye health company dedicated to protecting and enhancing the gift of sight for millions of people around the world—from the moment of birth through every phase of life. Our mission is simple, yet powerful: helping you see better, to live better.
Our comprehensive portfolio of over 400 products is fully integrated and built to serve our customers across the full spectrum of their eye health needs throughout their lives. Our iconic brand is built on the deep trust and loyalty of our customers established over our 170-year history. We have a significant global research, development, manufacturing and commercial footprint of approximately 13,000 employees and a presence in approximately 100 countries, extending our reach to billions of potential customers across the globe. We have long been associated with many of the most significant advances in eye health, and we believe we are well positioned to continue leading the advancement of eye health in the future.
Objectives/Purpose Of Job
The Senior Manager, Manufacturing is responsible for leading 24/7 manufacturing operations across Aseptic Filling, Preparation/Cleaning, and Packaging. This role provides end-to-end operational ownership for safety, quality, delivery, cost, compliance, and people leadership while ensuring production activities are executed in accordance with GMP, regulatory expectations, approved procedures, and site standards. The role also provides weekend operational support and serves as a key escalation point to maintain continuity of operations across all shifts.
Key Activities/Responsibilities
Provide tactical and long-range operational directives for Aseptic Filling, Preparation/Cleaning, and Packaging to achieve safety, quality, delivery, cost, and compliance objectives in a 24/7 manufacturing environment.
Maintain operational ownership across all shifts, including weekend responsibilities, issue escalation, resource coordination, and decision-making to ensure production continuity.
Establish expectations for team’s understanding of and compliance with GMP, FDA, Annex 1, ISO requirements, approved batch records, SOPs, contamination-control expectations, and internal quality systems. Ensure line leaders properly coach their teammates to routinely achieve these standards, driving recognition and accountability throughout the entire team.
Set performance expectations and provide managerial oversight for Aseptic Filling, ensuring line leadership has the resources, priorities, and cross-functional support needed to meet daily safety, quality, delivery, and compliance targets; remove systemic barriers and address issues escalated by line leadership.
Provide strategic and operational oversight for Preparation and Cleaning, holding line leadership accountable for production readiness, sanitation performance, and adherence to established standards while resolving cross-functional constraints and escalated operational risks.
Direct Packaging performance through clear priorities, governance, and accountability for safety, quality, delivery, cost, compliance, and customer service; enable line leadership to achieve daily targets by aligning resources, removing obstacles, and addressing escalated issues.
Drive operational excellence through Lean, Six Sigma, OEE improvement, 5S, visual management, waste reduction, changeover optimization, downtime reduction, and continuous improvement.
Partner with Supply Chain, Maintenance, Engineering, Quality, and Warehouse to coordinate production schedules, preventive maintenance, reliability activities, investigations, CAPAs, deviations, change controls, validations, inspections, and new equipment startup.
Create an environment conducive to the development of teammates primarily through timely coaching, feedback, and recognition, helping ensure everyone has an opportunity to do their best work.
Manage staffing, labor planning, productivity, and budget performance while ensuring the organization is appropriately resourced to meet daily execution and long-term business needs.
Qualifications/Training
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, Life Sciences, Operations Management, or a related field preferred; equivalent manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
Experience leading GMP manufacturing operations in aseptic, pharmaceutical, medical device, biologics, or other regulated manufacturing environments.
Demonstrated ability to lead multi-shift or 24/7 operations, including weekend coverage, escalation management, and cross-functional coordination.
Knowledge of aseptic processing, cleaning practices, packaging operations, documentation practices, contamination prevention, and regulatory readiness.
Proven capability in people leadership, technical problem solving, continuous improvement, operational performance management, and change leadership.
This position may be available in the following location(s): US - Greenville, SC (Plant)
All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or veteran status.
Job Applicants should be aware of job offer scams perpetrated through the use of the Internet and social media platforms.
To learn more please read Bausch + Lomb's Job Offer Fraud Statement

Head of Global Customer Quality
EMD Electronics
Tempe, AZ
Work Your Magic with us! Start your next chapter and join EMD Electronics.
Ready to explore, break barriers, and discover more? We know you’ve got big plans – so do we! Our colleagues across the globe love innovating with science and technology to enrich people’s lives with our solutions in Healthcare, Life Science, and Electronics. Together, we dream big and are passionate about caring for our rich mix of people, customers, patients, and planet. That's why we are always looking for curious minds that see themselves imagining the unimaginable with us.
Everything we do in EMD Electronics is to help us deliver on our purpose of being the company behind the companies, advancing digital living. We are dedicated to being the trusted supplier of high-tech materials, services and specialty chemicals for the electronics, automotive and cosmetics industries. We foster a global collaborative organization made up of individuals who have the passion to win, obsess about the customer, are relentlessly curious and act with urgency. Together, we push the boundaries of science to make more possible for our customers.
Location:
The Head of Global Customer Quality is a remote role from US, Korea or Taiwan.
Travel
This role requires approximately 20–30% travel, including both domestic and international, with the potential to exceed that based on business and customer needs.
Your Role
As the Global Customer Quality Manager, you will drive Customer Quality engagement for our customers across all Business Units (BUs) in the Electronics division. In this role, you will collaborate closely with the Global Key Account Managers (GKAMs) and Account Teams to nurture customer relationships and deliver exceptional performance and results. You will serve as the vital communication bridge between EMD Electronics and our customers, ensuring their needs are understood and addressed while advancing their technology. Additionally, you will represent the Voice of the Customer for Quality to internal stakeholders, playing a crucial role in aligning our services with customer expectations and fostering long-term partnerships.
Key Responsibilities
Develop and lead our proactive Customer Quality engagement strategy with a focus on strategic customers to drive customer systems collaboration, customer scorecard optimization, and customer quality roadmap engagement.
Act as the second point of escalation for Customer Quality issues.
Develop and mentor a Global Customer Quality Team with an optimal mix of technical and commercial competency.
Drive the development and maintenance of Electronics Customer Quality Roadmaps.
Lead and manage the successful completion of Customer Quality Initiatives and Programs across all Electronics businesses.
Drive team ownership of customer engagement between Electronics and customers for Quality issues.
Ensure the Customer Quality team leads and drives customer taskforces to ensure customer trust in our performance and Quality.
Ensure Customer Quality is a key stakeholder in the troubleshooting and problem solving of Customer Quality Issues including review and approval of 8D reports with high power factor corrective and preventive actions (CAPA).
Drive management of Customer Quality Inquiries with internal and external stakeholders to ensure accurate and timely responses.
Ensure facilitation of Customer Quality Audits to drive preparation, enhance performance, and ensure follow-up and closure.
Who You Are
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, chemistry, or other technical disciplines with 8+years of manufacturing, business, and quality experience in a fast-paced time sensitive environment.
5+ years of successful Customer Engagement in the semiconductor industry or similar large scale production industry.
Previous experience supervising or managing staff.
Preferred Requirements
Chemical manufacturing and/or semiconductor experience preferred.
Confidence interacting with customers and senior internal leaders.
Demonstrated leadership and coaching experience with global teams.
Excellent communication skills (English) – oral and written.
Ability to collaborate with people from various backgrounds/cultures/functions in a highly matrixed global organization.
Excellent time management and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple activities, projects, and demands independently.
Semiconductor fab experience
Significant commercial negotiation experience
Moderate Statistical knowledge
Experience in Quality tools for problem solving (5 Why, Model Based Problem Solving), FMEAs, Continuous Improvement (CI) activities, Management of Change (MOC), and Document Control systems.
Experience with ISO9001 Quality Management Systems
SAP experience

The actual compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level of experience, education, skills, and other job-related factors. Position may be eligible for sales or performance-based bonuses. Benefits offered by the Company include health insurance, paid time off (PTO), retirement contributions, and other perquisites. We are curious minds that come from a broad range of backgrounds, perspectives, and life experiences. We believe that this variety drives excellence and innovation, strengthening our ability to lead in science and technology. We are committed to creating access and opportunities for all to develop and grow at your own pace. Join us in building a culture of inclusion and belonging that impacts millions and empowers everyone to work their magic and champion human progress!

Director, Electrical BoP Engineering
RWE Americas
Austin, TX
RWE Americas, LLC
To start as soon as possible, full time, permanent
Functional area:
Engineering
Remuneration:
Exempt
The Director Electrical BOP Engineering, Operations
, supports RWE America's renewable generation assets by managing the team focusing specifically on balance of plant (BOP) equipment and systems. The Electrical BOP team provides engineering expertise for a wide range of BOP components, such as transformers, cables, dynamic and static reactive power devices, substations, relays, breakers, and power plant controllers. By collaborating closely with teams in Operations, Asset Management, Compliance, and Development/Construction, the Electrical BOP team helps ensure that current and future generating assets consistently operate at their best.
We are seeking a strategic engineering leader with deep expertise in high-voltage infrastructure and utility-scale electrical Balance of Plant (BOP) architecture. The ideal candidate combines authoritative technical expertise with strong executive presence—equally skilled at setting multiyear fleet reliability strategies, navigating complex NERC/FERC compliance landscapes, and building high-performing engineering teams. You bring a strong owner-operator mindset, excel at cross-functional alignment across field operations and development, and thrive at translating technical electrical risk into actionable business decisions.
Role Responsibilities:
Define engineering vision, standards, and goals across the renewable generation fleet. Translate business objectives into technical action
Shape multiyear investment plans for substation upgrades, reliability enhancements, and compliance readiness
Oversee NERC/FERC audit preparedness and evidence reviews. Establish frameworks for continuous improvement and documentation rigor
Define the org structure, span of control, and career pathing for the Electrical BOP function. Sponsor key talent and hiring efforts
Represent engineering to executive leadership. Align initiatives with Asset Management, Field Operations, and Compliance
Evaluate and champion adoption of new engineering tools, modeling platforms, or controls testing technologies
Assess electrical risk and integration effort for acquired sites. Standardize onboarding of models, settings, and testing procedures
Define thresholds for technical sign-off, model review, and restoration support across the engineering team
Lead technical forensic investigations, Root Cause Analyses (RCAs), and major failure recovery efforts for critical fleet assets (e.g., main power transformers, HV breakers, dynamic VAR systems)
Oversee technical relationships with major equipment OEMs, engineering consultants, and testing contractors; establish standardized technical specifications and quality control guidelines for fleet repairs and retrofits
Job Requirements and Experiences:
Bachelor of Science or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering (EE) required (or equivalent deep experience in high-voltage power systems engineering)
Professional Engineer (PE) preferred
A minimum of 11 years of professional experience in electrical operations, asset management, or design (3+ years leading a team and/or function)
HV/EHV & Grid Interconnection Experience
Detailed knowledge of power generation and distribution equipment, transformers, switchgear, transmission feeders, substations, and renewable energy
Knowledge of Codes and Standards: NFPA 70E, IEEE 1584, NEC, NESC, OSHA regulations
Strong understanding of protective device coordination and relay settings
Familiarity with the North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC) standards
Familiarity with industry modeling software such as PSSE, PSLF, PSCAD, TSAT, and ETAP (a plus)
Serves as functional leader and internal expert
Establishes engineering policy and technical direction aligned with strategic goals.
Leads resolution of complex, ambiguous problems with long-term impacts
Balances competing priorities
Partners with senior leadership and external parties
Communicates vision and status of engineering initiatives
Strong interpersonal skills, with ability to manage customer relationships
Proven experience utilizing AI and other automation skills to optimize and organize work practices
Proven ability to empathize, build relationships, and effectively communicate with people from a diverse set of backgrounds
Is detail-oriented, has strong business acumen, and a sound understanding of business concepts
Work Environment:
This position is an office-based role with some travel and visits to other RWE Americas offices and field locations. The employee must be able to sit, walk, or stand for long durations of time.
Applicants must be legally authorized to work in the United States. RWE Americas is unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of employment visas at this time.
Pay range:
The annual base salary range for this position in California or New York is $210,000- $230,000. The listed salary range represents our good faith estimate for this position and represents the range for new hire salaries across all U.S locations. RWE considers factors such as (but not limited to) scope and responsibilities of the position, candidate’s education & work experience, training & certifications, and key skills as well as market and business considerations at the time of the offer.
Benefits offered:
Medical, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, Short-Term Disability, Long-Term Disability, 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, EAP, Education Assistance, Parental Leave, Paid time off, and Holidays. Eligible employees also participate in short-term incentives, in addition to salary.

Director: Operations Group/Transformation Services

Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 10,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. Lead end-to-end program management for complex technical operations initiatives including new product introductions, technology transfers, process validations, and facility fit assessments.
Develop integrated program plans, critical path analyses, risk registers, and resource plans; proactively identify and escalate risks and issues.
Own stage-gate processes and governance deliverables, ensuring milestones are met on time, within scope, and aligned to regulatory commitments.
Coordinate cross-functional workstreams across Manufacturing, Process Development, Quality, Regulatory Affairs, Supply Chain, and Engineering.
Partner with technical subject matter experts to translate scientific and process requirements into executable operational plans and develop staff awareness of critical process parameters (CPP) and critical quality attributes (CQA).
Support technology transfer activities from development into GMP manufacturing, including documentation, gap assessments, and readiness reviews.
Facilitate resolution of technical, operational, and quality issues that arise during operations, startup or shutdown of manufacturing equipment.
Develop manufacturing batch records, SOPs, validation protocols, and regulatory filing sections as required.
Represent operations in regulatory audits, including defense of process control strategy and executed batch records.
Perform comprehensive operational readiness assessments to confirm that manufacturing areas, equipment, processes, materials, personnel, and support systems are prepared for safe, compliant, and reliable GMP operations.
