Serve as the primary point of contact and program communicator for senior leadership, cross-functional partners, and external collaborators or CDMOs.
Prepare and deliver high-quality program status reports, executive briefings, and governance committee presentations.
Drive alignment across stakeholders with competing priorities; facilitate trade-off discussions and decision-making.
Champion operational excellence and lean principles within technical operations, identifying opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, and cycle time.
Support the development and deployment of program management frameworks, tools, and best practices across the organization.
Contribute to capacity planning, portfolio prioritization, and resource management processes.
Lead, coach, and develop a team of technical professionals to deliver high‑quality work aligned with project, client, and business objectives.
Provide day‑to‑day people leadership, including onboarding, training, mentorship, and ongoing skills development, to build a strong and capable technical team.
Set clear performance expectations and provide regular feedback, coaching, and guidance to support individual growth and accountability.
Other duties as assigned.
Attributes for Success
Technical Delivery: Applies advanced technical knowledge and professional expertise.
Innovation & Continuous Improvement: Seeks better ways, adapts to change and champions new ideas.
Customer Focus & Professionalism: Represents PF with consistent professionalism, appropriate escalation and respect for internal stakeholders, even during high-stress delivery situations.
Integrity & Humility: Demonstrates self-awareness and puts PF mission above ego.
Collaboration & Communication: Communicates clearly and proactively and drives transparent alignment with clients.
Project Execution: Delivers reliably, manages priorities and drives for high-quality outcomes.
Growth Mindset: Shows openness to new ideas, feedback, and change.

Bachelor’s Degree in Life Science, Engineering, or related discipline (OR a combination of equivalent work experience in capital project engineering, pharma cGMP facility start-up, CapEx/OpEx project management and/or comparable military experience).
20+ years of experience in operations management within pharmaceutical, biotech, or regulated manufacturing environments.
Demonstrated experience leading cross-functional programs or technology transfer projects in a GMP environment.
Strong understanding of pharmaceutical development and manufacturing processes (biologics, small molecule, or both).
Ability to interpret technical documentation and engineering drawings.
Working knowledge of cGMP regulations (FDA 21 CFR Parts 210/211, ICH guidelines, EMA requirements).
Exceptional organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
Proven ability to manage multiple priorities and drive results in a fast-paced, matrixed environment.
Experience leading teams.

Familiarity with ISO standards and FDA audit processes.
Experience supporting equipment qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ).
Experience with aseptic processing is a plus.
Experience with CDMOs and external manufacturing partner management.
Familiarity with regulatory submission processes (IND, BLA, NDA, MAA).
Proficiency with program management tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, Veeva Vault).
Six Sigma, Lean, or other continuous improvement certification.
Manufacturing startup, ramp-up, or remediation experience.
Operational excellence / reliability / OEE improvement experience.
Experience supporting client-facing consulting engagements.
Experience developing technical teams, delivery standards, or reusable frameworks.

Job Description


About FIS


Are you curious, motivated, and forward-thinking? At FIS you’ll have the opportunity to work on some of the most challenging and relevant issues in financial services and technology. Our talented people empower us, and we believe in being part of a team that is open, collaborative, entrepreneurial, passionate and above all fun.


Current and future sponsorship are not available for this position


Jacksonville, FL Hybrid (three days in-office, two days virtual)


About the team


The Quality Engineering Platform is part of FIS Developer Experience, the platform engineering group that builds the tools, pipelines and services more than 5,000 FIS engineers use to build, test and ship software. As AI coding assistants and agents write a growing share of our code, the volume of change is climbing fast. Our job is to make sure quality keeps pace, giving every team fast, trustworthy signal on whether a change is safe to release, whether a person or an AI wrote it.


What you will be doing


You will own the direction of the entire Quality Engineering Platform and lead the teams that build it, reporting to the head of Developer Experience platforms. You will decide where the platform goes as AI changes how software is written and tested, turn that into a roadmap teams across FIS want to adopt, and be accountable for the results.


  • Set the vision, strategy and multi-year roadmap for the Quality Engineering Platform, designed for a world where AI writes and tests a large share of our code.
  • Lead and grow the Quality Engineering Platform teams, including early-career engineers, in close partnership with the platform’s Principal Engineer and Delivery Manager.
  • Build quality capabilities for AI-generated code, such as automated test generation, checks that run before code is merged, and ways to measure whether AI tools actually improve outcomes.
  • Drive adoption across FIS engineering teams by making the platform the easiest path to fast, reliable testing, measured by adoption, release confidence and defects that reach clients.
  • Partner with DevSecOps, Developer Experience, observability and AI platform teams so quality is built into the developer workflow from first commit to production.
  • Own the platform’s operating model, including priorities, budget, tool and vendor choices, service levels and the metrics you report to senior leadership.

What you bring


  • Significant experience leading software engineering teams, including leading through managers or technical leads.
  • A track record of owning a platform or product end to end: strategy, roadmap, delivery and adoption by its users.
  • Deep, hands-on understanding of test automation, CI/CD and modern quality practices, enough to challenge technical decisions and earn the trust of senior engineers.
  • Practical experience with AI coding tools such as GitHub Copilot or Claude Code, and a clear point of view on how they change testing and quality.
  • Ability to express quality in numbers leadership cares about (escaped defects, release frequency, recovery time, test reliability) and use them to make decisions.
  • Confident communication with senior stakeholders and a habit of influencing teams you don’t directly manage.

Bonus if you have


  • Experience in financial services or another regulated industry where quality failures carry real client and compliance impact.
  • Experience building or adopting AI-driven testing, such as generated tests, self-healing tests or evaluation of AI agent output.
  • Experience running an internal platform as a product, with user research, adoption metrics and internal customer support.
  • Experience building teams that include early-career engineers or college hire programs.
  • Familiarity with tools such as Playwright, Cypress, k6 or Selenium at enterprise scale.

What we offer you


  • A competitive salary and benefits.
  • A variety of career development tools, resources and opportunities.
  • The chance to work on some of the most challenging, relevant issues. in financial services & technology.
  • Time to support charities and give back in your community.
  • A work environment built on collaboration, flexibility and respect.

FIS is committed to protecting the privacy and security of all personal information that we process in order to provide services to our clients. For specific information on how FIS protects personal information online, please see the Online Privacy Notice.

  • Drive adoption across FIS engineering teams by making the platform the easiest path to fast, reliable testing, measured by adoption, release confidence and defects that reach clients.

evidence.text:
Manufacturing Engineering Manager
McLaren Automotive Ltd
Sheffield, TX
What to Expect
To lead the Manufacturing Engineering team and take responsibility for all manufacturing processes from Job 1 onwards at the McLaren Composites Technology Centre. The role combines people management, reporting on team progress and planning the future direction of the team with hands-on technical support when required. It drives improvements in quality, scrap reduction, cost reduction, cycle time reduction and equipment availability, while owning the manufacturing engineering budget and engineering change process and providing consultation during product introduction.
What You'll Do
As Manufacturing Engineering Manager, your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:
Leading and managing a team of Manufacturing Engineers, setting priorities, allocating resources and supporting individual development.
Taking responsibility for all manufacturing processes from Job 1 onwards, using process data to prioritise improvements in quality, scrap, cost, cycle time and equipment availability.
Overseeing Practical Problem-Solving (PPS) activities to resolve quality and process issues within agreed timeframes and ensure corrective actions are sustained.
Ensuring production process documentation, including process flows, PFMEAs and control plans, remains accurate and up to date.
Ensuring standard operating procedures, work instructions and product standards reflect current manufacturing requirements.
Owning the engineering change process for manufacturing, including approvals and the controlled implementation of changes.
Providing manufacturing engineering consultation during product introduction, advising on process capability, manufacturability and production readiness.
Owning the manufacturing engineering budget, planning expenditure and prioritising investment to support manufacturing objectives.
Coordinating manufacturing engineering support for Production and Maintenance teams and providing hands-on technical assistance when required.
Reporting team progress, project status, risks and key performance indicators to stakeholders, with a focus on quality, scrap reduction, cost reduction, cycle time reduction and equipment availability.
Planning the future direction, capability and resource needs of the Manufacturing Engineering team to support manufacturing priorities.
What You'll Bring
Essential Experience / Skills:
Previous experience in a manufacturing environment.
People management experience, including setting objectives, supporting development and managing workloads.
Proficiency in structured problem-solving methodologies, such as 8D and PPS.
Ability to manage process improvement projects using structured approaches such as DMAIC.
Ability to analyse complex process data and use it to prioritise manufacturing improvements.
Ability to establish accurate and relevant data collection systems.
Ability to plan and manage a manufacturing engineering budget and prioritise expenditure.
Understanding of manufacturing process documentation, including process flows, PFMEAs and control plans.
Strong presentation skills, with the ability to report team progress and communicate complex issues clearly.
Understanding of structured engineering change management and approval processes.
Strong IT proficiency and the ability to use digital tools for analysis, planning and reporting.
Desirable Experience / Skills:
Experience leading a team, preferably within manufacturing engineering.
Automotive manufacturing experience.
Familiarity with engineering CAPEX procurement.
Experience composite manufacturing.
Personal Attributes / Competencies
Self-motivated, with the ability to balance people management, team planning and hands-on technical support.
Adaptable to a dynamic and fast-paced environment.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
Effective in influencing, negotiating, and resolving conflicts.
Flexible and open-minded approach to tasks and responsibilities.
What We'll Do for You
We offer a wide – ranging benefits package, which includes:
Structured career development framework
25 days’ holiday, plus bank holiday. Annual buy & sell up to five days
Enhanced company pension scheme
Discretionary annual bonus award
Private medical insurance and health cash plan
Life assurance benefit
Ability to apply for a sabbatical of up to one year after only two years’ service
Benefits you can adapt to your lifestyle, such as discounted shopping
Generous parental leave policies
A range of wellbeing initiatives, such as employee assistance programme and free financial & mortgage advice
Who Are We?
No restraints. No limitations. We don’t simply push boundaries. We completely rethink them. McLaren Automotive exists to create breath-taking performance road cars.
It takes a community to do what we do. A diverse group of people with many areas of expertise, united by their passion to deliver visionary products and set new benchmarks.
McLaren Automotive commits to equal opportunity for all. Diversity, Equality and Inclusion is at the heart of our impact, it drives our innovation and enables us to truly create something special. Join us on our journey.

evidence.text:
Head of Bedrock Operations Center
Bedrock Robotics
Lockhart, TX
Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world
At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.
In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic
In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.
This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.
About The Role
We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.
This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.
The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.
What You'll Do
Operations Center Strategy & Build-out
Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales
Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists
Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types
Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity
Remote Assistance
Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority
Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams
Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators
Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time
Customer & Partner Support
Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering
Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment
Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes
Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health
Central Operations / Command & Control
Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site
Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing
Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review
Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms
Performance & Analytics
Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve
Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership
Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support
What Success Looks Like
Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it
Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution
Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently
Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements
The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service
Required
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)
Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces
Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments
Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth
Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)
Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations
Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives
Preferred
Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining
Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems
Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry
Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products
Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools
Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones
Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience
WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS
Every autonomous machine Bedrock deploys depends on the Operations Center to keep it safe, productive, and supported. You'll build the function that lets our fleet scale with confidence, and directly shape the experience every customer and partner has with Bedrock.

evidence.text:
Head of Bedrock Operations Center
Bedrock Robotics
Lockhart, TX
Join the team bringing autonomy to the built world
At Bedrock, we're moving AI out of the lab and onto real job sites. Our team includes veterans who helped launch Waymo, scaled Segment to a $3.2B acquisition, and grew Uber Freight to $5B in revenue. We retrofit the heavy equipment contractors already own, starting with excavators, so experienced crews can safely take on more projects and deliver more of the critical infrastructure our society needs.
In August 2026, Bedrock-equipped excavators began doing fully autonomous, paid work on live commercial job sites. We've more than doubled our customer base since 2025, and our machines now work with contractors across the South, Midwest, and Mid-Atlantic
In October 2026, we raised a $600M Series C co-led by CapitalG and Emergence Capital, bringing our total funding to nearly $1B. We're using it to put more autonomous machines to work, build the field and operations teams behind every deployment, and expand into new machine types and job-site tasks.
This is where algorithms meet steel-toed boots. You'll work alongside construction veterans and world-class engineers to solve physical-world problems that simulations can't touch. If you're ready to do meaningful work on hard problems, we'd love to have you join us.
About The Role
We are seeking a Head of Bedrock Operations Center (BOC) to build and lead the central, always-on hub that oversees our deployed autonomous machines. As the Bedrock System deployments scale across new states, new machine types, and a next-generation platform, the BOC is how we keep every machine safe, productive, and supported around the clock.
This role owns three core functions: Remote Assistance, supporting autonomous machines in real time when they need a human decision; Customer & Partner Support, the single front door for customers, partners, and field teams; and Central Operations, which provides live visibility, dispatch coordination, and incident coordination and command.
The Head of BOC owns the Operations Center's operating model, organization, tooling requirements, performance, and manpower oversight. The BOC is accountable for the safe remote operations, uptime, and responsiveness our customers experience. Reporting to the VP of Operations, this leader is a critical thought partner to Product and to Operations Leads across the company.
What You'll Do
Operations Center Strategy & Build-out
Define the BOC operating model, org structure, and coverage model (shifts, time zones, follow-the-sun) as the fleet scales
Build and lead the BOC leadership team and a growing workforce of shift leads and specialists
Own workforce planning and ensure adequate, qualified staffing; Partner with Product and Engineering on machines-per-operator ratios against fleet growth, product mix, and new machine types
Own the physical and technical readiness of the Operations Center, including infrastructure, redundancy, connectivity, and business continuity
Remote Assistance
Own round-the-clock remote operations for autonomous machines, including response-time SLAs, escalation protocols, and clear decision authority
Establish safety-first standards for remote interventions, remote stops, and hand-offs to on-site personnel, in partnership with Safety teams
Build training, certification, and quality-assurance programs for remote assistance operators
Analyze intervention data and partner with Autonomy Engineering to reduce interventions and improve machine autonomy over time
Customer & Partner Support
Build and lead a tiered support function (L1 / L2 / L3) with clear escalation paths into Field Operations, Service, Hardware, RA, and/ or Engineering
Define and deliver support SLAs tailored to each product line and customer commitment
Own ticketing, knowledge base, and customer communication standards; turn voice-of-customer trends into fixes
Partner with the Commercial team on customer onboarding, service commitments, and account health
Central Operations / Command & Control
Own live, fleet-wide situational awareness: machine status, health, location, and utilization across every site
Coordinate daily dispatch, service, and maintenance with Field Operations, including parts and technician routing
Serve as incident command for operational and safety events, with clear playbooks for triage, escalation, communication, and post-incident review
Own runbooks, shift hand-off standards, and change management for new sites, new machine types, and new platforms
Performance & Analytics
Define and track core BOC metrics: intervention rate and response time, resolution time, SLA attainment, fleet uptime, customer satisfaction, and cost to serve
Run operational review cadences that drive accountability and bring key insights to leadership
Lead continuous improvement through process, automation, and data, increasing the number of machines each operator can safely support
What Success Looks Like
Autonomous machines get fast, safe human support whenever they need it
Customers and partners have one clear front door and consistently fast resolution
Real-time visibility into every machine and site, with incidents handled calmly and transparently
Machines-per-operator rises steadily as intervention insights drive autonomy improvements
The Operations Center scales ahead of fleet growth, new sites, and new machine types without a drop in service
Required
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
12+ years in operations leadership, including 5+ years building and leading 24/7 or mission-critical operations (command centers, remote operations, network or fleet operations, or large-scale support organizations)
Experience building an operations organization from early stage to scale, including hiring and developing managers and shift leads and managing large hourly and/or contract workforces
Track record defining and managing SLAs, escalation paths, and incident response in safety-critical or high-availability environments
Experience influencing engineering, product, and commercial leaders, driving difficult decisions, and managing risk through rapid growth
Strong analytical skills; comfortable with operational data, dashboards, and forecasting models (SQL / BI tools a plus)
Experience with workforce planning, scheduling, and shift-based operations
Excellent written and verbal communication with customers, field crews, and executives
Preferred
Experience running operations centers for autonomous vehicles, robotics, trucking, aviation, or mining
Experience leading remote assistance, teleoperation, or fleet response teams for autonomous systems
Familiarity with heavy machinery and/or the construction industry
Experience building B2B or technical support for industrial equipment or hardware products
Familiarity with fleet telemetry, monitoring and alerting, ticketing, and workforce-management tools
Experience launching operations across multiple regions or time zones
Continuous improvement / Lean / Six Sigma experience
WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS
Every autonomous machine Bedrock deploys depends on the Operations Center to keep it safe, productive, and supported. You'll build the function that lets our fleet scale with confidence, and directly shape the experience every customer and partner has with Bedrock.
Bedrock Robotics is an Equal Opportunity Employer
We’re committed to building a diverse and inclusive workplace. We consider all qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, veteran status, genetic information, or any other protected characteristic.
Reasonable Accommodations
We want our hiring process to be accessible to everyone. If you need an accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let your recruiter know so we can support you.

evidence.quote: 15+ years in food manufacturing operations
evidence.text:
VP Manufacturing & Operations
Chocxo Chocolatier
Rockwall, TX
ChocXO Chocolatier LLC is a leading North American premium chocolate manufacturer grounded in innovation, quality, and sustainability. We are a fast-growing, vertically integrated food manufacturing company operating across branded CPG and contract manufacturing. In the past year, we have scaled from one manufacturing facility to two, expanded our brand portfolio, and invested heavily in new capacity, innovation, and infrastructure. Our footprint includes Delta, British Columbia: Our 60,000 sq ft, fully automated, SQF Level 3 operational flagship, and Rockwall, Texas: Our new 225,000 sq ft manufacturing and warehouse complex, scheduled to open in 2027. We are now at the stage where systems, discipline, and repeatability matter as much as growth. We are building an enterprise-grade operations platform designed to scale—not a collection of plants dependent on heroics. We foster a culture of accountability where professionals thrive in structured environments and uphold rigorous standards.
The Role:
The VP, Manufacturing & Operations reports directly to the President and leads plant operations at both of ChocXO’s manufacturing facilities: Delta, British Columbia and Rockwall, Texas. The Plant Managers at each location report directly to this role. The VP is the senior leader accountable for end-to-end operational performance across both sites, including manufacturing execution, food safety leadership, QA capability, OT systems oversight, and operational excellence.
This is a hands-on, high-accountability leadership role. It requires deep manufacturing judgment, disciplined execution, and the confidence to stop production, reset standards, and enforce compliance when required.
Key Responsibilities
Multi-Plant Leadership
Directly lead, develop, and hold accountable the Plant Managers for Delta, BC and Rockwall, TX
Establish consistent expectations, KPIs, and operating cadence across all sites
Ensure alignment between plant-level execution and enterprise standards
Be visibly present in plants — especially during audits, trials, startups, and corrective actions
Operational Technology (OT) & Systems
Provide leadership and oversight for OT systems supporting manufacturing operations
o production monitoring
o process controls
o data integrity
o system discipline
Ensure OT systems support repeatability, visibility, and accountability, not workarounds
Partner with engineering and IT, but own operational effectiveness of systems on the floor
Food Safety, Quality & Audit Readiness
Provide senior leadership on food safety expectations and audit readiness
Set the standard for:
o regulatory compliance
o customer audits
o third-party food safety certifications
Build and lead a strong, credible QA organization
Ensure quality systems are proactive, documented, and enforced — not reactive or cosmetic
Personally set the tone that food safety and quality are non-negotiable
Process Discipline & Validation
Establish and enforce standardized operating procedures (SOPs)
Own process validation, trial approval, and GO / NO-GO decision gates
Eliminate reliance on undocumented adjustments, heroics, or tribal knowledge
Ensure processes run within defined parameters, with normal staffing, on repeat days
Inventory, Scrap & Loss Control
Own accountability for scrap, rework, obsolete inventory, and yield loss
Implement root-cause analysis and corrective action discipline
Drive early-warning indicators and corrective action — not post-event explanations
Embed cost awareness without compromising safety or quality
Training, Safety & Accountability Culture
Build structured training systems for operators, supervisors, and plant leadership
Lead facility safety as a core operational priority
Establish and enforce an accountability culture:
o clear expectations
o clear consequences
o consistent follow-through
Partner with HR, but retain operational authority and standards
Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement
Drive operational excellence across safety, quality, delivery, cost, and morale
Standardize best practices across plants
Lead continuous improvement initiatives grounded in data and discipline
Ensure improvements are institutionalized, not personality-dependent
AI, Automation & Digital Efficiency
Use AI and advanced analytics to drive efficiency, throughput, and yield improvement across manufacturing and warehouse operations
Identify, evaluate, and deploy practical AI tools (e.g., predictive maintenance, demand and production scheduling, quality and vision inspection, downtime and scrap analysis)
Leverage AI-enabled insights from OT and ERP data to make faster, fact-based decisions and catch issues before they become losses
Build team capability and comfort with AI tools, ensuring adoption is disciplined, documented, and compliant with food safety and data integrity requirements
What Success Looks Like
Plant Managers are strong, accountable leaders — not firefighters
Food safety audits are predictable, calm, and well-prepared
QA is respected, not overridden
OT systems provide clarity and control, not noise
Scrap, rework, and operational “surprises” trend down materially
Operations run consistently across plants and shifts
The President is not required to intervene in day-to-day operations
AI and automation tools are delivering measurable gains in efficiency, yield, and uptime
Required Experience & Profile
Experience
15+ years in food manufacturing operations
Proven multi-plant leadership experience
Deep, practical expertise in:
o food safety systems
o quality assurance
o audit management
o allergen control
o sanitation validation
o process control
Experience scaling operations in fast-growth environments
Sufficient, hands-on experience applying AI, automation, and data analytics in a manufacturing environment to drive measurable efficiency gains
Cross-border operations experience (U.S./Canada) strongly preferred
Leadership Attributes
Exceptionally detail-oriented
Disciplined, methodical, and structured
Calm, firm, and decisive
Comfortable holding leaders accountable
Respected on the plant floor — not theatrical, not passive
Strong presence without ego
Comfortable saying “no” to bad ideas, shortcuts, or pressure
What We Are Not Looking For
“Idea-first” operators without execution depth
Leaders who normalize exceptions and workarounds
Consultants masquerading as operators
People who rely on heroics instead of systems
Anyone uncomfortable enforcing standards or stopping production
Location & Travel
Based at Rockwall, TX (DFW area). This is a fully on-site role, not remote, because presence matters
Regular travel between the Rockwall and Delta plants is required, including during audits, trials, startups, and corrective actions
Must be able to travel between the U.S. and Canada
Why This Role Matters
This role is central to building a durable, scalable manufacturing platform.
The right leader will:
Bring order to complexity
Reduce operational risk
Strengthen food safety and quality credibility
Enable profitable, disciplined growth
If you are a serious food manufacturing operations leader who believes strong systems beat heroics, we want to talk.
ChocXO Chocolatier LLC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, gender identity, and sexual orientation), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws. All employment decisions at ChocXO are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications.
ChocXO Chocolatier LLC is committed to providing reasonable accommodation to qualified individuals with disabilities throughout the recruitment process. Applicants who require accommodation during the application or hiring process will be considered on a case-by-case basis in accordance with applicable laws.

Director of Manufacturing
RK Industries
Denver, CO
Description
Salary: $160,000-200,000/annual
RK Company Overview
As a second-generation, family-owned enterprise, RK Industries, LLC (RK) offers a diverse range of construction, manufacturing, advanced fabrication and building services. Led by Rick and Jon Kinning, RK represents seven distinct lines of business that work together to provide seamless project collaboration. Our exclusive building methodologies, accredited safety standards and professional execution allow us to turn our customers’ greatest concepts into reality.
Position And Responsibilities Overview
Create, develop and train a world-class production and installation team.
Provide leadership for the production operation delivering quality products productively and efficiently.
Recruit, develop, and train a high performance team
Ensure that production processes are optimized for each product and that process controls are in place
Designs, implements and leads best-in-class business production processes
Oversees technical and professional development of the Production team and function
Serve as the principal company Production interface with the market and customers.
Lead in continual improvement, corrective action and customer satisfaction practices.
Responsible for the technical accuracy, quality and cost effectiveness of the production operation.
Provide production leadership in problem solving and troubleshooting of issues or problems.
Create a team oriented working environment that fosters growth, accountability & fun.
Provide clear leadership and vision, inspire and motivate the Production staff to achieve excellence.
Facilitate, direct and drive continuous Improvement across all production related areas of the business.
Lead value production, design optimization, and constructability efforts coordinating with production team
Lead the daily production to ensure assigned tasks are delivered within budget, on schedule and in accordance with established policies and procedures.
Accountable for the performance of the production team and the quality of the products.
Responsible and accountable for the development of a “zero injury” culture.
Compliance and implementation of all company policies and procedures
Accountable for the safety and well-being of direct reports and all other employees.
Qualification
Strong leadership skills and work ethic to enable the creation of a highly capable Production Operation
15+ years of relevant experience in Production, Manufacturing, or Construction
Proven ability to effectively lead, supervise, hire, develop, and mentor talented production resources
Experience in off-site manufacturing/production/modular environments
Demonstrated success in change management, problem solving, and solution development.
Action-oriented and innovative in leading the Construction and Production functions
Capable of driving change transformation to achieve specific business results
Skilled in production processes of modular businesses
Knowledgeable in Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma process improvements
Demonstrates a high level of ethical behavior in exercising judgment and discretion in matters of significance
Excellent oral and written communication skills with the ability to negotiate and influence
Outstanding interpersonal skills with the ability to build relationships with employees & customers.
Proven leadership and management skills with the ability to optimize team performance
Strong and confident negotiator with the ability to negotiate at all levels
Excellent communication, interpersonal, influencing, and problem solving skills
Experience and technical understanding of data centers, data center modules, and modular processes.
This position requires shop work. When working in the shop, one must exercise caution as this environment presents many naturally-occurring and potentially worker-produced hazards
It is very important that the incumbent of this position is able to work and communicate with prudence, while effectively managing time, completing tasks and working safely.
Completion of high school or equivalent education.
Post-secondary diploma is a plus
Analytical problem solver with good communication skills.
ISO, 5S, Lean Six Sigma, Kaizen, and Visual Factory Management experience preferred.
Lean Six Sigma Black Belt preferred.
OSHA 30 hour certification.
Experience with all safe practices, procedures, and overall processes associated with construction and manufacturing from raw materials to finished product.
Company Benefits
Comprehensive medical plans with HSA and FSA options for you and your family.
Generous 401(k) plan with immediate company match – 100% vested.
Dental and vision insurance for your well-being.
Short-term and long-term disability plans available after one year.
Company provided life insurance and AD&D with options for supplemental buy-ups.
Enjoy paid time off and holidays.
Get paid weekly for your convenience.
In-house Programs
Elevate your skills with career development training at RK University.
Unlock discounts on essential products and services like phones, internet and work apparel.
Participate in fun company and team-building events.
Make a difference with volunteering opportunities.
Partnership Programs
Access confidential counseling for personal issues and financial advice.
Enjoy exclusive discounts on entertainment, including amusement park tickets and restaurant specials.
Safety is Our Top Priority
Comply with all company policies and procedures.
All employees are accountable for safety and health and are empowered to stop work if an unsafe condition is present. Employees should immediately notify their supervisor so that the hazard may be corrected.
RK Mechanical employees and subcontractors are required to implement and maintain all safety and health systems practices including the training requirements of RK Mechanical Orientation, shop specific orientation, CPR/First Aid/AED/Bloodborne Pathogens, Hazard Identification and Reporting, and OSHA 10.
Minimum Physical Requirements
Work predominately inside and in dusty and noisy areas.
Work in high places, tight places, and confined spaces.
Ability to stand for long periods of time
Ability to lift and carry 51 to 75 lbs. occasionally, and/or 31 to 45 pounds of force frequently, and/or greater than negligible up to 16 to 22 pounds of force constantly to move objects.
Ability to balance, kneel, squat, crouch, bend, lean, stand, walk, and climb.
Use of Personal Protection Equipment will be required
Regularly works near moving mechanical parts and in conditions that include heat and cold.
Must be able to lift, push, pull or carry objects, use abdominal and lower back muscles to provide support over time without fatigue.
Why RK is a Great Place to Work
At RK, we take immense pride in our diverse business units, each specializing in delivering exceptional projects, products and services to our customers. What sets us apart is our unique ability to integrate these services, providing comprehensive solutions and offering our employees ample opportunities for growth and learning across different businesses.
RK Mechanical: commercial and industrial plumbing, mechanical, process and HVAC contracting.
RK Steel: custom fabrication and manufacturing of structural steel and miscellaneous metals for various industries.
RK Electrical: commercial and industrial electrical contracting and service.
RK Water: groundwater dewatering and remediation, facilities water treatment and custom fabrication.
RK Service: commercial and industrial building and maintenance services.
RK Energy: custom fabrication for various industries requiring ASME and modular skidded solutions.
RK Mission Critical: design and manufacturing for off-site constructed modular solutions.
Our commitment to excellence has been recognized with numerous awards for our outstanding performance and contributions, including high rankings in various categories from the Denver Business Journal and ABC’s Top Performers by Market, illustrating our broad expertise. We’ve been consistently recognized as a top private company and a leading employer by ColoradoBiz Magazine, and we're proud of our long-standing position as number one in the Top 50 Family-Owned Companies since 2011.
Our strong commitment to safety, wellness and employee development has earned us prestigious accolades:
ABC Step Awards
ACCA Award Member
AGC Safety Utah
American Heart Association Fit-Friendly Worksite Award
Wellness Workdays and Harvard Medical School Best Wellness Employer Certification
Colorado Workforce Development Council Excellence in Apprenticeship Award
Business Experiential Learning Commission Colorado Apprentice Award
In addition to our engagement with the community, we have been acknowledged in:
Denver Business Journal Corporate Philanthropy rankings
Named among The Civic 50 Colorado as one of the most community-minded companies
Each of our business units has its own impressive list of awards and recognitions, such as:
Engineering News Record Top 20 Firms in Steel Erection
ABC Excellence in Construction Awards
AGC Awards for Construction Excellence
Xcel Energy Top Trade Partner in Energy Efficiency
USGBC LEED Program Member
IECRM Annual Summit Awards
MFG Magazine Colorado Manufacturing Awards
We also adhere to rigorous quality standards and accreditations, including:
ISO 9001:2015
ISO 14001:2015
ISO 45001:2018
AISC certifications
As a new member of our team, you’ll be joining a company that’s not just award-winning but is also consistently striving to exceed expectations and deliver excellence in all we do. Become an essential part of our thriving and dynamic team, where your contributions will drive our continued success.
RK Industries, LLC is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status or any other status protected by applicable law

evidence.quote: 8+ years experience in shipbuilding, heavy manufacturing, or large-scale industrial production engineering.
evidence.text:
Production Engineering Manager
Saronic Technologies
Brownsville, TX
Saronic Technologies is a leader in revolutionizing autonomy at sea, dedicated to developing state-of-the-art solutions that enhance maritime operations through autonomous and intelligent platforms.
Job Overview
The Production Engineering Manager leads the development of the production engineering function required to stand up and scale shipyard manufacturing operations. This role is responsible for defining the build strategy, developing production processes, and ensuring that vessel designs are compatible with facility capabilities.
The Production Engineering Manager serves as the technical bridge between engineering, manufacturing, and facilities, translating ship designs into efficient and executable production plans. This includes defining block construction strategy, heavy lift and transport engineering, and establishing the production rules that govern how vessels are built within the shipyard.
A critical component of the role is developing and maintaining the Facilities Production Manual, which provides engineering teams with the design constraints and manufacturing rules required to ensure that vessel designs can be efficiently produced within Port Alpha’s facilities.
Responsibilities
Production Build Strategy
Define and maintain the shipyard’s production build strategy, including panelization, block construction, and erection sequencing.
Develop block breakdown structures and manufacturing strategies aligned with facility capabilities.
Ensure vessel designs align with yard constraints such as crane capacities, transportation limits, and assembly workflows.
Heavy Lift & Transport Engineering
Develop engineering strategies for lifting, transporting, and erecting ship blocks and major modules.
Define lift plans, rigging concepts, and transport methods for large assemblies.
Coordinate with heavy lift equipment operators and infrastructure teams to validate lifting and movement strategies.
Production Process Development
Develop standardized manufacturing processes for steel fabrication, block assembly, and erection.
Establish production workflows, takt planning concepts, and throughput assumptions.
Identify opportunities for automation and process optimization within shipyard operations.
Facilities Production Manual
Lead development of the Facilities Production Manual, establishing design rules for engineering teams.
Define constraints including maximum block weights, dimensions, lifting interfaces, transport paths, and production tolerances.
Ensure naval architects and vessel design teams incorporate facility manufacturing requirements early in the design process.
Manufacturing Integration
Work closely with ship design teams to ensure production feasibility.
Translate vessel design into manufacturing work packages and build sequences.
Support development of digital models and production simulations.
Startup & Industrialization
Support the startup of new shipyard facilities and manufacturing systems.
Validate production processes during early vessel builds.
Capture lessons learned and refine production engineering standards.
Cross-Functional Collaboration
Partner with engineering, facilities, automation, and operations teams to align production systems.
Provide production engineering input to equipment selection and facility design.
Support strategic planning for future production capacity expansion.
What Success Looks Like
Vessel designs consistently align with shipyard manufacturing capabilities.
Block construction and erection sequences are clearly defined and executable.
Production processes are standardized and scalable.
Engineering teams utilize the Facilities Production Manual as a core design reference.
The shipyard achieves predictable production flow during early vessel builds.
Qualifications
Required
8+ years experience in shipbuilding, heavy manufacturing, or large-scale industrial production engineering.
Strong experience developing build strategies for large fabricated structures.
Experience with heavy lift engineering, rigging, or large assembly operations.
Demonstrated ability to translate product design into manufacturing processes.
Strong cross-functional collaboration with engineering and operations teams.
Preferred
Ship Structural Design Experience experience.
Familiarity with panel line production and modular ship construction.
Experience with digital production planning or simulation tools.
Background in lean manufacturing or industrial system design.
Physical Requirements
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Occasional standing and walking within the office
Manual dexterity to operate a computer keyboard, mouse, and other office equipment
Visual acuity to read screens, documents, and reports
Occasional reaching, bending, or stooping to access file drawers, cabinets, or office supplies
Lifting and carrying items up to 20 pounds occasionally (e.g., office supplies, packages)
Benefits:
Medical Insurance:
Comprehensive health insurance plans covering a range of services
Saronic pays 100% of the premium for employees and 80% for dependents
Dental and Vision Insurance:
Coverage for routine dental check-ups, orthodontics, and vision care
Saronic pays 100% of the premium under the basic plan for employees and 80% for dependents
Time Off:
Generous PTO and Holidays
Parental Leave:
Paid maternity and paternity leave to support new parents
Competitive Salary:
Industry-standard salaries with opportunities for performance-based bonuses
Retirement Plan:
401(k) plan with company match
Stock Options:
Equity options to give employees a stake in the company’s success
Life and Disability Insurance:
Basic life insurance and short- and long-term disability coverage
Pet Insurance:
Discounted pet insurance options including 24/7 Telehealth helpline
Additional Perks:
Free lunch benefit and unlimited free drinks and snacks in the office

evidence.quote: Eight to twelve years of experience in video production, creative production, content production, agency environments, or internal brand teams.
evidence.text:
Production Director
Tactacam
Billings, MT
Company Overview
At Tactacam, we are a rapidly growing team of tech innovators, trail-blazers, and outdoor enthusiasts working to engineer the outdoors! We are proud to be a market-leading outdoor camera and technology company, but at our core, we are just a group of people obsessed with the great outdoors. We are far more than a technology company; we are a community that values fresh air as much as fresh ideas. As restless adventurers, we know that the best ideas rarely happen behind a desk, which is why we constantly encourage our team to get outside, use our products, and let the natural world inspire their next big breakthrough.
We also operate as tech trailblazers who are moving fast. With over 500,000+ active customers worldwide and a constantly expanding product line, we are actively pushing the boundaries of what outdoor technology can do. Because "good enough" isn't in our vocabulary, we intentionally foster an environment of ambitious dreamers where every team member is encouraged to aim higher, dream bigger, and drive innovation forward. We believe that your career should be an adventure too, and our rapid growth offers limitless possibilities for career advancement, personal development, and hands-on impact
Job Overview
The Director, Video Production leads the development, execution, and delivery of video content across the brand portfolio. This person owns the entire production process from the first idea through final delivery and ensures the work reflects the brand, serves business goals, and reaches a consistently high creative standard. This role sits at the intersection of creative leadership and production operations. Success requires someone who can move comfortably between shaping stories, directing on set, building production systems, managing budgets, and coordinating complex schedules across teams and partners. The Director creates the environment that allows great creative work to happen repeatedly and at scale.
Responsibilities
Lead the creative vision for video and motion content across campaigns, product launches, brand storytelling, retail content, social media, evergreen initiatives, and emerging opportunities.
Translate business objectives and brand strategy into visual concepts and compelling narratives that connect with audiences.
Direct productions during planning and execution, guiding visual style, pacing, performance, framing, and overall storytelling.
Establish and maintain creative standards across all video content while ensuring consistency in quality and brand expression.
Partner closely with Brand, Creative, Social, Community, Product Marketing, and Performance Marketing teams to shape content strategies and bring ideas to life.
Guide concept development, scripting, storyboarding, creative reviews, and final approvals.
Own production from beginning to end including planning, budgeting, scheduling, logistics, staffing, execution, editing, post production, delivery, and asset organization.
Develop and improve production workflows that increase output, reduce friction, and create greater consistency across projects.
Build production briefs, schedules, timelines, production documentation, and internal processes that support efficient execution.
Make decisions that balance creative ambition, production realities, timing, and budget. Create and manage a rolling twelve month production roadmap aligned with campaign calendars, product launches, seasonal priorities, and business objectives.
Develop annual and quarterly production schedules with clear priorities, resource allocation, and cross functional alignment.
Forecast production capacity and proactively identify future needs across internal teams, contractors, equipment, and external partners.
Coordinate production efforts across stakeholders to maximize content opportunitiesand eliminate inefficiencies.
Define and monitor production performance metrics including delivery timelines, budget health, asset utilization, output volume, and operational efficiency.
Build systems that support content reuse and scalable capture strategies to extend the value of every production.
Own relationships with production agencies, freelance crews, editors, photographers, production houses, and specialty creative partners. Negotiate and manage retained services, project contracts, scopes of work, statements of work, and external agreements.
Evaluate partner performance and continuously improve the network of trusted production resources.
Oversee production budgets, estimates, invoicing, and financial planning while
maintaining accountability and transparency.
Identify opportunities to increase production efficiency without reducing creative quality.
Lead and develop the internal video and production team while creating clear expectations and a culture of ownership.
Own and manage vendor relationships, budgets, and licensing for all external audio, video, and AI platforms, ensuring optimal value and proper licensing for all project deliverables.
Coach team members across concepting, production, editorial, and creative execution.
Support hiring, contractor selection, onboarding, and team growth.
Create an environment where creativity, accountability, craftsmanship, and operational excellence can coexist.
Requirements
Eight to twelve years of experience in video production, creative production, content production, agency environments, or internal brand teams.
Demonstrated success leading productions from concept through completion.
Strong experience managing production schedules, budgets, agencies, vendors, and external partners.
Deep understanding of production operations and post production workflows across multiple content formats and channels.
Comfort directing on set and making creative decisions in real time.
Strong communication, leadership, and organizational skills.
Experience building scalable content systems and supporting multiple priorities simultaneously.
Success in This Role
Video productions launch consistently and predictably.
Creative output strengthens the brand and raises the quality bar.
Production becomes a strategic capability rather than a reactive service.
Resources are planned effectively and teams spend more time creating and less time coordinating.
The organization gains confidence that ambitious ideas can move from concept to execution without unnecessary complexity.
Why you want to work here
Comprehensive Health & Wellness: Includes medical, dental, and vision coverage, along with life insurance and disability protection.
Generous Paid Leave: Offers competitive time off and in addition to pregnancy leave, parental and military leave, and unique "Hunting Holidays" for outdoor activities.
Financial Planning: Supports future retirement goals through a company-managed 401(k) plan.
Outdoor-Centric Culture: Features remote-first flexibility, employee discounts, complimentary camera gear, company-sponsored outdoor trips, and community projects.
Recognition & Values: Honors top performance through monthly "TactaValor Awards" that celebrate company values like innovation, tenacity, and customer focus.
Location Limitations:
Please note at this time, we are not accepting applications from candidates based in Alaska (AK), Connecticut (CT), Delaware (DE), Massachusetts (MA), New Mexico (NM), and South Dakota (SD)
Equal Opportunity Employer
Tactacam is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate against any applicant or employee based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other protected status. We are committed to providing a fair and inclusive work environment for all, and we encourage individuals of all backgrounds to apply for our open positions. If you require reasonable accommodation during the application process, please let us know, and we will be happy to assist.

evidence.quote: Knowledge of manufacturing processes and products as well as quality systems and associated literacy of SPC, SOP’s, process specifications etc.
evidence.text:
Plant Manager
Carlisle Construction Materials
Mead, NE
Job Description
Carlisle Companies is a leading manufacturer of building envelope products and solutions that make buildings more energy efficient, durable, and sustainable.   We deliver roofing, insulation, waterproofing, and architectural systems for commercial and residential projects using a focus on innovation and continuous improvement to solve today’s challenges.   We’re equally committed to our people, prioritizing safety, inclusion, career growth development, tuition assistance, and excellent benefits.
With manufacturing, engineering, R&D, and corporate functions across North America and globally, Carlisle offers stability, agility, and opportunity in a performance-driven culture. Do meaningful work and shape the future of building solutions; apply today and come grow with us.
We are looking for a Plant Manager to join our Insulfoam team in Mead, Nebraska.
Job Summary
The Plant Manager has general management responsibility for the overall manufacturing processes as well as the physical facility. This includes accountabilities for all products manufactured, all aspects of safety performance including environmental, product quality and quantity, personnel hiring and discipline, training, budgeting, shipping, and receiving, cost control and reduction, developing a strong team environment with clear and effective communications. Serve as the key interface with a variety of support personnel including R&D, Engineering, Technical Services, Scheduling, Sales and Customer Service and Logistics. Utilize the Carlisle Operating System framework as the foundation for the training of employees and to support operational requirements. Scope of the job hours of operations 7am to 5pm Monday through Friday with “On Call” 24 hours availability. Possible weekend hours to meet production demands in busy seasons. Occasional travel to other facilities for meetings or training, typically no more than 15% travel.
Duties And Responsibilities
Develop a manufacturing team to provide exceptional customer service by providing the required quantities of products at the lowest possible cost and highest quality while maintaining a safe work environment. Specific duties include employee development/training, plant scheduling, interviewing, hiring/firing, customer contact, root cause analysis, financial tracking, safety implementation, supplier evaluation, and process improvement.
Implementation of Lean Manufacturing. This includes orderly housekeeping (5S), adequate inventory turns, throughput time reduction, and advanced manufacturing techniques. The Plant Manager is expected to be the “champion” of the Carlisle Operating System implementation at this facility.
Inventory control. This involves releasing all raw materials, supplies, and finished goods. The Plant Manager is also responsible for implementation of an inventory audit procedure to ensure accurate inventories are always maintained.
Creating an environment for success among supervisory and production employees. It is pertinent that the Plant Manager convey an attitude that is positive and confident. He/she must direct the staff to achieve their highest level of performance while treating them with respect and dignity.
Interaction with the rest of the company. Work with purchasing, environmental, health & safety, engineering, human resources, and corporate staff. The Plant Manager will be called upon to be the local expert for their plant regarding these topics.
Utilize COS (Carlisle operating system) tools and training to identify opportunities to improve safety, quality, delivery and cost.
Other duties can include interactions with inside and outside customers as well as outside vendors and agencies.
Required Knowledge/Skills/Abilities
Knowledge of manufacturing processes and products as well as quality systems and associated literacy of SPC, SOP’s, process specifications etc.
Knowledge of government regulations as they relate to people, plant and process operations such as FMLA, OSHA, FLSA, ADA, Worker’s Comp, EPA and unemployment.
Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
Financial and accounting familiarity including budgeting, cost control, financial data and project justification and ACE Process.
Overall understanding of the logistics process including raw material and finished goods shipments and customer service.
Strong knowledge and experience with MS Office Suite
Strong knowledge and experience working in an ERP system, preferably SAP
Strong oral and written communication skills including the ability to speak in front of groups and make effective presentations.
Good organizational skills along with effective time management.
Ability to effectively delegate to subordinates and others in supporting roles.
Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to handle stress and make decisions under a variety of challenging circumstances.
Continuous Improvement
"Expectations to understand, participate in, and support company COS initiatives, with focus on developing a lean mindset”
Education And Experience
Required:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering field or Business-Related Area.
10+ Years of Experience in a manufacturing position, or plant operations.
Working Conditions

evidence.text:
Plant Manager - Quarry
Columbus Quarry, LLC
Columbus, GA
Company Description
Columbus Quarry, LLC is an aggregate production facility serving construction, infrastructure, and industrial customers in the Columbus, GA region and surrounding areas. The company focuses on safe, efficient extraction and processing of stone and related materials to meet a wide range of project specifications. Operations emphasize reliable supply, consistent product quality, and adherence to environmental and regulatory standards. Team members work in a hands-on setting where operational excellence, safety, and equipment care are central to daily activities.
Role Description
The Plant Manager – Quarry is a full-time, on-site role based in Columbus, GA, responsible for overseeing daily quarry and plant operations. This role manages production activities, including drilling, blasting coordination, crushing, screening, and material handling to meet volume and quality targets. The Plant Manager supervises and schedules team members, monitors equipment performance, coordinates maintenance, and enforces safety and environmental compliance. Daily tasks include reviewing production reports, optimizing workflow, managing inventories of aggregates and related materials, and collaborating with logistics and sales to ensure timely customer deliveries. The position also involves training staff, implementing continuous improvement initiatives, and maintaining clear communication with leadership on operational and financial performance.
Qualifications
Candidates should possess strong supervisory skills, including team leadership, scheduling, performance management, and safety coaching.
Candidates should possess hands-on experience with crushing operations, including plant setup, equipment operation, troubleshooting, and throughput optimization.
Candidates should possess practical knowledge of quarrying processes, such as extraction, material handling, pit planning, and compliance with mine safety regulations.
Candidates should possess familiarity with cement and aggregates applications, product specifications, and quality control standards relevant to construction materials.
Relevant qualifications include experience in heavy industrial or mining environments, strong safety mindset, and proficiency in basic computer and reporting tools.
Additional beneficial qualifications include prior plant management experience, understanding of maintenance planning, and a technical or vocational background in mechanical or industrial disciplines.

The Senior Director, Planning provides strategic and operational leadership for planning organizations supporting both a business area and a centralized manufacturing hub. This leader serves as a critical integrator across Business Area leadership, Operations, Supply Chain, Programs, Engineering, Finance, and other functional organizations, The role requires the ability to balance program priorities with enterprise manufacturing requirements while establishing clear accountability, decision rights, escalation paths, and performance expectations across a matrixed organization.

Success in this role depends on building capable leaders and accountable teams, improving how work moves across facilities, and balancing business performance with a strong employee experience. The Director partners closely with Human Resources, Finance, Retail, Sales, and Compliance on workforce planning, employee development, performance, budgets, and company-wide initiatives.
Key ResponsibilitiesPeople Leadership, Culture & Team Development
Lead, motivate, and develop facility managers, department leaders, and operational teams across Oregon
Build a people-first culture grounded in trust, accountability, respect, clear communication, and shared ownership of results
Maintain a visible, approachable leadership presence so employees feel informed, supported, and connected to company priorities
Set clear expectations, provide constructive feedback, recognize strong performance, and address performance or conduct concerns consistently and respectfully
Coach managers in communication, conflict resolution, decision-making, delegation, employee engagement, and day-to-day leadership
Establish consistent leadership meetings, site visits, one-on-ones, performance check-ins, and follow-through on commitments
Develop leadership capability and succession depth through coaching, mentoring, cross-training, and development planning
Partner with Human Resources on workforce planning, recruiting, onboarding, training, employee relations, performance management, retention, and organizational change
Assess staffing, morale, communication, and team effectiveness across locations and implement practical solutions with site leaders and Human Resources
Regional & Multi-Site Operational Leadership
Provide strategic and day-to-day leadership across cultivation, extraction, production, warehousing, distribution, logistics, and related operations
Translate company strategy and scaling initiatives into regional operating plans, staffing priorities, performance expectations, and measurable outcomes
Maintain regular on-site presence, assess operational and team performance, and ensure leaders have the resources and support needed to succeed
Establish consistent regional standards while accounting for differences in capacity, staffing, product flow, and local operating needs
Promote collaboration across locations and functions, reduce silos, and serve as the regional escalation point for significant operational and people concerns
Monitor regional priorities and performance indicators, holding leaders accountable for timely execution and sustainable results
Support the evaluation and integration of new initiatives, facilities, processes, and organizational changes as business needs evolve
Production, Supply Chain & Facilities
Oversee cultivation, extraction, manufacturing, and production workflows, including capacity planning, scheduling, quality standards, equipment utilization, and finished-goods delivery
Direct warehouse, inventory, distribution, transportation, and logistics activities to support reliable product movement
Partner with Retail and Sales leaders to align production and distribution priorities with demand, promotions, product launches, and inventory needs
Identify operational constraints and engage teams in solutions that improve service, quality, employee experience, and cost control
Maintain business-continuity plans and provide steady leadership during staffing, equipment, vendor, facility, or supply-chain challenges
Compliance, Safety & Quality
Ensure assigned locations operate in accordance with Oregon cannabis regulations, OLCC requirements, Metrc procedures, safety standards, and internal policies
Reinforce team ownership of compliance, safety, and quality through training, coaching, communication, and accountability
Maintain controls for inventory movement, chain of custody, waste, product handling, documentation, access, and reconciliation
Partner with Compliance, Human Resources, and site leaders on inspections, investigations, corrective actions, and incident follow-up
Financial Management & Business Partnership
Partner with Finance and Human Resources on budgets, forecasts, labor models, staffing plans, capital needs, and cost-management priorities
Monitor operational, financial, and workforce performance; explain material variances and implement appropriate corrective action
Use data to guide staffing, resource allocation, capacity decisions, vendor strategy, and improvement priorities
Provide executive leadership with clear updates regarding regional performance, risks, needs, and recommendations
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Operations, Supply Chain, Business Administration, Manufacturing, Organizational Leadership, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience
Eight or more years of progressive operations experience, including responsibility for multiple locations or geographically dispersed teams
Five or more years of people-management experience, including direct supervision and development of managers or senior leaders
Professional experience in the regulated cannabis industry, with an understanding of the operational demands of a licensed business
Demonstrated ability to build engaged teams, coach leaders, manage performance, and lead through growth or change
Experience leading manufacturing, production, warehousing, distribution, logistics, facilities, or other inventory-intensive operations
Proven ability to establish standards, use performance metrics, manage competing priorities, and improve processes across locations
Strong judgment, emotional intelligence, communication, accountability, and discretion in a fast-paced, regulated environment
Ability to travel regularly throughout Oregon and respond to time-sensitive operational and people needs
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in a vertically integrated cannabis organization, with exposure to multiple functions such as cultivation, manufacturing, extraction, production, and distribution
Working knowledge of OLCC requirements and Metrc workflows
Experience overseeing multiple functions in a business that includes both wholesale and retail operations
Background in consumer packaged goods, food and beverage, manufacturing, agriculture, retail supply chain, or another regulated industry
Experience leading integrations, facility launches, expansions, reorganizations, or significant process improvements
Confidentiality ExpectationsThis role has access to sensitive operational, financial, personnel, compensation, security, inventory, vendor, and strategic information. The Director of Operations must maintain confidentiality, exercise sound discretion, and handle sensitive information in accordance with company policy and applicable law.
This description outlines the general nature and level of the role and is not an exhaustive list of all duties or qualifications. Responsibilities may change based on business needs.
