evidence.text:
Production Director, Signage
Haptica
Owings Mills, MD
Description
The Production Director leads all signage manufacturing operations, including fabrication, wide-format printing, finishing, assembly, production quality and installation. This leader is accountable for meeting customer commitments, maximizing production capacity, controlling costs, and achieving departmental financial objectives.
This is a high-accountability leadership role requiring operational expertise, financial discipline, and a growth mindset. The Director will build a high-performing team, establish clear expectations, improve productivity, eliminate bottlenecks, and ensure the department can scale efficiently as Strategic Factory grows.
The objective is to deliver exceptional quality, flawless execution, and profitable growth through strong leadership, disciplined processes, and measurable results.
Essential Responsibilities
Financial Performance and Profitability
Own departmental performance against revenue, gross margin, labor, material, and profitability targets.
Monitor job costing, estimated versus actual labor, material usage, overtime, waste, and rework to protect margins.
Establish cost controls and identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce expenses, and increase throughput.
Align staffing, equipment, purchasing, and production capacity with work orders, forecasts, and company growth objectives.
Partner with the VP of Signage, Finance, Sales, and Project Management to ensure production decisions support company-wide financial goals.
Production Leadership and Execution
Lead all daily signage production operations, including fabricated signs, channel letters, dimensional signage, wide-format printing, finishing, and assembly.
Own production scheduling, workflow, capacity planning, and on-time completion.
Establish clear priorities, deadlines, and ownership across production teams.
Coordinate with Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, and Installation to ensure projects move efficiently from order to completion.
Identify constraints early, resolve production issues quickly, and maintain visibility into work in progress, material availability, and equipment utilization.
Ensure production commitments are realistic, communicated, and consistently achieved.
Leadership and Accountability
Build and develop a high-performing team focused on urgency, quality, teamwork, and results.
Establish clear roles, measurable expectations, and accountability for supervisors and production employees.
Hold team leaders accountable for schedules, staffing, productivity, quality, safety, and financial performance.
Coach and develop supervisors to solve problems, make decisions, and own their results rather than relying on constant intervention.
Address performance issues promptly, recognize strong performance, and ensure appropriate training and staffing.
Foster a positive, high-energy culture that values continuous improvement, direct communication, and follow-through.
Leadership standard: Set expectations, provide the tools to succeed, measure results, coach consistently, and hold people accountable.
Quality and Customer Satisfaction
Establish quality standards for all fabricated, printed, and finished signage.
Ensure work meets approved artwork, engineering specifications, material requirements, and customer expectations.
Track defects, rework, scrap, and customer complaints; implement corrective actions to prevent recurring problems.
Partner with Project Management and Installation to resolve issues and protect customer commitments.
Promote a customer-first mindset in which quality, communication, and on-time delivery drive retention and future revenue.
Operational Excellence and Growth
Continuously improve workflows, production methods, standard operating procedures, and equipment utilization.
Eliminate bottlenecks, unnecessary handling, downtime, waste, and inefficient labor practices.
Develop a scalable production plan aligned with sales forecasts and annual revenue goals.
Identify staffing, equipment, facility, and technology investments needed to support growth, with clear financial justification.
Make disciplined in-house versus outsourcing decisions based on cost, capacity, quality, and delivery.
Use production data and performance scorecards to identify trends, assign corrective actions, and measure results.
Materials, Equipment, and Safety
Manage material planning, inventory accuracy, purchasing coordination, and supplier performance.
Control material waste and ensure supplies are available to meet production schedules without unnecessary inventory.
Oversee preventive maintenance and ensure equipment is operated and maintained properly.
Maintain a safe, organized production environment and enforce company safety policies and applicable OSHA requirements.
Ensure required training, maintenance records, and safety procedures are consistently maintained.
Communication and Cross-Functional Leadership
Provide regular reporting on financial performance, production schedules, capacity, staffing, quality, and operational risks.
Communicate schedule changes, material shortages, and customer delivery risks proactively.
Work collaboratively with Sales, Engineering, Project Management, Purchasing, and Installation to achieve company objectives.
Support leadership decisions, communicate priorities consistently, and focus on solutions rather than excuses.
The Director will be evaluated against established company targets, including:
Financial: Revenue achievement, gross margin, labor costs, and departmental profitability.
Execution: On-time delivery, schedule adherence, throughput, and production cycle time.
Quality: Rework, scrap, defects, and customer complaints.
Productivity: Labor efficiency, overtime, equipment utilization, and capacity.
Growth: Ability to increase production volume while controlling costs and maintaining quality.
Leadership: Staffing, employee development, accountability, and performance improvement.
Operational discipline: Material waste, inventory accuracy, safety, and completion of improvement initiatives.
Requirements
7–10 years of progressive experience in sign manufacturing, fabrication, wide-format printing, or a related production environment.
At least 5 years of leadership experience managing production teams and preferably multiple production functions.
Demonstrated experience with fabricated and printed signage, production scheduling, workflow management, and quality control.
Proven ability to manage job costs, labor, materials, capacity, and profitability.
Track record of improving productivity, quality, on-time delivery, and financial results.
Strong leadership, communication, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
Experience with ERP/MIS systems, production reporting, and performance metrics.
Knowledge of equipment maintenance, workplace safety, and manufacturing best practices.
Relevant degree preferred; equivalent experience and demonstrated results will be considered.

evidence.text:
Image Sensor Engineer
Tesla
Palo Alto, CA
What To Expect
As an Image Sensor Engineer at Tesla, you will own implementation and industrialization of CMOS image sensors and camera modules—from validated design intent through process freeze, production test, factory ramp, and sustained high-volume manufacturing. Your focus is not research-grade pixel invention; it is making sensors work reliably, repeatably, and cost-effectively at Tesla scale across vehicle programs.
You will translate electro-optical and system requirements into manufacturable module designs, supplier process controls, incoming/EOL test coverage, and line-ready build instructions. You will lead NPI gates, yield and cosmetic defect reduction, second-source and capacity ramps, and field/factory issue closure with CIS vendors, module makers, Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain. Expect heavy time on characterization benches, pilot lines, and production floors—not only in the lab.
What You'll Do
Own end-to-end implementation of image sensor and camera-module designs into production: DFM/DFA, stack-up freeze, BOM readiness, build documentation, and release criteria for NPI through HVM
Industrialize sensor/module processes with module manufacturers and internal lines—die attach, wirebond/flip-chip, active alignment, lens/barrel assembly, filter/cover glass, sealing, and cure profiles—driving Cp/Cpk, scrap reduction, and cycle-time targets
Define production test and inspection strategy (wafer/probe correlation where applicable, module EO test, cosmetic AOI, functional/EOL, burn-in or stress screens as required); set guardbands, golden samples, and MSA for factory metrology
Establish and maintain EO and image-quality specs that are factory-executable: QE/response, noise, defective pixels, PRNU, black level, HDR/flicker behavior, multi-camera matching—balanced for perception needs and manufacturing yield
Lead yield, defect, and process excursions: Pareto analysis, DOE on assembly and test, root-cause with FA (optical, electrical, physical), and permanent corrective actions into supplier control plans and Tesla work instructions
Drive automotive-grade qualification and production validation for sensors/modules (TC, THB/HAST, mechanical shock/vibe, solar/UV load, life tests); lock process change management (PCN) and requalification triggers
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering, Test Engineering, and Quality on line bring-up, takt and capacity models, traceability, and containment playbooks for factory and field escapes
Manage CIS and camera-module supplier industrialization programs: process capability audits, dual-source enablement, cost-down without quality regression, and ramp readiness for new vehicle launches
Resolve implementation issues at the system boundary—thermal, EMI, flex/PCB interface, connector/sealing, contamination, stray light introduced by assembly tolerances—and feed learnings into next-gen designs
Mentor implementation and camera manufacturing engineers; standardize playbooks for sensor NPI, factory metrics dashboards, and cross-program industrialization best practices
What You'll Bring
Degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Optics, Physics, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field, or equivalent practical experience. Industrialization track record outweighs pure research pedigree
8+ years (12+ years preferred) bringing CMOS image sensors and/or camera modules from prototype into high-volume manufacturing—automotive, mobile, industrial machine vision, or similar high-reliability volume products
Proven ownership of camera or imaging-module NPI: process development, equipment/fixture bring-up, production test deployment, yield ramp, and sustained HVM support
Working fluency with CIS electro-optical behavior and failure modes (noise, defectives, thermal dark current, HDR/flicker, packaging stress) sufficient to set specs, debug lines, and challenge vendors—without requiring a pure pixel-design background
Hands-on experience with module assembly processes (active alignment, bonding, sealing, optical stack) and factory quality systems (control plans, FMEA, SPC, 8D, traceability)
Demonstrated ability to define EO/functional production tests, correlate lab-to-line metrology, and use data (Python, JMP, or equivalent) to drive yield and process improvement
Experience with automotive or equivalently rigorous qualification, PCN/change control, and supplier process audits for imaging or precision optoelectronic assemblies
Comfortable operating across Design, Manufacturing, Test, Quality, and Supply Chain; clear communicator who can freeze a process, call a line stop, or present ramp risk to program leadership
Own industrialization strategy across camera platforms, unblock multi-site ramps, dual-source critical sensors/modules, and raise the manufacturing bar for imaging hardware
Bias to the factory floor and supplier lines; willingness to travel to module makers and Tesla manufacturing sites as needed (often 25%+ during ramps)
Benefits
Along with competitive pay, as a full-time Tesla employee, you are eligible for the following benefits at day 1 of hire:
Medical plans > plan options with $0 payroll deduction
Family-building, fertility, adoption and surrogacy benefits
Dental (including orthodontic coverage) and vision plans, both have options with a $0 paycheck contribution
Company Paid (Health Savings Accounts) HSA Contribution when enrolled in the High-Deductible medical plan with HSA
Healthcare and Dependent Care Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
401(k) with employer match, Employee Stock Purchase Plans, and other financial benefits
Company paid Basic Life, AD&D
Short-term and long-term disability insurance (90 day waiting period)
Employee Assistance Program
Sick and Vacation time (Flex time for salary positions, Accrued hours for Hourly positions), and Paid Holidays
Back-up childcare and parenting support resources
Voluntary benefits to include: critical illness, hospital indemnity, accident insurance, theft & legal services, and pet insurance
Weight Loss and Tobacco Cessation Programs
Tesla Babies program
Commuter benefits
Employee discounts and perks program
Earned Wage Access: Real-time pay access paid daily, subject to eligibility and schedule (applicable for below Sr. Managers levels)
Expected Compensation
$132,000 - $240,000/annual salary + cash and stock awards + benefits
Pay offered may vary depending on multiple individualized factors, including market location, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package for this position may also include other elements dependent on the position offered. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided if an employee receives an offer of employment.

Director of Product & Process Engineering
Rubbercraft
Long Beach, CA
$195,000.00/yr - $236,000.00/yr
Director of Product and Process Engineering & Development
Rubbercraft
is seeking an experienced Director of Product and Process Engineering & Development
to lead product design, process development, and engineering innovation at our Long Beach, CA facility. This role is responsible for developing advanced products, materials, and manufacturing processes that meet or exceed customer and industry expectations while supporting new business growth.
The Director will lead a team of engineers and collaborate closely with Business Development, Operations, Manufacturing Engineering, Program Management, and New Product Introduction (NPI) to drive innovation, improve manufacturability, and support the successful transition of new products into production.
About Rubbercraft:
Rubbercraft is a trusted leader in engineered elastomer solutions serving the aerospace, defense, and industrial markets. We design and manufacture precision-molded seals, gaskets, and custom rubber components that perform in the world's most demanding environments. Our culture is built on innovation, collaboration, quality, and customer commitment.
Key Responsibilities
Lead the development of innovative products, materials, and manufacturing processes to support customer requirements, new business opportunities, and organizational growth.
Drive the creation and development of intellectual property, including trade secrets and patents, related to new products, materials, and processes.
Serve as a subject matter expert in product and process technology, sharing technical knowledge and best practices across the organization.
Lead, mentor, and develop a team of engineers, fostering a collaborative, innovative, and high-performing environment.
Oversee day-to-day engineering activities, including product and tooling design, fixture development, process improvements, and structured problem-solving.
Partner with Business Development to support new business opportunities, first-time bookings, and technical customer engagements.
Collaborate directly with customer engineering and design teams to develop innovative solutions utilizing Rubbercraft's technical expertise and intellectual property.
Support the development of a technology roadmap focused on strengthening Rubbercraft's competitive position through innovation and intellectual property development.
Lead the preparation and review of Critical Design Reviews (CDRs) for advanced rubber and silicone products used in aerospace, defense, space, and energy applications.
Mentor engineers in developing technical documentation, engineering analyses, and customer design presentations.
Analyze engineering data and technical findings to provide sound recommendations and support data-driven decision-making.
Develop and implement policies, procedures, and best practices for product and process engineering and development.
Identify and implement opportunities to reduce scrap, improve molding processes, enhance tooling performance, and increase manufacturing efficiency.
Partner with Manufacturing Engineering to evaluate production processes, improve manufacturability, and identify cost-reduction opportunities.
Collaborate with NPI teams to ensure new products, processes, and tooling are production-ready and successfully transitioned from development to full-scale manufacturing.
Lead tooling and process design initiatives, including improvements to rubber molding, vulcanization, and deflashing processes.
Provide technical support during customer discussions, proposal development, and bid/no-bid evaluations, including leading the QQF process.
Partner with Program Management to align engineering deliverables with project timelines, customer requirements, and business objectives.
Promote the effective use of Salesforce Edge to track new business opportunities, product development activities, and first-time bookings.
Ensure timely completion of technical customer meeting reports and related documentation in Edge.
Communicate effectively with internal and external stakeholders to ensure alignment on technical requirements, project objectives, and deliverables.
Support cross-functional initiatives that improve operational performance, customer satisfaction, and overall business results.
Provide ongoing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development opportunities for direct reports.
Qualifications
Education:
Bachelor's degree in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field; advanced degree preferred.
Years Experience:
Minimum of 15 years of experience in aerospace manufacturing, product design, or engineering, including at least 5 years in a leadership role.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in aerospace rubber molding, including molding tool design and improvements to vulcanization, deflashing, and trimming processes.
Minimum of 5 years of experience applying advanced Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T) principles to molding tools and rubber products.
Minimum of 3 years of experience developing engineering testing and qualification procedures.
Minimum of 3 years of experience preparing and developing Critical Design Reviews (CDRs).
Minimum of 3 years of experience conducting technical discussions and presentations with OEM engineering teams within the aerospace and defense industries.
Skills:
Strong knowledge of rubber molding manufacturing processes, Value Analysis/Value Engineering (VA/VE), cost-reduction strategies, and process design for new product introduction.
Proficiency in CAD applications for product and tooling design.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret engineering data and make informed technical decisions.
Demonstrated success leading, mentoring, and developing high-performing engineering teams.
Strong leadership skills, including the ability to provide constructive feedback, evaluate performance, and support employee development.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to present complex technical information to customers and executive leadership.
Proven ability to make sound, timely decisions in complex or uncertain situations.
Strong negotiation, facilitation, and consensus-building skills.
Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and PowerPoint, including data analysis and preparation of technical and executive-level presentations.
Ability to collaborate effectively across engineering, manufacturing, operations, and commercial functions.
Work Environment & Physical Requirements
This is a fully onsite position based at Rubbercraft's facility in Long Beach, CA.
Travel of up to 35% may be required to customer locations, supplier facilities, and industry events.
Work is performed in both office and manufacturing environments.
Manufacturing areas may require the use of personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, masks, and other required safety equipment.
May be exposed to manufacturing conditions such as noise, dust, fumes, varying temperatures, and confined spaces.
Physical requirements include approximately 70% sitting and 30% standing, with occasional lifting or pushing of up to 20 pounds.
Requires regular computer use and visual attention to detailed technical information.
BENEFITS:
At Rubbercraft, we recognize how important your career and benefits are to you and your family. We offer a full suite of benefits, including medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability coverage, accident insurance, critical illness insurance, basic and supplemental life insurance, employee assistance plan, retirement savings and matching, and other developmental opportunities. We are committed to supporting the way you live and work.
RCC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other legally protected status. Applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to complete the application process may contact Human Resources.
This position requires access to information subject to the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Employment is contingent upon the applicant being a “U.S. person” as defined by ITAR (22 CFR §120.15), which includes U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, refugees, or asylees, as required by U.S. export control laws.

FlexTek is partnered with a growing industrial manufacturing organization to find a
Sr. Director of Operations / General Manager to lead a significant manufacturing expansion and facility relocation from Southern California into Mexico. This is a high-impact leadership opportunity for an operations executive who combines hands-on industrial engineering expertise with strong business acumen, P&L ownership, and experience scaling manufacturing operations. The initial focus will be on evaluating, planning, and executing a facility transition, followed by full operational leadership of a rapidly growing business. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable developing a plant layout, navigating cross-border operational challenges, and building the teams and infrastructure necessary to support growth.
What You'll Do
Lead a U.S.-to-Mexico manufacturing relocation, overseeing site evaluation, facility selection, equipment transfers, plant layout, operational readiness, and integration.
Develop and execute a comprehensive transition strategy, including workforce planning, staffing, regulatory requirements, infrastructure, and production continuity.
Apply industrial engineering principles to optimize manufacturing layouts, production workflows, equipment utilization, and overall operational efficiency.
Assume full P&L and operational responsibility
following the initial integration phase, driving profitability, production performance, and business growth.
Build and develop the organizational structure, including recruiting and managing site leadership teams as operations expand.
Partner with executive and commercial leadership to align manufacturing capabilities, capacity planning, and go-to-market strategies with revenue growth objectives.
Establish scalable operational processes and performance metrics to support continued expansion, acquisitions, and long-term business objectives.
What We're Looking For
Proven leadership experience as a Director of Operations, General Manager, Plant Director, or similar senior manufacturing operations leader.
Fluency in both English and Spanish is required
, with the ability to lead teams and navigate business operations across the U.S. and Mexico.
Demonstrated experience relocating, establishing, or transitioning manufacturing facilities, including hands-on involvement in planning and execution.
Strong industrial engineering background with expertise in plant layout, manufacturing processes, production flow, and operational optimization.
Experience managing a manufacturing P&L, including budgets, profitability, capital expenditures, and financial performance.
Knowledge of manufacturing operations, workforce planning, supply chain, and the operational considerations involved in establishing facilities in Mexico.
Ability to transition from hands-on project execution into broader strategic and operational leadership of a growing business.
Ideal Background
Experience with discrete manufacturing, particularly engineered products, industrial components, seals, gaskets, elastomers, or polymers.
Direct involvement in the discovery, feasibility assessment, site selection, and execution of a manufacturing facility relocation or startup.
Experience managing manufacturing operations in Mexico, particularly cross-border operations involving the U.S. and Mexico.
Background in rapidly growing, acquisition-driven, or operationally transforming manufacturing organizations.
Exposure to international supply chains, distribution, and cross-border shipping, including Asian markets, is a plus.

Position may be based in Southern California or Mexico
, with regular on-site involvement during the facility transition.

evidence.quote: Audit leadership — registrar, customer, and regulatory; you’ve led companies through first-time certification and passed cleanly
evidence.text:
Head of Quality
Foundational Industries
San Francisco Bay Area, CA
Foundational Industries · SF Bay Area · Full-Time
About Foundational
Foundational is building a network of AI-native, autonomous factories for modern contract manufacturing — reshoring critical supply chains so companies can produce high-quality products domestically, quickly, and at competitive cost. Recent breakthroughs in robotics and physical AI have shifted autonomous manufacturing from theoretical to deployable, and we're focused on operationalizing these capabilities at scale during a decisive decade for American industrial leadership.
WHO — Who Thrives Here
At Foundational, we're building with people who want to own something — to do work that matters, in an environment where what you ship is what counts.
The people who thrive here:
Take ownership before they're asked. They see the gap and close it.
Operate with a high degree of judgment. We move fast, and good judgment travels farther than a playbook.
Communicate directly — concise, clear, and candid, especially when stakes are high.
Hold a high bar for themselves first, then for everyone around them.
Are genuinely energized by hard problems in physical, real-world environments. Energized — not just interested.
Stay effective when things are ambiguous, changing, or under pressure. That's the job.
This is a place for people who want to build something that has never existed before and leave a clear mark on it.
MISSION
This person owns the quality system that earns Foundational the right to build — across every vertical we serve and every standard our customers run on. Without it, we don’t pass first audit, we don’t win regulated programs, and our customers can’t ship.
OUTCOMES — What Success Looks Like in 6–12 Months
We track results. Here's what we expect this person to own and deliver:
Stand up a single QMS that serves every vertical Foundational builds in — architected from day one to absorb the toughest standards (AS9100, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, ISO 9001) so layering on additional certifications and customer-specific requirements is a configuration step, not a rebuild.
Own the certification roadmap end-to-end — ISO 9001 as the baseline, then the vertical-specific standards our first programs require (AS9100, ISO 13485, IATF 16949, NADCAP, and others as the customer mix demands) — and pass each audit on the first attempt.
Build supplier quality from zero — qualification, FAIs, PPAP where required, source inspection, and counterfeit-mitigation controls aligned to AS9100 / AS6171.
Establish the operating cadence that keeps quality real on the floor — control plans, FAIs, in-process inspection, NCR/CAPA discipline, MRB, SPC, and the closed-loop feedback that drives yield and cost of poor quality down every quarter.
Define the digital QMS — document control, training records, NCR/CAPA, audit, supplier quality — and partner with engineering so traceability and inspection data are software-native, not paper retrofitted into a database.
SKILLS
Multi-standard QMS architecture — deep fluency in ISO 9001, AS9100, ISO 13485 / FDA QSR (21 CFR 820), and IATF 16949, and a working sense of where they converge, where they don’t, and how additional customer- and vertical-specific standards layer on top
Audit leadership — registrar, customer, and regulatory; you’ve led companies through first-time certification and passed cleanly
Core quality engineering toolkit — APQP/PPAP, FMEA, control plans, MSA, SPC, 8D, root cause and CAPA discipline that actually closes loops
Electronics & precision-manufacturing quality — IPC-A-610 / J-STD-001, FAIs (AS9102), source inspection, dimensional metrology, and special-process accreditation (NADCAP)
Digital QMS & data fluency — comfortable defining the systems and data model (eQMS, traceability, inspection records) that the function runs on, not just operating off a shared drive
COMPETENCIES
These are the behavioral patterns that predict success here — in practice, under pressure.
Accountability
— You own outcomes. If something's off track, you say so and fix it.
Bias for action
— You ship. You iterate. You move toward the hard thing.
Clarity of communication
— Direct and concise, especially when it counts.
Learning agility
— You get up to speed fast in unfamiliar territory.
Resilience
— You stay sharp when things are hard, ambiguous, or moving fast.
High standards
— You raise the bar rather than match it — and hold yourself to it first.
Building from zero
— You can stand up a quality system from scratch — documents, processes, certifications, the team — and run it yourself until there’s a team to hand it off to.
Why Foundational
This is a filter as much as it is an invitation.We're turning reindustrialization from a talking point into an operating reality. The work is hard, the environment is demanding, and the stakes are real. We compensate with base, bonus, and equity to reflect impact, responsibility, and results, with meaningful upside for the people who help build and scale this company.
For those aligned with the mission and motivated by execution at scale, Foundational offers the opportunity to help define one of the most consequential industrial transformations of the next decade.
Compensation
Foundational is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. The annual salary range for this role is $180K - $200K . Compensation is determined based on your qualifications and experience. Our total compensation package also includes generous equity in Foundation.
Benefits
Foundation offers the following benefits, subject to applicable eligibility requirements:
Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance with HSA and FSA options
Generous paid time off, company holidays, and sick time
Life and Disability Insurance
Pre-tax commuter benefits for transit and parking
Foundational Industries is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex (including gender identity, sexual orientation, and pregnancy), age, disability, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law. Foundational complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws governing nondiscrimination in employment. We evaluate every candidate on what they can do and who they are.

Actively create/sustain a strong talent management process and committee for all people. Create a dynamic learning culture in which people grow within and beyond the facility

Plant Manager
No longer accepting applications
Harbour Industries LLC, a Marmon | Berkshire Hathaway Company
Shelburne, VT
Harbour Industries LLC
As a part of the global industrial organization Marmon Holdings—which is backed by Berkshire Hathaway—you’ll be doing things that matter, leading at every level, and winning a better way. We’re committed to making a positive impact on the world, providing you with diverse learning and working opportunities, and fostering a culture where everyone’s empowered to be their best.
The Plant Manager is responsible for the overall leadership, strategic direction, and operational performance of Harbour Industries manufacturing facility. This role oversees all continuous improvement, production, maintenance, and shipping activities while ensuring a world-class safety culture, operational discipline, and alignment to customer, business, and compliance requirements. This role also sets and executes long-term operational strategy, enables future growth, and strengthens customer confidence through responsiveness, reliability, and operational consistency.
The Plant Manager is a hands-on, people-first leader with focus on coaching, developing talent, driving cross-functional collaboration, building resilient and high performing teams, and fostering a culture of accountability, operational excellence, continuous learning, and trust. This role has P&L responsibility for the direct cost drivers of the facility and needs to ensure financial goals are met by managing costs and maximizing revenue generation opportunities, while ensuring best-in-class quality standards. Supply Chain, Safety, Process Engineering and Production reports directly to the Plant Manager
Essential Duties And Responsibilities
Safety & Continuous Improvement
Champion and drive a safety-first culture throughout the facility with employee feedback and participation in driving improvement in the safety culture, ensuring compliance with all safety regulations, and implementing and sustaining ongoing safety training and initiatives.
Ownership of Safety Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) for the facility and driving improvement of such.
Regularly assess and update safety protocols, ensuring a safe working environment for all employees.
Lead behavior-based safety initiatives, auditing routines, risk identification, root cause investigations, and implementation of corrective/preventive actions.
Ensure robust Job Hazard Analysis process for all new or modified equipment and processes.
Champion plant and enterprise-wide continuous improvement culture through LEAN and Kaizen initiatives, fostering broad employee involvement and ownership to streamline processes, reduce waste, and improve overall efficiency.
Mentor team members across all levels to adopt a problem-solving mindset grounded in data-based decisions, curiosity, and shared accountability.
Partner with Applications and Process Engineering, Quality, and other business functions to implement improvements that reduce waste and scrap, improve yield and quality, and optimize throughput.
Analyze financial performance and identify areas for improvement, implementing corrective actions to enhance profitability.
Quality
Build a culture of ownership of quality at the source, coaching leaders and operators in quality awareness, documentation accuracy, and risk reduction.
Ensure all products meet rigorous aerospace and defense industry standards such as AS9100, customer specific compliance, and facility maintains compliance audit readiness.
Oversee implementation and sustainment of in-process quality inspections conducted by Operations.
Collaboration with Quality, Supply Chain, and Process Engineering on root cause investigation, implementing and sustaining corrective actions, and investigating and implementing robust quality control systems to identify and correct defects early in the production process.
Drive culture of accurate reporting of inventory such as finished good production, scrap, and other future metrics within company’s systems such as Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) and real-time data tracking.
Operations
Lead and oversee daily manufacturing operations, ensuring production schedules are met and shipment goals are achieved while maintaining high standards for quality, efficiency, and safety.
Ensure alignment of production planning, capacity, staffing, and material availability to meet customer and revenue requirements through ownership of Production and collaboration with Planning, Supply Chain, and Sales functions.
Key team member in Sales & Operations Planning (S&OP) to ensure accurate revenue forecasting, volume planning, and customer alignment.
Drive performance to meet operational KPIs including shipments, throughput, scrap, labor and material efficiency, on time delivery, and other cost reduction initiatives.
Oversee facility capital equipment planning, justification, installation, and performance integration.
Leverage company data systems to drive cross functional improvements in current workflows to eliminate waste and streamline process and information flow.
Develop and execute preventative and corrective maintenance strategies to minimize downtime and optimize equipment performance.
Develop, manage, and report on various departmental budgets, ensuring financial discipline and resource optimization.
Support digital transformation initiatives to improve process visibility, data accuracy, and decision-making effectiveness.
People
Build and sustain a high-performing, resilient, and engaged workforce grounded in communication, feedback, empowerment, accountability, and clear KPIs and developmental goals.
Coach and mentor leaders at all levels, fostering strong succession pipelines, leadership maturity, and development plans.
Promote an environment centered on trust, transparency, and continuous improvement.
Partner with HR on hiring, performance evaluations, disciplinary processes, and workforce planning.
Ensure consistent execution of feedback systems, annual reviews, training programs, corrective action management, and recognition programs.
Lead effective communication rhythms, including weekly team meetings, shift handoffs, and plant-wide updates.
Promote and enforce attendance and utilization standards to support plant performance.
Actively engage and lead by example on the production floor to support issue resolution, coaching, problem identification, and cross-functional escalation.
Collaborate closely with other departments, including Sales, Engineering, Automation, Data Transformation, HR, and Finance, to align operations with broader organizational goals
Serve as a key point of contact between other business units to drive innovation, operational effectiveness, and customer satisfaction.
These are the general duties required to fulfill the Plant Manager job description, not a detailed description of all work required. Additional responsibilities may be assigned as business needs evolve.
Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or related field (MBA or advanced degree preferred).
10+ years of progressive leadership experience in manufacturing, with 5+ years in a Plant Manager or equivalent operational leadership role preferred.
Exceptional communication, interpersonal, and leadership skills, with the proven capability to coach and develop leaders, build high performing teams, and foster collaborative cross-functional relationships.
Excellent external customer presentation and verbal communication skills for interactions such as plant tours.
Experience in aerospace, defense, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments strongly preferred.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex operations through transformation initiatives, manage P&L performance, achieve operational excellence, and navigate change.
Strong knowledge of LEAN, Continuous Improvement, and operational excellence methodologies (Green or Black Belt preferred).
Robust data-driven decision-making abilities with advanced problem-solving capability.
Strong proficiency in Microsoft Office, data analysis tools, and quick ability to learn company systems, such as ERP.
Expertise in production planning, quality systems, maintenance strategies, and process engineering fundamentals.
In-depth knowledge of safety regulations and compliance requirements within manufacturing environments.
Proven capability to manage budgets, capital expenditures, and long-term strategic planning.
LANGUAGE SKILLS:
Must be able to effectively communicate with co-workers and other department personnel where English is second language.
Must be able to read, write, understand, and communicate in English
CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATION:
LEAN Green or Black Belt preferred
AS9100 training preferred
PHYSICAL DEMANDS:
This position requires some physical demand. Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs.Ability to travel occasionally, < 15%, to other business units, suppliers, and customers.
Ability to bend, move between equipment, and aisles of product.
Ability to stand and move around production facility for extended period of time if needed.
Ability to sit at a desk and conduct computer work for extended periods of time if needed.
Ability to wear Safety attire or protective gear on a daily basis.
Pay Range
121,600.00 - 182,400.00

Here at Baylor Scott & White Health we promote the well-being of all individuals, families, and communities. Baylor Scott and White is the largest not-for-profit healthcare system in Texas that empowers you to live well.
Our Core Values Are
We serve faithfully by doing what's right with a joyful heart.
We never settle by constantly striving for better.
We are in it together by supporting one another and those we serve.
We make an impact by taking initiative and delivering exceptional experience.
Benefits
Our benefits are designed to help you live well no matter where you are on your journey. For full details on coverage and eligibility, visit the Baylor Scott & White Benefits Hub to explore our offerings, which may include:
Immediate eligibility for health and welfare benefits
401(k) savings plan with dollar-for-dollar match up to 5%
Tuition Reimbursement
PTO accrual beginning Day 1
Note: Benefits may vary based upon position type and/or level.
Job Summary
Director Quality Improvement plans, directs, and coordinates quality and patient safety programs for Baylor Scott and White Health (BSWH). These programs include activities that aim for zero preventable harm and apply safe, timely, effective, efficient, equitable, and patient-centered care. The director develops and implements plans, programs, procedures, and practices to improve patient care quality at BSWH hospitals, clinics, and ambulatory facilities. They review current programs and seek opportunities to resolve clinical quality problems or operational issues. The director develops key metrics for clinical quality and patient safety and directs data testing, trending, forecasting, and reporting to improve health care processes. They ensure clinical performance improvement programs comply with all regulatory, legal, and organizational requirements. The director partners with clinical staff, operations, and other stakeholders to improve processes impacting patient safety and care quality at BSWH.
An entity Director translates and implements strategic plans and goals for their entity. They make final judgments on operational matters and ensure goals are met. They recommend policies and organizational changes for the entity. They plan and execute projects and initiatives that meet annual goals. They plan and direct department operations, handling staffing, processes, budgets, and costs. They manage and advise subordinates to meet schedules, resolve technical problems, and monitor performance. The director oversees a larger, more complex organization or area than a manager. The director may have one or more managers or supervisors reporting to them.
Essential Functions Of The Role
Direct the quality improvement function for assigned area of responsibility for BSWH.
Direct and collaborate with cross-functional teams, including patient safety, infection prevention, nursing, risk management, and medical staff. Works with other stakeholders to promote continuous improvement in quality and patient safety for the assigned area.
Direct, facilitate, and support hospital quality improvement and patient safety committees. These councils provide oversight to ensure high-quality and safe patient care.
Direct and guide process improvement teams and activities using quality and patient safety best practices, improvement tools, and standardization methods.
Direct data monitoring, collection, testing, tracking and trending care processes to ensure safety, effectiveness, and efficiency.
Partner with hospital and system teams to advance health initiatives.
Direct quality improvement analytics, data validation, and data analysis activities. This includes data submission, testing for facility-identified data registries, and ensuring data confidentiality.
Direct the identification of real and potential safety concerns in BSWH facilities. Direct programs like variance reporting, patient safety response, and compliance with state and federal safety regulations.
Partner with clinical and corporate compliance to manage regulatory surveys, certifications, and compliance requirements.
Establish hospital and system processes to monitor quality and patient safety. Ensure all reporting requirements are met. Engage with internal and external stakeholders as required.
Key Success Factors
Bachelor’s degree in healthcare management, nursing, business, or related field preferred. Master’s degree highly preferred.
CPHQ certification highly preferred.
5+ years of experience in healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, risk management, or related areas.
3+ years of direct leadership experience in healthcare quality improvement, patient safety, risk management, or related areas highly preferred.
Experience in leading interdisciplinary initiatives in process improvement.
Knowledge of healthcare quality, patient safety management, benchmarking, and outcome measurement.
Knowledge of statistics, data collection, testing, and data presentation.
Critical thinking, process testing, and problem-solving skills.
Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
Belonging Statement
We believe that all people should feel welcomed, valued and supported.
Qualifications
EDUCATION - Bachelor's or 4 years of work experience above the minimum qualification
EXPERIENCE - 3 Years of Experience

Product Engineering Manager - Mechanical
Keysight Technologies
Santa Rosa, CA
Overview
Keysight is a mission-critical design enablement partner for organizations solving the world’s most complex engineering challenges. With deep engineering expertise and leading design, emulation, and test solutions, our ~16,800 employees help customers in over 100 countries accelerate innovation across communications, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace and defense, semiconductor, and artificial intelligence markets. Learn more about what we do.
At Keysight, people come together to explore new ideas, challenge what's possible, and advance the technologies defining the future. Here, you'll find opportunities to do your best work, take your career further, and thrive in an award-winning culture. Learn more about our benefits.
Responsibilities
The Precision Meso-scale Technology Center (PMTC) provides the high-precision mechanical solutions that enable Keysight’s industry-leading RF, microwave, mmWave, and 5G/6G solutions in various industries, including AI infrastructure, communications, aerospace & defense, automotive & energy, and semiconductor measurement equipment.
Responsibilities:
PMTC is forming a Product Engineering team, and this role is at our Headquarters in Santa Rosa, CA. The Product Engineering Manager builds and leads a team of Product Engineers, each of whom owns a mechanical product family end-to-end, and is accountable for the team’s results in product-level yield, product quality and customer support across PMTC. We’re looking for an accomplished, hands-on leader who sets a clear direction, develops people, and consistently drives results. The ideal candidate communicates clearly and effectively, partners well with Keysight product lines, operations, process engineering, and cross‑functional engineering teams, and is comfortable facilitating technical discussions and resolving priority conflicts among diverse stakeholders. This role requires sound judgment, strong problem‑solving skills, attention to detail, and the ability to make informed decisions in a fast‑paced, dynamic environment while managing multiple priorities and meeting deadlines.
The primary responsibilities of a PMTC Product Engineering Manager include:
Team leadership and development
Hire, coach and develop a team of Product Engineers; set clear goals and performance expectations, and assign product families by volume, complexity and yield risk.
Define how Product Engineering works with Process Engineering and Integration Engineering: ownership boundaries, NPI-to-production handoff exit criteria, and escalation paths.
Product-level yield and quality
Own yield and cost-of-poor-quality targets across all product families: first-pass yield, scrap, rework and cost of poor quality. Review top losses with the team, and make sure cross-process RCCA (8D, DMAIC) is led to closure when a failure spans more than one process block.
Ensure product conformance to drawing, GD&T and customer intent (AS9100 / ISO 9001): consistent NCM / MRB disposition, CAR / CAPA closure, ER / waiver and deviation governance, and SPC on critical-to-quality features in partnership with process engineering.
Customer interface and cross-functional leadership
Be the escalation point for Keysight product lines and R&D on quality events, recovery plans and delivery risk. Make sure Product Engineers give early, factual notice when yield or quality will affect delivery.
Partner with operations, process engineering, integration engineering and metrology to prioritize across competing demands and to balance yield recovery, delivery and cost.
Capability and continuous improvement
Build product-family knowledge and capability: critical features, failure modes, approved waivers and lessons learned; set the standard for production OSP qualification.
Provide DFM / inspectability feedback to Keysight R&D on new drawings and revision changes, and report team results and risks to PMTC leadership.
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, Manufacturing, Materials or Industrial Engineering, or equivalent experience.
8+ years in precision machining or precision mechanical component manufacturing in a product, quality, manufacturing or sustaining engineering role, including 3+ years leading engineers or technical teams.
Proven ability to hire, develop and retain engineers, set priorities, and hold a team accountable for results.
Working command of GD&T and of how machined features are measured (CMM, optical, surface profilometry); you can read a drawing and tell whether the inspection plan can actually prove it.
Hands-on structured problem solving: 8D, RCCA, DMAIC, FMEA; comfortable using yield and SPC data in Excel, Power BI, Minitab or JMP to set priorities.
Customer-facing communication: you have presented quality events, root cause and recovery plans to customers, program managers or senior leaders and kept their confidence.
Ownership mindset. You drive issues across functions to closure and expect the same of your team.
Visa sponsorship is not available for this position.
Santa Rosa, CA Pay Range: MIN $163,000.00 - MAX $273,000.00
This position requires access to certain goods, software, technology, or technical data subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations. Under these laws and regulations, U.S. persons (which includes U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees) working for Keysight can access export-controlled items without authorization from the U.S. government. For any individual who is not a U.S. person, Keysight may need authorization from the U.S. Department of State, U.S. Department of Commerce, or other appropriate federal agency before the individual can access export-controlled items. Employment in this position for non-U.S. persons is contingent on Keysight’s ability to obtain any required government authorizations.

evidence.quote: Required Experience | Technical Critical to Quality and Success Requirements:
evidence.text:
Vice President of Operations – Multi-Site - Make-to-Order Manufacturing
The Avery Point Group, Inc - Executive Search Catalysts for Change™
Memphis Metropolitan Area
Vice President of Operations – Multi-Site, Make-to-Order Manufacturing
Confidential Search | Privately Held High-Growth Company | Modular Engineered Fabrication
Memphis Metropolitan Area | On-Site | Two Manufacturing Facilities
Why You Should Be Interested in This Role:
The Avery Point Group has been retained by a growing manufacturer to identify a Vice President of Operations to lead two manufacturing facilities in the Memphis metropolitan area. This is a hands-on executive role within a small, nimble business where leadership decisions directly impact production performance, customer delivery, and profitability. The right leader will be actively engaged with the people leading the work, with regular floor presence across both locations.
The company operates in a high-mix, make-to-order environment built around a modular engineered and fabricated product platform. A meaningful portion of orders requires customer-specific customization. Success depends on coordinating engineering readiness, material availability, skilled labor, and manufacturing capacity so that customer requirements translate into executable production plans. The opportunity is to strengthen that coordination while improving throughput, delivery, quality, and cost.
As the business scales, this leader will build greater consistency in how both facilities operate, develop the capabilities of site leadership, and establish practical disciplines that support growth. Lean experience matters, particularly the ability to improve flow and reduce waste in a variable production environment. The expectation is sound operating judgment: standardize repeatable work, address the constraints that limit output, and preserve flexibility where customization requires it.
Position Summary:
The Vice President of Operations will own manufacturing performance across both sites, with accountability for safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and operating cost. The role combines daily execution with longer-term improvements in production planning, leadership capability, manufacturing processes, and capacity.
This role will work closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Sales, and other business leaders to align customer commitments with operational capability. A central responsibility will be strengthening the connection between order requirements and shop-floor execution, ensuring that production has the information, materials, equipment, and skills needed to perform reliably.
Key Responsibilities:
Multi-Site Leadership and Operating Discipline
Establish a practical approach to Lean across both facilities through Lean daily management, visible performance measures, structured problem solving, and clear escalation and follow-through. Develop and implement leader standard work for site leaders and frontline supervisors, including regular shop-floor observation, daily performance reviews, coaching, and verification that corrective actions are effective. Apply these disciplines to improve safety, quality, delivery, flow, throughput, and cost in a high-mix, make-to-order environment.
Build the organization’s Lean capability through hands-on training, coaching, and application to actual operating problems. Develop leaders and teams who can identify constraints, address root causes, implement improvements, and sustain effective work practices without constant executive intervention. Establish common operating expectations across both sites while preserving the flexibility required by changing product mix and customer-specific work.
Production Planning, Capacity, and Flow
Improve production scheduling and capacity planning in a high-mix, make-to-order environment. Ensure schedules reflect actual constraints, including engineering release status, material readiness, equipment availability, and skilled-labor capacity. Manage work-in-process and order sequencing to reduce congestion, unnecessary handling, and avoidable interruptions. Coordinate workload across both sites where capabilities and customer requirements support it.
Throughput, Delivery, and Productivity
Identify and address bottlenecks through fabrication, welding, finishing, and assembly. Improve schedule adherence, lead times, and on-time delivery through better preparation, balanced workloads, practical standard work, and focused problem solving. Apply Lean methods appropriate to variable order quantities and product configurations, with measurable improvements in flow and labor productivity.
Safety, Quality, and Process Control
Set clear expectations for safe work practices and consistent execution across both facilities. Partner with Quality and Engineering to strengthen in-process controls, documentation discipline, and corrective-action effectiveness in a certification-driven manufacturing environment. Reduce scrap and rework by addressing recurring process issues and ensuring that production teams work from current, accurate instructions and specifications.
Cost, Margin, and Working Capital
Manage operating performance with a clear understanding of labor efficiency, overtime, material utilization, scrap, rework, inventory, and operating expenses. Improve visibility into actual job performance relative to planned labor and material requirements. Use that information to address execution losses and support better estimating, routing, and costing decisions. Connect operational improvements to measurable financial results.
Engineering-to-Manufacturing Coordination
Partner closely with Engineering to ensure orders enter production with build-ready drawings, accurate bills of material, practical routings, and clear revision status. Establish expectations for resolving incomplete information before work reaches the floor. Coordinate engineering changes so their effects on materials, schedules, labor, and customer commitments are understood and managed. Provide production feedback that improves manufacturability and repeatability.
Materials Readiness and Commercial Alignment
Work with Supply Chain and Sales to align order commitments, purchased-material availability, and manufacturing capacity. Strengthen the handoffs between quoting, order acceptance, engineering, planning, and production. Establish a practical approach to priority changes and expedited orders so teams understand the tradeoffs and can protect existing customer commitments.
People and Leadership Development
Coach site leaders and frontline supervisors in planning, performance management, problem solving, and employee development. Clarify responsibilities and strengthen accountability without making every decision dependent on the VP of Operations. Build skills coverage and cross-training in critical processes, address performance gaps, and develop the leadership bench needed to support a growing two-site business.
Equipment Reliability, Capital, and Technology
Partner with Engineering and Maintenance to improve equipment availability and preventive-maintenance discipline. Prioritize equipment, layout, process, and technology investments based on their expected contribution to safety, quality, throughput, delivery, and cost. Strengthen the use of ERP/MRP and shop-floor information where it improves planning and execution. Carry investments through implementation, training, and verification of results.
Required Experience | Technical Critical to Quality and Success Requirements:
Progressive manufacturing leadership:
Typically 15+ years of manufacturing experience with increasing responsibility for production, people, operating performance, and cost.
Direct make-to-order experience:
Demonstrated success in high-mix, low-volume, configured-to-order, or engineered-to-order manufacturing with meaningful variation in customer requirements.
Fabrication operating background:
Hands-on leadership experience in fabrication-intensive environments involving welding, paint or finishing, and assembly. Experience with comparable engineered industrial products is particularly relevant.
Multi-site or complex-site leadership:
Proven leadership across multiple manufacturing locations, or substantial responsibility for a complex single facility with multiple production areas and a developed management team.
Demonstrated operating improvement:
A record of improving safety, quality, throughput, delivery, productivity, and cost, with evidence that results were sustained.
Practical Lean application:
Demonstrated experience implementing Lean daily management and leader standard work in a high-mix, make-to-order manufacturing environment. Proven ability to improve flow, throughput, and operating performance while developing the problem-solving and coaching capabilities of plant leaders, frontline supervisors, and production teams. Experience must extend beyond leading isolated improvement events to establishing operating practices that teams consistently use and sustain.
Planning and manufacturing systems:
Strong understanding of capacity planning, production scheduling, work-in-process management, material readiness, and ERP/MRP-supported execution.
Engineering and quality coordination:
Experience working with drawings, bills of material, routings, labor standards, revision control, and manufacturing documentation in an engineered-product environment.
Financial and investment discipline:
Ability to connect operating decisions to labor and material costs, inventory, margin, and the expected returns from capital or technology investments.
Leadership development:
Evidence of strengthening plant management and frontline supervision, building workforce capability, and establishing accountability beyond personal involvement.
Education
A bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations Management, Business, or a related field is preferred. Relevant manufacturing leadership experience and demonstrated operating results will be important considerations.
Leadership and Behavioral Profile:
Reporting to the CEO, the right candidate is comfortable moving between the shop floor and executive-level decisions. This leader earns credibility by understanding the work, listening to operators and supervisors, and following through on commitments. Expectations are clear, performance discussions are grounded in facts, and problems are addressed directly.
The role requires urgency without constant changes in direction. When delivery pressure increases, this role helps the organization understand the constraint, establish priorities, and execute a workable plan. They can make difficult people and operating decisions while developing the capability of others to take greater ownership.
A strong fit will also understand the scale of the business. This is an opportunity for someone who can introduce useful structure in a small-team environment, work through imperfect information, and remain personally engaged in implementation.
Location and On-Site Expectations:
This position is based in the Memphis metropolitan area and requires regular, visible leadership at both manufacturing facilities. It is not a remote or primarily travel-based oversight role.
Compensation:
Excellent Base and Bonus

Experience supporting or leading IATF, ISO, customer, and process audits; VDA 6.3 experience is desirable.

Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively with production employees, engineers, senior management, customers, suppliers, and international teams.

Ability to cope with stress and handle multiple tasks smoothly with a high accountability level.

Set up and operate a variety of machine tools to manufacture parts, mechanisms, tools, or machine components to precise tolerances and dimensions
Interpret blueprints, sketches, and engineering specifications to determine sequence of operations, number of cuts required, and setup methods
Utilize machinist hand tools and precision measuring instruments to ensure dimensional accuracy
Perform shop math calculations related to dimensions, tooling, feeds, and speeds
Measure, mark, and scribe reference points to lay out stock for machining operations
Fit and assemble precision parts into mechanical systems and determine required materials, parts, and equipment

Maintaining lubrication and coolant levels as part of basic preventative maintenance
Move materials and components within the manufacturing area using shop-assigned equipment
Complete required documentation and transactions to support product movement to next operation
Support continuous production flow by assisting and training employees of equal or lower classification
Train toward MVP qualification as required
Perform additional duties as assigned with provided training and certification

evidence.text:
Manufacturing Engineering Manager
Skild AI
San Mateo, CA
Company Overview
At Skild AI, we are building the world's first general purpose robotic intelligence that is robust and adapts to unseen scenarios without failing. We believe massive scale through data-driven machine learning is the key to unlocking these capabilities for the widespread deployment of robots within society. Our team consists of individuals with varying levels of experience and backgrounds, from new graduates to domain experts. Relevant industry experience is important, but ultimately less so than your demonstrated abilities and attitude. We are looking for passionate individuals who are eager to explore uncharted waters and contribute to our innovative projects.
Position Overview
We are looking for a Manufacturing Engineering Manager to own the transition of our electromechanical robotics hardware from prototype into repeatable production. You will lead a team of assembly technicians and manufacturing engineers, own build execution against schedule, and take responsibility for bringing new hardware platforms into production. The core infrastructure — assembly stations, Kanban inventory, BOM architecture, and controlled work instructions — is already in place, and your job is to run it, improve it, and scale it.
Responsibilities
Deliver units against schedule, owning sequencing around actual part availability, daily floor priorities, and the escalation path when a build stalls
Lead and develop the assembly technicians and manufacturing engineers, setting the standards for quality and the path for people to grow
Bring build hours down substantially through process design, fixturing, and improved documentation across our high-mix, high-complexity assembly
Take new hardware platforms from engineering release into producible builds, running pilot builds and feeding manufacturability issues back to design with actionable specificity
Stand up the processes and fixtures each new platform needs
Own the controlled work instructions and build documentation the floor works from, keeping them current as designs change
Depending on your strengths, may own the BOM and production data layer — part numbering discipline, MBOM accuracy, and the automation connecting engineering data to operations
Preferred Qualifications
7+ years in manufacturing or NPI engineering for complex electromechanical hardware, with meaningful time in low-volume, high-complexity production rather than high-volume line manufacturing
Direct experience taking a product from prototype into repeatable production
Experience leading technicians and engineers — formally or as a lead — with a real interest in doing it
Fluency with PLM and BOM systems, and the judgment to keep BOM data trustworthy as designs move
Hands-on process development: fixture design, assembly method development, tooling selection
Demonstrated ownership of work instructions and build documentation under revision control
Comfort working closely with mechanical and electrical engineers, including holding a position on manufacturability when it is inconvenient
Scripting for manufacturing data — Python, Apps Script, or REST integration work between engineering and operations systems — is a plus
Wire harness fabrication and cable assembly experience is a plus
Exposure to MES, serialization, or traceability systems is a plus
Experience standing up manufacturing processes at a company doing it for the first time is a plus
Base Salary Range: $100,000 USD - $300,000 USD

evidence.text:
Vice President, Hardware Quality
WHOOP
Boston, MA
At WHOOP, we're on a mission to unlock and inspire performance for life. WHOOP empowers members to perform at a higher level through a deeper understanding of their bodies and daily lives.
WHOOP is seeking a Vice President of Hardware Quality to lead the vision, strategy, and execution of quality across our global hardware ecosystem. This leader will be responsible for ensuring quality is embedded throughout the product lifecycle — from early product development through manufacturing, supplier management, and field performance. Working closely with Hardware Engineering, Supply Chain, Operations, Membership Services, Finance, and manufacturing partners, you will build scalable systems, drive operational excellence, and create a culture of continuous improvement that enables WHOOP to deliver exceptional products and member experiences at scale.
Responsibilities
Define and execute a comprehensive quality strategy spanning product quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, field quality, and containment across the hardware lifecycle.
Build, lead, and develop a world-class global quality organization that enables operational excellence and unlocks growth and scale.
Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Product Development teams to ensure robust quality planning, validation, and risk mitigation throughout new product introduction and sustaining engineering activities.
Establish quality metrics, operating mechanisms, and executive reporting frameworks that provide visibility into quality performance, risks, and opportunities across the supply chain.
Drive closed-loop quality improvement initiatives by connecting field performance, reliability testing, manufacturing data, supplier performance, and product design insights.
Lead supplier quality programs, including qualification processes, factory audits, corrective and preventive actions, and strategic supplier development efforts across a global manufacturing network.
Qualifications
10+ years of leadership experience in hardware quality, manufacturing quality, supplier quality, or related functions supporting consumer electronics, wearable technology, or other complex hardware products.
Demonstrated success building and scaling high-performing quality organizations in fast-paced, high-growth environments.
Deep understanding of consumer electronics manufacturing processes, including electro-mechanical assemblies, PCB/SMT manufacturing, batteries, plastics, and critical component qualification.
Experience working with global manufacturing and supplier partners and managing quality across geographically distributed operations.
Expertise in quality systems and methodologies, including statistical process control, auditing, corrective and preventive action programs, root cause analysis, FMEA, Design for Manufacturing, Lean manufacturing, and Six Sigma principles.
Strong executive communication and stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence decisions through data-driven insights and cross-functional partnership.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
Willingness and ability to travel up to 25% internationally to support manufacturing partners, suppliers, and quality initiatives.
Strong commitment to embracing and leveraging AI tools in day-to-day tasks, ensuring AI-assisted work aligns with the same high-quality standards as personal contributions.
This role is based in the WHOOP office located in Boston, MA. The successful candidate must be prepared to relocate if necessary to work out of the Boston, MA office.
Interested in the role, but don’t meet every qualification? We encourage you to still apply! At WHOOP, we believe there is much more to a candidate than what is written on paper, and we value character as much as experience. As we continue to build a diverse and inclusive environment, we encourage anyone who is interested in this role to apply.
WHOOP is an Equal Opportunity Employer and participates in E-verify to determine employment eligibility
