evidence.text:
Manufacturing Ops Leader
C/A Design Inc.
Raleigh, NC
Note: This job description provides an outline of the essential functions and qualifications necessary for this position. It is not all-inclusive and duties may change, be added or deleted according to business need.
Summary
The Manufacturing Operations Leader will own and drive the performance of two key value streams within our aerospace and defense manufacturing environment. This leader will be responsible for delivering safe, high-quality, cost-effective products on schedule while developing a high-performing operations organization.
The ideal candidate is an experienced manufacturing leader with 5+ years of progressive experience in a people-leading role who can translate business objectives into disciplined operational execution. This role requires strong leadership, cross-functional collaboration, continuous improvement, and a deep commitment to quality and customer mission success.
Essential Duties And Responsibilities
Strive toward a culture of proactive safety.
Establish operational priorities, performance goals, and accountability across both value streams.
Develop and execute production plans to meet customer schedules and business objectives.
Monitor key performance indicators and drive corrective actions when targets are not achieved.
Partner closely with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Program Management, Human Resources, and other functions to resolve production issues.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, and other operational excellence methodologies.
Identify and eliminate bottlenecks, waste, production constraints, and process inefficiencies.
Ensure compliance with aerospace and defense quality standards, company procedures, and applicable regulatory requirements.
Support new product introduction, production ramp-up, process improvements, and manufacturing readiness activities.
Manage capacity, labor, equipment, and resource requirements across both value streams.
Lead root-cause analysis and corrective/preventive actions for recurring operational issues.
Develop and manage operating budgets while identifying opportunities to improve cost and productivity.
Establish effective visual management and daily operating rhythms to maintain focus on critical metrics.
Communicate operational performance, risks, and improvement plans to senior leadership.
Foster a collaborative environment focused on delivering reliable aerospace and defense products that support the warfighter.
Other duties as assigned.
Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Operations Management or related field preferred.
5+ years of progressive manufacturing or operations leadership experience, preferably within aerospace, defense, aviation, or another highly regulated industry.
Demonstrated experience leading multiple manufacturing teams, production areas, or value streams.
Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, production planning, capacity management, and operational metrics.
Proven ability to lead through complex production challenges and deliver measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, and cost.
Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
Strong knowledge of quality systems and manufacturing requirements applicable to aerospace and defense environments.
Demonstrated ability to develop and retain high-performing teams.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, and communication skills.
Ability to effectively collaborate across Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, Program Management, and executive leadership.
Experience with ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing performance metrics.
Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities and demanding customer requirements.
Physical Requirements
Ability to stand and walk for extended periods throughout the work shift.
Ability to frequently use hands and fingers to operate machine controls, tools, and measuring instruments.
Ability to lift, carry, push, and pull materials and components weighing up to 40 pounds, with or without reasonable accommodation.
Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and reach as required to load, unload, and inspect parts and equipment.
Ability to perform repetitive motions involving the hands, wrists, and arms.
Ability to visually inspect parts, interpret and read blueprints, technical drawings, work instructions, and use gauges, and measuring devices.
Ability to distinguish colors, dimensions, and surface defects when performing quality inspections.
Ability to hear and communicate effectively in a manufacturing environment.
Ability to safely operate equipment in a fast-paced production setting while wearing required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hearing protection, safety shoes, and other equipment as required.
Ability to work in an environment with exposure to machine noise, metal chips, cutting fluids, lubricants, and varying temperatures.
Ability to maintain regular attendance and work scheduled shifts, including overtime as required.
Work Environment
Manufacturing environment with exposure to moving mechanical equipment.
Frequent interaction with machine tools, raw materials, and finished products.
Compliance with all company safety policies, housekeeping requirements, and Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention practices.
Required use of appropriate PPE and adherence to all safety procedures.
Essential Functions Disclaimer
Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.
About HEICO
Heico has a history of success. Since its founding over 40 years ago The Heico Companies has grown from a single business to over 80 separate companies through a strategic acquisition policy, and by reinvesting its earnings into internal growth and new prospects. Historically talented at restoring distressed companies, Heico now strategically targets acquisitions that will complement its ever-growing portfolio of companies in manufacturing, construction, and industrial services.
These four core operations are organized into groups: Metal Processing Group, Construction Solutions Group, Applied Solutions Group, and Industrial Technologies Group. Once acquired, new Heico companies are assigned to a group and run on a stand-alone basis, allowing for great independence as well as the opportunity to share knowledge about markets, production processes, and management practices across other Heico groups and companies. Each Group has its own corporate team.
Heico continues to seek out new opportunities and maintain its standard of success. The Heico Companies has remained a privately held company since its creation and maintains a majority ownership in each of its operations, which generates more than $3.3 billion dollars in revenues. Many of our businesses are certified Woman-owned Business Enterprises (WBE).
More information about the holding company and overall organization can be found at www.heicocompanies.com.

DuPont
Minneapolis, MN
At DuPont, our purpose is to empower the world with essential innovations to thrive. We work on things that matter. Whether it’s providing clean water to more than a billion people on the planet, producing materials that are essential in everyday technology devices from smartphones to electric vehicles, or protecting workers around the world. Discover the many reasons the world’s most talented people are choosing to work at DuPont. Why Join Us | DuPont Careers
Quality Business Systems Director
Transform the Future of Quality at DuPont
At DuPont, we are advancing manufacturing and supply chain performance through Operational Excellence, digital enablement, and the DuPont Business System to deliver safer, more reliable, higher-quality outcomes for our customers.
We are seeking a Quality Business Systems Director
to define and scale DuPont’s global manufacturing quality strategy. Reporting to the Vice President, Enterprise Excellence
, this leader will partner closely with Business Quality Leaders, Business Operational Excellence Directors, Integrated Operations Leaders, and functional partners to improve quality performance, reduce cost of poor quality, and strengthen enterprise-wide capability.
This role is ideal for a quality and operational excellence leader who can connect strategy to execution, influence across a matrixed organization, and build a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and customer focus.
What You'll Do
As the Quality Business Systems Director, you will lead a small global team responsible for developing and deploying quality standards, tools, playbooks, metrics, and capability-building programs that improve customer outcomes and operational performance across DuPont.
You will:
Define and deploy DuPont’s global manufacturing quality excellence strategy across businesses and manufacturing sites.
Partner directly with Business Quality Leaders, Business Operational Excellence Directors, Integrated Operations Leaders, and Manufacturing, Engineering, Digital, Automation, and IT leaders to improve end-to-end SQDIP performance.
Develop and continuously improve global quality standards, toolkits, playbooks, training, and communities of practice.
Leverage and integrate artificial intelligence to develop/improve quality management approaches and techniques
Serve as a trusted advisor to business and site leaders by facilitating Kaizen events, problem-solving workshops, and transformation initiatives.
Establish quality performance metrics, analytics, and single sources of truth that enable data-driven decisions from the plant floor to senior leadership.
Integrate quality excellence practices into the DuPont Business System to create a consistent enterprise approach.
Build organizational capability and foster a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and customer-focused execution.
Why This Role Matters
The Quality Business Systems Director will help shape how DuPont improves quality, reliability, delivery, productivity, and cost across the enterprise.
By working across Operations, Quality, and business leadership, this role will translate business needs into practical standards, capability-building routines, and measurable improvements that strengthen customer confidence and operational performance.
You'll have the opportunity to:
Influence quality performance across multiple global businesses and sites.
Strengthen the relationship between manufacturing quality COE, business quality leadership, and customer outcomes.
Build scalable standards, tools, and routines that support quality aligned to the DuPont Business System.
Develop quality leaders and practitioners through coaching, training, and communities of practice.
Deliver measurable improvements in safety, quality, delivery, inventory, productivity, and cost.
Experience
What We're Looking For
15+ years of experience in manufacturing, quality, supply chain, operations, or operational excellence, including significant exposure to plant operations.
Demonstrated success leading enterprise or business-level quality, manufacturing, or operational excellence transformation.
Experience partnering with Business Quality, operations, and functional leaders to improve customer service, reliability, and operational performance.
Proven ability to influence across a global, matrixed organization and lead through others without relying solely on direct authority.
Experience leading and developing high-performing technical or subject matter expert teams.
Technical and Operational Excellence Expertise
Deep expertise in quality management systems, Lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, Kaizen, structured problem solving, and operational excellence methodologies.
Experience deploying business systems such as the DuPont Business System, Danaher Business System, Toyota Production System, Honeywell Operating System, or similar frameworks.
Strong track record of using data, performance metrics, and operational insights to identify losses, prioritize action, and sustain results.
Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or equivalent certification preferred.
Leadership Skills
Strategic thinker who uses data, customer insights, business priorities, and diverse perspectives to shape quality strategy and make sound, timely decisions.
Results-oriented leader who translates strategy into clear priorities, builds accountability, simplifies work, and removes barriers to execution.
Collaborative influencer who builds strong relationships across business, site, and functional teams and leads effectively in a global, matrixed environment.
Capability builder who coaches others, develops talent, and strengthens organizational routines that sustain continuous improvement.
Inclusive and trusted leader who communicates with authenticity, demonstrates commitment and care, encourages teams to speak up, and connects work to customer and business impact.
Location & Travel
Preferred Location:
Wilmington, Delaware (DuPont Corporate Headquarters highly preferred), Midland, Michigan, Minneapolis, Minnesota.
Travel:
Approximately 50% global travel to manufacturing sites and business locations.

DuPont has job leveling frameworks that help organize roles based on progressive levels of responsibility, proficiency and qualifications. Job Title:
Director of Manufacturing
Location:
Sacramento, CA (on-site; relocation available)
Pay:
$155,000-$185,000 per year
Company Information
Athena Ag supports the modern grower at any scale. The company's operating philosophy is to improve quality, reduce costs, drive consistency, and make the complex simple through disciplined products, procedures, technical support, and hands-on facility guidance. We continue to invest in the people, systems, and technology that support our rapidly growing portfolio of products and brands.
About The Role
Athena is seeking a Director of Manufacturing to lead safe, reliable, and efficient production as our business grows. Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer, you’ll own manufacturing performance across safety, quality, production planning, cost, equipment reliability, and team development.
This role calls for a technically capable leader who can move comfortably between operational planning and hands-on problem-solving. You’ll develop supervisors and production teams, strengthen manufacturing processes, and adapt quickly as demand, materials, and equipment availability change.
What You’ll Do
Manufacturing Leadership: Lead manufacturing operations, production teams, and day-to-day execution, with clear expectations for safety, quality, service, and cost.
Production Planning: Own production planning, scheduling, capacity, and staffing; adjust priorities quickly and communicate changes to downstream teams.
Performance and Cost Management: Establish manufacturing KPIs, analyze performance, and manage budgets, labor efficiency, operating costs, and throughput.
Continuous Improvement: Lead Lean and continuous improvement initiatives that reduce waste, resolve recurring problems, and improve quality and productivity.
Equipment Reliability: Assess operational risks, troubleshoot production issues, and partner with Maintenance and Engineering to improve equipment reliability.
Team Development: Hire, coach, and develop supervisors and production employees while building engagement and accountability.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Supply Chain, Quality, Distribution, Product Development, and Operations to align production with business needs.
Capacity and Growth: Support new equipment, automation, product launches, and manufacturing processes that expand capacity and support continued growth.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, technical training, and relevant manufacturing leadership experience.
At least 10 years of progressively responsible manufacturing experience, including at least 5 years leading manufacturing operations, supervisors, and production teams at comparable scale and complexity.
Experience managing production planning, scheduling, capacity, staffing, and day-to-day execution while responding to changes in demand, materials, and equipment availability.
Demonstrated success using Lean manufacturing, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement methods to improve safety, quality, throughput, labor efficiency, and cost.
Experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor and operating costs, and performance metrics, with the ability to analyze results and implement corrective actions.
Experience implementing workplace safety practices, standard operating procedures, and quality management systems in a manufacturing environment.
Experience partnering with Maintenance and Engineering to troubleshoot equipment, improve reliability, and implement equipment or process improvements.
Experience using ERP or manufacturing planning systems and data analysis tools to support production decisions, inventory accuracy, and performance reporting.
Experience hiring, coaching, and developing supervisors and production employees, managing performance, and leading teams through operational change.
Calm, pragmatic leadership, strong mechanical aptitude, and sound judgment when balancing safety, quality, cost, and competing production priorities.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing management, operations management, business administration, or a related discipline.
Professional certification such as Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, APICS CPIM, or a comparable manufacturing or operational certification.
Experience in fertilizer, agricultural inputs, chemical processing, or a comparable batch manufacturing environment, including dry blending, liquid formulation, filling, or packaging operations.
Experience expanding manufacturing capacity, commissioning new equipment or production lines, or implementing automation and scalable manufacturing processes.
Experience operating in an ISO 9001-certified or similarly quality-controlled manufacturing environment, including supporting audits and corrective actions.
Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP system used for production planning, work orders, bills of materials, and inventory control.
Why Join Athena
You’ll have the opportunity to shape Athena’s manufacturing operations and make a direct impact on product quality, production reliability, and cost. Working with the COO and cross-functional leaders, you’ll help build the processes and capabilities needed for continued growth.
This is a role for someone who enjoys solving practical problems, developing people, and turning operational data into measurable improvements. Your leadership will help teams deliver consistently while adapting to a growing business.

Cross-Functional Collaboration: Partner with Supply Chain, Quality, Distribution, Product Development, and Operations to align production with business needs.
Capacity and Growth: Support new equipment, automation, product launches, and manufacturing processes that expand capacity and support continued growth.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor’s degree in Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Operations Management, Business Administration, or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education, technical training, and relevant manufacturing leadership experience.
At least 10 years of progressively responsible manufacturing experience, including at least 5 years leading manufacturing operations, supervisors, and production teams at comparable scale and complexity.
Experience managing production planning, scheduling, capacity, staffing, and day-to-day execution while responding to changes in demand, materials, and equipment availability.
Demonstrated success using Lean manufacturing, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement methods to improve safety, quality, throughput, labor efficiency, and cost.
Experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor and operating costs, and performance metrics, with the ability to analyze results and implement corrective actions.
Experience implementing workplace safety practices, standard operating procedures, and quality management systems in a manufacturing environment.
Experience partnering with Maintenance and Engineering to troubleshoot equipment, improve reliability, and implement equipment or process improvements.
Experience using ERP or manufacturing planning systems and data analysis tools to support production decisions, inventory accuracy, and performance reporting.
Experience hiring, coaching, and developing supervisors and production employees, managing performance, and leading teams through operational change.
Calm, pragmatic leadership, strong mechanical aptitude, and sound judgment when balancing safety, quality, cost, and competing production priorities.
Preferred Qualifications
Master’s degree in engineering, manufacturing management, operations management, business administration, or a related discipline.
Professional certification such as Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt, APICS CPIM, or a comparable manufacturing or operational certification.
Experience in fertilizer, agricultural inputs, chemical processing, or a comparable batch manufacturing environment, including dry blending, liquid formulation, filling, or packaging operations.
Experience expanding manufacturing capacity, commissioning new equipment or production lines, or implementing automation and scalable manufacturing processes.
Experience operating in an ISO 9001-certified or similarly quality-controlled manufacturing environment, including supporting audits and corrective actions.
Experience with NetSuite or a comparable ERP system used for production planning, work orders, bills of materials, and inventory control.

You’ll have the opportunity to shape Athena’s manufacturing operations and make a direct impact on product quality, production reliability, and cost. Working with the COO and cross-functional leaders, you’ll help build the processes and capabilities needed for continued growth.
This is a role for someone who enjoys solving practical problems, developing people, and turning operational data into measurable improvements. Your leadership will help teams deliver consistently while adapting to a growing business.

Director of Manufacturing & Operations
Company:
HEN Technologies
Location:
Livermore, CA
Department:
Manufacturing & Operations
Employment Type:
Full-Time
About HEN Technologies
HEN Technologies is an innovative hardware and technology company transforming fire suppression through advanced nozzle systems, fluid dynamics, and intelligent firefighting solutions.
We are building next-generation technologies that improve firefighting effectiveness, water efficiency, and operational safety. As we continue to scale, we are looking for a hands-on manufacturing leader who can build, optimize, and scale our manufacturing operations while maintaining exceptional standards for quality, reliability, and efficiency.
About the Role
We are seeking a Director of Manufacturing & Operations
to lead and scale our manufacturing, production, equipment, and facility operations.
This individual will be responsible for ensuring our manufacturing processes, production equipment, and operational infrastructure can support increasing production volumes while maintaining high standards for quality, cost, and delivery.
The ideal candidate combines deep technical knowledge of manufacturing processes and equipment with strong operational leadership. This is a hands-on role requiring someone who is comfortable working directly on the manufacturing floor, troubleshooting production challenges, implementing processes, and building teams.
You will partner closely with Engineering, Supply Chain, Quality, and leadership to transition products into scalable manufacturing operations, improve production efficiency, and establish the systems and processes necessary to support HEN's continued growth.
Manufacturing & Production Operations
Lead day-to-day manufacturing operations, ensuring production targets are consistently met across quality, cost, throughput, and delivery.
Develop and execute manufacturing strategies to support increasing production volumes and new product introductions.
Establish standardized manufacturing processes, work instructions, and standard operating procedures (SOPs).
Identify and eliminate production bottlenecks, improve workflow, and optimize manufacturing capacity.
Implement and monitor operational KPIs, including production output, cycle time, yield, scrap, downtime, and overall equipment effectiveness (OEE).
Work closely with Engineering to ensure products are designed for manufacturability, assembly, and scalable production.
Equipment, Maintenance & Facility Operations
Own the reliability, performance, maintenance, and availability of manufacturing equipment and facility infrastructure.
Develop and implement preventive and predictive maintenance programs to minimize downtime and maximize equipment utilization.
Lead equipment troubleshooting, root-cause analysis, and corrective actions to resolve production issues.
Oversee equipment installation, commissioning, calibration, and qualification.
Manage relationships with equipment manufacturers, OEMs, and service vendors to ensure reliable equipment performance.
Implement and maintain manufacturing execution systems (MES), computerized maintenance management systems (CMMS), and other operational tools as appropriate.
Ensure manufacturing facilities operate safely, efficiently, and in compliance with applicable requirements.
Manufacturing Process Improvement & Scalability
Drive continuous improvement initiatives using Lean manufacturing, Kaizen, and other operational excellence methodologies.
Identify opportunities to improve production efficiency, reduce manufacturing costs, and increase equipment uptime.
Develop scalable manufacturing processes capable of supporting growth from early-stage production to higher-volume manufacturing.
Partner with Engineering and Quality to identify manufacturing defects, implement corrective actions, and improve product consistency.
Evaluate opportunities for automation, tooling improvements, and capital equipment investments.
Establish repeatable processes, documentation, and training programs that support operational consistency and scalability.
Cross-Functional Leadership & Supply Chain
Collaborate with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality teams to ensure manufacturing readiness and successful product launches.
Support new product introduction (NPI), including production planning, tooling readiness, process validation, and manufacturing ramp-up.
Coordinate material availability, inventory requirements, and production schedules with Supply Chain.
Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners to resolve quality, delivery, and production challenges.
Contribute to make-versus-buy decisions, manufacturing capacity planning, and operational strategy.
Manage manufacturing-related budgets, capital expenditures, and operational forecasts.
Team Leadership & Development
Build, lead, and develop a high-performing manufacturing and operations organization.
Establish clear performance expectations, accountability, and operational KPIs.
Provide hands-on technical guidance and mentorship to production, maintenance, and manufacturing personnel.
Develop training programs and standardized procedures to ensure employees can operate equipment safely and effectively.
Foster a culture of ownership, continuous improvement, safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Remain actively involved in solving manufacturing challenges while building the organizational structure needed to support growth.
Required Qualifications
6+ years of experience in manufacturing, production operations, equipment engineering, or related industrial environments.
4+ years of experience leading manufacturing, production, maintenance, or operations teams.
Demonstrated experience managing manufacturing operations in a high-volume or scaling production environment.
Strong technical understanding of manufacturing equipment, production processes, equipment maintenance, and troubleshooting.
Experience implementing preventive maintenance programs, equipment reliability initiatives, and process improvements.
Proven ability to improve manufacturing KPIs, including throughput, equipment uptime, yield, quality, and operational efficiency.
Experience developing SOPs, work instructions, training programs, and standardized manufacturing processes.
Working knowledge of Lean manufacturing, Kaizen, root-cause analysis, and continuous improvement methodologies.
Experience collaborating with Engineering, Supply Chain, and Quality teams to resolve production challenges.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage teams while remaining directly involved in day-to-day manufacturing operations.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-paced, evolving environment where processes and infrastructure are still being developed.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience in precision manufacturing, mechanical assemblies, fluid systems, industrial equipment, or electromechanical products.
Background in semiconductor, automotive, aerospace, industrial hardware, or other technically demanding manufacturing environments.
Experience scaling manufacturing operations from low-volume production to higher-volume commercial manufacturing.
Familiarity with CNC machining, precision assembly, tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing automation.
Experience with MES, ERP, and CMMS platforms.
Experience overseeing equipment procurement, installation, qualification, calibration, and maintenance.
Knowledge of design for manufacturability (DFM), design for assembly (DFA), and new product introduction (NPI).
Experience managing capital equipment budgets, operational expenditures, and vendor relationships.
Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Operations Management, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
Why Join HEN?
Build and Scale:
Take ownership of manufacturing operations at a growing hardware technology company.
Hands-On Impact:
Work directly with Engineering and production teams to solve challenging manufacturing problems.
Technical Innovation:
Help bring advanced mechanical and fluid-dynamics technologies into scalable production.
Ownership and Autonomy:
Play a key role in defining the manufacturing processes, equipment strategy, and operational infrastructure that will support HEN's next phase of growth.
Meaningful Mission:
Help develop and manufacture technology designed to improve firefighting effectiveness and safety.

evidence.quote:
Job Description
Our employees work on the world’s most advanced electronics. At Electronic Systems, you’ll be among the brightest minds, working on the aerospace and defense industry’s most difficult problems. Drawing strength from our differences, we’re innovating for the future. And you can, too. We put our customers first – exemplified by our missions: “We Protect Those Who Protect Us®” and “We Innovate For Those Who Move The World™.” Sound like a team you want to be a part of? Come build your career with BAE Systems.

Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location here at our BAE Systems facility in Austin, TX. 100% of the time.

This role drives integrated strategies that elevate safety, quality, cost, and delivery while cultivating a culture of disciplined problem‑solving and operational rigor. The director oversees the development of data‑driven systems and processes that strengthen decision‑making, transparency, and compliance across a 1,000‑person defense manufacturing facility. They collaborate closely with senior leadership and cross‑functional teams to align improvement initiatives with long‑term strategic objectives and customer commitments. Through strong leadership and effective change‑management, the director enables sustainable operational excellence and advances the factory’s mission.


  • Lead Lean Six Sigma and CI initiatives: Kaizen events, 5S, VSM, FMEA, root cause analysis, and other best practices.
  • Coach and mentor at all organization levels to instill a culture of continuous improvement tools and methodologies.
  • Establish KPI tracking, dashboards, and ROI metrics to highlight impact, decision-making and operational performance
  • Shape and execute an industrial engineering strategy that optimizes facility layout, throughput, takt time, labor standards, capacity planning, and simulation modeling.
  • Elevate standardized work, visual management, and digital factory tools to ensure consistency and efficiency.
  • Design and implement training programs on Lean, Six Sigma, CI tools, industrial engineering, and compliance for all levels of the workforce.
  • Establish Lean champions, CI practitioners, and cross-functional improvement teams.
  • Oversee continual upskilling to maintain high standards in process discipline and data-driven thinking.


Required Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree required (Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing, Business, or related); Master’s or MBA preferred.
  • Experience:
    • 12+ years in industrial/operations leadership in regulated or defense manufacturing environments.
    • Proven execution of CI initiatives with measurable outcomes in cost, quality, and productivity.
    • Demonstrated IE expertise: layout optimization, simulation, takt time, DFMA, and capacity modeling.
    • Strong background in compliance with standards like ITAR, AS9100, DFARS, and internal/external audits.
    • Experience building BI tools, cross-functional dashboards, and applying data insights in operations.


Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
    • Lean Six Sigma Black Belt or Master Black Belt (preferred); PMP or similar a plus.
    • Advanced proficiency with data analysis and BI tools.
    • Outstanding leadership, communication, facilitation, and change management skills.
  • Security Requirements:
    • Ability to obtain Secret clearance (or higher).



Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.


About BAE Systems, Inc.
BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.

Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

We are conducting a search for an experienced Director of Operations on behalf of a growing healthcare services organization providing outsourced operational support to healthcare and life sciences companies.

We're looking for someone who can build structure, drive accountability, and improve operational performance while supporting continued organizational growth.

Provide operational leadership and accountability for patient support services and related program activities.
Oversee daily operations, staffing requirements, workflow management, and overall program performance.
Evaluate operational processes and implement improvements to enhance efficiency, quality, and service delivery.

Manager, Supplier Industrialization Engineering
Amperesand
San Francisco, CA
Company Overview
Amperesand is reinventing how the world powers its most critical systems.
We are facing a once-in-a-generation opportunity for infrastructure disruption. Electricity demand is skyrocketing, driven by AI factories, electric vehicles, and modern industrial growth. Energy supply is shifting to incorporate a more diverse mix of resources – including solar, gas, and batteries – at a massive scale.
And yet the power infrastructure behind our latest mega-projects hasn’t meaningfully changed in nearly 100 years. Supply chains for today’s infrastructure equipment can’t match the pace and sophistication of critical energy projects. Amperesand is building hardware and software that rewrites this broken power infrastructure playbook to support a new era of energy abundance.
We’ve built a new class of intelligent, software-defined power infrastructure products leveraging a decade of advanced medium voltage Solid State Transformer research that’s now ready for commercial deployment.
Our products and solutions go far beyond the capabilities of traditional electrical equipment. We make power systems that are faster to deploy, dramatically smaller and more efficient, and capable of supporting modern, dynamic energy needs for tomorrow’s most demanding energy consumers.
Scalable in-house advanced manufacturing capability is our foundation for meeting timeline and quality expectation to serve infrastructure customers around the world.
Amperesand is led by breakthrough energy hardware development veterans and funded by top tier investors who share our vision of building a category-defining energy technology company.
With hubs in San Francisco, Reno, and Singapore, our global team is laser focused on building foundational technology to solve the most pressing problems in power infrastructure at scale.
Join us in building the power foundation of the future!
Role Summary
As Manager, Supplier Industrialization, you will build and lead Amperesand’s global SIE function, owning the strategy, processes, and team that bring new suppliers from development into volume production.
Responsibilities
Team Leadership
Hire, develop, and manage a globally distributed team of Supplier Industrialization Engineers
Set priorities and performance expectations, provide coaching and clear growth paths for direct reports
Strategy and Process
Own the global supplier industrialization roadmap, aligning supplier onboarding and ramp milestones to NPI timelines and production forecasts
Define and standardize playbooks, tools, and processes across the full supplier lifecycle, from qualification through volume ramp
Partner with Supply Chain, Engineering, and Manufacturing leadership to keep supplier readiness aligned with technical requirements and delivery commitments
Supplier Development and Quality
Serve as the senior escalation point for complex supplier issues, engage supplier leadership when management level involvement is needed
Oversee supplier quality across the portfolio and drive systemic corrective action for escapes or delivery disruptions
Cross Functional and Program Management
Bridge global suppliers and internal Engineering, Manufacturing, and Supply Chain teams on design alignment, material readiness, and DFM feedback
Maintain portfolio level risk visibility, own global KPI reporting for the SIE function including OTD, first pass yield, and ramp attainment
Provide regular program updates and escalations to Supply Chain leadership
Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or related field, Master’s preferred
Electrical, mechanical, or manufacturing background strongly preferred
10 plus years across engineering, supply chain, and or program management, with 2 plus years in a people management role
Demonstrated success leading supplier industrialization or supplier development in hardware manufacturing, power electronics, energy, or adjacent capital equipment preferred
Track record hiring and developing high performing technical teams in NPI heavy or startup environments
Experience managing globally distributed supplier portfolios across multiple geographies and time zones
Strong communication skills across technical and business audiences, able to work effectively across cultures
Travel Requirement: 30-50% travel required.
Frequent onsite engagement with suppliers to support qualification, process development, issue resolution, and production ramp efforts.
Salary: $170,000-$200,000/annual DOE and location
SF Pay Range
$175,000—$205,000 USD
Please note
: This role requires working on-site 5 days a week. We do not offer hybrid or remote options.
While this role is listed for the location above, we may consider candidates in other locations on a case-by-case basis.
Onsite Collaboration Rationale
Given the highly collaborative and cross-functional nature of hardware, embedded systems, and product development, in-person partnership across engineering and product teams is critical to enabling rapid execution, technical alignment, and successful development outcomes.
Why Join Amperesand
Work on next-generation power infrastructure systems
High ownership and visibility
Cross-functional collaboration
Opportunity to shape future products and infrastructure
Fast-moving startup environment
Pay Disclosure & Benefits
Compensation will be determined based on experience, location, and other factors permitted by law.
The benefits outlined below apply exclusively to employees located in the United States:
Competitive Salary + Incentive Stock Options
Medical, vision, and dental benefits for employees and their dependents, effective from the start of hire
Company paid Basic Life, AD&D, short-term and long-term disability insurance
401k retirement savings plan through Empower
Employees receive paid time off (PTO), paid sick days, and paid company holidays

Employer and employee Central Provident Fund contributions in accordance with the CPF Act (for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents)
Annual leave, paid sick leave, hospitalisation leave, and all Singapore public holidays, in line with or exceeding the Employment Act

Additional benefits may be available depending on the role and employment type. Benefits are subject to the terms of applicable company policies and plans.

As part of our commitment to protecting confidential and proprietary information, candidates should not disclose or provide Amperesand with any confidential, proprietary, or trade secret information belonging to a current or former employer or any other third party during the application or interview process.
Please do not submit or present employer-owned source code, schematics, designs, technical documentation, internal presentations, customer information, prototypes, or other confidential materials. Candidates should discuss their experience and accomplishments at an appropriate level and use only information and materials they are authorized to share.

evidence.quote: Principal Engineer - Quality Enablement
evidence.text:
Principal Engineer - Quality Enablement
IRIS
Remote
About IRIS
IRIS Software Group is one of the UK's largest privately held software companies, trusted by 100,000+ businesses, schools and accountancy firms to keep their operations running. Our software pays 1 in 6 UK employees, supports over 12,000 schools, and is relied on by 91 of the top 100 UK accountancy firms.
We're a Great Place to Work® certified employer, recognised for our commitment to well-being, inclusion and development - and we're growing fast.
IRIS is in the middle of a step-change in how we build software.
Our Agentic SDLC programme is moving the organisation from tool-assisted engineering to agentic as the default way of working, with a 3x productivity target for FY27. As coding velocity rises, the constraints on quality shift. Manual testing as the dominant model no longer fits and the legacy assumption that parts of our estate "cannot be automated" is being actively disproved by modern AI-assisted tooling.
We're looking for an exceptional Quality Engineering leader to define and drive what quality engineering looks like at IRIS in this new world.
This is a strategic transformation role first, and a delivery role second. You'll set the vision, establish standards, lead organisational change, and build the quality engineering model that supports the next generation of software delivery at IRIS.
The destination is clear: smaller, more specialist quality engineering functions, confident in automation, embedded in pods, owning curated end-to-end capability per product, and over time extending into performance, resilience, and chaos engineering.
Importantly, this is a quality strategy, not a cost exercise. Our focus is on better product quality, faster feedback loops, lower defect leakage, and creating a quality function whose impact compounds rather than scales linearly with engineering output.
What You'll Be Doing:
Quality Engineering Strategy & Transformation
You'll own the global quality engineering strategy across all five Product & Engineering divisions and define the destination model for Quality Engineering across IRIS.
Key responsibilities include:
Own the global quality engineering strategy across all five P&E divisions, including the destination model for the QE function and the transition path to it.
Lead the automation maturity assessment across the estate — baseline current state, including the legacy and on-prem portfolio, and build the evidence base for subsequent decisions.
Support defining and transitioning to the right Eng:QA ratio by pod archetype and divisional context.
Define and own the standards for automated testing across the toolchain: unit, integration, contract, E2E, and AI-generated test coverage. Integrate with the standard PDLC and the agentic workflows being rolled out.
Establish the curated E2E capability suite per product line, what is owned centrally, what sits in pods, and how it is maintained.
Partner with the Director of Agentic SDLC on the QE-specific elements of bootcamp cohorts, agentic workflows for test generation, and the upskilling pathway for manual testers moving toward automation engineering.
Provide the evidence and framing the divisional VPs need to lead the QE workforce conversation in their divisions, supporting the destination model, the upskilling pathway, and the honest position on roles that cannot make the transition.
Support the small specialist Quality Engineering practice that can carry the standards, tooling choices, and harder testing problems that don't belong in any single pod.
Practice Leadership
You'll build influence across a large engineering estate while leading a specialist quality practice.
You'll:
Build and lead a small, senior, specialist central Quality Engineering practice.
Lead the global QE community of practice across approximately 170 QA professionals.
Define development pathways from manual testing to automation engineering and specialist disciplines.
Partner with Engineering VPs to drive capability maturity across divisions.
Develop a Quality Engineering career framework aligned with broader engineering frameworks.
Future-Focused Growth
As the practice matures, you'll help shape several strategic growth areas:
Performance and scalability testing as a first-class discipline.
Resilience and chaos engineering across critical services.
The evolution of IRIS's future Scalability & Resiliency practice and eventual SRE capability.
Quality signals as a product input through the integration of observability, telemetry, and customer experience data.
What We're Looking For
Essential Experience
Experience leading quality engineering at scale in a multi-product, multi-team software organisation. B2B SaaS background strongly preferred.
A track record of moving a QE function from manual-dominant to automation-dominant, not as a theoretical exercise but in an organisation with real legacy, real customer commitments, and real people to bring with you.
Deep working knowledge of modern automated testing across the stack, unit, integration, contract, E2E, performance and of AI-assisted testing where it is genuinely useful versus where it is hype.
Experience supporting and driving specialist QE functions/Team that influences a much larger distributed engineering estate. Comfortable with the team topologies model and the distinction between enabling teams, platform teams, and stream-aligned pods.
Exposure to performance, resilience, or chaos engineering at a meaningful level, enough to credibly grow the role into those areas. Full SRE leadership experience is welcome but not required at hire.
Leadership Style & Approach
We are looking for someone who:
Leads with quality, not headcount. Holds the line on the destination model even when the conversation is uncomfortable.
Is direct and clear, comfortable challenging peers, including the Programme Director and the CTO, with evidence and a point of view.
Builds trust with engineers and QAs on the ground as well as with VPs in the room.
Is comfortable operating with incomplete information and adjusting as evidence builds.
Brings opinions, not just frameworks.
Nice to Have
Experience in regulated or compliance-heavy software environments.
Familiarity with modern agentic engineering tools such as Cursor, Copilot, CodeRabbit and Claude Code.
Experience working within federated operations or platform engineering models.
Why You’ll Love Working Here
Impact:
Your work will influence millions globally.
Growth:
Continuous learning and career development opportunities.
Belonging:
A culture that celebrates diversity and empowers every individual.
Remote Working
Please be advised, permanent remote working, is only available to those living more than 25 miles (in a direct line) from their nearest IRIS office.
Ready to Apply?
Click Apply
- we’re excited to learn about your unique perspective and experience. If you need adjustments during the process, let us know. We’re committed to making this opportunity accessible to everyone.
What to expect from our hiring process
Our process is designed to be fair, transparent and straightforward. Stages vary depending on the role — more senior positions may involve additional steps, and some areas include role-specific assessments such as a technical test or case study — but typically you can expect:
Application review
— we assess your experience and potential
Initial call
— a short conversation to learn about you and share more about the role
Skills assessment
— tailored to the position, e.g. case study, coding challenge or portfolio review
Final interview
— meet the team and explore how you'll make an IMPACT at IRIS
We'll always walk you through the specific stages at the start of the process so you can prepare with confidence.
If you need any adjustments or accommodations during the process, let us know, we’re committed to making this experience accessible for everyone.

Dematic
Atlanta, GA

This director leads the strategy, governance, and execution needed to convert drawing-based product knowledge into structured, reusable, and change-controlled digital product definitions. The role aligns Product Development, Product Management, Solution Development, Manufacturing, IT, Business Transformation, and regional teams to establish a scalable digital thread across Teamcenter, Solution Suite, SAP S/4HANA, CAD, and related platforms. The position creates organizational value by improving product-data quality, configuration accuracy, reuse, traceability, order handoff, and manufacturing readiness while enabling responsible use of AI with human review and release controls.

Global Opportunities

items.title: Director / Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement

evidence.quote: You have experience in manufacturing leadership, as a supervisor, manager, or plant manager, and you can speak to how you improved the area you were responsible for.
evidence.text:
Director | Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement
POLYWOOD®
Syracuse, IN
Director | Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement
Syracuse, Indiana | On-Site | Full-Time
Help us build the way POLYWOOD® runs, improves, and grows.
At POLYWOOD®, we have built a strong business on hardworking people and the knowledge they bring to the job every day. As we grow, we have an opportunity to give our teams a common, structured way to solve problems, improve performance, and sustain the gains.
We are hiring a Director, Operational Excellence - Quality & Continuous Improvement to help us take that next step. This position partners directly with our COO to build and deploy THE POLYWOOD WAY, our management system and operating philosophy, across our manufacturing operations in Syracuse, Indiana, and Roxboro, North Carolina.
You will work alongside site and functional leaders to find the real root cause of problems, lead structured improvements in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team performance, and build the routines that keep those improvements in place.
This is not a role for a scholar who teaches tools from a conference room. It is a hands-on opportunity for a practitioner who has led manufacturing teams, improved the areas they were responsible for, and enjoys helping others become better problem solvers.
Reporting directly to our Chief Operating Officer, you will have the opportunity to shape how POLYWOOD® manages, improves, and grows for years to come.
────────────────────────────────────────
The Work You Will Own
You will help turn THE POLYWOOD WAY into practical routines our teams use every day, from tiered management and daily huddles to standard work, visual management, and structured problem solving.
Your work will connect Quality, Lean, Continuous Improvement, data, and people development. You will put on your safety shoes and safety glasses, seek to understand the process first, and then help the people closest to the work make improvements that last.
────────────────────────────────────────
Where You Will Make an Impact
Partnering with the COO to develop, deploy, and continuously improve THE POLYWOOD WAY across both sites
Strengthening our tiered management system so goals on the floor line up with company goals for safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team
Leading setup reduction, value stream mapping, and root cause and countermeasure problem solving with the subject-matter experts who do the work
Leading quality strategy across both sites, including process controls, defect prevention, and corrective and preventive action
Applying structured problem solving beyond the plant floor, to challenges like team member turnover, warranty replacements, downtime, and training
Analyzing operational, quality, and cost data and turning findings into clear priorities for site and executive leaders
Validating the operational and financial results of improvements and building plans to sustain them
Building a network of Continuous Improvement resources and coaching supervisors and site leaders to solve problems on their own
Sharing effective practices between Syracuse and Roxboro and keeping standards consistent
────────────────────────────────────────
What You Bring
You have experience in manufacturing leadership, as a supervisor, manager, or plant manager, and you can speak to how you improved the area you were responsible for.
You have significant experience in manufacturing operations, Operational Excellence, Lean, Continuous Improvement, or Quality. You have personally led improvements, not only taught them, and you can explain tools like setup reduction, value stream mapping, and root cause problem solving in plain language.
You know that improvement starts with data you can trust, and when the data is noisy, you start by understanding the process gaps. You are comfortable influencing across functions and levels, including people who do not report to you.
Most importantly, you are hands-on, practical, and collaborative. You build the skills of others, follow through without unnecessary bureaucracy, and measure success by results that last.
Bonus Points
Experience with tiered management systems and strategic goal deployment
Experience leading improvements across more than one manufacturing site
Experience with Training Within Industry (TWI) or other structured training programs
Experience applying problem solving to turnover, hiring, or other business processes
Experience in extrusion, plastics, or building products manufacturing
────────────────────────────────────────
About Us
At POLYWOOD®, we design and build outdoor furniture that brings people together and stands the test of time. We do this using sustainable materials, including our genuine POLYWOOD® lumber made from recycled plastics. The strength of our products starts with the strength of our people.
Our manufacturing teams in Syracuse, Indiana, and Roxboro, North Carolina, build the products our customers love. THE POLYWOOD WAY will give those teams a common language and a structured way to keep getting better, together.
────────────────────────────────────────
What Makes This Role Special
You will help build something new.
You will shape THE POLYWOOD WAY and how it comes to life across both sites.
You will partner directly with the COO.
You will work closely with a leader who is passionate about building systems and developing people.
Your work will show up in real results.
Your improvements will be visible in safety, quality, delivery, cost, and team performance.
You will help people grow.
Many of our leaders have grown up within POLYWOOD®, and you will help them learn new ways of working that can change their careers.
You will join an “All Hands on the Rope” culture.
Improvement is everyone’s job here, from the leadership team to the shop floor.
You will be based in Syracuse with reach across both sites.
This position is on-site in Syracuse, Indiana, at least 80% of the time, with travel to Roxboro, North Carolina, as needed and up to 20% remote flexibility.
────────────────────────────────────────
If you are a hands-on leader who builds systems, develops people, and delivers results that last, we would love to hear from you.
────────────────────────────────────────
POLYWOOD is an equal opportunity employer. POLYWOOD evaluates qualified applicants without regard to characteristics protected by federal, state, or local laws.

evidence.text:
Director of Continuous Improvement
hireneXus
Boston, MA
Location:
North of Boston, MA (on-site)
About The Company
Our client is a growing, private equity-backed food manufacturer producing fresh, ready-to-cook proteins and meal solutions for leading grocery retailers and foodservice customers nationwide. Their products, including hand-crafted, value-added meats combined with fresh vegetables and seasonings, have earned a strong position in the specialty section of the grocery store. The company is growing, and leadership is now investing in operational excellence to support the next phase of that growth.
The Opportunity
This is a newly created role and the company's first dedicated continuous improvement leader. You'll partner closely with plant leadership to build a CI function from the ground up across a 250-person production floor. The operation is high-mix and labor-intensive: much of the product is assembled by hand, the product is perishable, and daily needs change based on customer demand. This is not machine-paced manufacturing, and it calls for someone who knows how to improve operations where people, not equipment, drive output.
Leadership is excited about this role and fully behind it. The right person will have the independence and support to make a real, measurable impact on cost, yield, and how work gets done.
What You'll Do
Lead cost-out initiatives across the plant, with a focus on labor productivity, yield, and waste reduction
Build the KPI and metrics foundation the operation currently lacks, including labor standards, yield tracking, and performance dashboards
Shorten the loop between labor planning and actual results so the team can manage to standard daily
Rethink how manual work is organized and performed, including line layout, staffing models, work methods, and labor standards for high-mix hand assembly
Identify and attack sources of product loss, giveaway, and waste in a perishable environment
Drive structured root cause analysis and make sure fixes stick
Introduce practical Lean and Six Sigma tools and build a CI culture where none exists today
Work hands-on on the floor alongside supervisors and team members, coaching and training as you go
Partner with quality and food safety to make sure improvements support regulatory and customer requirements
Use NetSuite and Power BI to turn operational data into clear, actionable reporting
What We're Looking For
5+ years of continuous improvement, operational excellence, or industrial engineering experience in manufacturing, with progressive leadership responsibility
Proven success improving labor-intensive, high-mix, manual assembly operations. This is the most important requirement.
Food manufacturing experience strongly preferred, especially fresh, perishable, or protein processing environments
Strong working knowledge of Lean and Six Sigma. Green Belt or Black Belt certification preferred.
A track record of building metrics, labor standards, and accountability systems from scratch
Documented cost savings and yield improvements you can speak to in detail
An independent, self-directed style: someone who can assess an operation, set a plan, and execute without a lot of structure around them
A hands-on leader who is comfortable on the production floor and earns credibility with frontline teams
Experience with NetSuite and Power BI, or similar ERP and BI tools
Bilingual in English and Spanish is a strong plus
Must be local to the Greater Boston / North Shore area or willing to relocate. This role is on-site.
Why This Role
Build the CI function from the ground up with real ownership and visible impact
Leadership and investors who are committed to the investment and eager to support it
A growing company with room for advancement as the business scales

As the Fort Wayne OEM Director of Manufacturing, you will be a key leadership contributor to the success of the Fort Wayne Manufacturing Hub. Reporting to the Hub Director of Manufacturing, you will provide inspirational leadership in a rapidly growing business and have responsibility for all original equipment manufacturing at the site. This role demands a strategic, results-oriented leader with a proven track record of building and scaling rapidly growing organizations. Because of the need for consistent, in-person collaboration and/or the requirement to perform all work onsite due to the nature of this particular role, it will be performed full-time on site. This means work will be conducted on location at a BAE Systems facility 100% of the time.
Key responsibilities include:

Strategic Product Stream Leadership

  • Own the strategic direction, execution, and performance of the Circuit Card Assembly and Unit Integration factories
  • Serve as the primary point of contact between production and program management

Program Execution

  • Oversee execution of manufacturing in alignment with program schedules
  • Ensure all contractual obligations (cost, schedule, performance) are met or exceeded

Performance Improvement

  • Drive continuous improvement using Lean, Six Sigma Principles
  • Implement metrics to monitor production performance
  • Initiate corrective actions to resolve production variances, quality escapes, and manufacturing cost variances
Required Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Bachelors degree in Manufacturing, Industrial Technology, Operations Management, or related field; equivalent experience considered OR 20 years manufacturing experience with no degree
  • Minimum 10 years experience in production/manufacturing
  • Minimum 6 years experience leading production/manufacturing teams including managing people leaders
  • Proficiency with manufacturing management concepts
  • Proficiency applying Lean Manufacturing principles and visual management tools
Preferred Education, Experience, & Skills
  • Proficiency with Oracle ERP
  • Formal Lean or Six Sigma training/certification
  • Minimum 10 years experience leading people leaders of production/manufacturing teams


Pay Information
Full-Time Salary Range: $153377 - $260743

Please note: This range is based on our market pay structures. However, individual salaries are determined by a variety of factors including, but not limited to: business considerations, local market conditions, and internal equity, as well as candidate qualifications, such as skills, education, and experience.

Employee Benefits: At BAE Systems, we support our employees in all aspects of their life, including their health and financial well-being. Regular employees scheduled to work 20+ hours per week are offered: health, dental, and vision insurance; health savings accounts; a 401(k) savings plan; disability coverage; and life and accident insurance. We also have an employee assistance program, a legal plan, and other perks including discounts on things like home, auto, and pet insurance. Our leave programs include paid time off, paid holidays, as well as other types of leave, including paid parental, military, bereavement, and any applicable federal and state sick leave. Employees may participate in the company recognition program to receive monetary or non-monetary recognition awards. Other incentives may be available based on position level and/or job specifics.
About BAE Systems, Inc. BAE Systems, Inc. is a defense, aerospace, and security company headquartered in Falls Church, Virginia, with more than 40,000 employees worldwide. We serve, supply, and protect those who protect us. As one of the most geographically diverse international defense companies, we deliver a full range of products and services spanning air, land, maritime, space, and cyber, including advanced electronics, intelligence solutions, and dedicated customer support.

Our culture is performance-driven and values-led, built on curiosity, creativity, and collaboration. Purpose isn't a tagline here. It's what drives us. We're developing breakthrough technologies that defend national security and make a lasting impact on our communities and our planet. When you join BAE Systems, you're not just building a career. You're contributing to a mission that truly matters.

This position will be posted for at least 5 calendar days. The posting will remain active until the position is filled, or a qualified pool of candidates is identified.

Nexus Search
United States
Nexus Search are partnered with a $B revenue Pharma manufacturer to appoint two Site Quality Heads for major sterile injectables manufacturing sites in the US. One site in the Midwest employs 600+ people, and the other with 200+ . Both are scaling on the back of sustained demand and investment.

The presence to hold the line on quality while partnering closely with operations and commercial leaders

evidence.text:
Sr. Manager of Adventure Products
Rivian
Irvine, CA
About Rivian
Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract.
As a company, we constantly challenge what's possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations.
Role Summary
As the Senior Manager of Adventure Products, you will lead our Industrial Design Product Team focused on expanding the Rivian experience beyond the vehicle itself. Reporting directly to the Senior Director of Exterior Design, you will oversee the end-to-end design strategy and execution across vehicle accessories, off-the-shelf brand partnerships, gear, apparel, lifestyle merchandise, and toys.
This role requires a proven design leader with extensive hands-on production experience and deep factory-level relationships. You will bridge high-level visionary product strategy with rigorous manufacturing execution, ensuring every product meets Rivian's world-class design standards while scaling effectively into mass production.
Responsibilities
Design Leadership & Team Management
Lead, mentor, and inspire a high-performing team of industrial designers focused on vehicle accessories, hardgoods, softgoods, lifestyle gear, and toys.
Expand the aesthetic, functional, and strategic design vision for all non-vehicle physical products, maintaining alignment with Rivian's core vehicle design language.
Manage project workflows, design reviews, timelines, and resource allocation across multiple concurrent product programs.
Product Strategy & Range Execution
Vehicle Accessories:
Drive design innovation for internal and customer-facing vehicle accessories (e. g. , gear tunnel components, roof racks, camping gear, cargo management, lighting, and overland equipment).
Toy & Merch Strategy:
Build and execute a cohesive brand merchandise and toy strategy that engages enthusiasts, children, and Rivian owners worldwide.
Off-the-Shelf & Licensing Partnerships:
Evaluate, curate, and direct third-party supplier products and collaborative brand partnerships, ensuring off-the-shelf items are elevated to meet Rivian's premium design standards.
Production, Manufacturing & Factory Engagement
Leverages extensive production experience and direct factory contacts to push concepts through DFM (Design for Manufacturing) into successful mass production.
Work directly on factory floors-both domestically and internationally-to troubleshoot prototyping, tooling, material selection, CMF (Color, Material, Finish), and production challenges.
Collaborate closely with Purchasing, Supply Chain, Hardware Engineering, and Quality teams to ensure design intent, cost targets, and launch schedules are strictly maintained.
Qualifications
To Apply:
Please include a direct link to your portfolio (and any access credentials if password-protected), featuring work in industrial design, softgoods/hardgoods, and production-ready physical products. Experience:
10+ years of professional industrial design experience, with at least 3-5+ years in a team management or leadership capacity.
Production Mastery:
Demonstrated track record of bringing complex physical products from concept through high-volume mass production.
Factory Network & Technical Expertise:
Must-have
established direct relationships and hands-on experience working directly with factories, suppliers, and overseas/domestic manufacturing partners. Proven capability to push factory partners to achieve tight design tolerances and premium finishing.
Category Diversity:
Prior background designing across diverse categories-such as outdoor/adventure gear, automotive accessories, consumer electronics, hardgoods, toys, or technical softgoods-is highly preferred.
Design Excellence:
Exceptional portfolio demonstrating strong ID fundamentals, form development, sketching, 3D CAD modeling, CMF mastery, and user-centered design thinking.
Cross-Functional Collaboration:
Strong ability to communicate design vision and negotiate technical/budget constraints with engineering, supply chain, and executive stakeholders.
Travel:
Ability to travel domestically and internationally (up to 20-30%) to visit factory partners, suppliers, and testing environments.
Bonus Qualifications
Passion for the outdoors, electric vehicles, overland travel, and adventure culture.
Background in developing both hardgoods (tooling, injection molding, metal fabrication)
and softgoods/textiles.
Pay Disclosure
The salary range for this role is $196,000 - $259,700 for California based applicants. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An employee's position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, geographic location, shift, and organizational needs.
The successful candidate may be eligible for annual performance bonus and equity awards.
We offer a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and part-time employees, their spouse or domestic.
