evidence.text:
Operations Director
Danone
Dallas, TX
About The Job
At Danone, Manufacturing the best products and supplying them to meet demand is a key driver for our plant teams. We are currently looking to hire an Operations Director
based in Dallas, Texas
. The Operations Director will strategically manage manufacturing operations at our state-of-the-art, extra-large beverage production facility. This role partners closely with the Plant Director to oversee all daily production activities, directly manage business unit leaders and drive strategic initiatives, while also fostering a culture of continuous improvement and safety. This role is responsible for ensuring customer orders are produced timely in a cost-effective manner with safety and quality as top priorities.
Key Responsibilities
Lead short- and medium-term production strategies to optimize labor, materials, and workflows.
Drive accountability and cultural change through Danone’s Integrated Work Systems (IWS).
Monitor and improve SQCDMN metrics (Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, Mobilization, Nature).
Provide administrative direction across departments including Production, Packaging, Processing, Planning, and Purchasing.
Manage operational budgets, cost controls, and profit/loss statements.
Partner with HR in a union environment on hiring, performance, and employee relations.
Oversee capital project planning and execution.
Ensure compliance with GMP, FDA, safety, and food quality standards.
Foster a collaborative, ethical, and high-performance culture across teams.
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential function of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand; walk; sit; use hands to handle or feel objects, tools, or controls; reach with hands and arms; climb stairs and ladders, balance; stoop, kneel or crouch; talk and hear. Occasionally required to lift and / or move up to 50 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by the job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus.
Work Environment
The work environment characteristics described here are representative of those an employee encounters while performing the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
While performing the duties of this job, the employee regularly works near moving mechanical parts and is regularly exposed to wet and/or humid conditions. The employee may be exposed to fumes or airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals and may be exposed to loud noises in the plant. The employee occasionally works in high, precarious places and is occasionally exposed to extreme cold, risk of electrical shock and vibration.
Engagement in our Integrated Work Systems
Ensure adherence to plant standards (including but not limited to GMP, AIB, FDA, Quality, Safety, Finance, ISO, Daily Direction Setting, Driving Operational Efficiency). As a fundamental piece of the organization, your responsibility is to participate and own the implementation and deployment of related integrated work systems and corresponding pillars (Leadership foundation, Daily Direction Setting, Driving Operational Efficiency; Autonomous Maintenance; planned Maintenance; Focused Improvement; Education and Training; Environmental, Health and Safety; Quality; Organization; Supply Network; Early Equipment Management) with the objective of owning your space, owning your performance (Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, Mobilization, Nature) and owning your continuous improvement.
Compensation & Benefits
Danone North America additionally offers a performance-based bonus and has a strong benefits package including Medical, Dental, Vision, Prescription Drug Coverage, 401k Plan, Wellness Program, Life Insurance, Tuition Reimbursement, Flexible Time Off, and Paid Parental Bonding Leave, among other benefit plan options.
About You
The ideal candidate will bring a combination of education, experience, and skills that enable them to excel in this position. The following qualifications outline what we’re looking for, including both required and preferred criteria
Education & Experience
A high school diploma or GED is required. A bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, Food Science, or related field is preferred. In lieu of completed degree, a combination of education and work experience will be considered.
10+ years of production management experience in a high-speed food / beverage/ CPG manufacturing environment, required.
2+ years of UHT dairy processing experience (preferred).
Experience in consumer packaging and continuous improvement methodologies (i.e. IWS, Lean, TPM), required.
Experience with budget and cost management, required.
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities
Ability to establish and react to changing priorities
Ability to prioritize plant operations in light of multiple priorities and conflicting demands.
Strong knowledge of GMP’s - to include regulations which govern food products
Knowledge of safety policies and procedures regarding chemicals, equipment/machinery
Excellent negotiation skills. - including an ability to understand sensitive situations.
Strong leadership skills, strong influential ability and strong interpersonal and communication skills required to interact successfully with all levels of plant and organization, as well as to develop and coach teams.
Strong analytical ability and have demonstrated problem solving and decision-making skills; ability to make decisions with limited information and to handle uncertainty and change.
Strong organizational skills, with the ability to schedule activities, and are process-oriented; able to identify process improvements and implement change successfully.
You have ability to support a 24/7 production environment as business needs dictate. Work schedules could include day or night shift schedules, and occasional weekends as business needs dictate.
About us
Danone U.S. is part of Danone North America, a purpose-driven company and an industry leader in the food and beverage category. You’ll work with some of the best-known food and beverage brands in the world. Our strong portfolio of brands includes Activia®, DanActive®, Danimals®, Dannon®, evian®, Follow Your Heart®, Happy Family® Organics, International Delight®, Light + Fit®, Nutricia ®, Oikos®, Silk®, So Delicious® Dairy Free, STōK® Cold Brew Coffee ®, Too Good & Co™, and YoCrunch®.
With approximately 5,000 employees and 13 production locations across the U.S., Danone North America's mission is to bring health through food to as many people as possible.
You’ll be part of one of the largest Certified B Corps™ in the world
, working to make sure our company creates real value for people and the planet. Come join our movement for a healthier world One Planet. One Health BY YOU.
Danone North America is proud to be an Equal Opportunity employer. It is our policy to give equal employment opportunities to all qualified persons without regard to legally protected characteristics, or any other consideration made unlawful by applicable federal, state/provincial and/or local law. Director of Manufacturing-Combustion
Power Flame Incorporated
Parsons, KS

Astec is a global, environmentally focused infrastructure and manufacturing company of asphalt road building and aggregate processing. Our mission is to design and build the most innovative products for the industries we serve. Leveraging innovative solutions and technologies, we serve customers all over the world.
ABOUT THE POSITION
The Director of Manufacturing will lead manufacturing activities while executing strategic initiatives and coordinating resources to fabricate, paint, and assemble heaters, tanks, piping, and accessories. The Director of Manufacturing will provide oversight to management and operations staff with the primary goal being to ensure a work environment that promotes safety, quality, and productivity while driving continuous improvement activities.
LOCATION: This is an onsite position at our Power Flame facility in Parsons, KS. Corporate relocation assistance is available.

Responsible for all manufacturing operations including the safety, production efficiencies, quality, and customer service.
Leads team members by managing and executing plant processes.
Supports continuous improvement processes to ensure safety, quality, goals are cost, and customer service are met.
Creates and maintains an engaged and team-oriented workforce to meet business demand.
Comply with all of Astec’s safety protocols.

Manage the manufacturing facility by ensuring all safety, quality, delivery, and financial goals and standards are consistently met
Ensure a healthy and safe working environment while complying with federal and state regulations through active collaboration with environmental, health, and safety (EHS) staff
Lead the manufacturing organization to build a strong culture of employee engagement and involvement, productivity, and accountability

Create and deliver progress and production reports to executive team members on a regular basis

Ability to manage conflict and resolve issues in the most positive fashion for all parties concerned
Ability to identify problems or potential problems at both a strategic and functional level and make or recommend decisions to resolve the same
Projects strong leadership skills

Willingness to accept responsibility and take on new challenges
Ability to influence others via communication to get desired results
Ability to exercise a high level of independent judgement on a customary and regular basis

Build and lead the Thermal Processing Equipment Reliability function — hire, mentor, and develop reliability and design engineers across the discipline
Own reliability engineering for thermal processing equipment

evidence.quote: Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
evidence.text:
Senior Manager, Manufacturing (Robot Production)
Genesis AI
San Carlos, CA
About Genesis
We are a full-stack general-purpose robot company, born across San Francisco and Paris and bound by a single mission: to make general-purpose robots a reality, unlocking infinite physical labor for the world and freeing people for creativity, exploration, and the pursuits they love for their own sake.
We are French and American by birth and global by nature. We are backed by partners who share our vision, including Eclipse, Khosla Ventures, Bpifrance, and HSG, alongside Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel, Daniela Rus, and Vladlen Koltun. Our people work across the Bay Area and Europe, building the engine that will teach robots to do real work in the real world. We recently unveiled Eno, our wheeled, dexterous robot powered by our GENE foundation model, and we are starting to put it to work with real customers.
The role
We build general-purpose robots, and next year we start building them in volume. You will be the manufacturing leader who takes the robot from engineering builds to production. Our CA facility is where new products are introduced: the process is designed, the first stations are built and proven, and the technicians are trained there. Volume production runs with a manufacturing partner, on their floor or on ours with their people, and you own the process in both cases. You design how the robot gets built, you lead the engineers and technicians who prove it, and you own the quality gate that decides when a unit leaves.
This is hands-on work. You design the first station, write the first work instruction, and bring the partner's team up to our standard. What exists today: an engineering build process with our design team, a production partner, a bill of materials and a plan. What does not exist yet is the production process, and that is the job.
What You'll Do
Design the production process: layout and cycle time, line balancing, station and fixture design, end-of-line test and calibration, material flow.
Capacity planning: stations, equipment, people and hours by build phase, from the first units to rate, and the plan to add capacity ahead of demand.
Specify, source and commission fixtures, tooling and test equipment: requirements, RFQ with Supply Chain, acceptance at the vendor and on the floor.
Own process documentation under revision control: work instructions with photos and video, PFMEA, control plans, inspection plans, SOPs; keep the manufacturing BOM aligned with the engineering BOM and run engineering changes through to the floor.
Run the transfer from engineering builds to production: pilot builds, DFM and DFA feedback with the authority to push back, build readiness reviews at each phase gate, release to volume.
Package the process so it can be copied: one documented set of stations, fixtures, test, instructions and training that a partner's floor can run to the same yield as ours.
Build and lead the team: manufacturing engineers, test engineers and technicians; hiring pace, training and certification, trainer capacity, shift structure as volume grows.
Own the quality gate: first-pass yield, defect capture, root cause (8D, SPC, DOE where it earns its keep), closed-loop feedback to engineering and suppliers; nothing ships that quality has not passed.
Partner with Supply Chain on clear-to-build so no unit starts without a complete kit, and with the manufacturing partner so their team runs our process to our standard.
Stand up the systems as we grow: traceability by serial, MES-lite at first, then the real thing; the weekly numbers (yield, hours per unit, cost per unit, downtime, schedule adherence) and the readout to leadership.
What We're Looking For
You have taken a complex electromechanical product from prototype through pilot to volume and designed the process yourself, not inherited it. Robots, vehicles, drones, medical devices, industrial equipment all count.
You have transferred a process to a contract manufacturer and held them to your standard.
Strong manufacturing engineering foundation: time studies, line balancing, capacity planning, fixture and tooling design, test strategy, PFMEA and control plans, lean and continuous improvement; CAD and GD&T fluency.
You have hired and trained technicians, written certification criteria, and know that trained people are the real constraint on throughput.
You have run a quality gate and held it under schedule pressure.
You are on the floor every day and rigorous in the data.
8 or more years in manufacturing engineering or production, with time in a mature organization so you know what good looks like at scale, and 3 or more years leading people.
Bonus: actuators, gearboxes or precision assemblies; PLM, MES and ERP implementation; product safety certification processes.
Working conditions
Production and lab environments; travel to partner sites, up to 25%.
Why this role
You build the way our robots get built, from the first station to rate, and the process and the team that do it are yours.
How We Work
We are always looking for people who are driven to work on hard problems and want to shape what the world will look like in ten years. A few of the values that guide us:
Limitless ambition. We hold ourselves to the highest bar in everything we build.
Relentless urgency. Iterate faster, learn faster. Time is the denominator.
Type-2 Fun. Take the work seriously, not yourself. Embrace the grind and find joy in the struggle.
Radical transparency. Candid communication builds trust, and direct feedback drives growth.
Multiculturalism. We come from across the world. Be curious. Meet people on their terms.
Team over ego. Help others, share context, and win as a team.
A joyful journey. We take pride in the craft.

The role is centered on vertical integration, operational excellence, and the development of scalable manufacturing capabilities that improve throughput, quality, and cost performance. This individual will partner closely with Engineering and cross-functional teams to strengthen production readiness, automation, and data-driven execution across the operation.
Location: Long Beach, CA
Compensation: $300,000 – $350,000 annually
Responsibilities
Lead all manufacturing and production test operations for product lines
Develop and execute production strategies for scaling
Own execution of vertical integration including test capabilities
Build scalable systems to improve throughput and quality
Drive lean manufacturing and data-driven management practices
Own development of tooling, automated test systems, and fixtures
Partner with Engineering to drive design-for-manufacturing into product development
Establish and review production metrics focused on efficiency
Lead quality execution across manufacturing and production verification
Drive automation of test execution and data collection
Collaborate cross-functionally for production readiness
Build and mentor high-performing teams for operational scale
Qualifications

15+ years leading manufacturing, production, integration, or operations in complex industries
Proven experience scaling production operations into repeatable environments
Strong background in manufacturing and assembly for complex electromechanical or aerospace systems
Experience establishing vertically integrated manufacturing capabilities

Overview
Englert - Director of Manufacturing
As the Director of Manufacturing, you will lead daily operations and drives sustained performance across Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, and People. Reporting to the President of Manufacturing, this role partners with Quality, Maintenance, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Supply Chain, Production Planning, and other support functions to achieve plant objectives.
This leader is accountable for production performance, labor productivity, schedule attainment, manufacturing cost, capacity utilization, talent development, and continuous improvement. The role establishes disciplined shop-floor management, develops manufacturing leaders, and builds a culture of accountability, problem solving, teamwork, and operational excellence.
Pay Range: Starting at $130,000 per year with variable comp
Responsibilities
Lead daily manufacturing operations to meet or exceed targets for Safety, Quality, Delivery, Cost, Productivity, and People.
Convert forecasts, demand, and business priorities into manufacturing plans, staffing models, capacity requirements, and execution priorities.
Lead, coach, and develop manufacturing managers, supervisors, and frontline leaders with clear expectations, accountability, and performance standards.
Maintain a disciplined daily management system with shift meetings, production reviews, KPI boards, escalation routines, and corrective-action follow-up.
Monitor manufacturing KPIs including safety performance, schedule attainment, output, labor efficiency, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, productivity, and manufacturing cost.
Ensure production issues and performance gaps are quickly identified, root causes addressed, corrective actions assigned, and results sustained.
Partner with Quality to improve first-pass yield, reduce defects and rework, resolve customer concerns, and strengthen process controls.
Partner with Maintenance to improve equipment reliability, reduce unplanned downtime, strengthen preventive maintenance, and increase asset utilization.
Collaborate with Production Planning and Supply Chain to align schedules, material availability, inventory needs, and customer commitments.
Partner with Engineering and Continuous Improvement to improve productivity, capacity, material flow, ergonomics, quality, and manufacturing cost.
Drive Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement through standard work, 5S/6S, visual management, problem solving, waste elimination, line balancing, and process optimization.
Increase output and capacity utilization while reducing labor hours, overtime, scrap, rework, downtime, and operational waste.
Establish, document, train, audit, and sustain standardized work processes and operating procedures.
Develop capacity and labor plans that support current demand, growth initiatives, new products, and changing customer requirements.
Use ERP systems and operational data to analyze performance, identify trends, set priorities, and drive factbased decisions.
Maintain daily, weekly, and monthly reporting that compares results to targets and highlights trends, gaps, and corrective actions.
Support the annual operating plan, manufacturing budget, capital requirements, productivity initiatives, and cost-reduction targets.
Manage manufacturing expenses within budget and deliver year-over-year improvements in labor productivity, conversion cost, scrap, and operational efficiency.
Champion safety by ensuring compliance with standards, participation in safety initiatives, and proactive risk identification and elimination.
Ensure manufacturing operations comply with company policies, regulatory requirements, quality systems, environmental requirements, and operating procedures.
Build succession plans and strengthen the leadership pipeline through coaching, performance management, cross-training, and talent development.
Partner with Human Resources to support hiring, onboarding, training, and retention of manufacturing employees and leaders.
Foster a culture where employees identify problems, recommend improvements, and engage in continuous improvement.
Perform other duties and lead special projects as assigned by the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations.
Qualifications
Key Performance Indicators
Success Will Be Measured By Sustained Improvement In
Safety performance
First-pass yield and internal quality
Customer quality and manufacturing-related complaints
Schedule attainment and on-time completion
Labor productivity and efficiency
Overtime
Scrap and rework
Equipment downtime and capacity utilization
Manufacturing cost
Inventory and material flow
Continuous improvement savings
Employee development, engagement, and retention
Skills, Knowledge, And Abilities
Manufacturing Leadership: Proven ability to lead complex manufacturing operations and deliver results through execution, accountability, and disciplined follow-through.
Operational Excellence: Strong command of manufacturing systems, production management, standard work, capacity planning, labor optimization, and performance management.
Lean Manufacturing & Continuous Improvement: Ability to apply Lean principles and structured problem solving to eliminate waste, improve flow, increase productivity, and reduce cost.
Financial Acumen: Strong understanding of manufacturing cost, labor performance, budgeting, productivity, capital investment, and plant profitability drivers.
Data-Driven Decision Making: Ability to use ERP systems, KPIs, dashboards, and financial data to identify trends, prioritize opportunities, and drive corrective action.
People Leadership: Proven ability to coach, develop, and hold leaders accountable while building a highperformance, respectful, and collaborative culture.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Ability to work effectively with Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering, Continuous Improvement, Finance, Human Resources, Sales, and other partners.
Problem Solving: Strong analytical skills with demonstrated use of structured root-cause analysis and corrective-action methods.
Change Leadership: Ability to lead organizational and operational changes while building ownership and accountability across manufacturing.
Shop-Floor Leadership: Hands-on leadership style with consistent floor presence and direct engagement with employees, supervisors, and operations.
Education And Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business or related field required; equivalent education and significant manufacturing leadership experience may be considered.
Minimum 7–10 years of progressive manufacturing experience, including at least five years in manufacturing leadership.
Experience managing multi-shift manufacturing operations and leading managers and supervisors.
Strong background in Lean Manufacturing, continuous improvement, structured problem solving, and performance management.
Experience using ERP/MRP systems and manufacturing data to manage performance and guide operational decisions.
Experience managing manufacturing budgets, labor productivity, cost reduction, and operational improvement programs.
Experience working within formal safety and quality management systems.
Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent practical continuous improvement experience preferred.
MBA, advanced technical degree, or Lean Six Sigma Black Belt preferred.
Bilingual Spanish preffered
Leadership Expectations
The Director of Manufacturing must be a visible shop-floor leader who creates accountability, develops leaders, and prevents recurring operational issues.
The successful leader will establish disciplined operating routines, use data to guide decisions, challenge existing processes, and continuously improve safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost.
This role works with the Sr. Director of Manufacturing Operations and leaders across Quality, Maintenance, Supply Chain, Engineering/Continuous Improvement, Finance, and Human Resources to achieve site and business objectives.
Physical Requirements
Prolonged standing and walking.
Must be able to lift 50 to 100 pounds and additional weight with assistance.
The physical demands described are representative of those required to perform the essential functions of this role. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these functions.
Benefits
Major Medical, Dental, Vision, 401(k), Flexible Time Off (FTO), Quarterly Bonus, advancement opportunities, and additional perks.

Grand Prix Plaza, home of the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix, is a world-class entertainment and event destination spanning approximately 39 acres in the heart of the Las Vegas Grand Prix circuit.  The 300,000-square-foot facility features immersive Formula 1 attractions, premium hospitality experiences, event and meeting venues, retail, food and beverage offerings, and year-round activations that attract guests from across the globe.  As both a daily operating entertainment venue and a critical component of one of the world's most recognized sporting events, Grand Prix Plaza requires a high-performing operational structure capable of delivering exceptional experiences while maintaining the highest standards of safety, service, and facility excellence.


 POSITION OVERVIEW
 The Director of Production serves as the leader responsible for all the experiences and production operations across Grand Prix Plaza.  This position provides strategic leadership for Production, Guest Experience, Box Office, and Karting operations, ensuring all attractions, technical systems, guest interactions, and show elements consistently deliver a premium and memorable experience.
 
Working closely with the General Manager and cross-functional departments, the Director of Production drives operational strategy, financial performance, workforce development, guest satisfaction, and continuous innovation across the venue's immersive attractions and entertainment offerings.  This role is responsible for ensuring all production and guest experience elements remain operationally ready to support daily business, private events, seasonal activations, and the Formula 1 Heineken Las Vegas Grand Prix.


 RESPONSIBILITIES 
 Develop and execute operational strategies that support organizational goals, business growth, and long-term venue objectives. 
 Provides overall leadership and direction for Production, Guest Experience, Box Office, and Karting departments.
 Leads, develops, and mentors departmental leadership teams, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, safety, and continuous improvement. 
 Establishes operational standards, guest service expectations, performance metrics, and departmental goals to drive exceptional guest satisfaction and revenue performance. 
 Oversees annual operating budgets, capital planning, labor strategies, and financial performance for all production and guest-facing departments. 
 Directs the planning, integration, and execution of attraction enhancements, technical upgrades, new experiences, venue activations, and special events. 
 Provides executive oversight of attraction reliability, show quality, technical systems, and operational readiness across all guest-facing experiences. 
 Manages key vendor relationships, production partners, service providers, and equipment suppliers to ensure performance, quality, and financial objectives are achieved. 
 Partners with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to support venue-wide initiatives, operational readiness, and organizational goals. 
 Ensures compliance with all applicable safety standards, operational procedures, regulatory requirements, and risk management practices associated with attractions, entertainment, and guest operations.
 Other responsibilities as assigned
 

 QUALIFICATIONS 
 9+ years of progressive leadership experience within entertainment venues, attractions, theme parks, sports venues, immersive experiences, or hospitality operations. 
 Demonstrated experience leading multi-disciplinary teams across production, guest experience, attractions, entertainment, box office, or related operational functions. 
 Proven experience managing operating budgets, labor planning, capital expenditures, and departmental financial performance. 
 Strong knowledge of attraction operations, live entertainment production, technical systems, guest experience management, and venue operations. 
 Experience overseeing third-party vendors, production contractors, service providers, and strategic partnerships. 
 Knowledge of OSHA requirements, risk management practices, life safety standards, and operational compliance requirements. 
 Experience supporting large-scale events, attraction launches, venue activations, or public-facing entertainment operations. 
 Strong business knowledge with the ability to analyze operational metrics, guest feedback, revenue performance, and financial reporting. 
 Exceptional leadership, communication, organizational, and stakeholder management skills. 
 Ability to effectively manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
   
 WORK SCHEDULE: 
 This is a full-time position that works a flexible schedule including weekdays, weekends, evenings, and holidays.   
  
 SEASONAL & EVENT-BASED RESPONSIBILITIES: 
 This role includes a seasonal period during which responsibilities extend beyond standard operations.  During load-in and load-out of the Grand Prix Plaza facility, race week activations, and other special projects, this position may support non-traditional functions that fall outside a routine.  Flexibility, cross-functional collaboration, and adaptability are essential and required during these high-impact times.
  
 PHYSICAL DEMANDS 
 Physical ability to walk, stand, take stairs/elevators/escalators, and navigate the elements during the day and night
 May need to remain in a sitting or standing position for prolonged periods, and repeat motions that may include the wrists, hands, and/or fingers
 Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
 Ability to handle exposure to loud noises at live events, attractions, entertaining programs, and crowd
 Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds at times. 
  
 Other Duties: Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities, duties or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job.  Duties, responsibilities and activities may change at any time with or without notice. 
 
Las Vegas Grand Prix, Inc. provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type. All employment decisions are based on business needs, job requirements, and individual qualifications without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex (including pregnancy), parental status, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws.
